# 0. How to read and govern this document

This is the single top-level source of truth for product intent, cross-system architecture, delivery boundaries and outstanding decisions. It contains the latest HTTP and realtime schema artifacts plus verbatim CR policy appendices so that product decisions, protocol details and validation evidence remain together.

## 0.1 Decision-status vocabulary

| Label | Meaning | May a developer treat it as final? |
|---|---|---|
| **OWNER CONFIRMED** | Explicitly confirmed by the product owner in the project decisions. | Yes for product behavior, subject to security and technical feasibility. |
| **ENGINEERING DRAFT** | A CR policy or schema has specified proposed behavior but has not received all required sign-offs or runtime verification. | No. Implement behind review only; do not infer approval. |
| **RECOMMENDED DEFAULT** | A technical/product recommendation intended to reduce risk or complexity. | No, unless elevated by a dated decision record. |
| **OPEN DECISION** | A genuine unresolved choice or numeric limit. | No. Block the affected implementation or use a reversible neutral design. |
| **EXTERNAL REQUIREMENT** | A requirement arising from a referenced standard or platform security rule. | Apply as appropriate, verify the specific standard and version during implementation. |
| **DEFERRED** | Deliberately scheduled after the initial production release. | Do not build in Phase 1 unless a dated scope change approves it. |
| **OUT OF SCOPE** | Explicitly excluded from the product plan. | Do not implement. Any reintroduction requires a product change decision. |
| **SUPERSEDED** | Historical material retained for traceability but replaced by a later decision. | No. The current main-body rule wins. |

## 0.2 Authority and conflict precedence

1. **Latest explicit product-owner decisions** govern product scope and user-visible behavior. In particular: Workspace is the primary work container; Projects/Lists are not part of the hierarchy; uploads/attachments are removed; cross-workspace transfer carries only task names and structural tree information; offline selected-field edits are in the initial release scope.
2. **This master document's main body** translates those decisions into the intended cross-system product and domain model. Any mismatch discovered in a source appendix is listed as a blocker and must not be silently followed.
3. **The latest HTTP and realtime schemas** govern the wire shape only after joint contract review. The Workspace-first candidate is OpenAPI `0.3.20-draft`; it is not frozen and must not be treated as implementation-authoritative until remaining product decisions and joint FE/BE/Security review are recorded.
4. **CR-01 through CR-16 policies** specify engineering behavior where compatible with the main body. Their current statuses remain draft unless the register explicitly says otherwise; engineering specificity does not equal stakeholder approval.
5. **Historical PRD/research and earlier CR policy snapshots in Appendices D onward** are preserved verbatim for traceability. They are non-normative wherever a historical statement conflicts with the current v1.5.0 main body, owner-confirmed decision register or API 0.3.20-draft. In particular, earlier open recommendations for DEC-OPEN-06/07/08/09/10/11/15 are superseded by the recorded 31 October 2026 owner approvals.
6. **No implementation may invent an API route, DTO field, enum, capability, database column, event or error code.** Change the contract first, review it jointly, regenerate types/mocks, then implement both sides.

## 0.3 Single-source change control

Every change to feature behavior must update this master and its feature/decision traceability. Every change to HTTP or WebSocket behavior must update the authoritative contract files in the same change set. Every data-model change must update database design/migrations, RLS policies, generated DTO types, event payloads, tests and migration/rollback notes. A PR is not complete if only one of these artifacts changes.

A scope change must record: decision ID; date; requestor/approver; previous behavior; new behavior; rationale; affected features, endpoints, entities, events and tests; migration/backfill plan; privacy/security implications; rollout and rollback. Never resolve a conflict by silently editing an old appendix.

# 1. Executive summary and product direction

## 1.1 Product vision — OWNER CONFIRMED

Build an original, modern, low-learning-curve work-management platform for an initial community of approximately 70–90 people, supporting engineering groups, event committees, operations teams, student clubs and study groups. The architecture must support multiple independent communities from day one without imposing enterprise-level administrative overhead on ordinary members.

The experience should combine the useful depth of a mature task tracker with the clarity and speed of a lightweight tool. A new member should be able to sign in, understand their personal work, create a task and update progress without training. Owners and administrators should be able to configure roles, access, workflows, saved views and governance from structured settings rather than forcing all members to deal with that complexity daily.

## 1.2 Core product problem

Lightweight boards become inadequate when teams need reliable identifiers, task hierarchy, dependencies, multiple synchronized planning views, role-aware editing, auditability and workspace-level ownership. Enterprise tools often solve those needs with a high configuration and learning burden. This product targets the middle ground: deep enough for complex community work, simple by default and governed at the right boundary.

## 1.3 Primary users and jobs to be done

| User type | Primary job | Product value |
|---|---|---|
| Community member / contributor | See work assigned to them across joined workspaces, update progress quickly, comment and manage private personal tasks. | My Work, rapid task creation, four consistent views, simple status actions and app-like mobile UX. |
| Coordinator | Organize shared work, assign tasks, resolve blockers, manage deadlines and help members. | Workspace coordination capabilities, hierarchy, dependencies, saved shared views and planning views. |
| Workspace Owner | Create and govern a workspace, control membership/roles, configure task behavior and recover mistakes. | Six-category settings, custom roles, workflow settings, role preview, task transfer and audit visibility. |
| Community Administrator | Manage community membership and shared-workspace policies, and perform limited emergency recovery when justified. | Community-scoped administration, default coordinator pool, governance audit and audited Personal Workspace break-glass. |
| Platform Operator | Maintain infrastructure without routine access to community content. | Operational-plane tools only; no silent tenant-content privilege. |

## 1.4 Binding product principles

1. **Simplicity first; depth on demand.** The default task composer should show no more than five fields. Advanced options live in contextual menus or categorized settings.
2. **One canonical task model.** List, Board, Calendar and Timeline are projections of the same authorized task set and the same canonical filters.
3. **Recognition over recall.** Use visible status/priority labels and icons, searchable keys, clear filter pills and familiar navigation rather than requiring a query language.
4. **Safe exploration.** Draft view/filter changes locally; explicitly save shared changes; provide undo/recovery for destructive actions where specified.
5. **Explain permissions.** The backend makes the decision; the UI explains why a control is unavailable in plain language.
6. **Privacy by default.** Community membership, workspace membership, task visibility and Personal Workspace privacy are separate and rechecked on every request.
7. **Mobile as a first-class client.** Core task create, status update and comment flows work comfortably on narrow touch screens.
8. **Contract-first parallel delivery.** Frontend and backend teams use the same reviewed schemas and mock fixtures; neither side invents behavior independently.

## 1.5 Explicit product non-goals — OUT OF SCOPE

- JQL or another complex text query language.
- Enterprise workflow transition screens, arbitrary workflow scripts or post-functions.
- Billable timers and worklog accounting.
- PMO scenario sandboxes, generic dashboard widget builders or enterprise ITSM/SLA/CMDB suites.
- Live scraping, reverse-engineering or copying proprietary hosted SaaS behavior/assets.
- File uploads, attachments, a workspace file hub, object-storage quotas or file recovery.
- Mandatory Projects, Lists or Milestone containers between a Workspace and its Tasks.
- Cross-community task transfer.
- Arbitrary user-authored automation scripts or unbounded automation loops.

# 2. Scope and release boundaries

## 2.1 Initial production release — Phase 1 — OWNER CONFIRMED

The Phase 1 release is complete only when all four views and the governance, privacy, collaboration and reliability gates pass. Work is sequenced to make delivery manageable; sequencing does not reduce launch scope.

### M1.1 — Core spine, identity, workspace and daily execution

- Email/password and Google sign-in, session lifecycle, account profile and community membership.
- Multi-community identity model and strict community/workspace authorization.
- Personal Workspace creation by every eligible user; Shared Workspace creation governed by community policy.
- Shared Workspace membership invitations, request/approval controls and default coordinator preselection/removal.
- Workspace Owner, Coordinator, Member and Viewer roles plus capability scaffolding for custom roles.
- Workspace → Task → Subtask hierarchy; task keys/aliases using the approved Community-wide prefix registry and Workspace-local monotonic sequence (database migration and runtime verification remain implementation work).
- Basic task create/read/update, assignment, status, priority, dates, estimates, labels and dependencies.
- List and Board views using shared query behavior.
- My Work cross-workspace dashboard and omnibar/search.
- Task detail drawer, comments, @mentions, watchers, in-app inbox foundation and realtime collaboration.
- Saved-view foundation with personal/shared scope and copy-on-write.
- Activity history, safe optimistic UI and online undo where approved.

### M1.2 — Complete planning and configuration experience

- Calendar and Timeline views; all four views operate from the same task data and filter semantics.
- Date windows, unscheduled tasks and dependency-conflict visualization.
- Workspace-level workflow statuses and simple five-category mapping.
- Workspace-level custom fields (Phase 1 types below).
- Exactly three built-in Workspace setup templates: General Purpose, Event Planning and Team Operations; each seeds configuration only, never sample tasks or members.
- Task/subtask hierarchy controls and key configuration, after project-removal remediation.
- Bulk task operations with atomic all-or-nothing semantics where included in the reviewed contract.
- Saved view lifecycle, presentation settings and workspace copying where permitted.
- Search/filter polish and cross-view parity tests.

### M1.3 — Governance, mobile, offline and production acceptance

- Custom role builder, capability delegation controls and preview-as-role simulator.
- Six workspace settings categories: General, Members, Permissions, Tasks, Views, Notifications.
- Audit log views/exports with correct workspace/community scoping and privacy safeguards.
- In-app/email notification preferences, quiet hours, digest behavior and deadline reminders.
- Selected-field offline editing for existing tasks, using the CR-15 allow-list, 14-day queue age, FIFO replay and per-field conflict handling. This is in the initial release scope, not deferred to Phase 3.
- Full mobile-first core flows: create task, update status, comment, inspect assigned work and navigate all four views with suitable mobile adaptations.
- Accessibility review, performance testing, backup/restore rehearsal, rollback rehearsal, security review and operational readiness.
- Product, frontend, backend, security and operations launch sign-off.

## 2.2 Roadmap after Phase 1

| Phase | Deferred capabilities | Guardrails |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 2** | Guided CSV import, shareable intake forms, extended custom-field types, richer/custom digest schedules. | Dry-run previews, validation and import rollback; form abuse controls; preserve Phase 1 field semantics. |
| **Phase 3** | Declarative one-hop automations, status sign-off gates, outbound HTTPS webhooks, field revision restore and further workflow automation. | No arbitrary scripts; bounded one-hop evaluation; SSRF controls for webhooks; permission-aware restore. Offline task-field editing is not deferred; it belongs in M1.3. |
| **Phase 4** | Opt-in agile cycles, charts and carefully scoped AI-assisted features. | Domain-neutral core terminology; no default Sprint/Burndown language for non-software teams; opt-in per workspace. |

These roadmap capabilities must remain traceable but must not expand Phase 1 by omission. A dated decision is required to move any feature between phases.

## 2.3 Excluded file capability — OWNER CONFIRMED

No task attachment, comment attachment, Workspace File Hub, binary upload/download, signed storage URL, storage quota, malware scanning pipeline, object-storage vendor or file recovery feature is in the current product. Remove stale file references from implementation prompts, DTOs, navigation, settings, acceptance tests and deployment estimates. Audit metadata may mention historical file-related actions only if an actual record existed in a prior compatible system; it must not imply new upload support.

# 3. Domain model and information architecture

## 3.1 Governing hierarchy — OWNER CONFIRMED

```text
Global User Identity
  └── Community (tenant boundary)
        ├── CommunityMembership
        └── Workspace (Personal | Shared)   ← primary work container
              ├── WorkspaceMembership (Shared only)
              ├── Workspace Settings / Roles / Workflow
              ├── Saved Views
              ├── Custom Field Definitions
              ├── Milestones (optional Workspace-level planning markers)
              └── Task
                    └── Subtask (configurable depth)
```

There is no Project or List layer. A team that needs a separate context creates another Workspace and invites the relevant members. Tasks and subtasks live directly inside a Workspace. This rule governs UI, domain model, persistence, API routes, permissions, filters, realtime events, tests and documentation.

## 3.2 Core entities and ownership boundaries

| Entity | Scope / purpose | Key invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `User` | Global identity, independent of any one community. | One identity may join multiple communities; auth credentials remain outside community data. |
| `Community` | Tenant/security boundary. | All tenant-owned rows reference one community; no cross-community reads by guessed IDs. |
| `CommunityMembership` | User's membership and admin/coordinator-pool flags in one community. | Community Admin authority is scoped to this row/community only. |
| `Workspace` | Main unit of work; `PERSONAL` or `SHARED`. | Belongs to one community; Personal is private and single-owner; Shared has explicit membership. |
| `WorkspaceMembership` | Active user's access to a Shared Workspace. | One current role per member; role and membership are checked at every operation. |
| `WorkspaceRole` | Built-in or workspace-local custom role. | Built-in identities are stable; no role inheritance; grant ceiling enforced by backend. |
| `Task` | Canonical unit of work. | Workspace-scoped; internal UUIDv7 identity; title/key/type/status/priority/date/estimate/labels/custom values and relationships. |
| `TaskAssignee` | Assignment relation. | Stores `assignedByUserId` separately from assignee; supports multiple assignees if confirmed in the final DTO. |
| `TaskLineage` | Stable identity across same-community workspace transfers. | Holds current task/workspace pointer; not an authorization bypass. |
| `TaskKeyAlias` | Immutable historical key registry. | Maps issuing workspace namespace + normalized key to stable lineage; aliases never reassign or recycle. |
| `TaskLink` | Dependency or relationship between tasks. | BLOCKS graph must be acyclic; inaccessible target metadata is masked. |
| `WorkflowStatus` | Workspace-defined visible statuses. | Every status maps to one of five canonical categories. |
| `Milestone` | Optional planning marker directly in a Workspace. | OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-08; never a hierarchy container; tasks link directly to a milestone in the same Workspace. |
| `CustomFieldDefinition` / `CustomFieldOption` | Workspace-level schema for task metadata. | Field identity immutable; options use stable UUIDs; values validated server-side. |
| `SavedView` | PERSONAL or SHARED preset for one of four projections. | Stores query and display options separately; shared edits use explicit copy-on-write. |
| `Comment` / `TaskWatcher` | Task collaboration. | Sanitized Markdown AST; mentions/watchers resolved only among authorized users. |
| `Notification` / `NotificationPreference` | Recipient-scoped inbox and delivery controls. | One user's community stream; preference changes are per user/community. |
| `TaskActivity` | User-visible task history. | Separate from security/governance audit. |
| `AuditEvent` | Append-only governance/security evidence. | Hash chained, minimized, scoped read/export; retention/purge remains open. |
| `DomainEvent` / `OutboxOffset` | Durable transactional outbox and independent consumers. | Domain mutation, stream sequence and outbox intent commit atomically. Each consumer tracks its own progress. |
| `IdempotencyRecord` | Replay-safe mutation record. | Binds key to canonical request fingerprint and stored deterministic result; credentials never persisted. |
| `Session` / `AuthIdentity` | Authentication and session control. | Secure cookie, CSRF, rotation, revocation and account-linking invariants. |
| `Invitation` / `MembershipRequest` | Community and Shared Workspace onboarding. | Single-use expiring invitation; active community membership prerequisite for Shared Workspace invite. |

## 3.3 Proposed relational model — ENGINEERING DRAFT

The following is a logical design, not a claim that SQL migrations have been authored or run. PostgreSQL is the current preferred database recommendation, with row-level security (RLS) and composite tenant keys. Final table/column design must be co-signed by backend and security owners and reconciled to the repaired OpenAPI contract.

### Identity and tenancy

- `community_task_key_prefix_registry(community_id, normalized_prefix, workspace_id, reserved_at, retired_at nullable)`; unique `(community_id, normalized_prefix)` under case-folded normalization; insert-only reservations are never released or reassigned after rename, archive or Workspace deletion.
- `workspace_task_key_sequences(workspace_id, next_sequence, version)`; Workspace-local atomic allocator; never reset, decrement or reuse a sequence value.
- `workspace_template_catalog(template_key, template_version, immutable_definition_json, published_at)`; three built-in, read-only catalog entries; applied template key/version are recorded on the Workspace.


- `users(id UUIDv7 PK, email_normalized UNIQUE, display_name, account_state, created_at, updated_at)`.
- `auth_identities(id, user_id FK, provider, provider_subject, credential_hash_or_external_ref, verified_at, created_at)`; unique `(provider, provider_subject)`; prevent unlinking the last usable verified auth method.
- `communities(id, name, policy_json, created_at, ...)`.
- `community_memberships(id, community_id, user_id, state, is_community_admin, is_default_coordinator, joined_at, ...)`; unique `(community_id,user_id)`.
- `workspaces(id, community_id, kind, name, owner policy, key_prefix, next_task_sequence, applied_template_key nullable, applied_template_version nullable, settings, assignee_editable_field_groups_allowed JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', assignee_editable_field_groups_default JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', last_workspace_seq, archived_at, ...)`; enforce that the default is a subset of the allowed ceiling in the backend transaction; ensure Personal single-owner privacy and Shared owner floor.
- `workspace_memberships(id, community_id, workspace_id, user_id, role_id, state, joined_at, ...)`; unique `(workspace_id,user_id)`; FK includes community/workspace scope.
- `workspace_roles(id, community_id, workspace_id, system_key nullable, name, capabilities JSONB, version, ...)`; seeded role identities OWNER/COORDINATOR/MEMBER/VIEWER, custom roles scoped to one workspace; no inheritance.

### Tasks and relationships

- `tasks(id UUIDv7 PK, community_id, workspace_id, parent_task_id nullable, lineage_id, title, description, item_type, status_id/status_category, priority, start_date, due_date, estimate_points, assignee_editable_field_groups JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', rank_key, version, field_revisions JSONB, archived_at, created_by_user_id, created_at, updated_at, ...)`. Validate each task grant set as a subset of the current Workspace ceiling; include `assigneeEditableFieldGroups` in field revision tracking.
- Composite foreign keys ensure `(community_id, workspace_id)` agrees across parent, child, membership, alias and relationship rows.
- `task_assignees(task_id, user_id, assigned_by_user_id, assigned_at, ...)`; backend records assigner and validates current assignment context.
- `task_lineages(id, community_id, current_task_id, current_workspace_id, updated_at)`; update current pointer in the same transaction as transfer.
- `task_key_aliases(id, community_id, issuing_workspace_id, normalized_key, lineage_id, created_at)`; unique `(community_id, normalized_key)` in addition to namespace lookup; append-only; no reassignment/reuse. The permanent Community-wide prefix registry prevents ambiguous current and historical key strings.
- `task_links(id, community_id, source_task_id, target_task_id, link_type, created_by, created_at)`; unique and cycle validation for BLOCKS; target privacy filter is applied in DTO projection.
- `workflow_statuses(id, community_id, workspace_id, name, category, rank, is_default, ...)`; category in BACKLOG/TODO/IN_PROGRESS/DONE/CANCELED; deleting an in-use status requires atomic task migration to a fallback in the same Workspace.
- `workspace_milestones(id, community_id, workspace_id, title, description, target_date, ...)`; `tasks.milestone_id` references a milestone in the same Workspace. Milestones are OWNER CONFIRMED optional Workspace planning markers, never hierarchy containers.

### Configuration and collaboration

- `custom_field_definitions(id, community_id, workspace_id, name, key, value_type, required, archived_at, version, ...)`.
- `custom_field_options(id, field_definition_id, label, rank, archived_at)`; stable option UUIDs.
- `task_custom_field_values(task_id, field_definition_id, value_json, field_revision, updated_at, updated_by)` with unique `(task_id, field_definition_id)` and same-workspace validation.
- `saved_views(id, community_id, workspace_id, owner_user_id, scope PERSONAL|SHARED, view_type, query_spec_json, display_options_json, version, ...)`; personal access limited to creator; Shared access requires current task:read.
- `comments(id, community_id, workspace_id, task_id, author_user_id, parent_comment_id, markdown_source, sanitized_ast, version, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)`; enforce thread depth cap and markdown allow-list.
- `task_watchers(task_id, user_id, subscribed_at, source)`; mention/creator/assignee auto-watch behavior per CR-08, with explicit unsubscribe rules.
- `notifications(id, community_id, recipient_user_id, workspace_id nullable, task_id nullable, category, event_type, payload_metadata, read_at, created_at)`; user/community stream cursor separate.
- `notification_preferences(user_id, community_id, channel, category, enabled, quiet_hours, digest_schedule, ...)`.

### Operations and evidence

- `domain_events(id, community_id, workspace_id nullable, user_id nullable, stream_type, stream_seq, event_type, schema_version, payload_minimized, occurred_at)`; immutable event envelope; no one global `processed_at` marker.
- `outbox_consumer_offsets(consumer_group, shard_key, last_event_id/seq, updated_at)` and `outbox_consumer_failures(...)`; independent cursors for realtime, notifications and later consumers.
- `idempotency_records(scope_key, mutation_id, method, canonical_path, request_fingerprint, response_status, response_body_minimized, created_at, expires_at)`; transactionally coupled to mutation and outbox; never retain session/CSRF/Set-Cookie credential material.
- `task_activity_events(...)` distinct from security audit.
- `audit_events(id, community_id, workspace_id nullable, sequence, actor_user_id, event_type, metadata_minimized, previous_hash, entry_hash, occurred_at)`; append-only application grants; external write-only checkpoint sink; retention duration and legal hold are unresolved.
- `break_glass_grants(...)` and immutable `break_glass_evidence(...)` with grant/revoke/expiry and notification state.
- `invitations(...)`, `membership_requests(...)`, `sessions(...)`, `password_reset_tokens(...)`, `email_verification_tokens(...)`, `realtime_tickets(...)` with hashed one-time secrets.

## 3.4 Tenant and hierarchy invariants

1. Every tenant-owned row carries `community_id`; every workspace-owned row also carries `workspace_id`.
2. Composite foreign keys, RLS and application authorization must agree. RLS is defense in depth, not the only security control.
3. A task and all descendants belong to exactly one Workspace. A parent cannot be in another Workspace.
4. Parent changes are cycle checked and bounded by a Workspace-level maximum subtask depth. **OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-09:** default one subtask level (`maxSubtaskDepth = 1`); Workspace Owner may raise the maximum to two levels; unbounded nesting is not supported. A reduction is rejected atomically while any existing tree exceeds the proposed new limit; users must restructure those trees first.
5. Same-workspace parent/order changes preserve task identity and all content; children move with parent.
6. Cross-workspace transfer is a privacy boundary operation and uses the name-only policy in Section 8.
7. Do not add `project_id`, `list_id`, project membership, project-level capability scope or project-level key sequence to the target model.
8. Personal Workspaces are single-owner/private. Community Admins do not gain silent content access. Only the audited break-glass path grants time-bound read-only access under CR-01.
9. Workspace membership removal or role downgrade must revoke HTTP and active realtime access promptly; authorization is reevaluated on every operation.
10. Archived/purged record lookup must authorize against the current workspace before revealing a tombstone or 410 condition.

---

# 4. Task model and task lifecycle

## 4.1 Canonical task fields

A Task is the only work item container in a Workspace. Subtasks are Tasks with a parent relation, not a separate list/project resource. Core task fields:

- UUIDv7 internal ID; immutable lineage ID for same-community transfer continuity.
- Workspace ID and nullable parent task ID.
- Human-readable current key plus key-alias history.
- Title (required), optional description and task archetype/type.
- Configurable Workspace workflow status, mapped to a canonical status category.
- Priority: NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, URGENT (exact enum/order to follow reviewed schema).
- Assignee relation(s), creator identity and assigner identity kept distinct.
- Start date, due date, estimate points, labels and rank/order token.
- Optional Workspace milestone relation; milestone is a planning marker, not a hierarchy container.
- Workspace-defined custom-field values with per-field revisions.
- Task links/dependencies and version/updated timestamp.
- Created/updated/archive lifecycle timestamps.

## 4.2 Task type and status model

The current contract draft defines `TASK`, `DELIVERABLE`, `BUG` and `DECISION` archetypes, with `TASK` as the default. The exact user-facing type vocabulary is an engineering draft, not a separately approved product decision; keep additional type choices low-friction and do not let them become hierarchy containers. It is not a new hierarchy layer.

Every configured status maps to one of five canonical categories:

- `BACKLOG`
- `TODO`
- `IN_PROGRESS`
- `DONE`
- `CANCELED`

A Workspace starts with a simple default workflow. Owners (and delegated Coordinators where approved) may rename/add statuses or map statuses to categories inside Workspace settings. Any status deletion with assigned tasks requires an explicit fallback status and one atomic migration. Timeline and reporting must consistently distinguish completed (`DONE`/`CANCELED`) work from active work.

## 4.3 Dependencies and relationships

Supported relationship candidates are `BLOCKS`, `IS_BLOCKED_BY` (normally derived as the inverse of BLOCKS), `RELATES_TO` and `DUPLICATES`. BLOCKS must form a directed acyclic graph; adding a link that creates a cycle is rejected. Dependencies can connect tasks within a Workspace; cross-Workspace task links are not assumed and require a separate privacy/authorization decision. A user without access to the target must never receive its title, key, status or workspace identity in a task-link summary.

## 4.4 Task keys — OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-06

Task keys are short human-readable references such as `OPS-12`. They support discussion, search, mentions, URLs and support/debugging; they are not database primary keys. Internal UUIDv7 IDs remain immutable.

Every Workspace has a canonical uppercase prefix and a Workspace-local numeric sequence. Prefixes are unique across all current and historical namespaces within one Community (case-insensitive), and a prefix is never reassigned after rename, Workspace archive or deletion. Sequences are atomic, monotonically increasing, never reset and never reused after task archive, purge, transfer or prefix rename.

An active Workspace Owner may rename the prefix. The operation must be atomic: reserve the new Community-unique prefix; update the current display key for every active task while preserving its numeric suffix; insert each prior current key as an immutable alias; preserve all older aliases; append the governance audit record and outbox event; then commit. A collision with a current or historical prefix reservation rejects the complete operation with `409 WORKSPACE_KEY_PREFIX_ALREADY_IN_USE`.

Aliases map to stable task lineage, not transient task UUIDs. Resolution must authorize the caller against the lineage's current Workspace before revealing a current task key, task ID or lifecycle state. Unknown and unauthorized key lookups use indistinguishable 404 responses. Historical prefixes and aliases are never reassigned.

## 4.5 Task edit and execution permissions

Default task policy is `CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT` in the CR-05 engineering draft:

- Workspace Owners and Coordinators can manage task definitions, subject to security floors.
- Task creator retains the defined creator rights while they remain an authorized active member.
- An active task assigner can retain definition/assignment rights for the assignments they created, subject to current membership and assignment rules.
- Assignees can update execution status, comment and manage/create permitted subtasks within the assigned task scope.
- Workspace Owners configure the maximum additional field groups that may be delegated to assignees and the default grant set for newly created tasks. Both default to empty; the default must be a subset of the allowed ceiling.
- The Task Creator chooses the additional assignee field groups for each task from the Workspace-approved ceiling. The same task-level grant set applies to every active assignee on that task; per-assignee differences are not part of this contract.
- An active Workspace Owner may override per-task assignee grants for governance and continuity. Coordinators and Task Assigners do not receive this permission solely from their role.
- Members can create tasks, comment, watch and use views; other editing depends on configured task policy.
- `COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER` is an Owner-controlled alternative under which active non-Viewer members receive broader collaboration rights, but not governance, move/archive/purge or Workspace administration rights.
- Viewers remain read-only apart from any explicitly allowed watch behavior.

The Option A delegation ownership model is OWNER CONFIRMED under DEC-OPEN-02. The exact field-group catalog and implementation controls are engineering-defined and remain subject to joint Backend/Frontend/Security contract review. A relationship grant does not bypass community/workspace membership, Personal Workspace privacy, disabled/suspended membership or resource visibility. Mixed-field PATCH requests are all-or-nothing. Server-side permission checks are performed afresh for every operation. DTO `effectivePermissions` are UI hints only—not bearer authority.

---

# 5. Roles, membership, workspace governance and privacy

## 5.1 Identity and membership boundaries

- One global User identity can join multiple independent Communities.
- A `CommunityMembership` is independent from `WorkspaceMembership`.
- Community Admin authority comes only from the user's active membership in that same Community. It does not imply membership in all its Workspaces or task-level read access.
- Shared Workspace invitation requires active Community membership. Community invite acceptance precedes Workspace invitation acceptance where necessary.
- Personal Workspace creation is self-service for every eligible user. The Personal Workspace has one owner and is private; it does not accept additional workspace members.
- Shared Workspace creation is controlled by a Community policy. Workspace membership is explicitly invited/requested/approved and revocable.
- The community's Default Coordinator pool is preselected for new Shared Workspaces. The creator/owner can remove members from the preselected list before creation and the Owner can later remove a Coordinator. This default is for new workspaces only; it does not grant retroactive access to existing workspaces.

## 5.2 Built-in and custom roles

Built-in role identities: `OWNER`, `COORDINATOR`, `MEMBER`, `VIEWER`. The role model is flat: exactly one role per active WorkspaceMembership, no role inheritance and no implicit capability stacking. Custom roles are Workspace-local capability sets.

Custom role governance must enforce a grant ceiling: an actor cannot create/assign a role containing capabilities they do not personally hold and are allowed to delegate. Sensitive capabilities (ownership transfer, membership/role governance, audit export, purge and security configuration) require explicit reserved handling. Community Admin privileges remain separate from Workspace role capabilities.

Role preview is a read-only, downward-only simulation. It can demonstrate a more restrictive role view but must never grant a capability the actual actor does not possess. Preview mode is not a security boundary; backend authorization continues to use the authenticated user's real membership and the preview mask.

## 5.3 Workspace settings — OWNER CONFIRMED

The settings navigation has exactly six top-level categories:

1. **General** — name, description, archive/restore and ownership controls.
2. **Members** — invitations, requests, member list, role assignment and default Coordinator inclusion.
3. **Permissions** — built-in/custom roles, capabilities, per-setting access and role preview.
4. **Tasks** — task policy, task hierarchy depth, key prefix/sequence, statuses, priority defaults, labels, dependencies and custom fields.
5. **Views** — four views, default projection behavior, saved views, layout and display options.
6. **Notifications** — recipient preferences, channels, quiet hours, digest controls and Workspace deadline reminders.

The six categories supersede older nine-category mockups and navigation structures. Each setting needs an identified owner capability and a clear explanation of who may change it. If fine-grained per-setting authorization is offered, changes must be validated by the backend—not merely hidden in the frontend.

## 5.4 Ownership and recovery — OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-15

Shared Workspaces may have multiple active Owners. At least one active Owner must remain at every transaction commit. Owner promotion/transfer uses the dedicated atomic `owner-transfer` operation: promote an eligible active Workspace member first, then optionally demote or suspend the caller in the same transaction. A last active Owner cannot leave, be suspended, be removed or be demoted unless a replacement becomes Owner in that transaction. Generic membership/role patch endpoints cannot promote or demote an Owner.

Personal Workspaces remain single-owner and do not support multi-owner transfer. Community Admin recovery is separate, audited and explicit; it is not silent routine takeover authority. The API candidate already contains the dedicated owner-transfer operation; its runtime and audit behavior require joint Backend/Security verification.

## 5.5 Personal Workspace privacy and emergency access

**Privacy status — OWNER CONFIRMED.**

The selected product policy is `AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS`, not broad administrator access. Only an active Community Administrator belonging to the same Community as the target Personal Workspace may initiate. Platform Operators, cross-community administrators, Coordinators and ordinary members cannot initiate. The access is read-only and limited to one Personal Workspace. Fresh reauthentication is required; the justification uses a closed reason category plus a minimum non-whitespace explanation. The CR-01 draft chooses a 15-minute default, 60-minute maximum initial grant, one independently approved 30-minute extension and 90-minute absolute lifetime. Owner notification, grantor/peer-admin revocation and immutable pre-access audit evidence are mandatory. The exact procedure needs product/security/backend sign-off before freeze.

Routine support, curiosity, performance monitoring, convenience or ordinary management review are not valid reasons. A separate formal legal process is required for legal/regulatory disclosure; break-glass is not a substitute.

---

# 6. Functional product requirements

## 6.1 Workspace lifecycle

- A signed-in user can create a Personal Workspace without a community-wide administrator granting special permission, subject to account/community policy.
- Shared Workspace creation obeys Community-level controls.
- Workspace creation allows name, optional description, template/preset selection, default Coordinator preselection and initial membership where authorized.
- The creator becomes an Owner. Shared Workspaces maintain an Owner floor.
- Workspace owners can invite active Community members, approve membership requests, assign allowed roles, remove members, archive/restore and transfer ownership.
- Membership changes invalidate current REST and realtime authorization promptly.

## 6.2 Task creation and editing

- Quick-create task composer: title required; default visible input count capped at five. Advanced details are available after creation or in a secondary section.
- Create task at Workspace root or as a child of another task, subject to hierarchy depth.
- Support inline changes for status, priority, assignee, due date and labels where authorized.
- Support estimates, start/due dates, task archetypes, dependencies and Workspace custom fields.
- Provide clear validation and field-level errors; forbidden mixed updates fail atomically.
- Task detail is opened from any projection without losing the current view context.

## 6.3 Four synchronized views — all required at launch

All projections use the same query membership and authorization rules. Projection changes only response/presentation shape, not the set of accessible tasks.

### List

- Dense desktop tree/grid layout with expandable subtasks and inline property editing.
- Keyboard accessible row navigation and expansion.
- Fast inline creation and multi-select foundation.
- Touch row targets expand to suitable mobile size.

### Board

- Workflow status columns; optional backlog tray.
- Cards show key, title, status, priority, due date, assignee and subtask progress as configurable display options.
- Reorder/status changes supported by pointer and non-drag alternatives (menu or keyboard reorder).
- Mobile adapts to a stage/status switcher instead of forcing a wide desktop board.

### Calendar

- Month/week/agenda-like windows; tasks displayed by due date or start–due span.
- Unscheduled tray displays matching undated tasks and makes them schedulable without hiding them.
- Date editing works by keyboard/menu as well as drag interactions.

### Timeline

- Split view: task hierarchy table plus horizontal time axis.
- Day/week/month/quarter zoom where practical.
- Draw date spans and dependency relationships; show conflicts when a non-completed blocker finishes later than its dependent task begins.
- All edits remain possible without dragging timeline bars.

## 6.4 Canonical query and view state

One canonical `ViewQuerySpec` defines filters, sorting, grouping, subtask inclusion and date window. The frontend serializes transient filters into URL/local navigation state. Saved view query specification is stored separately from display options/projection. A changed filter/sort on a Shared View is local until an explicit save/update action. A user can save a Personal View without changing the Shared View. Shared view update rights are role/capability controlled.

Task query snapshots use the CR-15 fixed 900-second cursor policy. Realtime updates newer than the snapshot watermark invalidate or refresh the active projection without mixing incompatible membership snapshots. List/Calendar/Timeline task limits and Board per-group limits must follow the latest CR-15 specification until the post-remediation contract review revises it.

## 6.5 Search, omnibar and My Work

- Global omnibar supports task key/current alias, title, and saved-view/workspace discovery.
- All search is permission-aware and intersects current Community/Workspace memberships; never disclose hidden names, keys, counts or metadata.
- My Work aggregates tasks assigned to, created by or watched by the user across accessible Personal and Shared Workspaces.
- Default useful groups: Overdue, Due Today, Upcoming and Unscheduled. Allow filter/sort customization and return-to-workspace navigation.
- Search results and aliases must authorize the current lineage destination before disclosing the task.

## 6.6 Comments, mentions and watchers

- Task-scoped threaded comments with a safe Markdown subset.
- Server converts Markdown into a versioned typed AST; clients render safe elements, never raw HTML.
- Disallow scripts, raw HTML, arbitrary SVG/iframe/image/embed nodes and dangerous URL schemes.
- @mention candidate search is permission-aware and only resolves currently authorized users in the same Workspace/Community scope.
- `#KEY` tokens resolve through the task-key alias system; inaccessible/unknown keys remain unlinked plain text.
- Creator/assignees/mentioned users may be auto-watched according to CR-08 draft; any eligible member may toggle watch state.
- File attachments and comment file IDs are not supported.

## 6.7 Notifications and reminders

- In-app Inbox categories: Action Required and Updates (CR-10 draft).
- Events include mentions, new assignment, approved sign-off requests if added later, reminders, watched-task comments and status changes.
- Recipient-specific notification settings; email and in-app channel preferences; quiet hours/local timezone and digest options subject to final signoff.
- Workspace-configured deadline reminder offsets with recipient preferences, assignee/creator fallback and deduplication.
- Durable notification generation uses outbox and bounded retries; sending a message must not block realtime event consumption.
- Provider/sender/domain configuration is deployment-dependent and remains open.

## 6.8 Custom fields

Phase 1 engineering draft supports `TEXT`, `NUMBER`, `DATE`, `BOOLEAN`, `SINGLE_SELECT` only. Definitions belong to the Workspace, not a Project. Field values are typed and validated server-side; single-select option UUIDs are stable; labels are display-only. Required-field changes and deletion/archive behavior must preserve existing values through an explicit migration or archive strategy. Custom field value changes use per-field revisions for conflict detection. Filtering/sorting is allowed only for supported indexed field types and reviewed query operators. Extended types are Phase 2.

## 6.9 Templates, milestones and bulk actions — OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-07/08

Exactly three versioned, read-only built-in Workspace setup templates are included: `GENERAL_PURPOSE`, `EVENT_PLANNING` and `TEAM_OPERATIONS`. They seed workflow statuses, supported Phase 1 custom-field definitions/options and default SHARED saved views atomically with Workspace creation. They never create sample tasks/subtasks, assignees, assignments, comments, watchers, members, invitations or permission escalations. Existing Workspaces are not silently changed when the catalog version changes; Owners can edit the resulting configuration. A custom template builder is not part of the initial release.

Milestones are retained as optional Workspace-level planning markers linked directly to tasks. They may appear in Timeline/task context but are never hierarchy containers or an intermediate layer between Workspace and Task.

Bulk operations, if included in the reviewed release contract, are bounded, permission checked and all-or-nothing. A failed item means the transaction does not partially mutate the rest. Undo semantics must be explicit and durable enough for recovery.

### Task Trash and permanent purge — OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-11

Archived tasks remain restorable for exactly 30 days. Expiry ends the normal recovery window; it does not automatically hard-delete the record. Permanent purge is separate, explicit, Owner-authorized and audit-recorded, and applies to an archived task subtree atomically. Historical key aliases and minimum content-free lineage tombstones remain for privacy-safe resolution. The purge operation is specified in API 0.3.20-draft but remains feature-disabled until DEC-OPEN-03 audit-retention/legal-hold authority is approved. Audit-log retention is a separate policy and is not set by this decision.

## 6.10 Activity, audit and recovery

- Task activity is user-facing history of task changes and collaboration.
- Governance/security audit events are separate, append-only and tamper-evident.
- Break-glass evidence is a distinct security-sensitive record class.
- Audit metadata must avoid raw task descriptions, titles, comment bodies, credentials, personal contact details and custom field values unless a specifically approved legal/security requirement says otherwise.
- Audit read/export is scoped: Community Admin to that community, Workspace Owner to that workspace, with separate `audit:read` and `audit:export` capabilities. Coordinators/Members have no default audit access; Platform Operator has no silent tenant-content audit privilege.
- Audit retention duration, archive schedule, legal-hold authority and ultimate purge remain open. Do not enable automatic audit purge.

---

# 7. UX, interaction and visual requirements

## 7.1 Persistent application shell

- Left navigation rail on desktop, collapsible and optimized for fast workspace switching.
- Global navigation: Omnibar, Quick Create, My Work, Inbox, Workspace Switcher, Saved Views, Trash/Recovery and User Preferences.
- Active Workspace navigation: four views and Workspace settings; no Projects/Lists accordion.
- Community administration appears only to authorized Community Admins.
- Main canvas remains visible while task details open in a right-side Task Peek Drawer on desktop and a full-height bottom sheet/full-screen view on mobile.
- Task details deep-link to the current task key/ID without losing view context.

## 7.2 Progressive disclosure layers

1. **Daily work:** task quick-create, inline status/priority/assignee/date controls, saved-view access and filter chips.
2. **View tuning:** grouping, sorting, card properties, column visibility and view-specific preferences.
3. **Governance:** role matrix, custom fields, status configuration, hierarchy, key namespace and security settings inside the six settings categories.

Do not put the entire permission matrix or custom-field editor into the daily task view.

## 7.3 Responsive and mobile behavior

- Desktop should optimize density and keyboard productivity.
- Tablet should preserve the current view model with compact navigation and touch controls.
- Mobile should feel like a coherent app: bottom navigation or compact shell, task creation/update flows, stage switcher for Board, list row cards, calendar agenda and simplified timeline representation.
- Core flows required on mobile at launch: sign in, workspace switch, My Work, create task, status update, comment, mention, task inspection and notification handling.
- Touch targets should generally be at least 44×44 CSS px for primary mobile controls; no critical operation may require drag-and-drop.

## 7.4 Accessibility and interaction states

Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Provide semantic headings/landmarks, visible focus, accessible dialogs/menus/popovers, focus restoration after close, keyboard-only paths, status/priority text in addition to color, and no drag-only interactions. Complex grids use predictable roving focus. Shortcuts are suppressible and must not hijack typing in inputs. Every major view/component has loading, empty, error, populated, disabled/permission-limited and offline/stale states as applicable.

## 7.5 Safe interaction patterns

- Optimistic local rendering should be responsive but reconciled with server response.
- On conflict, preserve the user's local draft and show a clear conflict resolution path; never silently overwrite.
- Destructive changes need confirmation when impact is broad or irreversible; routine reversible actions can use an undo pattern if the backend supports it.
- Shared View modifications remain local until explicitly committed.
- Permission denials explain what role or setting controls the action without disclosing hidden data.

---

# 8. Task movement, transfer and key privacy

## 8.1 Same-Workspace movement

Reordering or changing a task's parent within the same Workspace preserves its UUID, lineage, current key and full content. If a parent is moved, all descendants move with it as one atomic tree operation. The target parent must be in the same Workspace, cannot be the task itself or a descendant, and the resulting tree must meet the Workspace depth limit. Workspace-level rank/order tokens must remain stable and deterministic.

## 8.2 Cross-Workspace transfer — OWNER CONFIRMED name-only rule

Cross-Workspace transfer is supported only within the same Community, subject to authorization in both source and destination. It is a privacy boundary crossing. Destination members must not inherit private execution state or commentary from the source.

**Carry only:** task/subtask names (titles) and the minimum parent-child structure/sibling ordering needed to recreate the same tree.  
**Do not carry:** `itemType`, descriptions (including subtask descriptions), assignees, assignment/creator identity, status/progress, dates, estimates, priority, labels, milestone relations, custom-field values, comments, mentions, watchers, dependencies/links, activity history, files (none exist), private metadata or source Workspace IDs.

New destination task rows receive fresh UUIDv7 IDs and fresh destination keys. The stable internal `taskLineageId` preserves alias resolution across repeated same-community transfers, but it does not reveal source content or bypass destination authorization. Old keys become immutable aliases to the lineage. The source rows become content-free tombstones and must not contain a destination pointer that can leak the target Workspace.

A preview is required before Personal → Shared transfer; the user explicitly confirms the audience/privacy change. Permission to move must be verified in source and permission to create in destination. The whole tree transfer, new IDs/keys, aliases, tombstones and outbox events commit atomically. If any condition fails, no partial transfer is allowed.

**OWNER CONFIRMED DEC-OPEN-10:** recreate the transferred root at the top level of the destination Workspace (`targetParentTaskId = null`). Descendants retain only the transferred tree's internal parent-child structure and sibling order. After transfer, authorized destination users may reorganize the tree normally. Selecting an existing destination parent is not supported for cross-Workspace transfer. Do not carry `itemType`.

## 8.3 Cross-community movement

Unsupported. Do not offer a direct transfer or use the same lineage/alias registry across community boundaries. If a future export/import or clone feature is requested, design it separately with explicit data minimization and a new lineage.
