~~~~markdown
# CR-06 — Workspace Roles, Capability Catalog and Delegation Policy

**Contract:** `0.3.7-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering policy specified; joint frontend/backend/security/product review and backend verification remain required before contract freeze.

## 1. Decision summary

CR-06 defines one canonical workspace-scoped capability vocabulary and a single, flat role model. A workspace membership has exactly one `roleId`; roles do not inherit from other roles and capabilities are not accumulated through role stacking. The backend evaluates the current membership, role capability set, workspace settings and CR-05 contextual task grants on every request.

The four immutable built-in role identities are `OWNER`, `COORDINATOR`, `MEMBER` and `VIEWER`. A role's stable `systemKey` is the policy identity; a display name is not. `WorkspaceMemberDto.roleSystemKey` exposes this identity (`null` for custom roles), while `effectiveCapabilities` on that DTO reports workspace-role grants only—not task relationship grants. Custom roles are workspace-local complete capability sets. Only active Workspace Owners can create, edit or delete custom role definitions. A custom role cannot contain reserved capabilities, even when the actor is an Owner.

The grant-ceiling invariant is:

`granted_caps ⊆ actor_workspace_role_caps ∩ delegable_capability_allowlist`

It is enforced on the server during custom-role creation/update and every member invitation/role assignment. Task Creator, active Task Assigner and active Task Assignee contextual grants, Community Admin authority, Platform Operator authority and break-glass access do not count toward the actor's workspace-role capability ceiling.

## 2. Role model and seeded roles

| Role | Default capability set and effect | Fixed restrictions |
|---|---|---|
| **Owner** | All `RoleCapability` values, including reserved Owner-only capabilities. Multiple active Owners are supported in a Shared Workspace. | Owner-only capabilities cannot be delegated. At least one active Owner must remain. |
| **Coordinator** | `workspace:read_metadata`, conditional `workspace:invite_members`, `task:read`, `task:create`, `task:edit_definition`, `task:update_status`, `task:assign`, `task:manage_subtasks`, `task:move`, `task:comment`, `task:watch`, `task:archive`, `task:restore`, `task:request_signoff`, `task:approve_signoff`, `project:create`, `project:configure_workflow`, `saved_view:manage_shared`. | No role administration, Owner-only setting changes, ownership transfer, audit access by default, or permanent purge. The invitation setting limits invitations to built-in Member or Viewer. Sign-off capabilities remain inert until the Phase 3 gate exists. |
| **Member** | `workspace:read_metadata`, `task:read`, `task:create`, `task:comment`, `task:watch`. | In `CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT`, ordinary Members do not receive task-definition, status, assignment or subtask-management permissions by default. CR-05 `COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER` mode is a separate Owner-controlled policy overlay. |
| **Viewer** | `workspace:read_metadata`, `task:read`, `task:watch`. | Read-only for all other actions. The collaborative policy does not elevate Viewer. |

A Shared Workspace is created with the four system roles available. Community Default Coordinators are preselected in the new workspace's member list as previously specified; the Owner can remove them during creation or later. `isDefaultCoordinator` is descriptive membership metadata, not a hidden grant. A user's effective role comes from their current workspace membership `roleId`; changing or removing that role removes Coordinator capabilities on the next request.

Personal Workspaces remain single-owner. They do not accept other members, Coordinators, custom roles or workspace ownership transfer. CR-01 break-glass remains separate: it is an audited, read-only access grant, not a role or membership assignment.

## 3. Capability catalog

`RoleCapability` is the typed union used by `WorkspaceRoleDto.capabilities`, `WorkspaceDto.effectiveCapabilities`, `WorkspaceMemberDto.effectiveCapabilities` and `RolePreviewDto.capabilities`.

| Bundle (role-builder card) | Capability codes |
|---|---|
| **Workspace Governance** | `workspace:read_metadata`, `workspace:update_settings`, `workspace:administer_roles`, `workspace:archive`, `workspace:restore`, `audit:read`, `audit:export` |
| **Member Management** | `workspace:invite_members`, `workspace:manage_members`, `workspace:transfer_ownership` |
| **Project & Workflow Structure** | `project:create`, `project:configure_workflow` |
| **Shared Views & Templates** | `saved_view:manage_shared` |
| **Custom Field Administration** | `workspace:manage_custom_fields` |
| **Task Execution & Collaboration** | `task:read`, `task:create`, `task:edit_definition`, `task:edit_title_description`, `task:edit_dates_priority`, `task:edit_custom_fields_links`, `task:edit_estimate`, `task:update_status`, `task:assign`, `task:manage_subtasks`, `task:move`, `task:comment`, `task:watch`, `task:request_signoff`, `task:approve_signoff` |
| **Task Destructive Actions** | `task:archive`, `task:restore`, `task:delete_permanent` |

The canonical task subset also includes `task:delete_permanent`. Capability codes are stable wire values; UI labels/bundles are presentation only. `task:edit_definition` remains the CR-05 aggregate compatibility capability and expands to the four granular definition capabilities. It never implies `task:assign`. A custom role may grant only granular task-definition capabilities, only the aggregate, or the allowed combination; the backend normalizes and evaluates the effective set consistently. `workspace:manage_custom_fields` is a separate delegable capability: it is not granted to default Coordinators/Members/Viewers, and custom roles receiving it must also include `workspace:read_metadata` and `task:read`.

`community:global_admin`, `community:create_shared_workspace` and `platform:operator` are intentionally outside `RoleCapability`. Community Admin is a CommunityMembership-scoped authority; Platform Operator is a separate operational-plane identity. Neither can be granted by a workspace role. File/attachment capabilities are absent because file uploads and attachments are out of current scope. Template CRUD remains Phase 2 and is not activated by `saved_view:manage_shared`.

## 4. Non-delegable and Owner-only capabilities

The following are reserved and cannot appear in a custom role capability set:

| Capability | Rule |
|---|---|
| `workspace:administer_roles` | Active Workspace Owner only; custom role definitions cannot delegate authority to create/update/delete roles. |
| `workspace:update_settings` | Active Workspace Owner only; includes `taskEditPolicy`, `assigneeEditableFieldGroupsAllowed`, `assigneeEditableFieldGroupsDefault` and `coordinatorCanInviteMembers`. |
| `workspace:transfer_ownership` | Active Workspace Owner only; ownership promotion uses the dedicated ownership-transfer operation. |
| `workspace:archive` / `workspace:restore` | Active Workspace Owner only. |
| `task:delete_permanent` | Active Workspace Owner only under CR-05. Never delegated, including to a custom role. |

A known reserved capability supplied in `CreateWorkspaceRoleRequest` or `UpdateWorkspaceRoleRequest` is rejected with `422 CAPABILITY_NOT_DELEGABLE`. Unknown capability strings are rejected with `422 CAPABILITY_CODE_INVALID`. Owner having the reserved capability does not make it delegable.

`workspace:invite_members` and `workspace:manage_members` are distinct. Invitation allows adding eligible users into a constrained role; management can change or remove existing member roles/states, subject to the grant ceiling and last-Owner invariant. `workspace:administer_roles` is separate from both.

## 5. Delegation and role assignment

### 5.1 Grant ceiling

The backend computes the actor's current workspace-role capabilities from the actor's active workspace membership. It checks the complete target role capability set, not just the changed fields. The same rule applies when the target role is a built-in role or custom role. A capability absent from the actor's current role set cannot be granted, assigned or invited.

A violation returns `403 CAPABILITY_GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR`. Record the denied attempt in the security/governance audit stream using actor, workspace, action, target role and capability codes; do not expose unrelated tenant data. Do not use task relationship permissions or the Preview-as-Role mask as inputs to delegation authority.

### 5.2 Coordinator invitation guard

`coordinatorCanInviteMembers` is an Owner-only workspace setting and defaults to `true`. When enabled, a built-in Coordinator with `workspace:invite_members` may invite/add only the built-in `MEMBER` or `VIEWER` role. It may not invite/assign `COORDINATOR`, `OWNER` or any custom role. This switch does not grant member removal, membership-state changes, arbitrary role assignment or custom-role management. When false, the Coordinator's invitation capability is suppressed. The frontend must show the reason for a disabled invitation affordance, but the server is authoritative.

Other custom roles with `workspace:invite_members` remain subject to the normal grant ceiling and target-role subset test. The Coordinator-specific restriction cannot be weakened by a custom role or request payload.

### 5.3 Owner promotion and membership lifecycle

There is one `roleId` per workspace membership. Generic add/update membership operations cannot assign built-in `OWNER`. Promoting a member to Owner is possible only through `POST .../owner-transfer`, performed by an active Owner. Multiple Owners are allowed; ownership transfer and caller demotion are atomic and the Shared Workspace must retain at least one ACTIVE Owner. The last Owner cannot leave, be demoted, suspended or removed (`409 LAST_OWNER_CANNOT_LEAVE`). Personal Workspaces remain single-owner.

Changing a member's role requires `workspace:manage_members` and a full target-role subset check. A user cannot use a membership-management capability to assign themselves or another user more authority than the actor currently holds. Removing or suspending a member, changing their role, or reducing the role's capability set takes effect on the next API request and invalidates affected realtime authorization/capability caches.

## 6. Custom role definition lifecycle

| Operation | Policy |
|---|---|
| List roles | Workspace read authorization; return built-in and custom roles with stable identity and typed capability codes. |
| Create | Active Workspace Owner in a Shared Workspace only. Name is trimmed, 1–80 characters, case-insensitively unique in that workspace and cannot equal a built-in role name. Optional description up to 500 characters. `capabilities` is a complete unique set (1–64 codes). |
| Update | Active Workspace Owner only; built-in roles immutable. Omitted PATCH fields remain unchanged. If `capabilities` is supplied, it replaces the full set; it never merges. Apply same reserved-capability, grant-ceiling, prerequisite and name-conflict checks as create. |
| Delete | Active Workspace Owner only; built-in roles immutable. A custom role referenced by any ACTIVE, INVITED or SUSPENDED membership returns `409 ROLE_IN_USE`. A pending workspace invitation creates an INVITED membership placeholder, so its role cannot be deleted until the invitation is accepted, expired or revoked. Reassign every membership explicitly first; no automatic fallback role. |

Each successful role-definition operation and role assignment creates an immutable audit event: `CUSTOM_ROLE_CREATED`, `CUSTOM_ROLE_UPDATED`, `CUSTOM_ROLE_DELETED` or `ROLE_ASSIGNED`. A denied capability-escalation attempt records `ROLE_CAPABILITY_ESCALATION_DENIED`. The role write and its audit/outbox record are atomic. Role IDs are never reused; historical audit references remain resolvable after deletion.

Errors:

| Status | Error code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `CAPABILITY_GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR` | Target set exceeds actor's current workspace-role capabilities. |
| 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_CAPABILITY` | Actor lacks the action capability. |
| 403 | `PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY` | A write was attempted while Preview-as-Role is active. |
| 409 | `ROLE_IN_USE` | Role still assigned to one or more memberships (including invited/suspended). |
| 409 | `ROLE_NAME_CONFLICT` | Name conflicts case-insensitively with another role or reserved system name. |
| 409 | `LAST_OWNER_CANNOT_LEAVE` | Operation would leave Shared Workspace without an active Owner. |
| 422 | `CAPABILITY_NOT_DELEGABLE` | Known but reserved capability included in custom role request. |
| 422 | `CAPABILITY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED` | Role capability set is missing a required prerequisite. |
| 422 | `CAPABILITY_CODE_INVALID` | Unknown capability code. |
| 422 | `ROLE_BUILT_IN_IMMUTABLE` | Attempt to rename, edit or delete a seeded role. |

## 7. Capability prerequisites and role-builder dependency locks

A role capability set is valid only if dependencies are satisfied. The UI should auto-enable and lock prerequisites where that is the established user experience; the API must independently validate and reject the whole role change with `422 CAPABILITY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED` and a safe list of missing codes.

| Selected capability | Required prerequisite |
|---|---|
| `task:create`, task edit/status/assign/subtask/move/comment/watch/archive/restore/sign-off capabilities | `task:read` |
| `task:edit_definition` | `task:read`; expands to the four definition capabilities; does not imply `task:assign` |
| `saved_view:manage_shared` | `task:read` |
| `workspace:manage_custom_fields` | `workspace:read_metadata`, `task:read` |
| `audit:export` | `audit:read` |

The role-builder shows a live blast-radius summary before saving (number of existing memberships affected and the capability changes). This is a confirmation aid, not a permission check. Backend authorization, validation and audit are mandatory even when the UI prevents a contradictory combination.

## 8. Preview-as-Role and effective authorization

Preview-as-Role is read-only. The final simulated workspace capability set is the intersection of the actor's current workspace-role capabilities, the selected preview role capability set and all security floors. It cannot add a capability to an Owner, Coordinator, Member, Viewer or custom role. All state-mutating API requests are rejected with `403 PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY`, including raw requests that bypass frontend locks. Preview does not change the membership's role, does not confer authority and is never a bearer token.

The backend continues to apply CR-05 task relationship grants and task policy only within its documented constraints. Preview never elevates the actor through a Creator/Assigner/Assignee relationship. Personal Workspace privacy, Community isolation, active membership, CR-01 break-glass read-only mode and Owner-only permanent purge remain non-overridable security floors. Actor-specific capability DTOs remain private/no-store.

## 9. Explicit dependencies and exclusions

- **CR-07:** `community-workspace-membership-policy.md` specifies invite lifecycle, recipient verification, workspace invite authority revalidation, membership suspension/restoration, Default Coordinator preselection and revocation. Provider selection and retry-worker implementation remain CR-13/CR-16; CR-10 defines provider-neutral retry policy.
- **CR-08:** `comment-and-mention-policy.md` specifies task comment parsing, mention recipient eligibility, edit/delete authorization and watcher behavior. CR-10 defines delivery preferences/retry policy; provider implementation remains CR-13/CR-16. CR-08 no longer blocks role-policy semantics.
- **CR-11:** `saved_view:manage_shared` is a capability code, but personal/shared saved-view scope, visibility, copy and delete ownership rules remain CR-11.
- **CR-12:** `workspace:manage_custom_fields` is a delegable capability for schema/option administration; task value updates continue to use CR-05 task permissions. The role-builder prerequisite set requires `workspace:read_metadata` and `task:read`.
- **Phase 2:** Custom template CRUD is deferred. The Shared Views & Templates card does not activate template CRUD.
- **Out of scope:** File upload/attachment capabilities are not present.

No backend authorization middleware, database migration, audit pipeline, role cache invalidation, frontend role-builder or runtime security tests are claimed by this policy. Joint review and execution evidence remain release gates.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# CR-07 — Community and Workspace Membership Policy

**Contract:** `0.3.8-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering policy specified; joint frontend/backend/security/product review and backend verification remain required before contract freeze.

## 1. Scope and governing model

The tenancy hierarchy remains `Community → Workspace → Project → Task`. A global User may belong to multiple independent Communities. A CommunityMembership is scoped to one Community. A WorkspaceMembership is scoped to one Workspace and references exactly one role as defined by CR-06.

Community membership and workspace membership are separate authorization boundaries:

- Community Admin authority is derived only from the active CommunityMembership's `isCommunityAdmin` flag. It is not a workspace role or a capability in `RoleCapability`.
- Workspace capabilities are derived only from an ACTIVE WorkspaceMembership and its current role. Community Admin status does not silently grant membership in, task access to, or role authority inside a Workspace.
- A user must have an ACTIVE CommunityMembership before receiving an invitation to a Shared Workspace.
- Personal Workspaces remain single-owner. They do not accept invitations, additional members, Coordinators, custom roles or ownership transfer.
- Platform Operator remains a separate operational-plane authority and is not a Community Admin or Workspace role.

## 2. Membership states

### CommunityMembership

| State | Meaning | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE` | The account has accepted the Community invitation or was validly restored by a Community Admin. | May enter this Community and can participate in eligible workspaces. |
| `SUSPENDED` | A Community Admin has suspended the membership. The membership record is retained. | No access to community-scoped services or Shared Workspaces in this Community. Other Communities and the global account session are unaffected. |

A pending Community invitation is an invitation record, not a CommunityMembership row. A new invitee receives a CommunityMembership only after acceptance.

### WorkspaceMembership

| State | Meaning | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `INVITED` | A pending invitation has reserved a target user and role. | No workspace read, task, search, export, realtime or mutation access. |
| `ACTIVE` | The invitation was accepted or an authorized restoration completed. | Workspace access is evaluated from the current CR-06 role and CR-05 task rules. |
| `SUSPENDED` | A Workspace Owner/member manager suspended the membership, the user left, or Community suspension cascaded. | No workspace access; role and historical identity remain stored. |

An invitation's own lifecycle is independent of membership state: `PENDING`, `ACCEPTED`, `EXPIRED` or `REVOKED`.

## 3. Community invitation lifecycle

### Create

`POST /communities/{communityId}/invitations` requires an ACTIVE Community Admin in the target community. The request contains a normalized email and optional `isDefaultCoordinator` (default `false`). It cannot grant Community Admin. A user must first accept the invite; only then may an existing Community Admin promote that active member through the existing community-member update operation.

Email is trimmed and case-folded for uniqueness and recipient matching. An ACTIVE or SUSPENDED CommunityMembership cannot be invited again; a suspended member must be restored through member management. At most one PENDING invitation exists for a `(communityId, normalizedEmail)` pair.

### Accept

`POST /invitations/accept` is authenticated and requires a verified primary email matching the invitation email after normalization. The token is single-use. Acceptance creates an ACTIVE CommunityMembership with `isCommunityAdmin=false`; the invitation's `isDefaultCoordinator` value sets the new member's community pool flag. Community acceptance does not automatically add the user to any existing Shared Workspace.

Unknown, mismatched, consumed and revoked tokens return the same generic 404. Do not disclose whether an email or account has an invitation. A valid recipient may receive a terminal-state response for an expired invitation.

### Resend and revoke

An ACTIVE Community Admin may resend or revoke a PENDING invitation in their community. Resend rotates the token, invalidates the old one immediately and resets the seven-day expiry. Revoke invalidates the token and leaves a terminal invitation record for audit. Terminal invitations cannot be reopened; create a new invitation instead.

## 4. Workspace invitation lifecycle

### Create

`POST /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations` requires an ACTIVE workspace member with `workspace:invite_members`. The target is specified by `userId`, and must already have an ACTIVE CommunityMembership in that same community. The invitation email is sent to the user's verified account email; this endpoint does not onboard a new Community member.

The chosen `roleId` is validated using the complete CR-06 target-role grant ceiling and assignment rules. Generic invite/assignment cannot grant built-in `OWNER`. The special built-in Coordinator exception remains constrained to built-in `MEMBER` or `VIEWER` while `coordinatorCanInviteMembers=true`; it never grants removal or role-administration rights.

Creation inserts an `INVITED` WorkspaceMembership with the requested `roleId` and a PENDING invitation in one transaction. The INVITED row exists for role-in-use protection and member-list visibility only. It grants no access until acceptance.

A target with any existing WorkspaceMembership (`ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED`) must be handled through workspace member management, not a second invitation. There can be at most one PENDING invitation per `(workspaceId, targetUserId)`.

### Accept

The target account accepts through the common `POST /invitations/accept` operation with the single-use token. Acceptance requires an ACTIVE CommunityMembership in the same community, an active Shared Workspace, an existing invited role, and no conflicting membership. The INVITED WorkspaceMembership becomes ACTIVE with the exact assigned `roleId`.

The server rechecks that the inviter is still ACTIVE and still authorized to invite that target role. It re-evaluates the full CR-06 role-capability grant ceiling, the Coordinator invitation restriction and workspace state. If the grant authority has been lost, mark the invitation REVOKED, remove the INVITED membership placeholder and return `INVITATION_AUTHORITY_REVOKED`. A custom role referenced by an INVITED membership remains protected by CR-06 `ROLE_IN_USE`.

### Resend and revoke

Resend requires the original inviter to retain current invite authority for the same target role, or an active Workspace Owner. All role/capability and Coordinator restrictions are rechecked. Resend rotates the token and resets expiry.

The original inviter may revoke their own invitation while still authorized to invite that target role. An active member with `workspace:manage_members` or a Workspace Owner may revoke any PENDING invitation. Revocation invalidates the token, deletes only the INVITED membership placeholder, retains the terminal invitation/audit record and emits the required scoped events.

## 5. Token, expiry and delivery controls

The engineering default is a seven-day invitation lifetime. This is a policy recommendation for stakeholder review, not an external standard or provider guarantee.

- Generate 32 cryptographically random bytes and encode them as base64url.
- Persist only `SHA-256(token)` with a unique constraint. Never persist or return the plaintext token.
- The email contains the token-bearing acceptance link. The frontend submits the token in the request body; never place it in API query strings, analytics, logs, audit data or referrer-bearing navigation.
- The token is single-use. A successful acceptance consumes it in the same transaction that activates membership.
- Resend rotates the token immediately; all prior links stop working.
- A PENDING invitation expires at `expiresAt`. A worker marks expired invitations at least every five minutes, but every read/resend/accept request also enforces expiry synchronously. Worker delay cannot extend the acceptance window.
- Invitation record, token hash, membership placeholder (workspace only), audit record and durable email-outbox event are committed atomically.
- The API reports `emailDeliveryStatus` as `QUEUED`, `SENT` or `FAILED`. `QUEUED` means durably enqueued, not delivered. The mail provider is deliberately abstract; CR-10 defines the shared provider-neutral retry/backoff and recipient preference policy, while provider selection belongs to CR-13.
- Failed delivery does not activate or revoke a membership. The invitation remains PENDING until expiry/revocation, and an authorized inviter may resend it.

## 6. Role defaults and Default Coordinator behavior

Community invitations never grant Community Admin. They may set `isDefaultCoordinator=true`, but only after acceptance. The Default Coordinator pool consists only of ACTIVE CommunityMembership rows with that flag set.

When a SHARED Workspace is created:

1. The creator becomes its initial OWNER.
2. If `CreateWorkspaceRequest.coordinatorUserIds` is omitted, every ACTIVE member of the current Default Coordinator pool is preselected.
3. The creating Owner may pass a subset, including an empty array, to remove preselected Coordinators before creation.
4. The selected IDs must still be ACTIVE members of the same community and remain in the Default Coordinator pool at transaction commit. The creator cannot be included because they are the initial OWNER.
5. Selected users are created as ACTIVE members with the built-in `COORDINATOR` role in the workspace-creation transaction.

A Default Coordinator is not automatically added to existing workspaces when the pool changes. Removing a person from the community Default Coordinator pool does not demote or remove them from existing workspaces; the Workspace Owner controls those current memberships. The workspace member's `isDefaultCoordinator` value is historical/pre-inclusion metadata only and grants no capability. `roleId`/`systemKey` remains the authorization source.

Personal Workspace creation rejects a non-empty `coordinatorUserIds` list.

## 7. Suspension, removal and restoration

### Community suspension/removal

`DELETE /communities/{communityId}/members/{userId}` is a soft suspension, not a destructive delete. It retains the CommunityMembership and history, sets `membershipStatus=SUSPENDED`, clears `isCommunityAdmin` and `isDefaultCoordinator`, suspends the user's Shared Workspace memberships in that community, and revokes pending workspace invitations addressed to the user.

If the user is the only ACTIVE Owner of any Shared Workspace, suspension is rejected with `409 COMMUNITY_MEMBER_IS_LAST_WORKSPACE_OWNER`. Ownership must be transferred or recovered first. This preserves CR-06's at-least-one-active-Owner invariant.

Community suspension is scoped. It invalidates only the affected community/workspace access context, authorization caches and realtime subscriptions. It must not globally log out the account or remove access to other Communities. Personal Workspace data is not deleted, transferred or exposed by the suspension operation; owner-only privacy rules remain in force.

`PATCH /communities/{communityId}/members/{userId}` may restore a suspended membership to ACTIVE or change Community Admin/Default Coordinator flags. Restoring the CommunityMembership does not restore any WorkspaceMembership automatically; each Shared Workspace requires an explicit authorized restoration. The community settings bulk `defaultCoordinatorUserIds` update replaces the same `isDefaultCoordinator` pool and accepts only ACTIVE CommunityMembership IDs; it affects future workspace preselection only.

### Workspace suspension/removal

`DELETE /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{userId}` soft-suspends a member. It preserves role and history but revokes all workspace access. Self-removal is permitted for non-Owners. A SUSPENDED member can be restored only when their CommunityMembership is ACTIVE and the acting manager passes the full CR-06 target-role capability grant ceiling.

Generic member PATCH/DELETE cannot demote, suspend or remove an OWNER. Owner departure/demotion uses the dedicated owner-transfer operation. That operation may promote an ACTIVE or SUSPENDED existing workspace member who has ACTIVE CommunityMembership (a SUSPENDED target is reactivated atomically), then can atomically `KEEP_OWNER`, `DEMOTE` the caller to a non-Owner role, or `LEAVE` (suspend the caller). INVITED workspace memberships cannot be promoted. The transaction must preserve at least one ACTIVE Owner. Personal Workspaces cannot use owner transfer.

### Immediate revocation

Every API request re-evaluates current community and workspace membership. Suspension, role change and invite acceptance/revocation are written with their audit/outbox records in one transaction. Affected workspace subscriptions and authorization caches are invalidated across all realtime instances before access can continue; the next API request observes the new state. The account session remains valid for unrelated communities.

## 8. Events, audit and privacy

Membership/invitation transitions produce immutable audit records and domain outbox events in the same transaction. The action taxonomy includes community/workspace invitation created, resent, accepted, revoked and expired; community member suspended/restored/flags changed; workspace member suspended/restored/role changed; and workspace ownership transferred.

Audit metadata contains scoped actor/target IDs and invitation ID where available. Email addresses are not copied into audit metadata; use a salted email hash for correlation where needed. Plaintext token and token hash are never logged or exported as ordinary audit metadata.

Workspace stream payloads contain invitation ID/status only and never recipient email or token. User-community invitation events are delivered only to the target user. `Cache-Control: private, no-store` is required for member, invitation and actor-sensitive membership responses. Do not use a shared cache or cross-community client cache key.

## 9. Error model

| Status | Error code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_COMMUNITY_ADMIN` | Actor is not an ACTIVE Community Admin in this community. |
| 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_CAPABILITY` | Actor lacks the relevant workspace capability. |
| 403 | `CAPABILITY_GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR` | Target role exceeds the actor's CR-06 delegation ceiling. |
| 403 | `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` | Authenticated account has no verified primary email. |
| 404 | `INVITATION_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown, mismatched, consumed or non-disclosable invitation token. |
| 409 | `INVITATION_ALREADY_PENDING` | A PENDING invitation already exists for the target/scope. |
| 409 | `INVITATION_NOT_PENDING` | Resend/revoke targets a terminal invitation. |
| 409 | `INVITATION_EXPIRED` / `INVITATION_REVOKED` | A valid recipient is attempting to accept a known terminal invitation. |
| 409 | `INVITATION_AUTHORITY_REVOKED` | Workspace inviter no longer has authority for the invited role. |
| 409 | `COMMUNITY_MEMBER_IS_LAST_WORKSPACE_OWNER` | Suspending a Community member would leave a Shared Workspace without an active Owner. |
| 409 | `LAST_OWNER_CANNOT_LEAVE` | Workspace operation would leave no active Owner. |
| 409 | `WORKSPACE_MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` / `COMMUNITY_MEMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS` | Existing membership must be managed/restored instead of re-invited. |
| 422 | `OWNER_PROMOTION_REQUIRES_TRANSFER` | Generic role assignment tried to grant OWNER. |
| 422 | `PERSONAL_WORKSPACE_MEMBERS_NOT_ALLOWED` | An invitation/member operation targets a Personal Workspace. |
| 422 | `COMMUNITY_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED` | Workspace target lacks ACTIVE CommunityMembership. |
| 422 | `COORDINATOR_NOT_IN_DEFAULT_POOL` | Workspace creation selected an ineligible Default Coordinator. |

## 10. Dependencies and implementation gates

- **CR-06:** Workspace role/capability model, reserved capabilities, invitation role-grant ceiling, Coordinator restriction, Owner protection and `ROLE_IN_USE` are defined there and remain binding.
- **CR-09:** The API requires immediate cross-instance realtime subscription revocation, but transport ticketing/heartbeat/reconnect protocol remains CR-09.
- **CR-10:** Notification fan-out, email retries/backoff, preferences, quiet hours and digest behavior are specified in `notification-delivery-policy.md`. CR-07 still governs invitation-specific state, token, resend/revoke and delivery-status semantics; CR-13 specifies the identity/email contract; actual sender-provider provisioning remains a CR-16 deployment gate.
- **CR-13:** Account-level identity verification, browser session and authentication policy are specified by CR-13; concrete trusted-origin values, sender-provider provisioning and production identity configuration remain CR-16 deployment inputs.
- **Backend/security:** Prove atomic token consumption, invitation race handling, current inviter-authority revalidation, community/workspace cascade suspension, Owner invariant locking, cross-instance cache/socket invalidation and generic anti-enumeration responses.
- **Frontend:** Build distinct Community Invite and Workspace Invite flows, verified-email acceptance, expiry/resend/revoke states, Coordinator preselection editing and disabled-action explanations. Never infer access from UI state.

No backend implementation, database migration, email provider, frontend flow, realtime runtime test or production delivery evidence is claimed by this policy.


## CR-13 account-authentication integration

Email verification is an account-level identity state owned by CR-13 (`authentication-deployment-policy.md` and `openapi.yaml` `x-authentication-policy`). Community and workspace invitation acceptance continue to check the account's verified primary email and invitation-specific recipient/subject matching as specified above. CR-07 does not implement its own password, OAuth, email-verification-token or browser-session mechanism. Sender-provider provisioning, DNS alignment and delivery-worker runtime remain deployment/operations acceptance gates; a verified email flag in an account DTO is not a substitute for the invitation token or live membership reauthorization.
~~~~

# CR-08 — Comments, Mentions and Watchers Policy

**Contract:** `0.3.9-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering policy specified; joint frontend/backend/security/product review and backend verification remain required before contract freeze.

## 1. Scope

Comments are task-scoped collaboration records. They obey the same current workspace membership, task-read authorization, tenant isolation and Personal Workspace privacy floors as the task itself. This policy retains the existing `task:comment` and `task:watch` capability primitives; it does not introduce a new role capability. File attachments are not supported and comment DTOs/requests cannot carry file IDs.

## 2. Markdown input, sanitization and rendering

`CreateCommentRequest.body` and `UpdateCommentRequest.body` carry raw Markdown source, limited to 20,000 characters. The server parses this source into a closed, versioned `CommentMarkdownAst`; clients do not submit HTML or an AST. The supported subset is paragraphs, headings levels 1–3, blockquotes, ordered/unordered lists, list items, emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code, fenced code blocks, safe links, mention tokens and resolved task-key tokens.

Raw HTML, styles, classes, arbitrary attributes, scripts, SVG, iframes, images, embeds and remote media are forbidden. The parser escapes or discards raw HTML; it never executes it. Only `http`, `https` and `mailto` links become link nodes. `javascript`, `data`, `vbscript`, `file`, protocol-relative and unknown schemes are rejected. External links render with `noopener` and `noreferrer`. Source and sanitized AST are stored; clients render typed AST nodes using ordinary React elements and never inject raw HTML.

The body is bounded to 20,000 characters and the AST to 2,000 nodes. Markdown nesting is bounded; unsupported constructs degrade to literal text. `#KEY` tokens are linked only after CR-03 resolves the alias/current lineage and proves the target is readable in the same workspace. Unknown or inaccessible keys remain plain text.

## 3. Mention syntax, candidate search and identity resolution

The editor serializes a selected mention as `@[label](user:<uuid>)`. The label and ID supplied by the client are untrusted. The server ignores the submitted label and resolves the canonical display name from the current account record.

`GET .../tasks/{taskId}/mention-candidates?q=...` requires `task:read`, searches only ACTIVE members of the current workspace who have task-read access to the task, returns at most 20 `userId`/display-name/avatar results, and never returns email or other membership metadata. Suspended/removed users and the actor are excluded. Candidate results are hints only; writes revalidate every mention at commit time.

On create and edit, each token must resolve to an ACTIVE CommunityMembership and ACTIVE WorkspaceMembership with `task:read` on the current task. Duplicate recipients are deduplicated. A malformed, stale, inaccessible, suspended, removed, cross-community or cross-workspace target rejects the complete write with generic `422 MENTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; no account-existence details are disclosed and no partial comment/watcher/notification writes occur.

When the author or mentioned member later leaves, is suspended or is erased, preserve stable historical references but show the generic **Former member** label and no email/avatar. The stored task content must not reveal that person's membership in another community.

## 4. Threading

`parentCommentId` must reference a non-deleted comment on the same task and workspace. Maximum nesting depth is five. Unknown, deleted, inaccessible, cross-task or cross-workspace parents fail without disclosing existence. Replies remain part of the same task activity stream.

## 5. Comment permissions and lifecycle

- List comments/activity: `task:read` and current workspace membership; private/no-store.
- Create: `task:comment`, `task:read` and ACTIVE workspace membership.
- Edit: only the author, while active in the workspace and holding `task:comment` and `task:read`. The complete Markdown/AST/mention set is replaced atomically. `version` is required; stale versions return `409 COMMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`.
- Delete: author may soft-delete their own comment. Any caller with `task:archive` may soft-delete any comment on a readable task.
- No hard-delete endpoint is exposed. A deleted comment returns `isDeleted=true`, `body=null`, `bodyAst=null`, `mentions=[]` and `deletedAt`; a minimal deletion activity entry remains. No deleted body or mention list is exposed through normal comment APIs.

Unknown/unreadable task, comment or parent returns generic 404. A readable task with insufficient capability returns 403. Every mutation rechecks current authorization.

## 6. Watcher semantics

Task Creator and each active Assignee are automatically followed. A user directly mentioned in an active comment is also auto-followed. Maintain independent follow reasons `CREATOR`, `ASSIGNEE`, `MENTION` and `EXPLICIT`, so removing one reason never removes another. Assignment or mention changes update only the corresponding reason.

`task:watch` changes only the authenticated user's explicit follow preference; callers cannot subscribe or unsubscribe another user. `watching=false` suppresses ordinary/non-mention update alerts even if an implicit follow reason remains. Direct mention notifications continue. `watching=true` explicitly resumes ordinary updates. Mentioning a user does not silently clear an existing mute.

When a comment is edited or deleted, remove its `MENTION` follow reason only if no other active comment still mentions that user; explicit, creator and assignee reasons remain. Do not clear an explicit mute.

## 7. Logical notification fan-out (CR-10 boundary)

On comment creation, each distinct eligible mention target other than the author receives one logical `MENTION` / Action Required notification intent. On edit, only newly added eligible mention targets receive a new mention intent; recipients retained in the edited body are not pinged again. Other followers who have not muted ordinary updates receive one logical `COMMENT_UPDATE` / Updates intent for a comment create or edit. The author is excluded. A recipient receiving a direct new-mention intent does not also receive a duplicate update intent for the same comment revision.

Comment writes, watcher-reason changes and durable notification intents are atomic through the outbox; delivery is asynchronous. This policy settles logical event classes and recipient selection only. CR-10 defines channel preferences, quiet hours, digest behavior, retry/backoff and duplicate suppression; CR-13 selects the deployed email provider/sender.

## 8. Realtime and privacy

Workspace events are `comment.created`, `comment.updated`, `comment.deleted` and `watcher.changed`. Payloads contain only taskId, commentId, version and event metadata; never Markdown, AST, mention recipient IDs, email or hidden task identifiers. Recipient-specific notification deltas use the user-community stream. Comment and candidate responses are `private, no-store`; current membership is rechecked for every read and mutation. CR-09 retains ownership of transport, tickets, reconnection and revocation propagation.

## 9. Validation and implementation gates

CR-08 is a contract/policy decision only. Backend tests must cover XSS/script payloads, unsafe URI schemes, malformed/stale mention tokens, task-key alias access, inaccessible mention candidates, deleted-member labels, max thread depth, version conflicts, atomic mention/watcher/outbox writes, moderator deletion, unwatch-vs-mention behavior and cache isolation. Frontend tests must prove AST-only rendering, keyboard mention selection, safe external links and correct deleted/Former member presentation. CR-10 now specifies notification delivery policy; provider deployment remains CR-13.
~~~~

# CR-09 — Realtime transport policy

**Contract:** `0.3.10-draft` · **Status:** engineering contract specified; joint FE/BE/security sign-off and runtime acceptance remain open.

## 1. Purpose and authority

Realtime is a low-latency **delta transport**, not a source of truth. Canonical state remains in the authorized HTTP APIs. The protocol uses WebSocket over TLS in production, subprotocol `work-platform.v1`, event schema version `1`, and the strict control frames in `ws-protocol.schema.json`. Server-to-client domain deltas are the raw envelopes in `ws-events.schema.json`; a second wrapper around those event envelopes is prohibited.

The contract has two independent streams:

- **Workspace stream:** scope `(communityId, workspaceId)`, sequence `workspaceSeq`.
- **User-community stream:** scope `(authenticatedUserId, communityId)`, sequence `userNotificationSeq`. The user ID is derived from the authenticated session and is never accepted from the client.

The streams have separate sequence spaces. A cursor from one stream must never be used for the other.

## 2. Endpoint, authentication and origin validation

The WebSocket endpoint is `wss://{configured-host}/api/v1/ws`, negotiated with `work-platform.v1`. Production requires TLS. The server rejects a browser `Origin` unless it exactly matches the environment-specific `TRUSTED_BROWSER_ORIGINS` allowlist. Wildcards, suffix matches, substring matches and implicit trust of an absent browser Origin are forbidden. CR-13 fixes the browser cookie to `__Host-session` (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`), with a 14-day sliding idle window, 30-day absolute expiry and 24-hour rotation. The concrete origin strings and TLS endpoint remain deployment inputs under CR-16.

Two authentication modes are supported:

1. **Existing session cookie.** The server validates the existing session during the Upgrade handshake. The cookie remains HTTP-only and is not copied into JavaScript, frames or URLs. Its exact `__Host-` attributes and lifetime are defined by CR-13; host-only cookie scope means the browser app and API must be same-site.
2. **Short-lived ticket.** The authenticated client calls `POST /communities/{communityId}/realtime-ticket` with the normal CSRF protection. The ticket is generated with at least 256 bits of entropy, expires 60 seconds after issuance, is single-use, is bound to the authenticated user and path community, and is stored only as a one-way hash. Redemption is atomic. The raw credential is returned once, is not logged, and is never placed in a query string, URL, subprotocol or telemetry. The first application frame must be `AUTHENTICATE` within five seconds of Upgrade. A ticket is not reusable after a failed/reconnected socket; obtain a new ticket for every new ticket-authenticated connection.

The ticket request may optionally include `workspaceIds`. This is a narrowing restriction only; it never grants access. The server still authorizes each subscription and every replay/event against current CommunityMembership, WorkspaceMembership and resource visibility. Ticket issuance deliberately does not use `X-Mutation-Id` replay because a retry must not return a previously issued raw credential.

Session-cookie-authenticated connections do not send `AUTHENTICATE`; the server authenticates during Upgrade. Successful setup returns `CONNECTION_ACK` with the authentication mode. Ticket mode additionally returns the ticket-bound `communityId`; neither mode exposes the authenticated user ID.

## 3. Control-frame protocol

Client controls are `AUTHENTICATE`, `SUBSCRIBE_WORKSPACE`, `SUBSCRIBE_USER_COMMUNITY`, `UNSUBSCRIBE_WORKSPACE`, `UNSUBSCRIBE_USER_COMMUNITY` and `PONG`. Server controls are `CONNECTION_ACK`, `SUBSCRIPTION_ACK`, `UNSUBSCRIPTION_ACK`, `PING`, `ERROR`, `WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED`, `WORKSPACE_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` and `COMMUNITY_ACCESS_REVOKED`.

Every request/response control operation uses a client-generated `requestId` for correlation. A workspace subscription includes `communityId`, `workspaceId` and `sinceSeq`; a user-community subscription includes `communityId` and `sinceSeq` only. No subscription frame may include `userId`, role, capability or claimed membership state. A ticket-bound connection cannot subscribe outside its ticket community or its optional workspace allowlist.

`SUBSCRIPTION_ACK` echoes `requestId`, identifies the stream scope and returns `currentSeq`, the authoritative sequence high-water mark captured when the subscription is established. The server must register the subscription and begin buffering before capturing that high-water mark, so events committed during setup are not lost. `UNSUBSCRIPTION_ACK` confirms removal of the caller's exact subscription. `ERROR` uses generic codes and must not reveal whether an inaccessible user, workspace or community exists.

Control frames are closed objects. Unknown fields and unknown frame types are rejected; the JSON Schemas are normative. Domain event envelopes are not wrapped in a control frame.

## 4. Event envelope, sequencing and delivery

Every workspace event carries `schemaVersion: 1`, its `communityId`, `workspaceId`, `workspaceSeq`, `eventId`, `eventType`, `occurredAt`, `actorId`, `entityId`, nullable `mutationId`, and a permission-filtered `payload`. User-community events carry `schemaVersion: 1`, `communityId`, `userNotificationSeq`, `eventId`, `eventType`, `occurredAt` and a recipient-scoped `payload`.

`workspaceSeq` is a strictly increasing, contiguous sequence per workspace. `userNotificationSeq` is a separate strictly increasing, contiguous sequence per authenticated user and community. Ordering is guaranteed only within each stream; there is no global order across workspaces or between the two stream types.

Delivery is **at least once**, not exactly once. Clients deduplicate by `eventId` and apply only contiguous sequence numbers. `mutationId` is only an optimistic-echo correlation value: when a mutation already changed the local UI, the client may suppress reapplying that optimistic echo while still advancing the stream sequence. It is not a replacement for `eventId` or sequence deduplication.

The domain write, each affected stream sequence allocation and its durable outbox event must commit atomically in the same database transaction. Outbox publishing is retryable and idempotent by `eventId`. A committed business mutation must not be lost merely because a process or broker fails after database commit. Broker/provider selection is an implementation/deployment decision; the delivery and ordering contract is not optional.

## 5. Subscription, catch-up and race-free recovery

The HTTP catch-up operations are:

- `GET /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/events?sinceSeq={n}`
- `GET /communities/{communityId}/user-events?sinceSeq={n}`

`sinceSeq` is **exclusive**. A successful response returns the complete ordered events after that cursor, no more than 500, and `latestSeq` observed for that stream. Both success and error responses are `private, no-store`. The server reauthorizes the current actor before returning replay data; a cursor never grants access.

The server retains at least the latest 500 committed events independently for each workspace and each user-community stream. If the cursor is ahead of the stream high-water mark, return `409 EVENT_CURSOR_AHEAD` with `latestSeq`. If the cursor predates retained history, return `410 EVENT_SEQ_OUT_OF_RETENTION` with `latestSeq`. Never return a partial replay with HTTP 200 when the requested complete interval is unavailable.

The client algorithm is:

1. Subscribe using the last **contiguous** cursor it has applied. The server establishes the subscription, buffers subsequent events and returns `SUBSCRIPTION_ACK.currentSeq`.
2. Call the matching HTTP catch-up endpoint from the saved cursor. Apply the complete ordered response through its `latestSeq`; deduplicate any live frames also received during this operation.
3. Release buffered/live frames only when they are contiguous with the applied cursor. If a gap appears, pause application for that stream and catch up again from the last contiguous cursor.
4. On `410`, refetch the canonical authorized projections. Then call catch-up from the `latestSeq` included in the 410 Problem Details response and reconcile any events committed during the refetch before releasing buffered live frames. If another 410 occurs, repeat; never jump to a client-invented cursor.
5. On `409`, use the returned authoritative `latestSeq` for correction and reconcile from canonical projections/catch-up before applying later frames.

Workspace and user-community cursors are persisted independently. A successful HTTP catch-up response is complete; the client must not infer completeness from receiving a WebSocket frame.

## 6. Heartbeat, disconnect and backpressure

The server sends application-level `PING` every 25 seconds. The client must answer `PONG` within 10 seconds. A connection is stale after 35 seconds without a valid heartbeat response and is closed. The client shows a non-blocking reconnect indicator after five seconds disconnected.

Reconnect uses exponential backoff with jitter, with nominal delays of 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s and 4 s and a 15-second maximum. Reconnection always reauthenticates; ticket mode obtains a fresh ticket. The client resumes each stream from its last contiguous cursor, never the last frame merely received.

The server uses a bounded per-connection send buffer. It must not silently drop events while pretending the subscription is healthy. If a client cannot keep up and the buffer is exhausted, close the connection; the client reconnects and uses HTTP catch-up. Exact buffer byte/event thresholds, connection limits and load targets are deployment/load-test decisions under CR-16.

## 7. Permission changes and immediate revocation

Authorization is checked at connection authentication, on every subscription, before every replay and before event delivery. The WebSocket connection itself is not proof of continuing access.

- Workspace member removal/suspension or loss of visibility sends `WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED`, detaches that workspace stream on every realtime instance and stops all further delivery for that workspace.
- A workspace role/capability change sends `WORKSPACE_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED`; clients invalidate permission-sensitive caches and reauthorize. If the actor no longer has the required access, the server also revokes and detaches the stream before any further event delivery.
- Community suspension sends `COMMUNITY_ACCESS_REVOKED`, detaches that community's user-community stream and all affected shared-workspace streams, but does not globally log out the user or affect other communities.

Membership/role/visibility changes create durable revocation intents and fan out to every realtime server instance. A cross-instance invalidation barrier is required before the change is treated as safely propagated. If current authorization or the barrier cannot be established, the server fails closed for the affected subscription. This contract does not mandate a specific broker/cache vendor.

## 8. Tenant privacy and payload limits

Workspace events never contain comment Markdown, rendered AST, mention recipient lists, email addresses, invitation tokens, session cookies, CSRF tokens, ticket values, or hidden/counterpart task or workspace identifiers. Comment/watcher workspace deltas contain only permitted task/comment identifiers, comment version and event metadata. Recipient-specific notification details travel only on the authenticated user's user-community stream.

Cross-workspace `task.moved` produces independently scoped SOURCE and TARGET events with a shared `transferId`, side and moved count/root identifier only; neither event exposes the counterpart workspace/task ID or transferred task content. Each audience is authorized within its own workspace. User-community invitation/notification events are delivered only to the authenticated recipient and never include the raw invitation token or another recipient's personal data.

All HTTP ticket and catch-up responses are non-cacheable. Credentials are excluded from logs, traces, analytics and event payloads. All subscription errors use privacy-preserving generic codes.

## 9. Explicitly deferred deployment and verification decisions

The following remain open and must not be guessed in application code:

- The session cookie attributes and lifecycle are fixed by CR-13; concrete browser-origin entries, TLS endpoint and trusted proxy addresses remain CR-16 deployment inputs.
- Realtime broker/provider, hosting topology, connection limits, buffer thresholds and production alerting: CR-13/CR-16.
- Provider-specific cross-instance delivery guarantees must be demonstrated against the required durable outbox and revocation barrier.
- Runtime tests for ticket entropy/expiry/replay races, Origin rejection, unauthorized subscription/replay/event delivery, sequence gaps, duplicate/out-of-order frames, 410/409 recovery, slow-client backpressure, multi-instance revocation, tenant isolation, load and failure injection are mandatory before release.

**Evidence boundary:** this document and its schemas define a contract. They do not prove a socket server, publisher, broker, revocation system or frontend reconnect client has been implemented. CR-09 is specified, not signed off or runtime-verified.


## CR-13 authentication integration note

CR-13 completes the HTTP session contract used by this protocol. A session revoke, logout-all, password reset/change, or identity unlink invalidates its realtime tickets and closes every associated socket across instances. Browser socket handshakes apply the same exact `Origin` allowlist and current server-side session validation; the raw session cookie is never copied into frames or tickets. Authentication audit entries and session lifecycle details are private records and do not become workspace or user-community events. Concrete WSS host, TLS termination, trusted proxy addresses and browser-origin entries remain CR-16 deployment/runtime inputs.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# CR-10 — Notification and reminder delivery policy

**Contract:** `0.3.11-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering policy specified; joint frontend/backend/product/security sign-off and runtime delivery acceptance remain open.

## 1. Purpose and governing boundaries

CR-10 defines the durable in-app inbox, notification categories, recipient selection, per-user preferences, workspace deadline-reminder schedules, email quiet hours/digests, retries and deduplication.

Notifications are recipient-scoped communication records, not an authorization grant. Every task/workspace-linked notification must obey the current community membership, workspace membership, task visibility, Personal Workspace privacy and CR-01 break-glass rules. The server derives the recipient from the authenticated session or from a validated domain event; clients never choose another `userId` as the inbox recipient.

The channels specified here are durable in-app inbox/realtime updates and optional email. Browser/mobile push notifications are outside this contract and must not be treated as a promised or implemented delivery channel.

There are three separate concerns:

1. **Domain intent:** a task/comment/governance event determines whether a recipient should receive a logical notification.
2. **Inbox record:** the app persists the notification for that one recipient in that one community.
3. **Channel delivery:** email and any interruptive UI presentation follow the recipient's preferences. Email failure never removes the in-app record.

CR-08 remains authoritative for comment/mention recipient selection and watcher semantics. CR-01 remains authoritative for break-glass security alerts. CR-07 remains authoritative for invitation state, tokens, accept/resend/revoke behavior and `QUEUED`/`SENT`/`FAILED` invitation delivery status. CR-09 remains authoritative for user-community realtime transport.

## 2. Notification taxonomy and recipient rules

The inbox has two stable categories, matching the product's two-tab notification model:

| Category | Reason | Recipient rule |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `MENTION` | Each distinct newly mentioned eligible user other than the author, after CR-08 server-side validation. |
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `TASK_ASSIGNED` | Each newly added active assignee. Assignment removal does not create an assignment notification. |
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `TASK_DUE_REMINDER` | Active task assignees; if there is no active assignee, the active task creator. Never every workspace member. |
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `TASK_OVERDUE` | Same recipient rule as a due reminder; one overdue notification per task/due date/recipient. |
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `GOVERNANCE_ALERT` | Only the actor/subject/authorized administrators specified by the originating governance policy. |
| `ACTION_REQUIRED` | `BREAK_GLASS_ALERT` | The Personal Workspace owner and same-community Community Admin audience required by CR-01. Mandatory security path. |
| `UPDATES` | `COMMENT_UPDATE` | Eligible active task followers who have not muted ordinary updates; author excluded. CR-08 direct-mention suppression takes precedence. |

No generic notification is emitted for every task edit or status change by default. This avoids alert fatigue. Further event classes require a later explicit contract change rather than frontend/backend assumptions.

`ACTION_REQUIRED` and `UPDATES` are inbox categories, not role/capability values. An inbox item contains a stable `reason` and source `eventType`, title, optional safe body summary and optional resource pointer. It never becomes proof that a resource is readable: the resource is reauthorized when the inbox response is generated and again before an email/digest includes a deep link or resource summary.

## 3. Inbox API and data behavior

The canonical inbox is `GET /communities/{communityId}/notifications`; it is scoped to the authenticated user and active CommunityMembership. Optional `category` filters to `ACTION_REQUIRED` or `UPDATES`; `unreadOnly=true` filters unread items. Results are newest first. Cursor format/expiry/consistency is deliberately left to CR-15.

`unreadCount` is the total unread count for the authenticated user in the community, independent of the active category or unread-only filters. This supports a stable application badge and category tabs without the client summing only the current page.

`POST /communities/{communityId}/notifications/{notificationId}/read` marks one of the caller's notification records read. `POST /communities/{communityId}/notifications/read-all` marks all of the caller's notification records in that community read. Unknown, foreign-recipient or cross-community notification IDs must not reveal existence; return the API's generic not-found response.

Every inbox response is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Notification list, mark-read and read-all operate only on the caller; no `userId` request parameter or administrative read-all path is added here.

## 4. Per-user, per-community notification preferences

Preferences are stored per `(authenticatedUserId, communityId)`. This is intentional: a user can participate in multiple independent communities and choose a different email, digest and quiet-hour policy in each. Read/write endpoints are:

- `GET /communities/{communityId}/me/notification-preferences`
- `PUT /communities/{communityId}/me/notification-preferences`

The update is self-service only, requires normal CSRF protection and mutation idempotency, and accepts no `userId`.

The preferences DTO contains:

- `timeZone`: a validated IANA time-zone identifier (for example, `Asia/Kolkata`). If no valid value has been supplied yet, the deterministic server default is `UTC`; the client should submit the browser-detected zone or the user's explicit selection.
- `actionRequiredEmailMode`: `IMMEDIATE` or `OFF`. Action Required email must never be placed in a digest.
- `updatesEmailMode`: `IMMEDIATE`, `DAILY_DIGEST`, `WEEKLY_DIGEST` or `OFF`.
- `quietHours`: `enabled`, `startTimeLocal`, `endTimeLocal` and `daysOfWeek`.
- `dailyDigestTimeLocal`: local wall-clock time, default `09:00`.
- `weeklyDigestDayOfWeek`: local weekday, default `MONDAY`.

In-app inbox persistence is always enabled and is not a preference toggle. Defaults for a new user/community preference record are `actionRequiredEmailMode=IMMEDIATE`, `updatesEmailMode=OFF`, quiet hours disabled, daily digest time `09:00`, weekly day Monday and time zone UTC until the client sends a valid local zone. Email requires a current verified primary email; otherwise only the in-app notification is created and email remains ineligible.

`ACTION_REQUIRED` only supports email `IMMEDIATE` or `OFF`. Attempting to set it to a digest mode returns `422 ACTION_REQUIRED_DIGEST_NOT_ALLOWED`. `UPDATES` email may be immediate, daily digest, weekly digest or off. A digest setting does not alter the in-app inbox record or CR-08 watch/mute relationships.

## 5. Quiet hours and digest schedule

Quiet hours are interpreted in the preference record's IANA `timeZone`. `startTimeLocal` and `endTimeLocal` are local wall-clock times. The interval may cross midnight; `daysOfWeek` identifies the local start day. An empty `daysOfWeek` means every day. Equal start and end times are invalid. Unknown IANA time-zone identifiers and invalid wall-clock values return `422`. Resolve local times using the IANA time-zone database: when a DST transition makes a configured wall time nonexistent, move it to the first valid instant after the gap; when a wall time occurs twice, execute once at its first occurrence. Keep the logical occurrence/digest key stable so a repeated hour cannot cause duplicate delivery.

Quiet hours defer ordinary email delivery until the first time at or after the end of the quiet interval. They do not delete, hide or delay the durable in-app inbox record or its unread count. The user-community realtime event still updates the inbox/badge; the frontend should suppress interruptive toast presentation while the user's local quiet interval is active. Mandatory CR-01 break-glass alerts bypass quiet hours.

Only `UPDATES` email items may be batched into daily or weekly digests. `ACTION_REQUIRED` is never digested. Daily digests run at `dailyDigestTimeLocal`; weekly digests run on `weeklyDigestDayOfWeek` at that local time. Digest construction uses the configured `timeZone`. Each digest includes only eligible notifications not already successfully accepted in a prior digest, and it rechecks that every referenced task/workspace is currently readable by that recipient. Comment Markdown/AST, mention-recipient lists, email addresses and hidden task/workspace identifiers are never placed in a digest.

## 6. Workspace deadline reminder schedule

The existing `GET/PUT /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/reminder-settings` endpoints remain. They configure **workspace-wide reminder generation only**. They do not choose recipient delivery channels; recipient email mode, time zone and quiet hours are read from each recipient's own notification preferences.

Updating reminder settings requires `workspace:update_settings` (Workspace Owner by default; delegation follows CR-06/CR-07 capability rules). Reading requires an active workspace member with `workspace:read_metadata`. The response is private/no-store.

New workspaces default to reminders enabled with offsets `[60, 1440]` (1 hour and 24 hours; sorted ascending). Owners or members with `workspace:update_settings` may disable reminders or configure zero to five unique offsets. Each offset is an integer from 1 through 10080 minutes (seven days), sorted ascending. Delivery channel fields are not accepted in this workspace DTO; those belong to recipient preferences.

Task `dueDate` remains a date-only value. For reminder scheduling, interpret the due-date boundary as `23:59:59` on that date in each recipient's preference `timeZone`; subtract `offsetMinutes` to calculate a pre-due occurrence. This keeps the displayed date stable across zones while making delivery local to the recipient. The workspace-wide offsets are the same for all recipients; the actual UTC delivery instant may differ by recipient time zone.

Eligible reminder recipients are all currently ACTIVE assignees. If there are no ACTIVE assignees, the active task creator is the fallback recipient. Do not notify the entire workspace. A task is eligible only when it has a due date, is not archived, belongs to an active workspace and has a status category other than `DONE` or `CANCELED`. At each dispatch, re-check current task state and active community/workspace membership.

Each configured pre-due offset may create one logical `TASK_DUE_REMINDER`. A single `TASK_OVERDUE` notification is generated when the task first crosses the recipient-local due-date boundary while still eligible. There are no daily recurring overdue reminders in this contract.

Changing due date, assignee relations, task status, archive state or workspace reminder settings transactionally cancels/rebuilds pending reminder occurrences. A removed assignee, inaccessible workspace or completed/canceled/archived task must not receive a stale queued reminder. A due-date change creates new reminder occurrences for the new date; a retry of the same occurrence does not create a second notification.

## 7. Transactionality, delivery and retry

The domain mutation, notification recipient records, deduplication keys and durable outbox intents commit atomically. If any required durable notification/outbox write fails, the governed transaction fails rather than leaving a committed domain change with a missing required notification. Provider delivery occurs asynchronously and never holds the domain transaction open.

In-app notifications are persisted once and become visible immediately. Email is dispatched by a provider-neutral worker. Use a stable provider idempotency key based on `(notificationId, channel)` where supported; if a provider does not offer idempotency, the application still deduplicates outbox work and records provider request/acceptance IDs to avoid resending accepted messages during worker retries.

For transient email provider timeouts, rate limits and 5xx responses, make six total attempts: initial immediately, then retries after `1`, `5`, `15`, `60` and `240` minutes. Honor provider `Retry-After` when present, capped at six hours; use the later of the scheduled backoff and provider delay. Hard bounces, invalid recipient addresses and permanent 4xx failures are not retried. After exhaustion, mark the email delivery dead-lettered, retain the in-app notification, and raise an aggregated operational alert without logging email content or personal task content.

CR-01 break-glass email delivery is a mandatory exception and remains exactly: immediate attempt, then retries at `+1`, `+5`, `+15`, `+30` and `+60` minutes; final failure writes `BREAK_GLASS_OWNER_ALERT_FAILED`, alerts Security Operations and same-community Community Administrators, and never revokes or silently removes the durable in-app alert. CR-10 generic retry settings do not override this schedule.

CR-07 invitation emails use the shared durable outbox/delivery worker, but their business lifecycle remains CR-07. `QUEUED` means durable enqueue, `SENT` means provider acceptance (not proof of inbox delivery), and `FAILED` means the terminal failure policy was reached. The invite token lifecycle, recipient verification and resend rotation do not change.

## 8. Deduplication and idempotency

A logical domain notification is unique by recipient, community, source event, reason and resource identity. Outbox retries, duplicate publisher delivery or repeated event consumption cannot create a second inbox row. Comment mentions and comment-update suppression remain exactly governed by CR-08.

Each email channel send is keyed by `(notificationId, channel)`. Retries reuse the same key and never insert another inbox row. Each digest has one stable digest key; a notification is included in at most one successfully provider-accepted digest.

A pre-due reminder occurrence is unique by `(recipientUserId, communityId, taskId, dueDate, offsetMinutes)`. An overdue occurrence is unique by `(recipientUserId, communityId, taskId, dueDate)`. A provider retry reuses the occurrence and notification identity. A due-date change produces new occurrence keys for the new date only; it does not resend an already delivered reminder for the same due date and offset.

## 9. Realtime notification events and privacy

`notification.created`, `notification.read` and `notification.read_all` remain on CR-09's user-community stream, never a workspace-wide broadcast. Their closed payloads contain only the recipient's `notificationId`, category/reason where applicable and the recipient's updated unread count. The event does not contain userId, email, full notification body, Markdown/AST, mention targets or hidden resource identifiers. The frontend refreshes the canonical inbox endpoint to obtain the safe DTO.

If the task/workspace/resource is no longer readable at inbox query or email/digest construction time, set its resource pointer to null and use a safe generic summary. Notification rows must not become a side channel for discovering another community's membership, another user's notification, or a task moved to a workspace the recipient cannot read.

## 10. Retention, deployment dependencies and acceptance boundary

Notification inbox retention/deletion duration is intentionally not inferred from CR-14 governance audit retention; Product/Ops must set the notification retention cost/privacy policy separately before production. Email sender/provider, domain authentication, bounce webhooks, secrets, sender reputation, rate limits and delivery dashboards remain CR-13 deployment choices. Queue hosting, dead-letter alert routing, operational backup and failure recovery remain CR-16 implementation/operations gates.

The contract validator can verify route/schema/policy consistency and representative payload shape. It cannot prove worker scheduling, exactly-once external email (not promised), provider acceptance, actual quiet-hour timing, digest correctness, database/outbox transactions, delivery monitoring or runtime security. Those require backend integration, frontend contract tests, provider sandbox tests, load tests and failure injection.
~~~~

## Appendix N — CR-11 Saved views policy
