~~~~markdown
# CR-15 — Pagination, cursors, idempotency and offline replay

**Contract:** `0.3.16-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering contract specified; joint frontend/backend/security/product sign-off and runtime acceptance remain open.

## 1. Scope and governing rules

This policy closes CR-15 while preserving the existing CR-04 canonical query AST/four-view model, CR-09 realtime sequence protocol, CR-12 custom-field value revisions, and the current authentication/security boundaries. It defines wire and persistence behavior; it is not evidence that backend code, database migrations or the frontend offline queue exist.

The exact task-view limits remain LIST 200, BOARD 50 per group, CALENDAR 200 and TIMELINE 200, with a hard maximum of 200 and existing 20-row backlog/unscheduled previews. Generic cursor-paginated collection endpoints default to 50 rows and allow 1–200 unless an endpoint-specific contract declares a narrower limit. Invalid values are rejected with `422 PAGINATION_LIMIT_INVALID`; the server never silently clamps a requested limit.

## 2. Cursor and collection pagination

A paginated endpoint uses opaque, server-managed cursors. Tokens contain at least 256 bits of cryptographically secure randomness; clients must not decode, construct, edit or infer offsets from them. Store only a token digest and retain server-side continuation state. All cursors expire 900 seconds after first-page creation; the deadline is absolute and non-sliding. Replaying the same cursor within that window is safe and returns the same continuation page—it is not a one-use token.

Every ordinary collection cursor is bound to the route/resource, authenticated principal, community/workspace scope, canonical filters, sort direction/order, page limit and continuation state. The server appends a unique UUIDv7 ID tie-breaker to the documented sort tuple. Offsets and client-defined sort expressions are prohibited. A changed filter, sort, limit, route or scope must not be applied to a prior cursor; reject it with `409 CURSOR_INVALID` (or `QUERY_CURSOR_INVALID` for task views). Generic collection keyset traversal is not a historical snapshot unless an endpoint explicitly says it is; new/deleted rows or mutable sort-key changes may be observed between pages.

Where a paginated DTO defines `pageInfo`, preserve its existing resource-specific response shape and use `nextCursor`, `hasMore` and optional `totalCount`. Do not wrap or rename existing response DTOs as part of CR-15.

## 3. Four-view task query snapshots

The first `POST .../tasks/query` request creates one consistent snapshot containing ordered task IDs, canonical membership, group/bucket assignments, counts and the workspace `snapshotSequence` watermark. `snapshotAt` is the snapshot creation instant; `snapshotExpiresAt` is exactly 900 seconds later. Page fetches and projection switches do not extend the expiry. All cursors and the `querySnapshotId` handle expire together; an expired handle/cursor returns `409 QUERY_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED` and the frontend restarts from the first page.

Task membership, ordering, bucket assignments and counts remain anchored to that snapshot. Task DTO values are read at page-fetch time. A task created after the watermark is not inserted into the existing snapshot; a reorder or filter-changing mutation does not reorder/re-filter the existing snapshot. A realtime workspace event newer than `snapshotSequence` invalidates the active query and prompts a fresh query. CR-09 workspace/user-community stream sequence numbers and event catch-up cursors remain separate from this query cursor protocol.

Cursors bind community, workspace, principal, canonical `querySpec` hash, snapshot, page scope and group key as applicable. Projection is excluded from the canonical query hash so LIST, BOARD, CALENDAR and TIMELINE can re-project the same snapshot with identical `querySpec`, preserving the existing CR-04 behavior. A cursor/handle is never an authorization token. Recheck current session, membership, `task:read`, Personal Workspace privacy and break-glass scope for every page and re-projection. Omit individually revoked/invisible rows without backfilling from outside the snapshot; a page may be shorter than requested. If workspace access itself is revoked, return the standard non-enumerating workspace authorization response without disclosing that a snapshot exists. A malformed, tampered, wrong-principal, wrong-workspace, wrong-query or inconsistent cursor returns generic `409 QUERY_CURSOR_INVALID`.

## 4. Mutation idempotency

### 4.1 Key and scope

Every state-changing POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requires `X-Mutation-Id`, formatted as the existing UUIDv7 `Uuid` schema. GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are exempt. Read-only POST queries/previews and one-time credential issuance are explicitly listed in `openapi.yaml`; no blanket rule should require an idempotency key on every POST.

The unique database key is `(principal_scope, mutation_id)`:

- Authenticated writes use `USER:{authenticatedUserId}` globally across every community, workspace, resource and route for that account. The key is not scoped to a workspace or operation.
- Unauthenticated pre-authentication writes use `PREAUTH:{server-HMAC-digest-of-active-__Host-auth-csrf-cookie}`. The server derives this from the CR-13 ten-minute pre-auth CSRF cookie; it never trusts an ID supplied by the client or an IP address as the principal.
- A client must mint a new key when switching from pre-authentication to an authenticated session or between accounts.

A request fingerprint includes canonical HTTP method, normalized route/path, canonical JSON request body, content type and `X-Mutation-Created-At` when present. CSRF token, cookies, Origin, `X-Request-Id` and other attempt-specific credentials are excluded. Reusing a key with a different fingerprint returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`, even when the second request targets another route.

### 4.2 Retention and replay

Keep idempotency records for 30 days from the server's first receipt. Expiry is fixed; replays do not extend it. Retain the principal scope, mutation ID, fingerprint, completion state, original HTTP status, safe response body/headers and creation/expiry timestamps. Never persist or replay `Set-Cookie`, session/CSRF/auth tokens, OAuth authorization codes, passwords or raw credentials. Credential-issuing operations that cannot safely replay their result return `409 AUTH_RESULT_NOT_REPLAYABLE` on duplicate and require the client to restart the flow with a new key.

Before returning any stored result, re-authenticate and re-check CSRF/Origin, current resource scope, membership, visibility and effective capability. If access has been revoked, return the current 401/403/404 result rather than the cached body. Context-sensitive response projections such as `effectivePermissions` must be recomputed under current authorization. A successful/deterministic completed-result replay includes `X-Idempotent-Replayed: true`; omit the header on first execution.

Every state-changing operation declares a generic 409 Problem Details response for `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` and `IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS`; the latter carries `Retry-After` and `retryable: true`. A task field conflict or other resource-specific conflict retains its typed conflict details while also accepting the generic idempotency Problem shape. Credential/step-up operations with non-replayable results declare `AUTH_RESULT_NOT_REPLAYABLE`.

Use a unique constraint/lock so concurrent requests with the same key cannot both execute. One request owns the mutation; a same-fingerprint duplicate waits for it and, if the bounded wait expires, receives retryable `409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` plus `Retry-After`. A different fingerprint immediately receives `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`. Commit the domain mutation, its completed idempotency result and durable domain-event/outbox intents in one database transaction. External email/notification/provider side effects occur only after commit and use downstream deduplication keys.

Persist successful responses and deterministic terminal domain/validation/conflict outcomes. Do not persist authentication/authorization failures, rate limits, transient 5xx responses or rolled-back transactions; the same key can be retried after those non-completions. A persisted 409 conflict is itself a completed decision: after a user resolves it, the changed request is a new logical mutation and must use a new key.

## 5. Scoped offline task-field replay

Offline support is limited to selected fields on an existing task. It reuses `PATCH /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/tasks/{taskId}`; CR-15 does not add a batch `/sync/mutations` route. The draft allow-list is `title`, `description`, `statusCategory`, `priority`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `estimatePoints` and individual `customFieldValues.{definitionId}` values. Relation/structure fields such as `itemType`, `assigneeIds`, `labelIds`, `milestoneId`, `rankPlacement`, dependencies/links, task lifecycle actions, comments, membership/role operations, transfers, bulk work and file operations are online-only.

Each queued mutation stores one stable UUIDv7 `X-Mutation-Id`, queue creation timestamp, exact partial patch and the `baseFieldRevisions` observed when editing began. Queue entries replay FIFO for the same account/workspace, sequentially; edits to one task preserve their order. A transport retry reuses the exact same key and request fingerprint. The offline header `X-Mutation-Created-At` carries the queued timestamp. The client blocks automatic replay after 14 days. The server checks for an already-completed idempotency record first so a late retry cannot duplicate an earlier successful write; otherwise a first-received offline mutation older than 14 days returns `410 MUTATION_EXPIRED`. A client timestamp over five minutes in the future is rejected. Client time is not used for authorization or conflict resolution and is not a trusted security clock.

Before every replay, require the same authenticated account and re-evaluate current workspace membership, task visibility and field-level capabilities. Never replay one account's queued content under another account. If access is revoked or a field is no longer authorized, do not apply the mutation; quarantine it in the local recovery drawer. Copying/recreating it into an accessible Personal Workspace requires explicit user action, current permissions and a new mutation ID.

For every changed field `f`, compare the server's current `fieldRevisions[f]` to `baseFieldRevisions[f]`. Equal revisions allow the edit even if unrelated fields have changed. A changed same-field revision returns `409 FIELD_REVISION_CONFLICT` with field paths in `conflictingFields[]` plus `conflictDetails[]` entries containing the client/server values and base/current revisions; no partial write. `fieldRevisions` (including `customFieldValues.{definitionId}`) are authoritative; client clocks and Last-Write-Wins are prohibited. The UI presents the structured client/server values and revision pair. After user confirmation, fetch fresh field revisions and submit a new logical mutation with a new `X-Mutation-Id`; never alter the body while reusing the old key.

## 6. Errors and retry matrix

| Condition | Response | Client behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| Expired task query snapshot/cursor | 409 `QUERY_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED` | Start a new query; do not attempt to extend the old snapshot. |
| Invalid/tampered/mismatched query cursor | 409 `QUERY_CURSOR_INVALID` | Discard cursor and start a new query. |
| Invalid/mismatched ordinary collection cursor | 409 `CURSOR_INVALID` | Discard cursor and restart collection. |
| Expired ordinary collection cursor | 409 `CURSOR_EXPIRED` | Restart collection. |
| Same key, changed request fingerprint | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` | Do not retry with that key; mint a new key only for a new logical mutation. |
| Same mutation still executing | 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` + `Retry-After` | Retry exact request with same key. |
| Current authorization has been revoked | Standard 401/403/404 | Do not replay; quarantine local offline entry where applicable. |
| First arrival of offline mutation older than 14 days | 410 `MUTATION_EXPIRED` | Require explicit user re-submit with new key and fresh field revisions. |
| Same-field revision changed | 409 `FIELD_REVISION_CONFLICT` | Show conflict resolver; refreshed, user-confirmed action gets a new key. |
| Page limit outside endpoint bounds | 422 `PAGINATION_LIMIT_INVALID` | Correct requested limit; do not silently clamp. |
| Non-replayable credential result | 409 `AUTH_RESULT_NOT_REPLAYABLE` | Restart the relevant auth flow with a new key. |

## 7. Acceptance criteria and boundaries

The backend must prove one mutation under concurrent duplicate delivery, exact replay without duplicate side effects, payload-mismatch rejection, 30-day fixed retention, authorization-before-replay, pre-auth scope isolation, no credential replay, transactional idempotency/outbox commit, expired offline-item rejection, live permission re-check, per-field non-overlap merge and atomic same-field conflict. The frontend must prove 14-day queue aging, account/workspace isolation, sequential retry with stable keys, explicit re-submit with fresh keys, recovery-drawer quarantine and field-level conflict UX. Cursor/snapshot acceptance must cover expiry, tampering, altered query/limit/scope, repeat cursor use, concurrent insertion, row revocation, workspace revocation, same-snapshot re-projection and realtime invalidation.

**Not implementation evidence:** no backend DB migration/locking/transaction test, offline IndexedDB implementation, replay worker, browser integration test, concurrency test, security penetration test, production retention-cost validation, official Redocly lint or generated frontend compilation is claimed by this policy. Numeric TTLs and exact offline field allow-list require joint FE/BE/security/product sign-off before contract freeze. The 30-day record retention is retained as the reconciled DEF-01 engineering recommendation; cost and operations validation remain part of CR-16.
~~~~

## Appendix R — CR-16 Reliability, operations and DR policy

**Status:** ENGINEERING DRAFT — SLO/PROVIDER/DR EXECUTION OPEN.

This is a verbatim source snapshot. Apply the main-body reconciliation rules where the draft uses superseded terminology or behavior.

~~~~markdown
# CR-16 — Reliability, Operations and Disaster Recovery

**Contract:** `0.3.17-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering operations contract specified. DEC-OPEN-04 targets remain provisional, and provider selection, budget, backup configuration, monitoring, restore exercises and measured target attainment remain open.

## 1. Decision boundary

CR-16 closes the reliability/operations contract design, not production procurement or operations execution. The product owner previously retained these targets as provisional:

| Measure | Provisional target | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Monthly availability | **99.5%** | User-visible service availability target; not an SLA or current measurement. |
| Database RPO | **Less than 5 minutes** | Maximum intended database data-loss window after a covered disaster; not a guarantee until WAL/PITR is provisioned and tested. |
| RTO | **Less than 60 minutes** | From incident declaration to verified critical service restoration; not a guarantee until a timed clean-room drill passes. |

At 99.5% over a 30-day month, the planning error budget is approximately 3 hours 36 minutes. Availability is measured using an external synthetic `GET /api/v1/health/ready` check every 60 seconds from two independent regions, retaining both regional results. Customer-visible downtime is recorded; do not silently exclude maintenance or provider incidents. The final measurement vendor, denominator and any formal maintenance exclusion require joint Product/Ops approval.

RPO applies to the primary PostgreSQL database. Continuous WAL archiving/PITR is the primary mechanism; daily encrypted logical backups are an independent recovery path, not a substitute for WAL. File/object storage recovery is not included because file upload/attachment functionality was removed from the current product scope. Reintroducing files requires a separate product and recovery decision.

## 2. Initial deployment topology

**Recommended default for the first 70–90 users:**

- Static Vite/React SPA/PWA served from an edge CDN with TLS, security headers, immutable hashed assets and atomic rollback to a prior build.
- One always-on containerized backend modular monolith serving REST and WebSocket connections. The transactional outbox/background worker runs in-process or as a lightweight worker using the same release image.
- Managed PostgreSQL 16/17 with RLS, connection pooling, automated snapshots and continuous WAL PITR.
- Centralized structured logs, metrics, a separate synthetic uptime monitor and actionable alerting.

Do not introduce Kubernetes, Kafka, a microservice mesh, or a self-managed database cluster for the initial community. Do not provision Redis/RabbitMQ by default; add a broker or more replicas only after measured load and a reviewed architecture change. Keep the transactional outbox as the durable source for asynchronous work.

This is a **recommendation**, not an approved provider choice. Render/Fly.io/Railway/AWS/Neon/Supabase/Cloudflare and other vendors must be compared with the backend developer for WebSocket support, managed PostgreSQL PITR, region, backups, secrets, egress, availability, budget and restore procedures before selection.

## 3. Environment separation and secrets

| Environment | Required boundary |
|---|---|
| `dev` | Local development, deterministic `seed-v1.json`, MSW or isolated local Docker services. No production credentials or tenant data. |
| `staging` | Production-like topology with separate database/secrets and sandbox email sink. Run migration, contract, restore and release gates here. |
| `prod` | Separate credentials/database/secrets, least-privilege service identities, restricted audited operational access; no routine direct workstation access to production data. |

Inject `DATABASE_APP_URL`, `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL`, session/OAuth/email and observability secrets using the chosen platform secret manager. Never commit secrets. Validate required configuration at startup and fail closed on missing/malformed values. The runtime database identity must not have DDL privileges; migrations use a separate owner identity. Rotate secrets through an auditable runbook.

## 4. Health probes and readiness

Two tenant-neutral, unauthenticated, `Cache-Control: no-store` probes are part of the HTTP contract:

- `GET /health/live` returns `200 { "status": "UP" }` when the process/event loop responds. It does not query PostgreSQL or external providers. A failed liveness probe permits the orchestrator to restart the process.
- `GET /health/ready` executes PostgreSQL `SELECT 1` with a 2-second timeout and requires an outbox-worker heartbeat no older than 30 seconds. Return `200 { "status": "UP" }` only if both pass; otherwise return generic `503` Problem Details with `Retry-After`.

Health responses reveal no dependency names, hostnames, connection details, query text, credentials or tenant data. Deeper diagnostics and metrics remain private to operations tooling. A readiness failure removes the instance from new traffic; it is not a substitute for incident alerts.

## 5. Observability, redaction and actionable alerts

Emit single-line structured JSON logs with `timestamp`, `level`, `correlationId`, `userId`, `communityId`, `workspaceId`, `operationId`, `statusCode`, `durationMs` and `errorCode`. Redact cookies, Authorization, CSRF values, passwords, access/refresh tokens, OAuth codes, session secrets, raw task titles/descriptions, comment bodies, custom-field values and free-text break-glass justifications. Do not use log lines as a copy of task content.

Track synthetic availability by region, HTTP error rates, latency percentiles, task-query p95, PostgreSQL connection/latency/WAL archive lag, outbox backlog/oldest pending age, worker heartbeat, WebSocket reconnect/sequence gaps, backup freshness, restore-drill outcomes and audit-chain verification.

| Alert | Severity | Trigger | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Readiness down | Critical | `/health/ready` non-200 for 2 consecutive minutes | Check release, DB reachability and worker heartbeat; assign incident owner. |
| HTTP 5xx spike | High | 5xx exceeds 1% of requests or more than 5 errors in 5 minutes | Inspect redacted correlated logs and recent releases; mitigate or rollback if release-related. |
| Outbox lag | High | More than 100 unprocessed `domain_events` older than 30 seconds | Inspect worker heartbeat, locks and provider throttling; preserve durable event rows. |
| Security/audit integrity | Immediate | Any `ADMIN_BREAK_GLASS`, audit hash-chain verification failure, or more than 50 401/403/429 responses from one actor in 5 minutes | Notify Security; review actor/session/audit evidence and contain access where warranted. |
| Backup/RPO risk | Critical | WAL/archive lag approaches 5 minutes, required backup is missing/invalid, or restore drill fails | Ops investigates immediately; do not claim RPO coverage until freshness and restore verification recover. |

The initial alert set should remain small and actionable. Thresholds are draft defaults and must be tuned against staging/production baseline data to avoid alert fatigue.

## 6. Backup and disaster recovery

**Primary recovery path:** managed PostgreSQL continuous WAL archiving/PITR plus automated daily encrypted `pg_dump --format=custom` backups. Copy logical backups to a separate isolated bucket/account or equivalent provider boundary; access to encryption keys must be separated from normal application credentials. A 30-day backup retention period is a **recommended default only**, subject to provider cost, recovery needs and security review. It is not CR-14 audit-log retention and does not resolve audit-retention policy.

**Restore drill:** complete a clean-room restore before M1.3 production sign-off and monthly thereafter. Use an isolated disposable PostgreSQL environment; restore a selected PITR target; verify schema/migrations, foreign keys, tenant/RLS policies, CR-14 audit hash chain, idempotency/outbox invariants and critical CHK-01 through CHK-06 smoke checks. Record source backup/WAL timestamps, recovery target, measured data-loss window, elapsed time, failed checks and corrective actions. `scripts/dr-restore-verify.sh` is the recommended reproducible entry point and must exit non-zero on mismatch. A drill must never write into production.

For a real disaster, preserve the incident evidence and current database/WAL state first. Restore into an isolated target, verify integrity and tenant isolation, obtain Incident Commander and database-owner approval, then perform controlled cutover and validate critical authenticated flows. A backup is not proven until the restore succeeds.

## 7. Deployment, migrations and rollback

Run five required CI gates on pull requests:

1. Contract gate: official OpenAPI lint and deterministic TypeScript type generation; generated output produces no unexpected diff.
2. Static/supply-chain gate: TypeScript check, ESLint, dependency vulnerability scan and lockfile integrity.
3. Backend gate: unit/policy/integration tests against an ephemeral PostgreSQL service with migrations applied from scratch.
4. Frontend gate: component/MSW/Playwright end-to-end tests and axe-core accessibility checks; zero critical/serious accessibility violations.
5. Build gate: production Vite build, smoke checks and monitored bundle budget (initial gzipped entrypoint target below 200 KB; lazy-load Calendar, Timeline and Settings).

Build immutable, versioned frontend/backend artifacts once and promote the same artifacts through dev, staging and production. Staging must pass contract, migration, health, backup/restore and launch checks before production promotion.

Use expand-and-contract database migrations: (A) add nullable/backward-compatible columns/tables/indexes; (B) deploy code that is compatible with application versions N and N-1; (C) backfill in bounded batches; (D) add constraints or remove old structures only after prior application versions are retired. Use non-blocking/concurrent index creation where supported. Backend rollback redeploys the previous immutable image only when schema compatibility is verified; otherwise use an approved forward fix or database restore. Never run an automatic destructive schema downgrade. Frontend rollback switches the CDN to the prior immutable build.

## 8. Incident response

**SEV-1:** tenant isolation breach, total service outage, suspected account/session compromise, destructive data corruption or audit-chain integrity failure. Assign an Incident Commander, technical operator and communications owner. Within 0–15 minutes where feasible: declare the incident, preserve evidence, revoke affected sessions/sockets, disable compromised credentials or feature paths, stop unsafe writes/enter maintenance mode (`503` + `Retry-After`), and roll back a bad application release when safe. Target verified restoration inside the provisional 60-minute RTO. If database corruption requires PITR, restore in isolation, verify audit/RLS/foreign keys, approve cutover and run critical smoke tests.

**SEV-2:** partial degradation such as realtime disconnect, email/notification delay or a non-critical background job failure while core authenticated task operations remain available. Use HTTP fallback where realtime is impaired; retain outbox work for retry; disable only affected non-critical paths and communicate degraded functionality.

Maintain a timestamped incident log with correlation IDs, impact, decisions and recovery checkpoints. Do not put secrets or task contents in incident channels. A blameless post-incident review within five business days is a recommended default; record timeline, impact, root/contributing causes, measured RPO/RTO, alerting/response gaps and tracked corrective actions.

## 9. Performance acceptance recommendations

These remain engineering recommendations, not approved availability SLAs or measured results: task query below 400 ms p95 on a workspace with up to 1,000 tasks; exact task-key lookup below 100 ms p95; optimistic local UI reflection below 50 ms on reference desktop hardware; Core Web Vitals INP p75 at or below 200 ms. Measure and report distributions rather than asserting a target from a single run.

## 10. M1.3 production acceptance gate

Do not sign off Initial Production Release until all are evidenced:

- Two-region synthetic readiness monitoring and alert delivery verified in staging.
- PostgreSQL WAL/PITR and encrypted logical-backup configuration verified on selected provider.
- Clean-room restore drill completed before launch and meeting the provisional RPO/RTO targets.
- Health probes, redacted logs, HTTP 5xx, outbox, security/audit and backup alerts verified.
- Five CI gates and contract/type generation pass.
- Expand-and-contract migration and previous-image rollback rehearsed.
- SEV-1/SEV-2 runbooks, owners, escalation and communications paths reviewed.
- Hosting/provider/budget selected and jointly approved by Product, Backend, Frontend, Security and Operations.

**Evidence boundary:** CR-16 specifies controls and acceptance criteria. It does not prove a provider has been selected, monitoring/backups are enabled, a restore drill occurred, incidents were rehearsed or any SLO/RPO/RTO target has been achieved.
~~~~

## Appendix S — CR-04 Four-view query policy

**Status:** ENGINEERING DRAFT — PROJECT FILTER/GROUP REFERENCES REQUIRE RECONCILIATION.

This is a verbatim source snapshot. Apply the main-body reconciliation rules where the draft uses superseded terminology or behavior.

~~~~markdown
# CR-04 — Canonical Query AST and Four-View Contract

**Original contract:** `0.3.5-draft` · **Pagination addendum:** `0.3.16-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering/query semantics specified for joint frontend/backend review. This is a contract decision record, not backend implementation evidence or contract-freeze approval.

## 1. Core decision

List, Board, Calendar and Timeline use one endpoint:

`POST /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/tasks/query`

The request contains two deliberately separate concepts:

- `querySpec`: one canonical, projection-independent `ViewQuerySpec` containing the filter AST, grouping, sort, subtask and inclusion/date-window rules.
- `projection`: `LIST`, `BOARD`, `CALENDAR` or `TIMELINE`. It changes only the response shape and auxiliary metadata, never the authorization or filter/membership pipeline.

`SavedViewDto.viewType` stores the preferred projection separately from `SavedViewDto.querySpec`. The API uses camelCase field identifiers. Older snake_case examples in planning notes are non-normative.

The active Task API exposes `statusCategory` as its status dimension. It does not currently define a `WorkflowStatus` resource or `statusId` field; the query contract therefore does not accept `statusId` and uses the five canonical status categories until a separate workflow-status contract is added. An identical normalized query specification evaluated against the same query snapshot yields the same canonical task ID set for all four projections. Grouping, swimlanes and response buckets are lossless partitions/presentations of that set; they do not add or remove task identities. `subtaskMode`, `includeCompleted`, `dateWindow` and the unscheduled inclusion flag are query semantics, not projection defaults, and are therefore shared by every projection using that query specification.

## 2. Authorization and baseline membership

Before evaluating the user-supplied AST, the backend applies:

1. Community and workspace path scoping.
2. Current active workspace membership and effective `task:read` authorization for each returned task.
3. CR-01 Personal Workspace privacy and audited break-glass constraints where applicable.
4. Active-task baseline (`archivedAt IS NULL`). The Trash view is a separate surface.

The query AST cannot replace or weaken any server-derived scope. Client-supplied project IDs, task IDs, custom-field keys or search terms do not grant access. Each cursor page rechecks current access; a cursor is not an authorization token.

After security and active-task scoping, the server applies the user filter and completion inclusion. When `includeBacklog=false`, matching BACKLOG tasks are partitioned into their own tray before date-window bucketing and are not counted as dated/unscheduled primary items. All remaining primary tasks then follow the date-window and unscheduled rules. When `includeBacklog=true`, BACKLOG tasks remain in the primary set and follow those same date-window/unscheduled rules. A revoked or newly inaccessible task is omitted from later pages, even if it belonged to the original snapshot.

## 3. Filter AST

The root node is `{ conjunction: "AND" | "OR", conditions: [...] }`. Conditions contain leaf `{ field, operator, value? }` nodes or one nested subgroup. A nested subgroup can contain leaves only: maximum depth is root plus one subgroup. There may be at most 50 leaf conditions in the complete AST. Empty root `AND` means match all otherwise-authorized active tasks; empty root `OR` matches none; empty subgroups are invalid.

The supported operator vocabulary is:

`EQ`, `NEQ`, `IN`, `NOT_IN`, `CONTAINS`, `IS_EMPTY`, `IS_NOT_EMPTY`, `GT`, `GTE`, `LT`, `LTE`, `BETWEEN`.

`IS_EMPTY` and `IS_NOT_EMPTY` take no `value`. Other operators require one. `IN`/`NOT_IN` take a non-empty array. `BETWEEN` takes exactly two inclusive, type-compatible bounds; a lower bound greater than its upper bound is invalid. `CONTAINS` takes a non-empty string. Runtime validation must reject a field/operator/value mismatch with `422 FILTER_OPERATOR_UNSUPPORTED`; it must not coerce types or silently ignore a condition. For nullable scalar fields, `NEQ` and `NOT_IN` do not match missing/null values; callers use `IS_EMPTY` or `IS_NOT_EMPTY` to address null explicitly. For relation-set fields, `NEQ`/`NOT_IN` means no related row matches, including an empty relation set.

### Canonical built-in fields and type-specific operators

| Field | Value type | Allowed operators |
|---|---|---|
| `projectId`, `createdById` | UUID | `EQ`, `NEQ`, `IN`, `NOT_IN` |
| `milestoneId`, `cycleId` | Nullable UUID | UUID operators plus `IS_EMPTY`, `IS_NOT_EMPTY` (cycle is feature-gated until cycles are enabled) |
| `assigneeId`, `watcherId`, `labelId` | UUID relation sets | UUID operators plus empty operators |
| `statusCategory`, `priority`, `itemType` | Enum | `EQ`, `NEQ`, `IN`, `NOT_IN` |
| `startDate`, `dueDate` | Nullable `YYYY-MM-DD` | Date comparisons, `BETWEEN`, empty operators |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | RFC 3339 timestamp | Timestamp comparisons and `BETWEEN` |
| `estimatePoints` | Nullable number | Numeric comparisons, `BETWEEN`, empty operators |
| `hasBlocker`, `isOverdue` | Boolean | `EQ`, `NEQ` |
| `q` | Text search | `CONTAINS` only |
| `cf.{fieldKey}` | Defined by active custom-field definition | Type-specific operators below |

For multi-value relation fields (`assigneeId`, `watcherId`, `labelId`), `EQ`/`IN` means at least one related value matches; `NEQ`/`NOT_IN` means no related value matches. `$CURRENT_USER` is accepted only for `assigneeId`, `watcherId` and `createdById`, and is resolved server-side to the authenticated user UUID. The `q` field performs full-text search over authorized task title and description content. `hasBlocker=true` means an active incoming `BLOCKS` predecessor is not `DONE` or `CANCELED`; inaccessible blocker identities remain masked. `isOverdue=true` means `dueDate` is before workspace-local today and the task is neither `DONE` nor `CANCELED`; a missing due date is false.

`$TODAY` and `$NEXT_7_DAYS` are supported only for `startDate` and `dueDate` date-only fields. They are resolved using the workspace IANA timezone and the workspace-local date captured when the query snapshot is created. `$TODAY` is a scalar date bound. `$NEXT_7_DAYS` is permitted only as the second/upper bound of a `BETWEEN` pair; it resolves to the seventh inclusive workspace-local date (today plus the next six local dates). A `BETWEEN` pair may therefore use `[$TODAY, $NEXT_7_DAYS]` to represent the next seven calendar dates. Date-only values use `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamp values are instants and are normalized/compared in UTC.

### Custom fields

The canonical field syntax is `cf.{fieldKey}`. The active API has no List resource or `TaskDto.listId`, so the legacy `listId` filter/grouping identifier is deliberately not accepted; use `projectId` until a Lists resource is explicitly added through a separate contract decision. Likewise, `statusId` is not accepted because the active Task API exposes only `statusCategory` and defines no WorkflowStatus resource; add status-ID queries only with that separate lifecycle contract. `fieldKey` is stable and workspace-unique; it is generated when the field definition is created and never changes. The server resolves it to the active `CustomFieldDefinition` and validates operator/value types against that definition. Unknown, archived or cross-workspace custom fields return `422 FILTER_FIELD_INVALID`.

Phase 1 queryable types are `TEXT`, `NUMBER`, `DATE`, `BOOLEAN` and `SINGLE_SELECT`:

| Custom field type | Filter operators | Comparison semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `EQ`, `NEQ`, `CONTAINS`, `IS_EMPTY`, `IS_NOT_EMPTY` | Unicode-normalized, case-insensitive comparison; `CONTAINS` is substring matching |
| `NUMBER` | `EQ`, `NEQ`, `GT`, `GTE`, `LT`, `LTE`, `BETWEEN`, empty operators | Numeric, not lexical, comparison |
| `DATE` | Date comparisons, `BETWEEN`, empty operators | Workspace-local date comparison |
| `BOOLEAN` | `EQ`, `NEQ`, empty operators | Boolean comparison |
| `SINGLE_SELECT` | `EQ`, `NEQ`, `IN`, `NOT_IN`, empty operators | Stable option UUIDs are values; option labels are presentation only |

Custom-field sorting uses the declared native type. `SINGLE_SELECT` uses configured option order; text uses normalized case-insensitive collation. Archived definitions remain visible historically on task records but cannot be used in newly executed query filters or sort terms. `SINGLE_SELECT` values are stable option UUIDv7s; labels are presentation-only. CR-12 defines `CustomFieldOptionDto`, option CRUD/ordering, archive/restore, optimistic schema versions and typed task value maps. Archived option IDs remain filterable on an active definition for historical tasks; archived definitions themselves are not filterable/sortable. Do not send option labels as query values.


### Canonical field-to-resource/DTO mapping

The filter registry uses stable domain names; these do not always have the same spelling as the response DTO or persistence column:

| Query field | Authoritative mapping |
|---|---|
| `createdById` | Task creator relation; exposed as `TaskDto.creatorId` |
| `assigneeId` | Task-assignee relation set; exposed as `TaskDto.assigneeIds` |
| `watcherId` | Workspace-scoped task-watcher relation; not inferred from a count/summary field |
| `labelId` | Task-label relation set; exposed as `TaskDto.labelIds` |
| `currentKey` sort | Canonical `Task.current_key`; exposed as `TaskDto.taskKey` |
| `cf.{fieldKey}` | Resolve the immutable workspace-unique `CustomFieldDefinitionDto.fieldKey` to its definition ID, then read the typed task custom-field value. `TaskDto.customFieldValues` is keyed by definition ID in the current DTO contract. |

No client may provide a storage column name, JSON path, custom-field definition ID or SQL expression as a substitute for a canonical field identifier. The server resolves the allowlisted field through this mapping.

## 4. Grouping and subtask semantics

`groupBy` supports `statusCategory`, `projectId`, `priority`, `assigneeId`, `milestoneId` and `none`. `subGroupBy` supports `none`, `assigneeId`, `priority` and `projectId`; it is used for Board swimlanes. Grouping is presentation-only and is applied after canonical membership is calculated. When grouping by `assigneeId`, a multi-assignee task appears once in each corresponding bucket; the union of bucket IDs equals canonical membership, but bucket totals overlap and must not be summed. Nullable milestone and assignee values use an explicit Unassigned bucket; priority order is `URGENT`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`, `NONE`.

`subtaskMode` supports:

- `NESTED` (default): return only tasks that match the canonical filters, preserving parent-child relationships among returned tasks; do not implicitly include non-matching descendants.
- `TOP_LEVEL_ONLY`: restrict the canonical result set to tasks with no parent.
- `FLATTENED`: include matching tasks/subtasks as peers while retaining `parentTaskId` for breadcrumb context.

When a descendant matches but its ancestor does not, the matched task remains in the result. The API does not return non-matching ancestor rows. `parentTaskId` is returned only if the caller is authorized to read the parent; otherwise it is null. No inaccessible ancestor title, key or identifier is disclosed through breadcrumbs.

Board's default surface shows top-level cards, with subtask counts/progress on the card; `subtaskMode` determines the canonical task set and does not vary by projection. A client may optionally render included subtasks as separate cards without asking for a different backend filter.

## 5. Backlog and completed tasks

`includeCompleted` defaults to `true`. When false, `DONE` and `CANCELED` tasks are excluded from all projections.

`includeBacklog` defaults to `false`. When false, `BACKLOG` tasks are placed in a separately paged backlog tray, not silently discarded; when true, they join the primary grouped results. Counts and pages make the partition inspectable. This is a presentation partition of the same query membership, not data deletion.

When a date window is present and `includeBacklog=false`, the backlog tray is formed from tasks matching the filter/completion rules and is separate from the dated/unscheduled Calendar or Timeline lanes. When `includeBacklog=true`, backlog tasks follow the same date-window and unscheduled rules as other tasks.

## 6. Date windows and unscheduled tasks

Calendar and Timeline projections require `dateWindow` with `dateField`, inclusive `from` and `to` dates, and `includeUnscheduled`. The workspace IANA timezone is authoritative; the browser timezone cannot override it. `from` must be on or before `to`; the inclusive range is limited to 366 calendar days. Invalid/missing ranges return `422 DATE_WINDOW_INVALID` or `422 DATE_WINDOW_REQUIRED`.

- `DUE_DATE`: a task is scheduled only when its `dueDate` is within the inclusive range. A task with `startDate` but no `dueDate` is unscheduled for this mode.
- `START_TO_DUE_SPAN`: use `startDate ?? dueDate` as the effective start and `dueDate ?? startDate` as the effective end. Include a task when that inclusive span overlaps the selected range. If both dates are null, it is unscheduled. Timeline requires this mode.

When `includeUnscheduled=true`, tasks without the selected date/span are returned in a separate unscheduled tray, not mixed into the dated page. `unscheduledPreview` is capped at 20; `unscheduledCount` and `unscheduledNextCursor` cover the entire tray. When false, unscheduled tasks are excluded from the returned query set. Without a `dateWindow`, unscheduled bucketing does not apply.

## 7. Sorting and deterministic order

Up to three user sort terms are accepted from `rankKey`, `priority`, `dueDate`, `startDate`, `createdAt`, `currentKey` and `cf.{fieldKey}`. `currentKey` sorts by the canonical internal `Task.current_key` and corresponds to `TaskDto.taskKey` on the wire. The server always appends `id ASC` as a deterministic tie-breaker; callers cannot supply or override `id`. Null values sort last in both ascending and descending directions.

Priority ordering is `URGENT`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`, `NONE`. Rank ordering uses fractional `rankKey` only within its owning project/status ordering container; cross-container order first uses deterministic project/status display order, then `rankKey ASC`, then task ID. Custom fields sort by native type. The default order is deterministic rank order with server-appended task ID as the final tie-breaker.

## 8. Projection response behavior

- **List:** flat canonical task pages; the client builds an expandable tree from `parentTaskId` and `subtaskMode`.
- **Board:** grouped buckets with per-group totals and independent continuation cursors. Initial page is 50 tasks per group; subsequent `pageScope=GROUP` requests identify the returned opaque `groupKey` and cursor. `groupBy` defaults to `statusCategory`; `subGroupBy` defaults to `none`.
- **Calendar:** scheduled tasks within the date window plus the separate unscheduled tray. Milestones remain ProjectMilestone markers, not Task records; Calendar/Timeline obtain marker metadata through the existing `GET /communities/{communityId}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/milestones` endpoint, and markers are excluded from task membership and counts.
- **Timeline:** hierarchical task rows plus dependency edges touching the query set. If the opposite endpoint is inaccessible, return only `{ access: "RESTRICTED", label: "Restricted Task" }`; do not return its task UUID, key, title or status.

Timeline dependency edges include only relationships for which the returned endpoint is authorized. Accessible opposite endpoints may include minimal task ID/key/title/status metadata, even when they are outside the active filter result. Inaccessible endpoints are never dereferenced into identifying data.

## 9. Cursor and query-snapshot consistency

The first request creates a server-managed query snapshot. It captures the ordered task ID membership, group/bucket assignment and counts for the canonical query AST, as well as the current workspace sequence watermark (`snapshotSequence`). The cursor is opaque, integrity-protected and server-generated; it is not a client offset or page number.

A cursor is bound to the community, workspace, authenticated principal, canonical query-spec hash, snapshot, page scope and group key where applicable. Projection is not part of the canonical query hash or snapshot membership: the same snapshot may be projected as LIST, BOARD, CALENDAR or TIMELINE. The first response returns `querySnapshotId`; a later projection switch may pass that handle without a cursor to retrieve the first page in another projection from the identical task-ID snapshot and identical querySpec. The requested projection must still satisfy its own preconditions (for example, Calendar/Timeline require a dateWindow and Timeline requires `START_TO_DUE_SPAN`). A continuation uses the returned cursor; if both cursor and querySnapshotId are supplied, they must reference the same snapshot. The server validates principal, community, workspace and query hash, then rechecks live authorization. Neither handle nor cursor grants access. Membership/order/counts remain anchored to the first snapshot; Task DTO field values are read at page-fetch time. The server rechecks current workspace membership, `task:read`, Personal Workspace privacy and break-glass grants on every page/re-projection, omitting any row no longer visible. Realtime events newer than `snapshotSequence` should invalidate/refetch the active query so live data and snapshot membership converge.

A stale/expired snapshot returns `409 QUERY_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED`; an invalid/tampered or differently scoped cursor returns `409 QUERY_CURSOR_INVALID`. CR-15 fixes the task-query snapshot and all associated cursors/handles to a 900-second absolute, non-sliding TTL from first-page creation. Cursors are opaque, server-managed, replayable within that TTL and bound to principal, community, workspace, canonical query hash, page scope/group key and snapshot. Query responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. See `pagination-idempotency-offline-policy.md` for the complete cursor, expiry, idempotency and offline replay contract.

The `total` field counts distinct task IDs across primary, backlog and unscheduled partitions. Group totals can overlap only when grouping by assignee; they are non-additive. The initial response exposes `backlogPreview` and `unscheduledPreview` (at most 20 rows each) with independent tray cursors. For `pageScope=UNSCHEDULED`, the request must use CALENDAR or TIMELINE, include a dateWindow, and set `includeUnscheduled=true`; for `pageScope=BACKLOG`, it must explicitly set `includeBacklog=false`. A tray continuation uses `pageScope=BACKLOG` or `UNSCHEDULED`; a Board group continuation uses `pageScope=GROUP` and `groupKey`. All pages carry the same query snapshot.

## 10. Saved views and URL draft state

Saved views persist `querySpec` and `viewType` as separate fields. Create and update requests can set `viewType` independently; changing the saved projection never rewrites the query AST. Filter, sort and grouping edits made while viewing a saved shared view remain transient URL draft state. They do not call PATCH automatically. The UI indicates the modified draft and permits reset, save as personal, or an authorized explicit update of the shared view. Calendar month navigation and Timeline horizontal date/zoom navigation are presentation state and do not mutate a shared saved view.

## 11. Performance and implementation notes

The endpoint remains a read-only POST and does not require `X-Mutation-Id`. The task-query limit is 200 for List, Calendar and Timeline; Board uses 50 per group. The fixed 900-second snapshot TTL, replayable cursor semantics and current authorization checks are finalized by CR-15. The client may normalize/cache results in TanStack Query and switch projections in memory when the needed canonical query snapshot is already present. The previous planning note's sub-100ms view-switch target is an optimization aspiration, not a server-side SLA or measured guarantee.

Backend implementation must use typed query builders/parameterized SQL and an allowlisted field/operator registry. Never interpolate AST field names or custom-field paths into SQL. Query planning and indexes for each typed field remain backend implementation work.

## 12. Error contract and gates

| Status | Error code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 409 | `QUERY_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED` | Snapshot expired; restart from the first page |
| 409 | `QUERY_CURSOR_INVALID` | Cursor is invalid, tampered, or bound to another scope/query |
| 422 | `FILTER_FIELD_INVALID` | Unknown, archived, feature-gated or out-of-scope field/custom field |
| 422 | `FILTER_OPERATOR_UNSUPPORTED` | Operator/value is not valid for the resolved field type |
| 422 | `DATE_WINDOW_REQUIRED` | Calendar/Timeline request omitted required date window |
| 422 | `DATE_WINDOW_INVALID` | Invalid ordering, date field/projection combination or range length |

CR-04 is specified in the draft. Required before contract freeze: frontend/backend/security review, backend tests for type-checked AST execution, tenant/workspace permission enforcement, snapshot/cursor isolation, group/tray page continuation, timezone/DST behavior, custom-field filter/sort, Board group totals, Timeline dependency redaction, and client invalidation on realtime sequence advances. Snapshot TTL remains CR-15.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
## CR-16 — Reliability, operations and disaster recovery

CR-16 is specified in `reliability-operations-policy.md` and OpenAPI `x-reliability-operations-policy`. The provisional targets retained from DEC-OPEN-04 are **99.5% monthly availability**, **database RPO under 5 minutes** and **RTO under 60 minutes**. These remain provisional stakeholder targets, not an SLA, production guarantee or measured attainment. At 99.5%, the planning error budget is approximately 3 hours 36 minutes in a 30-day month. The measurement recommendation is a 60-second synthetic readiness probe from two independent regions, with regional results retained.

### Topology and environments

The recommended initial topology for the 70–90 user community is a static Vite/React SPA/PWA on an edge CDN, one always-on containerized modular-monolith backend serving REST/WSS, an in-process or same-image transactional outbox worker, managed PostgreSQL 16/17 with RLS and continuous WAL PITR, and centralized redacted logs/metrics/alerts. Kubernetes, Kafka, a microservice mesh and self-managed database clusters are explicitly not recommended for the initial deployment. Additional replicas, brokers or regions require measured load and an approved operations change. Provider and budget are not selected.

Development, staging and production are isolated. Staging uses separate database/secrets and sandbox email. Production credentials/data are separate; app runtime and migration credentials are distinct. Secrets are injected through the selected secret manager, never committed. Migrations use expand-and-contract and preserve N-1 application compatibility.

### Health probes and monitoring

`GET /health/live` is a minimal unauthenticated liveness probe that only confirms process/event-loop responsiveness. `GET /health/ready` performs `SELECT 1` with a 2-second timeout and checks an outbox worker heartbeat younger than 30 seconds; it returns generic 503 plus `Retry-After` when dependencies fail. Health responses are no-store and reveal no dependency/tenant internals.

Structured JSON logging records timestamp, level, correlation ID, user/community/workspace scope, operation, status, duration and error code. Cookies, Authorization, CSRF values, credentials, tokens, task content, comment bodies, custom-field values and free-text break-glass justifications are redacted. Five draft alerts cover readiness failures, 5xx spikes, outbox lag, security/audit integrity events and backup/RPO risk.

### Backup, recovery and incident response

The primary recovery path is managed PostgreSQL continuous WAL archiving/PITR, supplemented by daily encrypted custom-format logical dumps in an isolated backup boundary. A 30-day backup retention is a recommended default only pending provider/cost/security review; it is distinct from the unresolved CR-14 audit retention. The clean-room restore drill must run before M1.3 and monthly thereafter, verify schema/FKs/RLS, CR-14 audit-chain integrity, outbox/idempotency invariants and CHK-01–CHK-06 smoke checks, and record measured RPO/RTO. The drill must never write to production.

SEV-1 covers tenant isolation breaches, total outage, account/session compromise, destructive data corruption or audit-chain failure; SEV-2 covers partial feature/service degradation. Runbooks require evidence preservation, session revocation where relevant, safe rollback/maintenance mode, isolated PITR restore, approved cutover and a blameless post-incident review.

### CI, deployment and release gate

Five CI gates cover contract lint/type generation, static and supply-chain checks, backend tests against ephemeral PostgreSQL, frontend MSW/Playwright/accessibility tests, and production build/bundle checks. Immutable artifacts are promoted through environments. Rollback uses prior frontend/backend artifacts only when N-1 schema compatibility is preserved; destructive automatic database downgrades are prohibited. M1.3 cannot be signed off until the provider is selected, health/alerts are verified, backups/PITR are evidenced, the clean-room restore drill meets provisional targets, migrations/rollback are rehearsed and Product/Backend/Frontend/Security/Ops approval is recorded.

File/object-storage recovery is excluded from CR-16 because file uploads/attachments were removed from the current product scope. Reintroducing files requires a scope change and a separate backup/recovery design.

## Validation evidence and limitations

`validate_cr16.py` executed **250 checks, 0 failures**. It includes the 160 checks previously used by `validate_cr15.py` (including inherited CR-01 break-glass and CR-14 audit controls) plus 90 CR-16 checks. It covers OpenAPI inventory/operation IDs/local references/schema meta-validation; provisional target classification; topology/environment/secret/migration rules; health routes and responses; structured logging/redaction; alert thresholds; PITR/backup/restore requirements; CI/rollback/incident response; written policy/register alignment and representative health schemas.

**This run does not claim a rerun of CR-02 through CR-13 validators**; those milestones have their own previously reported contract checks. The 250 count must not be presented as a full 16-milestone regression suite.
~~~~
