Complete Master Product Requirements Document (PRD)A. Product Vision, Problem Statement, Target Users, Personas, JTBD & PrinciplesProduct Vision: Empower mid-sized communities (70–90 members today, scaling to multiple independent communities tomorrow) to coordinate complex projects, events, engineering sprints, and personal tasks in a workspace platform that requires zero training to start and offers deep governance when needed.Problem Statement: Existing tools force communities into a broken trade-off: lightweight boards (Trello, basic checklists) collapse once projects require permanent task keys, cross-project dependencies, timeline planning, or role-based governance; meanwhile, enterprise platforms (Jira Cloud, ClickUp) bury everyday contributors under mandatory workflow schemes, custom query languages (JQL), and fragmented permission matrices.Target Users & Core Personas:Ordinary Community Member ("Sarthak" — Student Developer / Committee Volunteer): Belongs to 1 Personal Workspace and 2–3 Shared Workspaces. Job-to-be-Done (JTBD): "When I sign in between classes or meetings, help me see every task assigned to me across all projects, update my progress in two clicks or from my phone, and draft personal tasks privately without worrying about breaking a shared team board."Community Coordinator ("Reetabrata" — Operations & Tech Lead): Included by default in new Shared Workspaces to help structure work across committees. JTBD: "When organizing a 40-task event or release, let me rapidly batch-create tasks, link cross-project blockers, inspect deadlines on a Calendar or Timeline, and curate pinned Shared Views for the team."Workspace Owner ("Ananya" — Club President / Project Owner): Owns and governs a Shared Workspace (often alongside Co-Owners). JTBD: "When setting up a workspace, let me pick a starter template, configure custom project prefixes (FEST), decide which Coordinators or custom roles have edit rights, preview the workspace as a Member to verify permissions, and recover anything accidentally archived."Community Administrator ("Vikram" — Community Steward): Manages community-wide membership, security policies, and shared workspace creation rules. JTBD: "When governing a 90-person community, let me control who can provision Shared Workspaces, maintain the default Coordinators pool, audit security events, and perform an audited Break-Glass ownership recovery if a Shared Workspace owner leaves—without invading members' private Personal Workspaces."Five Binding Product Principles:Progressive Disclosure Over Upfront Configuration: Everyday actions show 5 or fewer inputs; custom fields, dependencies, and role matrices stay tucked in secondary drawers or categorized settings.One Canonical Task Model Across Four Views: List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline are synchronized projections of the exact same task data and filter state.Safe Exploration ("Draft Local, Commit Explicit, Undo Anything"): Filtering a Shared View isolates changes to the user's URL until explicitly saved; archiving or moving items offers an immediate 10-second Undo toast (Z) and a 30-day Trash safety net.Recognition Over Recall: Faceted filter pills and an instant Cmd/Ctrl + K Omnibar replace text query syntax; every status and priority pairs semantic color with a distinct geometric icon shape.Authoritative Backend Security with Transparent UI Explanations: The backend enforces all tenant and field permissions; the frontend explains locked controls with plain-language tooltips ("Only Owners and Coordinators can...") rather than silent failures.B. Goals, Measurable Success Criteria, Non-Goals & Scope BoundariesMeasurable Product Hypotheses & Engineering Targets (Labeled as [RECOMMENDED DEFAULT — Target Requiring Approval] unless backed by an external standard):First-Task Time-to-Value (TTV): Median elapsed time from first login to completing the starter task and updating an assigned task is <= 3 minutes during unassisted pilot testing (Provisional Product Target).Task Creation & Mutation Reliability: >= 95% of opened task composers result in a saved task; >= 99.9% of online mutations succeed without unhandled errors (Provisional Product Target).Zero Shared-View Contamination: 0 unintentional overwrites of Shared View configurations during pilot operation, enforced structurally by Copy-on-Write URL drafts (Confirmed Architectural Invariant).Usability & Accessibility: Post-pilot System Usability Scale (SUS) mean score >= 75; 0 critical or serious automated axe-core violations paired with 100% pass rate on manual keyboard-only and screen-reader walks across core flows (External Standard: W3C WCAG 2.2 Level AA).Interaction & Query Responsiveness: Field Interaction to Next Paint (INP) <= 200 ms at p75 (External Standard: Core Web Vitals), local optimistic UI state reflection < 50 ms on desktop (Provisional Target), and backend task-query API latency < 400 ms at p95 for projects up to 1,000 tasks (Provisional Target).Explicit Non-Goals & Deliberate Exclusions (6. REJECTED / OUT OF SCOPE):No custom text query language (JQL).No blocking modal workflow transition screens or custom post-function scripts (FEAT-D02).No stopwatch timers or billable worklogs (FEAT-A09).No enterprise PMO what-if scenario sandboxes (FEAT-B05) or drag-and-drop chart gadget builders (FEAT-E03).No ITIL helpdesk queues, SLA breach clocks, on-call rotations, or hardware CMDB asset registers (FEAT-I02).No live CDP attachment or bundle reverse-engineering against hosted third-party SaaS platforms.C. Role & Capability Model, Community/Workspace Boundaries & DelegationThree-Tier Identity & Tenancy Spine (SOT-01, THR-03):Global User (User): Single human identity authenticated via Email/Password or Google OAuth 2.0 (OIDC with PKCE).Community Tenant (Community & CommunityMembership): Independent organizational boundary. Designates isCommunityAdmin (scoped strictly to that communityId) and isDefaultCoordinator. (Platform-level infrastructure maintenance is performed by a separate operational role, Platform Operator, which has zero application-UI silent read access to community workspaces).Workspace (Workspace & WorkspaceMembership): Belongs to exactly one Community.PERSONAL Workspace: Any authenticated community member can create a Personal Workspace. Single owner (ownerId == userId), never accepts additional members or Coordinators. Under DEC-OPEN-01 (PRIVATE_STRICT Recommended Default), task contents and files are strictly private from Community Administrators (who can view only aggregate storage quota and task count metadata).SHARED Workspace: Creation is governed by community policy (canCreateSharedWorkspace). Supports multiple Workspace Owners, Coordinators (auto-included from the Community Default Coordinators pool upon workspace creation via a pre-checked removable list, and removable at any time by a Workspace Owner), Members, Read-Only Viewers, and Custom Roles.Ownership Invariant & Recovery: Every SHARED workspace must maintain at least 1 active Workspace Owner. The system blocks the last Owner from leaving or demoting themselves until another member is promoted to Owner. If a Shared Workspace's owners become inactive, a Community Administrator can invoke Audited Break-Glass Override (POST .../break-glass with a mandatory >= 15 char reason), which logs an immutable ADMIN_BREAK_GLASS audit event, notifies existing owners, and assigns a recovery Owner.Grant Ceiling & Permission Delegation (THR-05): No user may grant a role, invite a member to a role, or configure a custom role containing any capability that the acting user does not personally possess (granted_caps ⊆ actor_caps). Workspace Owners can toggle coordinatorCanInviteMembers (default true, restricted to inviting MEMBER or VIEWER roles).Effective Task Permissions (DEC-OPEN-02, DEF-07):Task Creator (createdByUserId) and Task Assigner (assignedByUserId on task_assignees) are recorded distinctly from the Task Assignee (userId on task_assignees).Under the CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT Recommended Default, Workspace Owners, Coordinators, the Task Creator, and the Task Assigner hold full edit rights (canEditTitleDescription: true, canEditDatesPriority: true, canEditCustomFieldsLinks: true). Task Assignees hold execution rights (canUpdateStatus: true, canManageSubtasks: true, canComment: true), with a Workspace Owner toggle (assigneeCanEditDatesPriority: boolean, default false) to allow Assignees to adjust due dates and priority. Ordinary Members can create tasks, comment, watch, and filter views, or gain full collaborative edit rights if the Workspace Owner flips taskEditPolicy to COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER.D. Information Architecture, Navigation, Hierarchy, Keys, Aliases & Cross-Workspace TransfersPersistent Application Shell:Left Navigation Rail (240px desktop, collapsible with [): Divided into Zone 1: Global Triage (Omnibar Cmd/Ctrl+K, + Quick Create (C), My Work, Inbox), Zone 2: Active Workspace (Workspace Switcher Pill with Personal vs. Shared badge, Saved Views, Workspace Files Hub, and Projects accordion with Lists), and Zone 3: Footer (Trash & Recovery, Workspace Settings, Community Admin Console [Admins only], and User Profile & Preferences).Main View Canvas + Right Task Peek Drawer (540px desktop / Draggable Bottom Sheet on <768px mobile): Clicking any task row, board card, calendar chip, or timeline bar opens the task in the synchronized right Peek Drawer (URL: .../t/FEST-14) without losing visual context or scroll position in the active view. Pressing Cmd/Ctrl + Enter expands the drawer to a full page.Work Hierarchy & Subtask Depth (SOT-05):Community → Workspace → Project → List (optional 1-level grouping) → Task (depth 0) → Subtask (depth 1..maxSubtaskDepth).project.maxSubtaskDepth defaults to 1 and can be set to 2 by a Workspace Owner/Coordinator in Project Settings. Converting a task to a subtask validates that the resulting subtree depth does not exceed maxSubtaskDepth.Task Keys, Prefix Renames, Cross-Project & Cross-Workspace Moves (SOT-06, DEF-06):Every task has an immutable RFC 9562 UUIDv7 (id) and a project-sequenced human-readable key (currentKey, e.g., FEST-14).Moving a task across projects (OPS-12 → FEST-45) or changing a project prefix (MKT → GRW) atomically assigns the new key and records the old key in task_key_aliases. Navigating to /t/OPS-12 or searching OPS-12 resolves to FEST-45 with a Redirected from OPS-12 badge.Personal-to-Shared Workspace Transfer-Preview & Confirmation Requirement: When a user moves a task from a PERSONAL workspace (ME-04) to a SHARED workspace (FEST), the UI must display a blocking Transfer-Preview & Confirmation Dialog before executing POST .../tasks/{id}/move with targetWorkspaceId:Displays destination workspace name and current member count ("This task, its 2 subtasks, 3 comments, and 1 attachment (4.2 MB) will become visible to all 18 members of 'Annual Tech Fest'").Previews the key change (ME-04 → FEST-next) and lists any personal custom field values that do not exist in the destination project (which are preserved as a formatted snapshot in the task's activity changelog).Requires explicit click on [Confirm & Move to Shared Workspace].E. Functional Requirements Summary by Feature Family (FEAT-A01 – FEAT-L01)All selected capabilities are mapped with full engineering traceability in Section 5. Key functional invariants include:Work-Item Archetypes (FEAT-A01): Every task has an itemType (TASK [default], DELIVERABLE, BUG, DECISION) rendered with a distinct SVG icon next to its key.Core Metadata & Fractional Ordering (FEAT-A03, FEAT-A08): Tasks support Status, Priority (URGENT, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, NONE), startDate, dueDate (YYYY-MM-DD), estimatePoints, labels[], milestoneId, and lexicographical rankKey ordering.Dependencies (FEAT-A06): Tasks support directed BLOCKS / IS_BLOCKED_BY, RELATES_TO, and DUPLICATES links within and across projects. BLOCKS links reject cycles via server-side BFS DAG validation (422 DEPENDENCY_CYCLE_DETECTED). Cross-project links to unauthorized projects mask target details (isAccessible: false, targetKey: null, targetTitle: null) (DEF-11).F. Functional Requirements for All Four Synchronized Task Views (FEAT-C01, FEAT-C02)All four views are mandatory for Initial Production Release sign-off (M1.3), consume POST .../tasks/query with the shared ViewQuerySpec AST, enforce effectivePermissions, and reconcile real-time WorkspaceStreamEvent deltas in place:List View (M1.1): Compact 36px height rows (44px on touch) organized as an accessible role="treegrid". Supports inline single-click property pill popovers (Status, Priority, Assignee, Due Date, Labels), inline ▸ subtask expansion, + Add task rapid bottom-row entry (Enter saves and opens next row), and multi-select checkboxes (M1.2 floating Bulk Action Bar).Board / Kanban View (M1.1): Columns map to project WorkflowStatus records (with a 1-click collapsible Backlog tray for BACKLOG-category statuses). Cards display Key, Title, Status icon, Priority icon, Due Date badge, Subtask progress ([✓ 2/4]), and Assignee avatar (configurable via M1.2 Card Property toggles and horizontal Swimlanes). Includes both @dnd-kit pointer drag-and-drop and single-click Move to Column / Position menu + keyboard reorder mode (Space + Arrow keys) per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7. On mobile (<768px), renders as a Single-Column Stage Switcher with horizontal status tabs.Calendar View (M1.2): Plots tasks by dueDate (or startDate..dueDate spans) across Month, Week, and 4-Day Agenda layouts. Includes a persistent, collapsible right-hand Unscheduled Tasks Tray displaying the count and list of undated tasks matching active filters so undated work is never silently hidden. Users can schedule undated tasks either by dragging onto a date cell or clicking [Set Date] on the task chip.Timeline / Gantt View (M1.2): Split-pane layout pairing a synchronized left hierarchical task table (Task Key, Title, Start Date, Due Date, Blocked By) with a right horizontal time-axis canvas (Day / Week / Month / Quarter zoom). Plots task duration bars, diamond Milestone markers (FEAT-B04), and SVG Bezier connector arrows for BLOCKS links. Whenever an upstream blocking task's dueDate is later than a downstream blocked task's startDate (and upstream status category is not DONE or CANCELED), the connector line and bar badge highlight in Danger Red (! Date Conflict). All date and dependency edits can be performed via keyboard in the left table without dragging canvas bars.G. Search, My Work, Saved Views, Collaboration, Notifications, Files & Bulk OperationsOmnibar (Cmd/Ctrl + K) & Permission-Aware Search (FEAT-C05): Instant search across task keys (FEST-14), historical aliases (OLD-09), task titles, projects, and views, strictly intersected with the caller's active workspace memberships.Personal Cross-Workspace Dashboard ("My Work" — FEAT-C03): Pinned top-left navigation view aggregating all tasks assigned to, created by, or watched by the user across their Personal Workspace and all joined Shared Workspaces, grouped into Overdue, Due Today, Upcoming, and Unscheduled.Personal vs. Copy-on-Write Shared Saved Views (FEAT-C04): Any member can save Personal Views. Modifying filters, grouping, or sorting on a Shared View updates only the browser URL query state and displays Modified • [Reset] [Save as Personal View] (plus [Update Shared View] for Owners/Coordinators).Comments, @Mentions & Watchers (FEAT-A04): Threaded Markdown comments (sanitized to AST on render) with @user and #TASK-KEY autocomplete. Task Creator, Assignees, and @mentioned users are auto-subscribed as Watchers; any member can toggle the Watch bell in 1 click.Segmented Notification Inbox & Reminders (FEAT-F01a): In-app Inbox split into Action Required (Mentions, New Assignments, Sign-Off Requests, 24h Due Reminders) and Updates (Status changes & comments on watched tasks).Attachments & Workspace File Hub (FEAT-A05a/b, DEF-08): Two-phase pre-signed upload (POST .../upload-url with atomic reserved_bytes lock → S3 PUT → POST .../complete). Downloads request a 60-second JIT pre-signed GET URL on click (GET .../download-url), served from a dedicated cookieless file domain with Content-Disposition: attachment for non-raster types. M1.3 exposes the workspace-wide File Hub browser over the same workspace_files table.Task Activity History (FEAT-A05a) vs. Bulk Operations (FEAT-A10b): Task Drawer includes a 3-way activity filter (All | Comments Only | History Log). Checking 2+ tasks in List/Board opens the floating Bulk Action Bar supporting atomic all-or-nothing updates (up to 100 tasks) with 1-click batch Undo.H. Workspace Settings, Custom Fields, Workflows, Roles, Audit Logs & Trash9 Categorized Workspace Settings Modules: 1. General, 2. Members & Invitations (with Default Coordinator toggle), 3. Roles & Permissions (with Custom Role Builder & Role Preview Simulator), 4. Projects, Hierarchy & Task Keys, 5. Custom Fields & Workflows (5-Category Status Mapper), 6. Views & Saved Layouts, 7. Notifications & Reminders, 8. Templates, 9. Files, Audit History & Recovery.5-Category Canonical Workflow Spine (FEAT-D01): Every project status maps to BACKLOG, TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, or CANCELED. Deleting a status that holds tasks requires selecting a migration fallback status in the same request.30-Day Trash & 10-Second Undo (FEAT-A10a/b): Archiving a task, list, or project triggers a 10-second Undo toast (Z) and soft-deletes the batch (archiveBatchId) to Trash & Recovery for 30 days before automated hard-purge.Append-Only, Tamper-Evident Security Audit Log (FEAT-G04, THR-10, DEF-12): Records role changes, member removals, prefix changes, CSV exports, and Admin Break-Glass actions. The application DB role has SELECT, INSERT privileges only (no UPDATE/DELETE), entries are linked via a per-community SHA-256 hash chain (prev_hash → entry_hash), and user identities are stored by UUID reference rather than raw email strings so account deletion anonymizes cleanly.I. UX, Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) & Responsive/Mobile RequirementsSix Mandatory Component States: Every view and data component must implement: (1) Geometry-Matched Loading Skeleton, (2) Zero-Data Empty State with CTA, (3) Zero-Filter-Match Empty State with [Clear Filters], (4) Populated State, (5) Permission-Locked State with explanatory tooltip, and (6) Network/Sync/Conflict Error State.Keyboard & Non-Dragging Parity (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1, 2.1.4, 2.5.7): Roving tabindex (1 Tab stop per grid/board group, Arrow navigation inside); single-key shortcuts (C, /, Z) suppressed inside text inputs and toggleable in user preferences; every drag-and-drop interaction on Board, List, Calendar, and Timeline paired with a single-click menu or keyboard date/rank input.Target Size & Focus Visibility (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11, 2.4.13, 2.5.8): Desktop interactive controls >= 24×24 CSS px; mobile/coarse-pointer controls >= 44×44 CSS px; 2px high-contrast focus ring (>= 3:1); sticky headers, bottom navigation bars, and Undo toasts never obscure focused elements.Combined Automated + Manual Accessibility Verification (DEF-17): Passing @axe-core/playwright is necessary but not sufficient for WCAG 2.2 AA sign-off. Each milestone gate requires a structured manual verification protocol covering keyboard-only completion, logical focus restoration on Drawer/Modal close, 200% browser zoom reflow at 1280px width without horizontal scrolling of task lists, and screen-reader announcements (aria-live="polite") for status updates and filter counts.J. Non-Functional Requirements (Security, Performance, Availability & Recovery)Security & Privacy: Argon2id password hashing (m=64MiB, t=3, p=4), OAuth 2.0 PKCE (S256) + state, __Host-session cookies + X-CSRF-Token + Origin validation, AST Markdown sanitization + strict CSP (script-src 'self'), and composite (community_id, workspace_id) query binding backed by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS).Performance Targets (DEF-16):Field Core Web Vitals INP (3. EXTERNAL TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT): p75 INP <= 200 ms across all views ([https://web.dev/articles/inp](https://web.dev/articles/inp)).Local Optimistic UI Reflection (2. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT): < 50 ms synchronous store update on desktop reference hardware.Backend Query Latency (2. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT): < 400 ms at p95 for POST .../tasks/query on workspaces with up to 1,000 tasks; < 100 ms at p95 for Omnibar exact task-key lookup.Availability, RPO & RTO (4. UNRESOLVED STAKEHOLDER DECISION — DEC-OPEN-04):Recommended Provisional Targets: 99.5% monthly uptime SLO, RPO < 5 minutes (via managed PostgreSQL continuous WAL archiving / PITR + daily encrypted logical dumps), and RTO < 60 minutes verified via clean-room restore drills.K. Observable Feature Acceptance Criteria SummaryEvery feature in the roadmap is verified against observable behavioral criteria (detailed per FEAT-ID in Section 5 and per vertical slice in Section 7):Task Creation & Keys (FEAT-A02, FEAT-C07): Submitting a title in the inline composer renders the new row optimistically, assigns a unique sequential PREFIX-NUM key under 20-way concurrency with 0 collisions, and resolves historical aliases via /tasks/by-key/{alias} with matchedAlias populated.Four Views & Filter Parity (FEAT-C01, FEAT-C02, FEAT-C04): Given a project with 25 scheduled tasks, 5 unscheduled tasks, and 2 blocking links (1 with upstream.dueDate > downstream.startDate), switching across List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline with filter Priority IN [HIGH, URGENT] returns the exact same set of matching task IDs, displays the unscheduled subset in the Calendar/Timeline Unscheduled Tray, highlights the conflicting blocker in red on Timeline, and isolates local filter edits to the URL without mutating the Shared View record in PostgreSQL.L. Release-Blocking ConditionsThe Initial Production Release (M1.3) must not be signed off if any of the following conditions exist:Any of the four task views (List, Board, Calendar, Timeline) is incomplete or fails cross-view filter parity (CHK-11).Any cross-community or cross-workspace BOLA/IDOR test fails (CHK-03, SEC-T02..T06), or a removed member continues receiving WebSocket frames for more than 1 second after removal.Any critical or serious axe-core violation exists, or core task flows cannot be completed using only the keyboard without pointer dragging (CHK-12).Clean-room PostgreSQL backup restoration (CHK-14) or audit_logs SQL immutability (SEC-T10) has not been executed with recorded pass evidence in the staging environment.4. Canonical System Architecture and Domain Model4.1 Reconciled Multi-Consumer Outbox & Cross-Instance Realtime ArchitectureTo resolve the two infrastructure defects identified in Prompt 08's audit (DEF-14 single processed_at column and multi-instance WebSocket revocation), the backend Modular Monolith enforces the following persistence and event guarantees:Code snippetflowchart TB
    subgraph Tx["1. Synchronous ACID Transaction (PostgreSQL 16+)"]
        CMD["Domain Command\n(e.g., PATCH /tasks or DELETE /members)"] --> LOCK["Verify SecurityContext + RLS\nUpdate Domain Row + Increment field_revisions"]
        LOCK --> SEQ["Increment workspace.last_event_seq\n(or user.last_notification_seq)"]
        SEQ --> OUT["INSERT INTO domain_events\n(Immutable Event Row)"]
        OUT --> IDEM["INSERT INTO idempotency_records\n(30-Day TTL)"]
    end

    subgraph Consumers["2. Independent Outbox Consumer Groups (outbox_consumer_offsets)"]
        OUT --> C_WS["Consumer Group 1: REALTIME_RELAY (M13)\nTracks last_processed_seq per workspace"]
        OUT --> C_NTF["Consumer Group 2: NOTIFICATIONS (M10)\nGenerates Inbox rows & Email jobs"]
        OUT --> C_AUT["Consumer Group 3: AUTOMATIONS_WEBHOOKS (M15 - Ph3)\nEnforces hop_count <= 1 loop guard"]
    end

    subgraph Bus["3. Cross-Instance PubSub & Socket Revocation Bus"]
        C_WS --> PUB["PubSubBroker Interface\n(Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY in Single-Node MVP;\nRedis Pub/Sub in Multi-Node Scale)"]
        PUB --> INST1["Backend Instance 1\n(WS Room Manager & Kick Handler)"]
        PUB --> INST2["Backend Instance N\n(WS Room Manager & Kick Handler)"]
    end
Independent Outbox Consumer Tracking (DEF-14 Fix): domain_events is an immutable log table with no single processed_at boolean. Instead, each asynchronous subsystem (REALTIME_RELAY, NOTIFICATIONS, and Phase 3 AUTOMATIONS_WEBHOOKS) maintains its own high-water mark in outbox_consumer_offsets (consumer_group PK, shard_key, last_event_id, updated_at) and records any per-event delivery exceptions in outbox_consumer_failures (consumer_group, event_id, attempt_count, next_retry_at, last_error). A slow email provider in NOTIFICATIONS can never delay REALTIME_RELAY WebSocket broadcasts.Cross-Instance WebSocket Revocation (PubSubBroker Contract): WebSocket room subscriptions and WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED kicks are never limited to a process-local memory map. When removeWorkspaceMember or logoutSession commits, the outbox relay publishes a high-priority control message (KICK_USER_WORKSPACE { userId, workspaceId } or KICK_USER_SESSIONS { userId }) over the PubSubBroker (PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY channel ws_control in single-DB deployments, or Redis Pub/Sub when horizontally scaled), ensuring every backend container instance immediately terminates that user's room subscription within 500ms.4.2 Reconciled Entity Ownership, Scope & Lifecycle SpecificationEntityPrimary Key (RFC 9562)Tenant & Workspace ScopeAuthoritative Ownership & Key InvariantsUser & AuthIdentityid: UUIDv7Global Instance Scope (Zero community_id column).Owned by M01. Supports multiple AuthIdentity rows (EMAIL_PASSWORD, GOOGLE_OIDC); blocks unlinking the last remaining auth method (409).Community & CommunityMembershipid: UUIDv7Root Tenant Scope (community_id).Owned by M02. CommunityMembership holds is_community_admin (scoped strictly to community_id) and is_default_coordinator.Workspace & WorkspaceMembershipid: UUIDv7Scoped to community_id.Owned by M03. Tracks used_bytes, reserved_bytes (DEF-08), quota_bytes, last_event_seq, and settings_jsonb. Enforces >= 1 active OWNER on SHARED workspaces.Roleid: UUIDv7System (workspace_id IS NULL) or Workspace-scoped.Owned by M04. Stores capabilities: TEXT[]. Enforces Grant Ceiling (granted_caps ⊆ actor_caps).Project, List & ProjectMilestoneid: UUIDv7Composite (community_id, workspace_id).Owned by M05. Project holds key_prefix, atomic next_task_seq, and max_subtask_depth (1|2). ProjectMilestone is the sole Milestone representation (SOT-07).Task & TaskAssigneeid: UUIDv7Composite (community_id, workspace_id, project_id).Owned by M06. Self-referencing parent_task_id (hierarchy_depth: 0..2), current_key, item_type ('TASK'|'DELIVERABLE'|'BUG'|'DECISION'), rank_key, version, and field_revisions JSONB. TaskAssignee stores (task_id, user_id, assigned_by_user_id) (DEF-07).TaskKeyAlias(workspace_id, alias_key)Scoped to workspace_id.Owned by M05. Maps historical keys (OLD-09) and cross-workspace tombstones (ME-04) to task_id. Never reuses sequence numbers after purge.TaskLinkid: UUIDv7Scoped to community_id.Owned by M06. Links tasks across projects within a community (BLOCKS, IS_BLOCKED_BY, RELATES_TO, DUPLICATES). Enforces cycle-free DAG on BLOCKS.WorkflowStatus & CustomFieldDefid: UUIDv7Scoped to workspace_id / project_id.Owned by M07. Every status maps to BACKLOG, TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, or CANCELED. Reserves requires_signoff for Phase 3.SavedViewid: UUIDv7Scoped to workspace_id (& optional project_id).Owned by M08. Stores scope ('PERSONAL'|'SHARED'), view_type, query_spec_jsonb, display_opts_jsonb, and version (DEF-10).Comment & TaskWatcherid: UUIDv7Composite (community_id, workspace_id, task_id).Owned by M09. Stores sanitized Markdown body, mentioned_user_ids, and version.WorkspaceFileid: UUIDv7Composite (community_id, workspace_id).Owned by M11. Tracks status ('PENDING'|'ACTIVE'|'ARCHIVED'), size_bytes, mime_type, storage_key, and nullable task_id/comment_id. Powers both Task Attachments (M1.1) and Workspace File Hub (M1.3).DomainEvent, OutboxOffset & AuditLogid: UUIDv7DomainEvent: (community_id, workspace_id).AuditLog: community_id.Owned by M12. AuditLog is append-only (SELECT, INSERT DB grants), chained via SHA-256 prev_hash -> entry_hash, and references user UUIDs rather than cleartext emails (DEF-12).IdempotencyRecord(scope_key, mutation_id)user:{userId} or anon:{ipHash} (DEF-02).Owned by M12. Retains mutation response snapshots for 30 days (DEF-01).5. Reconciled API, Realtime and Frontend/Backend Integration Blueprint6.1 Reconciled Contract Corrections Applied to Prompt 06 Draft (/contracts/)The Prompt 06 endpoint inventory and DTO specifications serve as the baseline, modified by these 10 mandatory reconciliations:Idempotency Scope & Exemption (DEF-01, DEF-02): X-Mutation-Id (UUIDv4) is required only on state-mutating operations (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), explicitly exempting read-only POST .../tasks/query, POST .../me/work/query, and POST .../tasks/export-csv. idempotency_records is keyed by (scope_key, mutation_id) (user:{userId} or anon:{ipHash}) with a 30-day retention TTL.Strict RFC 9562 UUIDv7 Identifiers (DEF-03): Every internal entity ID in openapi.yaml, ws-events.schema.json, seed-v1.json, and MSW mocks uses valid UUIDv7 format (0192d8f0-...).Dual Multiplexed WebSocket Streams (DEF-04): Over a single authenticated WebSocket connection (wss://<host>/api/v1/ws?ticket=<60s_single_use_ticket>), the server sends two discriminated envelope types:stream: "WORKSPACE" — ordered by workspaceSeq (TASK_CREATED, TASK_UPDATED, TASK_MOVED_OR_REORDERED, TASK_ARCHIVED, TASK_RESTORED, COMMENT_ADDED, COMMENT_UPDATED, COMMENT_DELETED, ASSIGNMENT_CHANGED, DEPENDENCY_CHANGED, FILE_ATTACHED, PROJECT_UPDATED, LIST_UPDATED, MILESTONE_UPDATED, SHARED_VIEW_UPDATED, MEMBER_ROLE_CHANGED, WORKSPACE_MEMBER_REMOVED, WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED, RESYNC_REQUIRED).stream: "USER_COMMUNITY" — ordered by userNotificationSeq across the community (NOTIFICATION_CREATED, MY_WORK_ASSIGNED, WORKSPACE_INVITE_RECEIVED).Purged Task Anti-Enumeration (DEF-05): GET .../workspaces/{wid}/tasks/by-key/{taskKey} verifies task:read membership in {wid} first. Unjoined callers always receive 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND; only authorized workspace members receive 410 TASK_PERMANENTLY_PURGED for purged keys.Cross-Workspace Move & Transfer Preview (DEF-06): POST .../workspaces/{wid}/tasks/{taskId}/move accepts { targetWorkspaceId?, targetProjectId, targetListId?, confirmedPersonalToSharedTransfer?: boolean }. If moving from a PERSONAL workspace to a SHARED workspace without confirmedPersonalToSharedTransfer: true, the endpoint returns 422 TRANSFER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with the preview summary (targetMemberCount, filesBytesToTransfer, unmappedCustomFields[]).Granular Task Effective Permissions & Assigner Tracking (DEF-07):TypeScriptexport interface TaskEffectivePermissionsDto {
  canEditTitleDescription: boolean;
  canEditDatesPriority: boolean;
  canEditCustomFieldsLinks: boolean;
  canUpdateStatus: boolean;
  canRequestSignoff: boolean;
  canApproveSignoff: boolean;
  canAssign: boolean;
  canManageSubtasks: boolean;
  canMoveProject: boolean;
  canArchive: boolean;
  canDeletePermanent: boolean;
  restrictedReasonCode: string | null;
}
TaskDetailDto.assignees includes { id, displayName, avatarUrl, assignedByUserId, assignedAt }.Atomic File Quota Reservation & 60-Second JIT Download URLs (DEF-08): POST .../files/upload-url atomically reserves sizeBytes in workspaces.reserved_bytes (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE). GET .../files/{fileId}/download-url is called only on user click, re-verifies live task:read access, and returns a 60-second TTL pre-signed GET URL on files.<domain> with Content-Disposition: attachment for non-raster files.Complete Route Coverage (DEF-09): Includes POST /auth/ws-ticket, POST .../tasks/bulk/undo, POST .../trash/{entityType}/{entityId}/restore, and full GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE operations for forms, automations, webhooks, and cycles.Standardized Sequence & Version Headers (DEF-10): Workspace mutations return X-Workspace-Seq: <int> in response headers, and SavedViewDto, CommentDto, and WorkflowStatusDto carry an integer version field.Restricted Cross-Project Link Masking (DEF-11): TaskLinkSummaryDto sets isAccessible: false and nulls targetKey, targetTitle, and targetStatusCategory when the viewer lacks read access to the linked task's project.6.2 Definitive Frontend / Backend Integration Ownership MatrixIntegration SurfaceAntigravity CLI (Frontend Developer) OwnsBackend Developer OwnsContract Change & Verification Gate1. Contract & Type PipelineRuns npm run contracts:generate (openapi-typescript + zod) to generate src/contracts/api-types.gen.ts. Zero handwritten DTOs or un-typed fetch calls.Authors/maintains /contracts/openapi.yaml & ws-events.schema.json jointly; validates all controller inputs/outputs against the contract in CI.Additive changes: PR + regenerate types/mocks.Breaking changes: Prohibited without joint ADR + simultaneous dual-PR update (CHK-01).2. Auth, CSRF & Logout HygieneRenders Auth/OAuth flows, stores csrfToken in memory, attaches X-CSRF-Token on writes, and wipes IndexedDB (deleteDatabase) on POST /auth/logout.Issues __Host-session cookie, verifies OIDC PKCE + state, enforces CSRF + Origin allowlist, and revokes server sessions & sockets on logout.Verified by CHK-02, SEC-T01, and SEC-T07.3. Authorization & Role PreviewBinds disabled states and lock tooltips to effectiveCapabilities[] and the 11-field TaskEffectivePermissionsDto; attaches X-Preview-Role-Id in Preview Mode.Enforces the 6-stage PolicyEvaluator + PostgreSQL RLS on every query/mutation, computes per-field effectivePermissions, and rejects mutations under X-Preview-Role-Id (403).Verified by CHK-02, CHK-03, and SEC-T02..T05.4. Four-View Query Cache & URL StateNormalizes tasks by UUID in TanStack Query, projects List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline from the shared cache, and isolates Shared View filter edits in URL query params (Modified • [Reset]).Compiles ViewQuerySpec AST into tenant-scoped SQL, populates unscheduledTasks for Calendar/Timeline, and enforces cursor pagination (sort_val, id).Verified by CHK-11 and VAL-03.5. Optimistic Mutations, Undo & ConflictsApplies <50ms optimistic updates, attaches X-Mutation-Id and baseFieldRevisions, displays the 10-second Undo toast (Z), and renders the 3-way 409 Conflict Resolver Drawer.Deduplicates X-Mutation-Id (30d TTL), checks fieldRevisions per patched field, auto-merges non-overlapping fields, returns 409 conflictingFields[], and runs all-or-nothing /tasks/bulk.Verified by CHK-04, CHK-05, and CHK-07.6. Realtime Streams & Gap RecoverySubscribes via single-use wsTicket, tracks lastSeenWorkspaceSeq and lastSeenUserSeq, deduplicates own mutationId, fetches /events?sinceSeq= on gaps, and handles WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED.Publishes DomainEvent rows via independent REALTIME_RELAY offset, broadcasts across instances via PubSubBroker, kicks revoked users in <1s, and serves the 500-event delta buffer (410 fallback).Verified by CHK-08 and SEC-T06.7. UNRESOLVED STAKEHOLDER DECISION)The Product Owner must review and sign off on these 5 explicit policy decisions (checking either the Recommended Default or the Alternative):Markdown### STAKEHOLDER SIGN-OFF CHECKLIST (REQUIRED FOR FINAL POLICY LOCK)

1. [DEC-OPEN-01] PERSONAL WORKSPACE PRIVACY VS. ADMIN INSPECTION (Blocks M1.3 Admin Console, Not M1.1 Contract Freeze)
   - ( ) APPROVE RECOMMENDED DEFAULT (`PRIVATE_STRICT`): Community Administrators view aggregate storage/task-count metadata only and can suspend accounts, but can NEVER read or break-glass into a user's Personal Workspace tasks. Break-Glass applies strictly to Shared Workspaces.
   - ( ) SELECT ALTERNATIVE (`AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS`): Permit Community Administrators to invoke Break-Glass on Personal Workspaces with a mandatory 15-char reason, immutable AuditLog entry, and immediate email alert to the Personal Workspace owner.

2. [DEC-OPEN-02] DEFAULT TASK-EDITING POLICY IN SHARED WORKSPACES (Blocks Default Seed Config, Not Contract Schema)
   - ( ) APPROVE RECOMMENDED DEFAULT (`CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT`): In new Shared Workspaces, Owners, Coordinators, Task Creator, and Task Assigner edit task definitions; Assignees update status, subtasks, and comments; ordinary Members create tasks and comment. (Workspace Owners can toggle `COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER` or `assigneeCanEditDatesPriority` per workspace).
   - ( ) SELECT ALTERNATIVE (`COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER` Default): Allow all Shared Workspace members to edit task definitions by default unless restricted by the Workspace Owner.

3. [DEC-OPEN-03] FILE UPLOAD LIMITS, STORAGE QUOTAS & AUDIT RETENTION (Blocks M1.2/M1.3 Quota Config)
   - ( ) APPROVE RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS: Max single file = `25 MB`; Shared Workspace quota = `5 GB`; Personal Workspace quota = `500 MB`; Searchable online Audit Log retention = `365 days` (+ CSV archival).

# CR-13 — Authentication, Session Security and Deployment Policy

**Contract:** `0.3.14-draft`  
**Status:** Engineering/security policy specified; provider provisioning, environment values, joint sign-off and runtime security verification remain open.

## 1. Purpose and authority

CR-13 completes the product's browser identity contract and defines the deployment boundary that CR-09 realtime, CR-07 invitations and CR-10 email delivery depend on. The active HTTP contract is `openapi.yaml` (`x-authentication-policy`). The browser application uses an opaque server-side session cookie. The cookie is not an access token and is never exposed to browser JavaScript.

This milestone chooses security behavior and required configuration names. It does **not** choose or configure a cloud host, DNS zone, email vendor, Google OAuth project, secret manager, or production URL. Those are explicit deployment inputs and remain subject to CR-16 operational acceptance.

## 2. Browser session transport

### 2.1 Session cookie

The only supported browser session credential is an opaque, cryptographically random server-side session secret (at least 256 bits). It is issued as:

```http
Set-Cookie: __Host-session=<opaque-random-value>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1209600
```

The cookie MUST:

- use the `__Host-` prefix, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/` and a 14-day `Max-Age`;
- omit the `Domain` attribute entirely; it is host-only;
- be sent only over HTTPS in deployed environments;
- never be copied into JSON, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, application logs, traces, analytics or URLs.

The server stores only a one-way HMAC-SHA-256 digest of the random session secret (with a versioned key identifier), never the raw bearer value. The session row contains the user, creation/last-seen timestamps, idle expiry, absolute expiry, current token digest, revocation state and non-secret device metadata.

### 2.2 Lifetime and rotation

The contract retains the previously agreed 14-day sliding inactivity window and 24-hour token rotation, and adds a 30-day absolute lifetime:

| Control | Value | Enforcement |
|---|---:|---|
| Idle timeout | 14 days | Server-side, sliding on authenticated activity |
| Absolute timeout | 30 days | Server-side, never extended by activity |
| Session secret rotation | 24 hours | Atomic; old secret invalidated when replacement is issued |
| Cookie Max-Age | 14 days | Refreshed with the sliding idle window |

The browser's cookie expiry is not the authority. The server rejects expired/revoked sessions even if a client retains a cookie. Rotation is required after login, verification completion, password reset/change, provider link/unlink and other step-up-sensitive identity changes. Password reset revokes every pre-existing session and issues one fresh session to the recovering user.

`GET /me/sessions` shows only the signed-in user's session metadata. `DELETE /me/sessions/{sessionId}` and `POST /auth/logout?all=true` revoke sessions server-side. Revocation also invalidates CSRF tokens and realtime tickets, closes authenticated WebSockets across instances, and clears the current browser cookie when applicable. Device labels are sanitized display metadata, not an authorization input. Full IP addresses and raw user-agent strings are not returned.

### 2.3 Browser token handling

The browser sends requests with credentials enabled to the configured API origin. It keeps the CSRF token in memory and sends it only in `X-CSRF-Token`. It does not read or persist the session cookie. The current HTTP contract does not define browser Bearer-token storage or an implicit JWT refresh flow; do not add either without a separate contract decision.

## 3. CSRF, Origin and CORS

### 3.1 Pre-authentication and authenticated CSRF

`GET /auth/csrf` has two modes:

1. Before login, it returns a short-lived synchronizer token and sets `__Host-auth-csrf` with `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=600` and no `Domain` attribute.
2. With an authenticated session, it returns a token bound to that session.

Tokens are 256-bit CSPRNG values. The server stores/verifies a one-way digest and binds the token to the relevant pre-auth transaction or session. Login, registration, email verification confirmation/resend, password reset request/confirmation, logout, session revocation and identity mutations require `X-CSRF-Token` and `X-Mutation-Id` as applicable.

Every cookie-authenticated state-changing request MUST also have an exact trusted `Origin`. Missing `Origin`, `Origin: null`, untrusted scheme/host/port, invalid CSRF token or absent required mutation ID is rejected before application writes. Safe GET/HEAD/OPTIONS do not mutate application state. Google callbacks are protected by the single-use OAuth state, nonce, PKCE and browser transaction cookie rather than a CSRF header.

### 3.2 Exact origin allowlist

`TRUSTED_BROWSER_ORIGINS` is an environment-specific list of exact origins (`scheme://host[:port]`). No wildcard, suffix/substring match, dynamic Origin reflection, `null` origin or untrusted `Referer` fallback is permitted. When `Origin` is absent on a protected browser mutation, reject rather than assume same-origin.

CORS uses `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only when the request Origin is an exact allowlist entry. Return that exact origin and `Vary: Origin`; never combine credentialed requests with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Preflight methods and headers are explicitly enumerated. The allowlist is different for local development, staging and production.

### 3.3 Deployment topology constraint

The production browser app and API must be same-site (same schemeful registrable site), for example `https://app.<owned-domain>` and `https://api.<owned-domain>`. The cookie remains host-only to the API host; the app does not receive a parent-domain cookie. A front-end on an unrelated registrable domain is unsupported by this cookie contract. Use a same-site reverse proxy or backend-for-frontend rather than weakening the cookie to `SameSite=None` solely to accommodate cross-site hosting.

## 4. Email/password lifecycle

### 4.1 Registration and email verification

`POST /auth/register` creates a `PENDING_VERIFICATION` account and queues a verification email. It returns a generic `202 AuthActionAcceptedDto`, not an authenticated session. No app session is issued until verification succeeds. Duplicate-address and already-registered behavior is indistinguishable from a new registration.

Email identity normalization is deterministic (trim surrounding whitespace, Unicode NFKC normalization and case-folded uniqueness key); the original display form may be retained separately. Email uniqueness is enforced at the account level. A verification token is a random 256-bit value, stored only as a digest, single-use and valid for 30 minutes. Email links place the token in the URL fragment (not the query string); the first-party verification page removes the fragment after reading it and submits the token in the HTTPS request body with pre-auth CSRF. It uses `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and no third-party scripts/assets.  Successful `POST /auth/email-verification/confirm` atomically consumes the token, marks the address verified and creates a fresh session. Resend requests use the generic `202` response and do not reveal whether an address exists or is already verified.

Community/workspace invitation acceptance continues to require the account's verified email/identity according to CR-07; CR-13 provides the account-level verification contract but does not change invitation scope or authority.

### 4.2 Login

`POST /auth/login` requires pre-auth CSRF and a mutation ID. Unknown account and incorrect password both return the same `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` body and status. Correct credentials on an unverified password account return `403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` and a verification resend path. Suspended/disabled accounts do not receive a session. Success creates a new server session, rotates any pre-authentication state, returns a session-bound CSRF token in `SessionDto` and sets `__Host-session`.

### 4.3 Password storage and policy

- Minimum 12 characters; maximum 1,024 characters. Do not trim or silently truncate passwords.
- No arbitrary uppercase/lowercase/digit/symbol composition rules. Permit passphrases and Unicode.
- Reject common/known-compromised passwords using a privacy-preserving breached-password check. Do not transmit a plaintext password to a third-party service.
- Store password verifiers with Argon2id, per-password random salt, at least 19 MiB memory, 2 iterations and parallelism 1. Benchmark on production hardware and increase cost where practical. Parameters are versioned so hashes can be upgraded after successful login.
- Passwords are never stored plaintext or reversibly encrypted. Password values, password hashes and reset tokens are excluded from logs and telemetry.

### 4.4 Password recovery

`POST /auth/password-reset/request` always returns the same generic `202` response, regardless of whether the address exists, is disabled, is federated-only or has no password method. The reset token is a random 256-bit value, stored only as a digest, single-use and valid for 15 minutes. Password-reset links place the token in the URL fragment, never the query string; the first-party page removes the fragment after reading it and submits the token in the HTTPS request body with pre-auth CSRF. It uses `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and no third-party scripts/assets. 

`POST /auth/password-reset/confirm` validates and atomically consumes the token, replaces the password verifier, revokes all prior sessions, invalidates existing CSRF/realtime credentials and issues exactly one new session to the recovering user. Invalid, expired, reused and unknown tokens return a generic failure without revealing account state. Notify the account email after successful reset; the notice contains no password or token.

## 5. Google OpenID Connect and account linking

### 5.1 Sign-in

Google authentication uses Authorization Code flow with PKCE `S256`; the server generates and retains the verifier, state and nonce. A browser transaction cookie binds the callback to the browser that initiated it. State is single-use and expires after five minutes. The callback URI is an exact, pre-registered HTTPS URI per environment; no wildcard callback or caller-supplied callback is accepted. A `__Host-oauth-state` browser-binding cookie uses `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=300` and no `Domain` attribute. The callback requires that cookie, validates state/nonce/PKCE once, then clears the cookie. Auth callback responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; edge logging redacts callback query parameters.  

Before establishing an identity, validate signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce, provider subject and `email_verified=true`. The stable identity key is `(provider, providerSubject)`, not email. The authorization code, ID token, access token and refresh token never enter frontend JavaScript, browser storage, ordinary logs or analytics.

`returnTo` is only a validated allowlisted relative path on the application origin. Absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, encoded alternate hosts and CR/LF redirect injection are rejected. The callback redirects only to the validated application path.

### 5.2 No automatic account merging

A Google identity is never attached to an existing password account merely because email strings match, even when Google's email is verified. A user must authenticate to the existing account and complete the explicit identity-link flow. If the provider subject is already linked to another account, return a generic conflict and do not reveal the other account. A newly verified Google identity may create a new account if no conflicting provider subject exists.

### 5.3 Link, unlink and step-up

`GET /me/auth-identities` returns only provider type and link timestamp for the current user. Step-up is concrete: password users call `POST /auth/reauthenticate` with the current password; Google users use `GET /auth/oauth/google/reauth/start` and its callback, which requires a fresh Google authentication and the same already-linked provider subject. Both create a five-minute server-side grant bound to the active session. Google linking then starts from the authenticated account, requires that grant, and binds the callback to the same active account and session that initiated it. Password addition/change also requires a recent step-up; when a password already exists, `currentPassword` is required.

Unlinking a provider requires CSRF, mutation ID and recent step-up. It is rejected with `409 LAST_AUTH_PROVIDER` if the account would have no verified login method remaining. The provider-subject uniqueness constraint prevents a provider identity from linking to two accounts. Successful link/unlink rotates the current session and revokes other sessions.

## 6. Session and authentication rate limits

Rate limits are enforced server-side with distributed counters so multiple API instances share one limit. Use normalized account buckets keyed by HMAC of the normalized email; never put raw emails into rate-limit keys or high-cardinality labels.

| Flow | Initial default limit |
|---|---|
| Failed login | 5 per account bucket / 15 minutes; 20 per source IP / 15 minutes |
| Registration | 5 per source IP / hour |
| Verification resend or reset request | 3 per normalized-account bucket / hour (continues to return generic 202); 10 per source IP / hour (generic 429 with `Retry-After`) |
| Google authorization start | 10 per source IP / 10 minutes |

Use progressive delay for repeated failed login without permanently locking an account (which would enable denial-of-service). For verification/reset requests, an account-bucket throttle continues to return the generic `202` so it cannot reveal whether the account exists; a source-IP throttle may return a generic `429` with `Retry-After`. Login and Google-start limits use generic rate-limit responses. These are initial contract defaults and must be load-tested/tuned by ops before production.

## 7. Deployment and secret configuration

Each environment must provide:

| Configuration key | Purpose | Secret? |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ORIGIN` | Canonical browser application origin | No |
| `API_ORIGIN` | Canonical API origin | No |
| `TRUSTED_BROWSER_ORIGINS` | Exact CORS/Origin allowlist | No |
| `GOOGLE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | Google OIDC client identifier | No |
| `GOOGLE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google OIDC client secret | Yes |
| `GOOGLE_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | Exact callback URL registered with Google | No |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | Selected outbound email adapter | No |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER_API_KEY` | Email provider credential | Yes |
| `EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` | Verified sender identity | No |
| `SESSION_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY` | Versioned HMAC key for session-token digests | Yes |
| `CSRF_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY` | Versioned HMAC key for CSRF-token digests | Yes |

Secrets live in a managed secret store/environment secret service, never source control, frontend build variables, logs, container images or developer-shared `.env` files. The canonical names are `SESSION_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY` and `CSRF_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY`; the key IDs are stored with digests to permit controlled rotation.  Dev/stage/prod use separate credentials, origins and callback URIs. Key rotation uses key identifiers and a migration window; secrets are not shared across environments.

Production deployment MUST:

1. Serve all browser/API and OAuth callback traffic over HTTPS; redirect HTTP to HTTPS at the trusted edge.
2. Enable HSTS after every covered subdomain is HTTPS-ready; preload is a separate reviewed decision.
3. Trust forwarded host/proto/client-IP headers only from known load balancers/proxies; reject unexpected host headers.
4. Configure exact Google callback URLs and authorized JavaScript origins for each environment.
5. Verify sender domain ownership and SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment before production identity email delivery.
6. Use a durable outbox/queue for verification and password-reset messages; email delivery is asynchronous and retryable, and HTTP responses do not reveal delivery/provider details.
7. Apply request-size limits, timeouts, dependency isolation, distributed auth rate limits and secret redaction at the edge and application layers.
8. Keep auth/session endpoints `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; never cache session, CSRF, identity, reset or verification responses in shared caches.
9. Fail readiness when mandatory identity config is absent or invalid; health endpoints must not disclose configuration values or secret presence details to unauthenticated callers.

`EMAIL_PROVIDER`, Google client credentials, domain records, concrete origins and cloud provider are deliberately not hard-coded in this policy. They are deployment records to be approved and tested under CR-16.

## 8. Logging, audit and realtime boundaries

Redact `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `Authorization`, passwords, session secrets, CSRF values, OAuth code/state, ID/access/refresh tokens, verification tokens and password-reset tokens at ingress, application logs, traces, exception reporting and analytics.

Record security-relevant outcomes (registration accepted, verification completed, login success/failure, password reset, identity link/unlink, session created/revoked) with user/session IDs where known, timestamp, correlation ID, outcome and coarse reason code. Do not record secret values or raw credential contents. Auth events are private security/audit records and MUST NOT be broadcast as workspace or user-community realtime events. Session revocation instead invalidates the server session and closes its active sockets/tickets through the CR-09 mechanism.

## 9. Explicit exclusions

MFA/TOTP, passkeys/WebAuthn, additional social providers, enterprise SAML/SCIM, device posture/trust, administrator-assisted account recovery and biometric authentication are outside CR-13. They require separate threat modelling, recovery semantics and API decisions; they must not be simulated as if they were already supported.

## 10. Acceptance gates

### Contract and automated tests

- All public auth mutations require pre-auth CSRF + mutation ID; all authenticated mutations require session CSRF + mutation ID.
- Missing, invalid, expired and cross-session CSRF tokens are rejected before writes.
- Exact Origin accepted; untrusted, missing and `null` Origin rejected; CORS never emits wildcard with credentials.
- Session cookie has the exact `__Host-` attributes and no Domain attribute; session secret never appears in API JSON.
- Idle and absolute expiry, daily rotation, logout, all-session logout, password reset revocation and cross-instance revocation are enforced server-side.
- Duplicate registration, reset and verification requests preserve anti-enumeration response/status shape.
- Verification/reset tokens are single-use, expire, are stored hashed and cannot be replayed concurrently.
- Unknown email and wrong password share a generic failure; unverified email cannot access protected APIs.
- OAuth state/nonce/PKCE mismatch, expiry, replay, invalid issuer/audience/signature, unverified email and unsafe returnTo are rejected.
- Email-matching identities are not auto-merged; provider subject uniqueness and last-provider guard are enforced.
- Rate limits work across instances and leak no account existence.
- Secrets and credentials are redacted from logs/traces/analytics.

### Deployment/runtime tests still required

- Provision real Google OIDC client and exact production/staging callback URIs.
- Provision email sender and verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC plus actual delivery/retry/complaint handling.
- Verify HTTPS termination, trusted proxy configuration, CORS/Origin values, cookie behavior in supported browsers and same-site topology.
- Run session revocation and WebSocket disconnect tests across multiple API instances.
- Run independent security review/penetration tests and production restore/failover tests under CR-16.

CR-13 is a specified contract milestone, not proof of a deployed identity provider, email provider, configured DNS, running security middleware or completed security approval.
~~~~~~~~~~

Public auth routes (POST /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/password-reset/*) and /me/profile have no workspace_id (or user_id), causing FK/null crashes in idempotency_records.1. E. Deployment, Observability, Backup and Incident-Recovery Recommendations (Task 4)1. Right-Sized Production Deployment Architecture (70–90 Users → Multi-Community Scale)For an initial community of 70–90 users (generating roughly 5–30 concurrent active WebSocket connections and 1–10 HTTP requests per second at peak), deploying Kubernetes clusters, Kafka brokers, or multi-service meshes is unjustified financial and operational waste. Below is the recommended low-cost, high-reliability production topology ([Recommended Default]):Code snippetflowchart LR
    subgraph Edge["1. Global Edge & CDN"]
        DNS["TLS 1.3 + WAF / Rate Limit Edge"]
        CDN["Static SPA/PWA Asset Hosting\n(Immutable Fingerprinted Bundles)"]
    end

    subgraph Compute["2. Application Compute (Private VPC / Managed Container)"]
        APP["Backend Modular Monolith + WS Broker\n(1–2 Container Instances, Auto-Restart)"]
        WRK["In-Process or Sidecar Worker\n(Outbox Relay, Reminders, Trash Purge, CSV)"]
    end

    subgraph Persistence["3. Managed Persistence & External Services"]
        PG[("Managed PostgreSQL 16/17\n(ACID + RLS + Daily Snapshots + WAL PITR)")]
        OBJ[("S3-Compatible Private Bucket\n(files.<domain> + 15m Orphan Cleanup)")]
        SMTP["Transactional Email API\n(SPF / DKIM / DMARC Verified)"]
        OBS["Centralized Log & Alert Sink\n(Structured JSON Logs + Uptime Monitor)"]
    end

    DNS -->|"https://app.<domain>"| CDN
    DNS -->|"https://api.<domain> (REST + WSS)"| APP

    WRK <-->|"Polls domain_events & pg_locks"| PG

Component Justification & Cost/Scaling Trade-OffsInfrastructure ComponentRecommended Production Setup (70–90 Users)Why Paid / Managed Is Justified (or Where Free/Included Tiers Suffice)Scale-Up Path (1,000+ Users / Multiple Communities)1. Frontend Hosting (Antigravity CLI Build)Static SPA/PWA deployed to an edge CDN (Cloudflare Pages, Vercel, or Netlify) serving immutable hashed assets (/assets/index-[hash].js) and security headers.Free / Zero incremental cost. Delivers global TLS, instant atomic rollbacks to any prior build hash, and zero server maintenance.Scales automatically at the CDN edge with zero architecture changes.2. Backend & Background WorkerSingle-binary/container Modular Monolith running on a managed container platform (Render, Fly.io, Railway, or a single DigitalOcean/AWS App Runner instance with 1–2 vCPU / 2 GB RAM). Runs the async outbox worker loop in-process (or as a lightweight worker process sharing the same image).$7–$20/month justification: An always-on instance (no cold starts) is required to hold persistent WebSocket connections and run the 1-second outbox relay loop without serverless invocation timeouts.Add a 2nd container replica behind the load balancer and attach a managed Redis Pub/Sub adapter when concurrent WebSockets exceed 2,000.3. Primary Database (PostgreSQL 16/17)Managed PostgreSQL instance (Neon, Supabase, Render Postgres, or AWS RDS t4g.micro/small) with automated daily snapshots + Continuous WAL Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR).$15–$25/month justification: Self-hosting PostgreSQL on a raw VPS shifts disk-full crashes, WAL corruption, and backup scheduling onto a single developer. Managed PITR is the highest-leverage reliability investment in the stack.Vertical CPU/RAM scaling + connection pooling (PgBouncer) + read replica if reporting queries grow heavy.4. Object Storage (Attachments)Private S3-compatible bucket (Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3) bound to a dedicated download hostname (files.<domain>).~$0–$2/month: For 70–90 users (~5–20 GB total files), Cloudflare R2's 10 GB free tier + zero egress fees costs virtually nothing while providing 11 nines of durability.Scales linearly per GB stored with zero architectural changes.5. Background Jobs & Pub/SubPostgreSQL Transactional Outbox (domain_events) + LISTEN/NOTIFY + Advisory Locks (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock) for scheduled reminders and trash purges.$0 extra cost: Eliminates the need to provision, secure, and pay for a separate Redis or RabbitMQ cluster in Phase 1.Swap the PubSubBroker interface implementation to Redis only when scaling past a single backend node.6. Transactional EmailManaged HTTPS Email API (Resend, Postmark, or AWS SES) with verified SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS records.Free / <$2/month (70–90 users generate fewer than 2,000 emails/month, well within free tiers). Avoids raw port-25 SMTP blocks and spam-folder blacklisting.Pay-as-you-go per 1,000 emails.2. Environment Separation, Secrets Management & Migration SafetyThree Strict Environments (dev, staging, prod):dev (Local): Runs against seed-v1.json (either via Antigravity CLI MSW mocks or local Docker Compose with PostgreSQL + MinIO + Mailpit).staging (Pre-Release Integration): Mirrors prod topology using a separate database, separate S3 bucket, and sandbox email sink. All M1.1, M1.2, and M1.3 release gates and backup restore drills execute here before promoting to prod.prod (Live Community): Strictly isolated credentials, database, and storage bucket; never accessed from local developer workstations except via audited operational runbooks.Secrets & Configuration Hygiene:All secrets (DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL, SESSION_HMAC_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY) are injected via platform environment variables—never committed to Git.Dual Database Credentials: The backend runtime connects using DATABASE_APP_URL (least-privilege role: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on domain tables; SELECT, INSERT only on audit_logs; zero DDL permissions). Schema migrations execute in CI/CD using DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL (DDL owner role).Startup validation (Zod / envalid) fails fast within 1 second if any required environment variable is missing or malformed.Zero-Downtime "Expand-and-Contract" Database Migrations:Every migration in /storage/migrations/ must be backward-compatible with the currently running application version (N - 1) so a bad deploy can roll back its container image without breaking against the database:Phase A (Expand): Add new nullable columns, new tables, or CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY. Deploy new code.Phase B (Backfill): Populate data in batches.Phase C (Contract — Next Release): Add NOT NULL constraints or drop deprecated columns only after confirming the prior code version is retired.3. CI/CD Pipeline Gates, Observability, Health Checks & AlertingA. Five Mandatory CI Pipeline Gates (Runs on Every Pull Request)Contract & Type Gate: redocly lint /contracts/openapi.yaml + verify npm run contracts:generate produces zero git diff in src/contracts/api-types.gen.ts.Static Analysis & Supply-Chain Gate: tsc --noEmit, ESLint, npm audit --audit-level=high (or osv-scanner), and lockfile integrity check (npm ci).Backend Unit, Policy & Integration Gate: Run CHK-01 through CHK-10 against an ephemeral PostgreSQL 17 service container with migrations applied from scratch.Frontend Component, MSW & Accessibility Gate: Run Vitest + Playwright E2E against MSW (seed-v1.json) including @axe-core/playwright (0 critical/serious WCAG 2.2 AA violations).Build & Bundle Budget Gate: Verify production Vite build succeeds and initial gzipped JS entrypoint stays under 200 KB (lazy-loading Calendar, Timeline, and Settings bundles).B. Structured Logging, Metrics, Health Probes & Actionable AlertsStructured JSON Logs with Mandatory Redaction: Every log entry outputs single-line JSON containing { timestamp, level, correlationId, userId, communityId, workspaceId, operationId, statusCode, durationMs, errorCode }. Logger middleware strips Cookie, Authorization, X-CSRF-Token, password, token, and raw task descriptionMd / bodyMd so user content and credentials never leak into operational logs.Health & Readiness Endpoints:GET /api/v1/health/live: Returns 200 OK { status: "UP" } immediately (verifies process event loop is responsive).GET /api/v1/health/ready: Executes a SELECT 1 with 2s timeout against PostgreSQL and checks outbox worker heartbeat (now() - last_outbox_poll < 30s). Returns 200 OK or 503 Service Unavailable (used by container orchestrator for zero-downtime rolling deploys).Four High-Signal Actionable Alerts (Zero Alert Fatigue):Uptime / Readiness Alert (Critical): /health/ready returns non-200 for 2 consecutive minutes.5xx Error Spike Alert (High): HTTP 5xx rate exceeds 1% of requests (or greater than 5 errors in 5 minutes).Outbox / Sync Lag Alert (High): Unprocessed domain_events (processed_at IS NULL) older than 30 seconds exceed 100 rows (indicates the realtime/notification worker is stuck).Security & Break-Glass Alert (Immediate): Any ADMIN_BREAK_GLASS event, broken audit_logs hash chain, or greater than 50 401/403/429 responses from a single actor within 5 minutes.4. Backup Strategy, Restore Verification & Incident-Recovery PlaybookNote on Targets: All numerical SLO, RPO, and RTO targets below are marked [Recommended Default — Requires Stakeholder Approval] rather than assumed requirements.Reliability ParameterProvisional Target ([Recommended Default])Concrete Technical Mechanism & VerificationService Availability Target (SLO)99.5% monthly uptime (~3.6 hours/month maintenance/incident budget — appropriate for a single-region community platform without 24/7 SRE paging).Monitored via external synthetic check calling GET /api/v1/health/ready every 60 seconds from 2 regions.Recovery Point Objective (RPO — Max Data Loss)Database: Less than 5 minutes (via Continuous WAL archiving / PITR).Object Storage: Near-Zero (S3/R2 synchronous multi-AZ durability + bucket versioning).Managed PostgreSQL continuous WAL streaming + automated daily full logical backups (pg_dump --format=custom) encrypted with AES-256-GCM and copied to an isolated backup bucket with a 30-day retention lock.Recovery Time Objective (RTO — Max Time to Restore)Less than 60 minutes from incident declaration to verified service restoration.Documented 1-command infrastructure-as-code / container redeploy + automated database restore script (scripts/dr-restore-verify.sh).Mandatory Restore Verification DrillExecuted before M1.3 Launch and Monthly Thereafter. (An untested backup is not a backup).Automated CI/staging job downloads the latest encrypted pg_dump backup, restores it into a disposable PostgreSQL container, verifies audit_logs hash-chain integrity, and runs CHK-01–CHK-06 smoke queries.Incident Severity & Response PlaybookSEV-1 (Critical Security Breach, Cross-Tenant Leak, or Total Outage):Containment (0–15m): If a compromised account or token is suspected, revoke all active sessions for the affected user/community (DELETE FROM sessions WHERE ...) and sever active WebSockets. If a buggy deploy caused a data leak, roll back the container/CDN deployment to the previous immutable release tag immediately (less than 2 minutes).Recovery (15–60m): If destructive data corruption occurred, place the API in maintenance mode (503 with Retry-After) and restore PostgreSQL via PITR to the timestamp immediately preceding the fault.Communication & Post-Mortem: Notify Community Administrators and affected Workspace Owners with an accurate timeline derived from audit_logs and domain_events; add a regression test to the CI suite before closing the incident.SEV-2 (Partial Feature Degradation — e.g., Realtime WebSocket Drop, Email Delay, or File Upload Failure):Containment: Clients automatically fall back to HTTP REST mutations and local URL/IndexedDB drafts; outbox worker queues failed emails/events for automatic retry once the downstream provider recovers.F. Updated Open-Decision RegisterAll items below are explicitly marked as [Unresolved Stakeholder Choice] paired with our [Recommended Default] so Prompt 08 can present a clear sign-off block without assuming unapproved requirements:Decision IDUnresolved Policy / Target QuestionRecommended Default ([Recommended Default])Architectural / Contract Impact if Stakeholder Chooses the AlternativeDEC-OPEN-01Community Admin Visibility into Personal Workspaces (Conflict 1): Can a Community Administrator inspect task contents inside a user's Personal Workspace?PRIVATE_STRICT: Community Admins view aggregate storage/task-count metadata only (adminListWorkspaceDirectory) and can suspend abusive accounts, but can never read or break-glass into Personal Workspace tasks. Break-Glass (POST .../break-glass) is restricted strictly to SHARED workspaces.Setting personalWorkspaceAdminPolicy = 'AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS' permits POST .../break-glass on PERSONAL workspaces, logging a high-priority AuditLog entry and emailing the Personal Workspace owner. Zero schema changes required.DEC-OPEN-02Default Task-Editing Mode in Shared Workspaces (Conflict 2): Who can edit task definitions (title, description, dates, priority, custom fields) vs. execution progress (status, subtasks, comments) by default?CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT: Owners, Coordinators, Task Creator, and Task Assigner edit definitions (canEditTitleDescription, canEditDatesPriority); Assignees update status, subtasks, and comments (canUpdateStatus, canManageSubtasks); ordinary Members create tasks and comment. Workspace Owners can toggle COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER or assigneeCanEditDatesPriority in Workspace Settings.Initializing new Shared Workspaces with taskEditPolicy = 'COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER' sets canEditTitleDescription = true and canEditDatesPriority = true on TaskEffectivePermissionsDto for all workspace members. Zero UI refactoring required.DEC-OPEN-03File Size Limits, Storage Quotas & Audit Retention (UNR-API-03): What are the initial numerical quota limits?• Max single file upload: 25 MB (26,214,400 bytes).• Shared Workspace quota: 5 GB.• Personal Workspace quota: 500 MB.• Searchable Audit Log retention: 365 days online + CSV export archival.Configured via community/workspace policy columns (max_file_size_bytes, storage_quota_bytes, audit_retention_days) exposed in MeContextDto and WorkspaceDetailDto.DEC-OPEN-04Service Level & Recovery Targets (SLO / RPO / RTO): What operational reliability targets govern production hosting?• Monthly Availability SLO: 99.5%.• Database RPO (Max Data Loss): Less than 5 minutes (Managed Postgres WAL PITR) + daily encrypted logical backups.• Disaster Recovery RTO: Less than 60 minutes.Higher targets (e.g., 99.95% multi-AZ hot standby with <1 minute RTO) would require doubling database and container hosting costs (~$100+/month vs. ~$25–$40/month).H. 1. Executive Architecture DecisionsTo support parallel implementation by Antigravity CLI (Frontend) and a separate Backend Developer while scaling cleanly from an initial 70–90 person community to multiple independent communities, the system architecture is governed by ten foundational decisions:Modular Monolith with a Transactional Event Outbox ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): The backend must be structured as a single deployable Modular Monolith partitioned into strict domain modules rather than distributed microservices. At a scale of 70–90 users (and even up to 10,000+ users across dozens of communities), microservices introduce network serialization latency, distributed transaction hazards, and operational overhead with zero domain benefit. Asynchronous workflows (notifications, audit logs, real-time broadcasts, and Phase 3 automations) decouple cleanly from synchronous HTTP mutations via an ACID Transactional Outbox (domain_events) committed in the same database transaction as the domain state change.Global User Identity Decoupled from Multi-Community Membership ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Reconciling a contradiction in earlier reports, a User record must never contain a single community_id foreign key. Identity (users and auth_identities) is global to the platform instance, while tenant membership is modeled via a dedicated community_memberships join entity (user_id, community_id, community_role, status). Every workspace and operational resource below the community level is strictly scoped to a single community_id from the first schema migration.Defense-in-Depth Tenant Isolation ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Every domain query, search index lookup, file download, WebSocket subscription, and background job must enforce an explicit (community_id, workspace_id) security context derived from authenticated session state—never from unverified client request parameters.Dual-Mode Policy Switches for Unresolved Governance Conflicts ([Recommended Architectural Decision] / [Unresolved Stakeholder Decision]): Where earlier requirements and usability recommendations diverged—specifically Conflict 1 (Global Admin access to Personal Workspaces) and Conflict 2 (Creator/Coordinator-gated editing vs. collaborative Member editing)—the architecture parameterizes the behavior via explicit policy enums (personal_workspace_admin_policy at the community level; task_edit_policy at the workspace level) rather than hardcoding one assumption into the controllers.Single Authoritative Representation for Milestones vs. Task Archetypes ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Reconciling Prompt 04's overlap between FEAT-A01 and FEAT-B04, Milestones are modeled exclusively as a container/target entity (project_milestones) to which tasks link via milestone_id. The Milestone label is removed from the task item_type enum and replaced with Deliverable (Task | Deliverable | Bug/Issue | Decision/Request), eliminating competing representations.Separated Task Identity vs. Display Key with Alias Resolution ([Established Requirement] / [Recommended Architectural Decision]): Every task is identified internally by an immutable UUID (task_id) and externally by a mutable project-scoped human-readable key (current_key, e.g., FEST-14). Cross-project task moves and project prefix changes atomically allocate a new key in the target prefix and register the prior key in task_key_aliases so historical URLs, #KEY mentions, and search queries resolve forever without collision.Lexicographical Fractional Indexing (rank_key) with Tie-Breaking ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Manual ordering inside Lists and Board columns uses a single lexicographical string key (rank_key) paired with a deterministic (rank_key ASC, task_id ASC) tie-breaker. Moving a task updates one row (O(1)) without renumbering sibling tasks.One Canonical Query AST Powering All Four Views ([Established Requirement] / [Recommended Architectural Decision]): List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline views are mandatory for Initial Production Release sign-off (Phase 1: M1.1 & M1.2) and consume a single shared task-query contract and client entity cache.Authoritative Live-RBAC Replay & Per-Field Watermarks for Offline Sync ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Every mutation carries a client-generated X-Mutation-Id UUID and a base_revision / per-field timestamp watermark. When Phase 3 offline mutations replay, the backend validates the user's current live permissions first (quarantining rejected edits to a local recovery store on 403) and performs per-field conflict detection (409 Conflict with structured server/client field diffs).Vite + React + TypeScript SPA Architecture for Antigravity CLI ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Because the platform is an authenticated, real-time, keyboard-intensive workspace application (with zero public SEO page requirements and a planned IndexedDB offline engine), a Vite + React 19 + TypeScript SPA/PWA architecture with TanStack Router, TanStack Query, and Headless ARIA primitives (Radix UI + React Aria + @dnd-kit) is strongly preferred over SSR-heavy Next.js App Router complexity.2. Domain Model and Data Dictionary2.1 Reconciling Conceptual Entities vs. Physical Storage AlternativesNot every conceptual domain concept requires a dedicated relational table. Before defining the schema, the following storage consolidations are established ([Recommended Architectural Decision]):Tasks & Subtasks (tasks): Stored in a single self-referencing tasks table (parent_task_id nullable, hierarchy_depth 0 | 1 | 2) rather than separate tasks and subtasks tables. Because subtasks have permanent keys (FEST-15), assignees, statuses, comments, and board/list visibility, splitting them across tables would double every query, foreign key, and API endpoint.Capabilities & Role Grants (roles.capabilities): Capabilities are immutable system string constants defined in code (e.g., task:create, view:update_shared). Instead of a 3-table normalized join (roles → role_capabilities → capabilities), each row in roles stores a validated array/set of capability strings (TEXT[] or JSONB), eliminating multi-way joins on every request.Custom Field Values (tasks.custom_fields_jsonb vs. EAV Table): Rather than a classic Entity-Attribute-Value (task_custom_field_values) table that requires expensive multi-join pivots to render a 50-row List View, custom field values are stored in an indexed custom_fields JSONB map directly on the tasks record (validated on write against custom_field_definitions), with a GIN index supporting fast faceted filtering.Task Attachments & Workspace Files (workspace_files): Stored in a single unified workspace_files table from Milestone M1.1 (with nullable task_id and comment_id references). In M1.1, files are uploaded via tasks; in M1.3, the Workspace File Hub simply queries workspace_files WHERE workspace_id = :id without any table migration.2.2 Entity-Relationship Diagram (Artifact #3)Textual Explanation of Diagram: The ER diagram below illustrates the four structural strata of the domain model: (1) Global Identity & Multi-Community Tenancy at the top (USER joining multiple COMMUNITY tenants via COMMUNITY_MEMBERSHIP), (2) Workspace Governance & RBAC (WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP, and ROLE), (3) the Core Work & View Spine (PROJECT, LIST, MILESTONE, WORKFLOW_STATUS, TASK, TASK_KEY_ALIAS, TASK_LINK, and SAVED_VIEW), and (4) Collaboration, Files & Event Auditability (COMMENT, TASK_WATCHER, WORKSPACE_FILE, DOMAIN_EVENT, AUDIT_LOG, and AUTOMATION_RULE).Code snippeterDiagram

3.2 Modular System Architecture Diagram (Artifact #2)Textual Explanation of Diagram: Inside the backend Modular Monolith, all incoming HTTP and WebSocket requests pass through the Identity & Tenant Context Middleware and the Authorization & Capability Engine before touching any domain module. Synchronous writes mutate domain tables and append to the Transactional Outbox (domain_events) in a single ACID commit.
