Tenant Isolation and Identity Model4.1 Reconciling Global Users vs. Multi-Community Tenancy ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Consistency Check Resolution: Earlier product notes suggested adding community_id NOT NULL directly to the users table. That design would break as soon as a single person (e.g., a student or advisor using samudra@example.com) joins both the SVIET Engineering Community and an Open-Source Contributors Community, forcing them to register duplicate email accounts.Authoritative Multi-Community Identity Architecture:Global Identity Layer (users & auth_identities): A human has one User record identified by user_id and authenticated via email/password or Google OAuth.Community Tenant Layer (communities & community_memberships): A User belongs to one or more Communities via community_memberships (community_id, user_id, is_global_admin, is_default_coordinator, status). Every API request is scoped to a single active community_id (passed via URL path /api/v1/c/{communityId}/... or header X-Community-Id and verified against community_memberships).Workspace Collaboration Layer (workspaces & workspace_memberships): Every Workspace (PERSONAL or SHARED) belongs to one and only one Community (workspaces.community_id NOT NULL). A Personal Workspace is scoped to a specific community (type = 'PERSONAL', owner_id = user_id) so personal tasks linked or moved into that community's shared workspaces never cross tenant boundaries.Denormalized community_id on All Operational Tables (Day-1 Migration Rule): Every operational table (workspaces, projects, lists, tasks, comments, workspace_files, saved_views, domain_events, audit_logs) must carry community_id UUID NOT NULL and workspace_id UUID NOT NULL from Migration 001, backed by composite foreign keys (e.g., FOREIGN KEY (community_id, workspace_id) REFERENCES workspaces(community_id, id)). This makes cross-community data leakage structurally impossible at the database constraint level.4.2 Isolation Safeguards Across All Six Infrastructure SurfacesSurfaceMandatory Isolation Requirement ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Candidate Implementation Technique ([Candidate Implementation Technique])1. Database QueriesEvery repository query must bind both community_id and workspace_id from the server-verified SecurityContext object. Composite foreign keys prevent linking a Task in Community A to a Project or Milestone in Community B.Hybrid Application Context + PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS): Application services open a transaction, execute SET LOCAL app.current_community_id = '...' and SET LOCAL app.current_workspace_ids = '...', and let Postgres RLS policies act as a fail-safe backstop against missing WHERE clauses.2. Search & IndexingGlobal search (/search) and Omnibar key lookups must intersect matches strictly with the caller's active accessible_workspace_ids list inside the active community_id.Partition search indexes by (community_id, workspace_id) so unauthorized workspaces are pruned before text scoring; return identical 404 / No Match responses for non-existent and unauthorized keys to prevent existence enumeration.3. File Storage & AttachmentsObject storage buckets must never be publicly readable. Object keys must be namespaced as {community_id}/{workspace_id}/{file_id}/{sanitized_filename}.Clients never hold static file URLs; calling GET /api/v1/files/{file_id}/download verifies live workspace read permission first, then returns a short-lived (15-minute TTL) S3/R2 pre-signed URL.4. Realtime SubscriptionsWebSocket clients subscribe to workspace-specific rooms (room:workspace:{workspace_id}). The server validates membership on SUBSCRIBE and immediately forces an unsubscribe (SOCKET_KICK) when a MEMBER_REMOVED event fires.Maintain an in-memory map user_id -> Set<socket_id> in the WebSocket broker; when M03 emits WORKSPACE_MEMBER_REMOVED, immediately sever that user's subscription to the workspace room.5. Background Jobs & RemindersEvery queued background job payload (due-date reminders, CSV imports, automation executions) must embed {community_id, workspace_id, actor_id} and re-verify tenant/workspace status at execution time.Worker middleware rehydrates the SecurityContext from the job envelope before invoking any domain service.6. Data Exports & CSVCSV exports execute through the exact same M08 permission-filtered query pipeline as the UI views and write an AUDIT_LOG record (DATA_EXPORTED_CSV) if exported by an Owner/Admin.Stream CSV rows directly from the tenant-scoped cursor query with a hard row cap (10,000 rows per export).5. 5.2 Formal Analysis and Resolution of Conflict 1 & Conflict 2Conflict 1: Global Administrator Authority vs. Personal-Workspace PrivacyThe Tension: An established governance requirement states that Global Administrators can manage users, security policies, and work across the platform, whereas our UX and privacy research (Prompts 02–04) found that users will not trust Personal Workspaces for private drafting or personal study tasks if Global Administrators can silently browse their task contents.Security & Usability Trade-Offs:Unrestricted Admin Read/Write on Personal Workspaces: Protects against a user storing prohibited content in a personal workspace, but destroys psychological privacy and turns Personal Workspaces into monitored company folders.Strict Personal Privacy + Metadata Quota Governance: Preserves 100% user trust in Personal Workspaces while still letting Global Admins view aggregate metadata (owner_id, task_count, storage_bytes_used), suspend abusive accounts, or delete a violating workspace in its entirety.Recommended Default ([Recommended Architectural Decision] / [Unresolved Stakeholder Decision]): Adopt Mode 1A (PRIVATE_STRICT) as the default while supporting Mode 1B (AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS) via a community-level configuration flag (community.settings.personal_workspace_admin_policy):Under Default Mode 1A (PRIVATE_STRICT): Global Administrators have full audited Break-Glass authority over all Shared Workspaces, and full visibility into Personal Workspace aggregate metadata (storage usage, task count, account suspension), but the API blocks (403) Global Administrators from reading or mutating task titles, descriptions, comments, or files inside another user's Personal Workspace.Under Alternative Mode 1B (AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS — Preserved Until Stakeholder Sign-Off): If the community stakeholder requires Global Admin inspection of Personal Workspaces, the Global Admin still cannot silently browse personal tasks via normal views/search; they must execute POST /admin/workspaces/{id}/break-glass with a mandatory reason string, which writes an immutable AUDIT_LOG entry and notifies the Personal Workspace owner that an administrative inspection occurred.Conflict 2: Creator/Coordinator-Gated Task Editing vs. Broader Member EditingThe Tension: The original requirements specify that task-detail editing is restricted to administrators, workspace owners, coordinators, and the task's creator/assigner (with configurable assignee rights for status/progress/subtasks), whereas later UX reports suggested allowing any workspace member to edit task fields collaboratively.Security & Usability Trade-Offs:Strict Role + Creator/Assignee Gating (CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT): Prevents ordinary volunteers or members from accidentally altering task scope, changing deadlines set by a coordinator, or reassigning someone else's work, at the cost of requiring a Coordinator/Creator when a peer wants to help update a task's due date or priority.Open Member Editing (COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER): Maximizes frictionless peer triage in small high-trust squads, but allows any member to alter deadlines or task definitions without coordinator oversight.Recommended Default ([Recommended Architectural Decision] / [Unresolved Stakeholder Decision]): Preserve the original requirement as the default (CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT with full Assignee execution rights) and expose workspace.settings.task_edit_policy as a 1-click Workspace Owner setting:Default Policy (CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT — Honors Original Requirement):Task Definition & Structural Fields (Title, Description, Project/List placement, Priority, Start/Due Dates, Custom Fields, Assignee list, Milestone): Editable by Workspace Owners, Coordinators, the Task Creator, and the Task Assigner.Task Execution & Progress Fields (Workflow Status transition, Subtask creation/completion on assigned task, Estimate progress, Attachments, Comments): Editable by the Task Assignee (in addition to Owners, Coordinators, and Creator).Workspace Owners can also toggle whether Assignees are permitted to edit Due Date or Priority (assignee_can_edit_dates_priority: bool, default false).Ordinary Workspace Members (neither Creator nor Assignee): Can View the task, Create new tasks, Post & edit their own Comments, Mention users, Watch/Unwatch, and Create Personal Saved Views.Owner-Configurable Alternative (COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER): Workspace Owners who want open wiki-style collaboration for a high-trust squad can flip Workspace Settings → Tasks & Permissions → Task Editing Mode to "Collaborative (All workspace members can edit task fields)", which grants task:edit_fields to the MEMBER role in that workspace.5.3 Precedence Hierarchy for Permission ResolutionWhen evaluating evaluatePermission(actor, capability, targetResource), the backend engine resolves rules in this exact 5-tier precedence order (highest to lowest):Tier 1 — Platform & Community Security Floor (Immutable Deny): Cross-tenant isolation (actor.community_id != resource.community_id), suspended user status, and Personal Workspace privacy boundary (Conflict 1). Cannot be overridden by any role.Tier 2 — Role Preview Downward Mask (Session Simulation): If X-Preview-Role-Id is active on the request, intersect the actor's capabilities with the previewed role's capabilities (effective = actor_caps ∩ preview_role_caps). Can only subtract permissions, never add them.Tier 3 — Workspace Ownership & Audited Break-Glass: Active Workspace Owners (and Global Admins holding an active, audit-logged Break-Glass session on a Shared Workspace) hold full workspace capabilities, subject only to the >= 1 Owner last-owner self-removal guard.Tier 4 — Workspace Role Capability Grants (Coordinator, Custom Role, Member, Viewer): Evaluates the capability array attached to the actor's WorkspaceMembership.role_id (modulated by workspace.settings.task_edit_policy for Conflict 2).Tier 5 — Dynamic Task-Relationship Grants (Creator, Assigner, Assignee, Comment Author): Evaluates contextual ownership on the specific Task or Comment instance (task.created_by == actor.id, actor.id IN task.assignees, or comment.author_id == actor.id).5.4 Authoritative Role & Contextual Permission MatrixLegend: ✓ = Permitted by default | ✓ (Audit) = Permitted only via Audited Break-Glass with mandatory reason | ✓ (Cfg) = Configurable via Workspace Settings (task_edit_policy / role capabilities) | Own = Permitted only on items authored by the user | — = Denied (403 Forbidden).Capability Code & ActionGlobal Admin (Unjoined Shared Workspace)Global Admin (Personal Workspace of Another User)Workspace OwnerCoordinator (Default in Shared, Removable)Task Creator / Assigner (Member Role)Task Assignee (Member Role)Ordinary Member (Not Creator or Assignee)Read-Only Viewer (Custom/Guest)workspace:read_metadata (Directory & Quotas)✓✓ (Quota only)✓✓✓✓✓✓task:read (View Tasks, Boards, Lists, Files)✓ (Audit)— (Mode 1A) / ✓ (Audit) (1B)✓✓✓✓✓✓task:create (Create New Tasks in Project)✓ (Audit)—✓✓✓✓✓—task:edit_definition (Title, Description, Dates, Priority, Custom Fields)✓ (Audit)—✓✓✓✓ (Cfg) (Default: Status/Exec only)✓ (Cfg) (Default: — under Mode 2A; Task Identity, Hierarchy and Workflow Design6.1 Bounded Configurable Hierarchy Semantics ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Canonical Spine: Community → Workspace → Project → List (optional 1-level grouping) → Task (hierarchy_depth = 0) → Subtask (hierarchy_depth = 1..max_subtask_depth).Owner-Configurable Subtask Depth Boundary: Every Project defaults to max_subtask_depth = 1 (Tasks can have Subtasks, and Subtasks cannot have children). In Project Settings → Hierarchy, a Workspace Owner or Coordinator can increase max_subtask_depth to 2 (Task → Subtask → Checklist Sub-item), which is the hard ceiling enforced by the system.Cross-View Consistency Rules:List View: Renders as an expandable role="treegrid" where expanding a parent row reveals its child rows indented by 24px * hierarchy_depth.Board View: Only top-level tasks (hierarchy_depth = 0) render as default standalone Kanban cards, displaying an interactive [✓ 2/4 subtasks] progress pill on the card face. Users can optionally toggle Show Subtasks as Cards in View Display Options, which renders subtasks with a parent breadcrumb header (FEST-14 › FEST-15).Timeline View: Left pane renders the expandable parent/subtask hierarchy; parent bars automatically display a span indicator if subtasks extend beyond the parent's due_date.Rollup Invariants: Completing subtasks updates the parent's completed_subtask_count / total_subtask_count badge immediately, but never forces an automatic status change on the parent task without user confirmation (instead, when the final subtask transitions to DONE, the UI shows a non-blocking prompt: "All subtasks complete — mark parent FEST-14 as Done?").Cycle & Invalid Parent Prevention:A task cannot be set as its own parent or a descendant of itself.When converting a standalone task into a subtask (PATCH /tasks/{id} setting parent_task_id), the backend verifies target_parent.hierarchy_depth + 1 + max_subtree_depth(task) <= project.max_subtask_depth and target_parent.project_id == task.project_id.On TaskLink creation (BLOCKS / IS_BLOCKED_BY), the backend runs a Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal over the project/workspace dependency graph (bounded to max 50 hops) and rejects any link that introduces a directed cycle (422 Unprocessable Entity: "Circular dependency detected: FEST-18 already blocks FEST-14").6.2 Task Identity, Atomic Key Generation & Alias Resolution ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Consistency Check Resolution: How can a task key be "permanent" if moving a task from Project OPS to Project FEST changes its key from OPS-12 to FEST-45?Architectural Resolution: A task key is permanently resolvable, not immutable in display prefix. Every task has two identifiers:Immutable Internal Identity (task.id — UUIDv7): Primary key used in all foreign keys (comments, workspace_files, task_links, domain_events). It never changes over the lifetime of the task.Canonical Display Key (task.current_key — e.g., FEST-45) + Historical Alias Ledger (task_key_aliases):Atomic Creation: When a task is created in Project OPS, the backend executes an atomic counter increment within the creation transaction:UPDATE projects SET next_task_seq = next_task_seq + 1 WHERE id = :project_id RETURNING key_prefix, next_task_seq - 1 AS seq;
It sets task.current_key = 'OPS-12' and also inserts 'OPS-12' → task.id into task_key_aliases.Cross-Project Move Semantics: When OPS-12 is moved to Project FEST, the transaction atomically allocates the next FEST sequence number (FEST-45), updates task.current_key = 'FEST-45', and inserts 'FEST-45' → task.id into task_key_aliases while retaining 'OPS-12' → task.id in task_key_aliases.Project Prefix Rename Semantics (Resolves UNR-01): When a Workspace Owner changes a project's prefix from MKT to GRW, a single transaction updates current_key = 'GRW-' || seq_num for all tasks in that project and bulk-inserts all new GRW-* keys into task_key_aliases while keeping all old MKT-* entries intact. Furthermore, retired prefixes (MKT) are reserved in task_key_aliases within that workspace so a new project in the same workspace cannot reuse MKT and cause key collisions.Lookup & URL Behavior: Any request to GET /api/v1/workspaces/{wid}/tasks/by-key/OPS-12, any #OPS-12 comment link, or any Omnibar search for OPS-12 joins against task_key_aliases, returns the task with current_key: "FEST-45" and matched_alias: "OPS-12", and allows the frontend router to replace the browser URL /t/OPS-12 with /t/FEST-45 while displaying a subtle Redirected from OPS-12 badge.6.3 Workflow Engine & Lightweight Approval Semantics ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Five Immutable Canonical Categories: Every WorkflowStatus record must map to one of five system categories:BACKLOG (Unscheduled / staged ideas; excluded from active board columns when Backlog tray is collapsed).TODO (Scheduled and ready to start; 0% progress state).IN_PROGRESS (Active execution; >0% progress state).DONE (Completed work; satisfies upstream BLOCKS dependencies and counts toward Milestone completion %).CANCELED (Closed without completion; satisfies/releases BLOCKS warnings without counting as completed scope).Status Deletion & Migration Invariant: Every project must retain at least one status in TODO, IN_PROGRESS, and DONE. Attempting to delete a custom status that currently holds tasks (COUNT(tasks) > 0) requires a mandatory fallback_status_id parameter in DELETE /statuses/{id}?migrate_to={fallback_id}, which atomically moves those tasks and writes a single batch DomainEvent.Simplest Domain Model for Phase 3 Approvals (FEAT-D03): Instead of building a state-machine transition table (status_transitions), WorkflowStatus includes two nullable columns: required_entry_capability VARCHAR (e.g., 'task:approve_status') and requires_signoff BOOL DEFAULT FALSE.In Phase 1 & 2, all statuses have requires_signoff = FALSE (any user with task:update_status can transition freely between any statuses).In Phase 3, if an Owner toggles Requires Coordinator/Owner Sign-Off on an Approved or Published status, an ordinary Member attempting to move a task into that status triggers a lightweight signoff_requested_Status_id flag on the task and notifies workspace Coordinators, who can approve the transition in 1 click.6.4 Reconciling Milestones vs. Work-Item Types ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Consistency Check Resolution: Prompt 04 listed Milestone both as a lightweight work-item archetype (FEAT-A01) and as a target bucket entity (FEAT-B04). Having both a Task with item_type = 'MILESTONE' and a separate ProjectMilestone entity creates severe domain confusion (users will not know whether to create a Milestone task or a Milestone bucket, or how subtasks vs. milestone-linked tasks differ).Authoritative Resolution:ProjectMilestone (project_milestones table — FEAT-B04) is the sole representation of a Milestone/Release. It has a title, target_date, description, and status, renders as a diamond marker on the Calendar and Timeline views, and aggregates completion progress (Done Tasks / Total Tasks) across all tasks where task.milestone_id = milestone.id.Work-Item Archetypes (tasks.item_type — FEAT-A01) are strictly task classifications: TASK (default), DELIVERABLE, BUG, and DECISION. None of them is named Milestone.7. Persistence, Ordering, Transaction and Event Strategy7.1 Mandatory Data-Integrity Invariants vs. Candidate TechniquesArchitectural ConcernMandatory Data-Integrity Requirement ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Selected Strategy & Rationale for 70–90+ User Scale ([Candidate Implementation Technique])1. Task Mutation & History AtomicityA task update and its corresponding DomainEvent (activity changelog + real-time delta) must never diverge (no dual-write bug where the DB updates but the WebSocket/changelog misses the event).ACID Transactional Outbox Pattern: Within a single READ COMMITTED database transaction, update the tasks row and INSERT INTO domain_events (...). Commit both together.2. Manual List & Board OrderingMoving a card between two items must execute in O(1) row writes (updating only the moved task) and maintain deterministic total ordering even under simultaneous drags by two users.Base-62 Fractional Indexing (rank_key) + Jitter + Tuple Tie-Breaking: Compute the lexicographical midpoint string between prev.rank_key and next.rank_key (using rocicorp/fractional-indexing or equivalent algorithm with random jitter bits) and always sort by ORDER BY rank_key ASC, id ASC. If LENGTH(rank_key) > 32, enqueue a background lazy rebalance for that list/column.3. Idempotent Mutation RequestsRetrying a timed-out HTTP POST /tasks or PATCH /tasks/{id} (or replaying an offline queue item) must never create duplicate tasks or double-apply state transitions.X-Mutation-Id Header + idempotency_records Lookup: Client generates a UUIDv4 X-Mutation-Id per logical action. The backend checks idempotency_records inside the transaction; if already committed for (user_id, mutation_id), it short-circuits and returns the stored response snapshot.4. Monotonic Event DeliveryConnected clients must be able to detect missed WebSocket packets after a brief Wi-Fi drop and fetch the exact missing delta sequence without reloading the whole workspace.Per-Workspace Sequence Counter (workspace_seq_id): Each workspace maintains a monotonically increasing last_event_seq BIGINT incremented when domain_events are written. Clients track lastSeenSeq and call GET /workspaces/{id}/events?since_seq={lastSeenSeq} upon reconnect.5. Per-Field Conflict DetectionConcurrent updates to different fields of the same task (priority vs. due_date) must both succeed, whereas concurrent updates to the same field from an older base state must be detected.Field-Level Timestamp Map (field_updated_at_jsonb): Every tasks row stores a JSONB map of { "title": 1730240000120, "status_id": 1730240005000, ... }. Mutations include base_field_timestamps; if server.field_updated_at[f] > client.base_field_timestamps[f], the server returns 409 Conflict for field f (in strict/offline mode) or LWW with audit diff (in online scalar clicks).6. Soft-Delete & Restoration IntegrityArchiving a parent Project or List and later restoring it must not inadvertently restore tasks that were already individually archived prior to the container archive.Batch Archive Token (archive_batch_id): When archiving a container (List or Project) or a multi-select batch, tag all newly archived child rows with the same archive_batch_id UUID. Clicking Undo or Restore on that batch restores only rows matching that archive_batch_id.7.2 Synchronous Mutation & Transactional Outbox Flow (Artifact #5)Textual Explanation of Diagram: The sequence diagram below traces a synchronous task mutation (PATCH /tasks/FEST-14) from Antigravity CLI through the backend. It demonstrates how idempotency, capability authorization, per-field timestamp updates, and the domain_events outbox insert happen inside a single atomic database transaction before the outbox relay asynchronously pushes the update to connected WebSocket peers and the notification engine.Code snippetsequenceDiagram

    SVC->>DB: UPDATE workspaces SET last_event_seq = last_event_seq + 1 RETURNING last_event_seq
    SVC->>DB: INSERT INTO domain_events (workspace_seq_id, before_jsonb, after_jsonb)
    SVC->>DB: INSERT INTO idempotency_records (mutation_id, response_jsonb)
    API->>DB: COMMIT TRANSACTION
    API-->>UI: 200 OK (Updated Task DTO + workspace_seq_id: 1045)
    UI->>UI: Confirm Optimistic State & Advance localSeq = 1045

    par Async Outbox Fan-Out
        RLY->>DB: Poll / Listen domain_events WHERE processed_at IS NULL
        RLY->>PEER: WS Push: TASK_UPDATED (seq: 1045, delta, mutation_id)
        PEER->>PEER: Reconcile Cache & Flash Updated Cell (500ms)
        RLY->>DB: Enqueue Notification for Task Watchers (M10)
    end
7.3 Realtime Synchronization & Reconnection Flow (Artifact #6)Textual Explanation of Diagram: This state flow shows how the frontend WebSocket client maintains cache consistency across normal operation, deduplicates its own echoed mutations using mutation_id, recovers smoothly from short network drops (since_seq delta catch-up), and falls back to full query invalidation if a disconnection exceeds the server's delta retention window (>500 events).Code snippetstateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Connected: Authenticate WS & Subscribe(workspace_id, lastSeenSeq)
    
    state Connected {
        [*] --> Listening
        Listening --> ProcessPacket: Receive WS Event (seq = N, mutation_id)
        ProcessPacket --> IgnoreEcho: mutation_id in localCommittedMutations
        ProcessPacket --> ApplyDelta: N == lastSeenSeq + 1
        ProcessPacket --> GapDetected: N > lastSeenSeq + 1
        IgnoreEcho --> Listening: Update lastSeenSeq = N
        ApplyDelta --> Listening: Patch Normalized Task Cache & Set lastSeenSeq = N
    }

    Connected --> Disconnected: Socket Close / Heartbeat Timeout (>5s shows Reconnecting Pill)
    GapDetected --> CatchUpSync: Fetch Missing Deltas
    Disconnected --> CatchUpSync: Socket Reconnects

    state CatchUpSync {
        [*] --> RequestDeltas: GET /workspaces/{id}/events?since_seq={lastSeenSeq}
        RequestDeltas --> ReplayDeltas: HTTP 200 (<= 500 events returned)
        RequestDeltas --> FullRefetch: HTTP 410 Gone (> 500 events gap) or Permission Changed
        ReplayDeltas --> [*]: Apply deltas in order & update lastSeenSeq
        FullRefetch --> [*]: Invalidate TanStack Query Cache & Refetch Active View
    }

    CatchUpSync --> Connected: Sync Complete (Hide Reconnecting Pill)
7.4 Offline Mutation Replay & Conflict Resolution Flow (Artifact #7)Textual Explanation of Diagram: This flow defines the Phase 3 offline synchronization protocol (FEAT-J02). When a disconnected client reconnects and replays its IndexedDB mutation queue sequentially, the backend enforces live RBAC authorization first, merges non-overlapping field edits automatically, and returns a structured 409 Conflict diff only when the exact same field was modified on the server after the client's base_field_timestamp.Code snippetflowchart TD
    OFF["User Edits Task While Offline\n(Create Task, Comment, or Scalar Field Edit)"] --> IDB["Append to IndexedDB Mutation Queue\n{mutation_id, task_id, field_deltas, base_field_timestamps}"]
    IDB --> NET{"Network Reconnected?"}
    NET -->|"No"| OFF
    NET -->|"Yes (Replay FIFO)"| SEND["Send Queued Mutation to Backend\nwith X-Mutation-Id & base_field_timestamps"]

    SEND --> AUTH{"1. Live RBAC Check:\nDoes Actor STILL Have Permission?"}
    AUTH -->|"No (403 Permission Revoked While Offline)"| QUAR["Quarantine Mutation in Local\n'Unsynced Personal Recovery Drawer'\n(Allow Save to Personal Workspace or Copy Text)"]

    AUTH -->|"Yes"| IDEMP{"2. X-Mutation-Id Already Processed?"}
    IDEMP -->|"Yes"| ACK["Return Cached 200 OK & Dequeue Item"]

    IDEMP -->|"No"| FCHK{"3. For Each Edited Field f:\nIs server.field_updated_at[f] > client.base_timestamp[f]?"}
    FCHK -->|"No (Or Different Fields Edited)"| MERGE["Auto-Merge Non-Overlapping Fields\nCommit Transaction & Emit DomainEvent (200 OK)"]
    MERGE --> ACK

    FCHK -->|"Yes (Same Field Modified Concurrently)"| CONF409["Return HTTP 409 Conflict\n{conflicting_fields: [{field, server_val, server_actor, client_val}]}"]
    CONF409 --> UI_RES["Open Side-by-Side Conflict Resolver Drawer in UI"]
    UI_RES --> CHOICE{"User Selects Resolution"}
    CHOICE -->|"Keep Server Version"| ACK
    CHOICE -->|"Overwrite With My Version"| FORCE["Resend PATCH with updated base_timestamp = server.updated_at"]
    CHOICE -->|"Keep Server & Save Mine as Comment"| CMT["POST /tasks/{id}/comments with Offline Text"]
    FORCE --> MERGE
    CMT --> ACK
8. Query and Four-View Architecture8.1 Shared Canonical Query AST Contract ([Recommended Architectural Decision])List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline views never query separate ad-hoc filter endpoints. All four views share a single canonical Query Specification AST (ViewQuerySpec) stored in saved_views.query_spec_jsonb and serialized cleanly into URL search parameters when modified transiently:JSON{
  "filter": {
    "conjunction": "AND",
    "conditions": [
      { "field": "status_category", "operator": "IN", "value": ["TODO", "IN_PROGRESS"] },
      { "field": "priority", "operator": "IN", "value": ["URGENT", "HIGH"] },
      { "field": "assignee_id", "operator": "EQ", "value": "CURRENT_USER" },
      { "field": "custom.sponsor_tier", "operator": "EQ", "value": "Gold" }
    ]
  },
  "groupBy": "status_id",
  "subGroupBy": "none",
  "sortBy": [
    { "field": "rank_key", "direction": "ASC" },
    { "field": "id", "direction": "ASC" }
  ],
  "includeSubtasks": "NESTED",
  "includeBacklog": false,
  "dateWindow": { "from": "2026-11-01", "to": "2026-11-30", "includeUnscheduled": true }
}

Frontend and Backend Module Maps9.1 Frontend Stack Evaluation & Justification ([Recommended Architectural Decision])Evaluation CriterionOption A: Vite + React 19 + TypeScript SPA/PWA + TanStack Router & Query (RECOMMENDED)Option B: Next.js App Router (SSR / React Server Components)Architectural VerdictRendering & Product Fit100% of our platform sits behind authentication and requires instant (<50ms) client-side view switching (List ↔ Board ↔ Calendar ↔ Timeline), persistent WebSocket rooms, and keyboard roving-tabindex focus.Optimized for public SEO content and server-rendered page transitions. Mixing RSC server trees with a live WebSocket-mutated client cache and offline IndexedDB queue creates dual-state friction.Select Option A (Vite + React SPA/PWA). Zero server-component serialization overhead; instant client view transitions.Antigravity CLI Velocity & TestingSub-second HMR dev server startup, straightforward Mock Service Worker (MSW) interception in browser/Playwright, and clean static bundle output deployable to any CDN or container.Slower build/HMR cycles, complex MSW setup across Node server actions vs. browser client components.Select Option A. Maximizes Antigravity CLI iteration speed and deterministic contract mocking.Future Offline Layer (FEAT-J02)Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa) + single client state layer backed by IndexedDB (Dexie.js / TanStack Query persister) works seamlessly across all routes.Offline Service Workers frequently conflict with Next.js RSC flight payload fetches on route navigation.Select Option A. Frontend Architectural Rules for Antigravity CLI:Strict Contract Boundary: Feature components must never call fetch() directly; all reads/writes go through typed domain hooks in features/*/api/ that automatically attach X-Community-Id, X-Mutation-Id, and (when active) X-Preview-Role-Id.Normalized Client Entity Cache: Tasks are normalized by task.id in the client cache so an optimistic status change or incoming WebSocket TASK_UPDATED event updates List, Board, Calendar, Timeline, My Work, and the open Task Peek Drawer simultaneously with zero duplicate network fetches.Centralized Permission Guards: UI components never write if (user.role === 'OWNER'). They must use useCan('project:configure_workflow') or task.effective_permissions.canEditDefinition, and wrap restricted buttons in <PermissionLockedControl reason="{...}"> so keyboard and screen-reader users always receive a clear explanation tooltip.9.3 Backend Logical Module Map (Technology-Independent Specification)Plaintextbackend/

Technology Options and Justified RecommendationsWhile the domain architecture and API contracts remain technology-independent so the backend developer can work idioms-first, the table below separates Mandatory Behavioral Specifications from Justified Technology Recommendations:Architectural LayerMandatory Behavioral Specification ([Established Requirement] / [Recommended Architectural Decision])Recommended Technology Option ([Candidate Implementation Technique])Alternatives Considered & Trade-Off Rationale1. Primary Relational DatabaseFull ACID transactions (READ COMMITTED / REPEATABLE READ), composite foreign keys, atomic sequence increment (UPDATE ... RETURNING), indexed JSONB storage for custom fields and field timestamps, and full-text search.PostgreSQL 16 / 17MySQL / MariaDB: Lacks native GIN indexes on JSONB and transactional SET LOCAL Row-Level Security policies.MongoDB / Document DB: Lacks referential integrity across multi-entity hierarchies and cross-project dependency joins.2. Backend Runtime & API FrameworkStrictly typed OpenAPI 3.1 contract generation/validation, native WebSocket room broadcasting, middleware pipeline for SecurityContext, and lightweight background worker loop for the domain_events outbox.TypeScript (Node.js 22 LTS + Fastify / NestJS) OR Go (Chi / Echo + sqlc) (Backend developer's preference)Both TypeScript and Go excel at JSON/WebSocket concurrency and compile clean OpenAPI contracts. TypeScript allows sharing Zod/OpenAPI schema tooling with Antigravity CLI; Go offers minimal memory footprint.3. Realtime & Rate-Limit StateSub-500ms workspace room event fan-out and token-bucket API rate limiting per user/IP.In-Process Memory + PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY (Single Node MVP) → Redis 7 Pub/Sub (Multi-Node Scale)For a 70–90 user community running on 1–2 backend instances, Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY + in-memory WebSocket rooms require zero extra infrastructure containers. Abstract behind a PubSubBroker interface so Redis can drop in later.4. File & Attachment StoragePrivate bucket storage supporting short-lived (15m) pre-signed PUT and GET URLs with Content-Type and Content-Length enforcement.S3-Compatible Object Storage (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3, or self-hosted MinIO)Storing binary files inside PostgreSQL BYTEA bloats database backups and degrades query buffer cache. Direct browser-to-S3 pre-signed uploads keep backend RAM flat.5. Frontend Application Stack (Antigravity CLI)Fast client-side view switching across 4 views, normalized optimistic entity cache, URL-serialized filter AST, WCAG 2.2 AA accessible primitives, and Phase 3 IndexedDB offline persistence.Vite 6 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + TanStack Router & TanStack Query + Radix UI / React Aria + @dnd-kit + MSWAvoids Next.js RSC hydration friction and heavy opinionated widget kits (MUI/AntD) that fight custom keyboard roving-tabindex navigation and 36px high-density task rows.12. Migration, Compatibility and Deferred-Feature Considerations (Artifact #12)To guarantee that shipping Phase 1 (M1.1 → M1.3) never requires a breaking database rewrite or API v2 overhaul when Phase 2 (Intake Forms, CSV Import, Extended Custom Fields) and Phase 3 (Automations, Status Sign-Offs, Webhooks, Offline Sync) are built, the following Day-1 Schema & Contract Compatibility Rules must be enforced in Migration 001:Tenant & Workspace Scoping Columns (Migration 001): Every operational table is created with community_id UUID NOT NULL and workspace_id UUID NOT NULL from Day 1, even if the initial 70–90 person launch operates within a single default Community record (default-community).Reserved Nullable Columns on Core Entities (Migration 001):On tasks: Include start_date DATE NULL, due_date DATE NULL, milestone_id UUID NULL, cycle_id UUID NULL, custom_fields_jsonb JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', field_updated_at_jsonb JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', and archive_batch_id UUID NULL.On workflow_statuses: Include requires_signoff BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE and required_entry_capability VARCHAR(64) NULL.On domain_events: Include workspace_seq_id BIGINT NOT NULL, is_automation BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, before_jsonb JSONB, and after_jsonb JSONB.Additive-Only API Evolution Rule: Shared REST endpoints (/api/v1/*) and WebSocket event payloads must follow additive-only schema evolution:New optional fields may be added to response DTOs in M1.2, M1.3, Phase 2, and Phase 3.Existing field names, enum values (BACKLOG | TODO | IN_PROGRESS | DONE | CANCELED), and status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429) must never be renamed or repurposed without bumping the route namespace.Outbox Table Partitioning & Archival Strategy: Because domain_events is append-only, index (workspace_id, workspace_seq_id DESC) for fast WebSocket catch-up queries and (entity_type, entity_id, created_at DESC) for Task Activity Drawer queries. Background worker M14 marks processed_at = NOW() once real-time/notification fan-out completes, allowing cold archival of raw outbox payloads older than 365 days while keeping task changelog summaries intact.13. Key Architectural Risks and Their MitigationsRisk ID & CategoryFailure Mode & Trigger ScenarioSeverityConcrete Architectural MitigationRISK-01: Cross-Tenant or Personal Workspace Data LeakA developer writes a search, dashboard, or file-download query that filters by project_id or task_key without filtering by community_id and workspace_id membership.CriticalRequire a non-nullable SecurityContext parameter on every repository method signature, enforce composite (community_id, workspace_id) foreign keys, and enable PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies in transaction-local scope (SET LOCAL). Back with automated negative authorization CI tests.RISK-02: Fractional Index (rank_key) Length Explosion or TiesRepeatedly dragging cards into the exact same top slot of a column 100+ times causes rank_key string length to grow past 50 characters, or two users drop cards into the same gap simultaneously.MediumUse base-62 fractional indexing with 30-bit random jitter on simultaneous inserts, always break ties deterministically with ORDER BY rank_key ASC, id ASC, and trigger an asynchronous column rebalance whenever LENGTH(rank_key) > 32.RISK-03: Automation Infinite Loops in Phase 3Rule A changes Status to In Progress when Assignee changes, and Rule B changes Assignee when Status becomes In Progress, causing an infinite storm of database writes and notifications.HighEvery DomainEvent carries is_automation: boolean and hop_count: smallint. The M15 Automation Engine strictly ignores any event where is_automation == true (hop_count >= 1), guaranteeing single-hop termination.RISK-04: Frontend / Backend Integration DriftBecause Antigravity CLI and the Backend Developer work in parallel, slight differences in filter query parameters, error payloads, or WebSocket event names cause integration failures at milestone boundaries.HighTreat /contracts/openapi.yaml and /contracts/ws-events.schema.json as the single source of truth. Generate Antigravity CLI TypeScript types and MSW mock validators directly from those files before writing view or controller code.RISK-05: Stale WebSocket State or Missed Events on Mobile/Campus Wi-FiA user's laptop sleeps or mobile connection drops for 30 seconds while teammates move 10 cards on the board, leaving the user interacting with stale column positions.Medium-HighTrack monotonic workspace_seq_id per workspace. On socket reconnect or window focus, immediately call GET /workspaces/{id}/events?since_seq={lastSeenSeq} to replay missed deltas in order (or trigger a clean TanStack Query refetch if >500 events elapsed).RISK-06: Silent Loss of User Work on Offline Permission RevocationA user edits a detailed task description offline while a Workspace Owner removes them from the workspace; on reconnect, a naive sync engine discards the 403 failed mutation.HighWhen M16 returns 403 PERMISSION_REVOKED_OFFLINE, the frontend moves the rejected payload into a persistent local Unsynced Personal Recovery Store and displays a banner allowing the user to save the draft into their private Personal Workspace or copy the text.14. Architecture Decision Register (Artifact #9)ADR IDDecision TitleClassificationAlternatives ConsideredChosen Decision & RationaleADR-01Backend Deployment Topology[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Distributed Microservices (Auth, Tasks, Search, Notifications)2. Modular Monolith + Async WorkerOption 2: Modular Monolith + Async Outbox Worker. Eliminates distributed network hops and 2PC complexity while preserving clean module boundaries (M01–M16) for a 70–90+ person community.ADR-02Multi-Community User Identity Model[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. community_id column on users table2. Global users table + community_memberships join tableOption 2: Global users + community_memberships. Allows a single human account to belong to multiple independent communities without duplicating credentials.ADR-03Task & Subtask Persistence Strategy[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Separate tasks and subtasks tables2. Single self-referencing tasks table (parent_task_id, hierarchy_depth 0..2)Option 2: Single tasks table. Subtasks share permanent keys, statuses, assignees, comments, and board/list projections; a unified table halves API and query complexity.ADR-04Permanent Task Keys & Project Moves[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Never change key on project move (OPS-12 stays OPS-12 inside FEST)2. Re-key to target prefix (FEST-45) + permanent task_key_aliases redirect ledgerOption 2: Re-key + task_key_aliases redirect ledger. Preserves project prefix consistency while guaranteeing every historical OPS-12 URL, #OPS-12 link, and search query resolves forever.ADR-05Milestone vs. Task Archetype Representation[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Milestone as a Task.item_type2. Milestone as a ProjectMilestone entity3. Both simultaneouslyOption 2: ProjectMilestone entity only (tasks.milestone_id FK). Eliminates ambiguous duplicate concepts; task archetypes are TASK, DELIVERABLE, BUG, DECISION.ADR-06List & Board Ordering Algorithm[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Integer gap indexing (1000, 2000...)2. Linked-list pointers (next_task_id)3. Lexicographical fractional indexing (rank_key string + id tie-breaker)Option 3: Lexicographical fractional indexing (rank_key). Delivers O(1) single-row writes on drag-and-drop and supports simple SQL ORDER BY rank_key ASC, id ASC without recursive CTEs.ADR-07Domain Events, Changelog & Realtime Fan-Out[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Direct synchronous publish to WebSocket/Email inside HTTP handler2. ACID Transactional Outbox (domain_events table)Option 2: ACID Transactional Outbox. Guarantees that a task mutation and its changelog/WebSocket event commit or roll back atomically.ADR-08Custom Fields Storage Model[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Normalized EAV table (task_custom_field_values)2. Schema-validated custom_fields_jsonb column on tasks with GIN indexOption 2: Validated custom_fields_jsonb on tasks. Avoids N-way EAV join bottlenecks when rendering 100+ rows in List and Board views.ADR-09Offline Sync & Concurrent Edit Resolution[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Full CRDT document state (Yjs/Automerge) across all task records2. Per-field timestamp watermarks (field_updated_at_jsonb) + X-Mutation-Id queue + 409 Conflict Resolver DrawerOption 2: Per-field timestamps + 409 Conflict Resolver. Full CRDTs across relational task schemas add massive overhead; per-field watermarks auto-merge non-overlapping edits and provide clear human resolution for same-field conflicts.ADR-10Frontend Application Framework[Recommended Architectural Decision]1. Next.js App Router (SSR/RSC)2. Vite + React 19 + TypeScript SPA/PWA + TanStack Router & QueryOption 2: Vite + React 19 SPA/PWA. Matches an authenticated, real-time, keyboard-driven workspace app with sub-100ms view switching and Phase 3 IndexedDB offline caching.15. Explicit Unresolved Questions (Artifact #11)While our architecture supports both options via configuration flags so engineering work is not blocked, the following three policy defaults ([Unresolved Stakeholder Decision]) require explicit stakeholder confirmation before locking the final PRD:UNR-ARCH-01 (Conflict 1 Default — Global Admin vs. Personal Workspace Privacy):Question: Should community.settings.personal_workspace_admin_policy be locked to PRIVATE_STRICT (Global Admins can see Personal Workspace storage quotas and suspend accounts, but can never view or break-glass into private Personal Workspace tasks), or should AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS also be permitted on Personal Workspaces?Architect's Recommended Default: Lock to PRIVATE_STRICT (Break-Glass applies only to Shared Workspaces).UNR-ARCH-02 (Conflict 2 Default — Task Editing Policy in Shared Workspaces):Question: When a new Shared Workspace is created, should workspace.settings.task_edit_policy default to CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT (Owners, Coordinators, and Task Creator edit task definitions; Assignees update status/progress/subtasks/comments; ordinary Members comment and create new tasks), or COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER (all workspace members can edit task fields), while allowing the Workspace Owner to toggle between the two in Workspace Settings?Architect's Recommended Default: Default to CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT (with Assignee execution rights) to honor the original specification, with a 1-click Owner toggle to enable COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER.UNR-ARCH-03 (Default Storage Quotas & Audit Retention Window):Question: For the initial 70–90 person community deployment, confirm the default numeric thresholds for:Max single attachment file size (Recommended default: 25 MB).Per-workspace storage quota (Recommended default: 5 GB per Shared Workspace, 500 MB per Personal Workspace).Security Audit Log retention window (Recommended default: 365 days online queryable + CSV archival).

1. Executive Decisions and Important DiscoveriesAtlassian's 2024–2026 Terminology & Packaging Consolidation ("Spaces" and "Work Items"): Official Atlassian documentation has unified Jira Work Management and Jira Software into a single Jira Cloud core, shifting canonical terminology from "Projects" and "Issues" to "Spaces" (Company-managed vs. Team-managed) and "Work Items". However, beneath the unified branding, the architectural divide between Team-Managed Spaces (autonomous, simplified per-space settings) and Company-Managed Spaces (centralized schemes shared across spaces) remains Jira's single biggest source of administrative confusion. Strategic Decision: Our platform will avoid dual project architectures entirely. Every Shared Workspace uses one consistent governance model: simple defaults at the workspace/project level with progressive disclosure for advanced settings.Eight Essential "Missed" Capabilities Discovered During the Audit: Auditing Jira's full capability surface revealed eight high-value, low-learning-curve features that were absent or underspecified in our earlier product scope and should be added to serve our 70–90 person community (spanning engineering, event planning, committees, and study groups):Explicit Watch / Follow Subscriptions (FEAT-A04): Decoupling "who is executing the task" (Assignee) from "who needs updates" (Watchers/Subscribers) with 1-click watch/unwatch.Multi-Select Bulk Edit & Single-Click Task Cloning (FEAT-A07, FEAT-A10): Essential for coordinators duplicating recurring event checklists or reassigning 15 tasks when a committee member changes roles.Lightweight Work-Item Archetypes (FEAT-A01): Instead of Jira's heavy "Issue Type Schemes," provide a standard Task default alongside 3 lightweight, icon-differentiated archetypes (Task, Milestone/Deliverable, Bug/Issue, Request/Decision) that share the same underlying model.Milestones / Target Buckets (FEAT-B05): A simpler, cross-domain alternative to software-only "Versions/Releases" that works equally well for Hackathon Day, Semester Exam Week, or v1.2 Launch.Lightweight Project Summary & Workload Rollup View (FEAT-E01, FEAT-E02): A built-in project overview showing task completion %, overdue count, and tasks per assignee without requiring users to configure JQL dashboard gadgets.CSV Task Import & Export (FEAT-J01): Critical for migrating existing community spreadsheets (Google Sheets / Excel) into a project on Day 1 and providing zero-lock-in data portability.Shareable Intake Forms (FEAT-I01 — Phase 2): Allowing a project or committee to publish a simple Workspace Intake Form (e.g., Submit Event Proposal or Report a Bug) without adopting Jira Service Management's heavy helpdesk portal.Single-Step Sign-Off / Approval Status Gate (FEAT-D03 — Phase 3): A lightweight "Requires Coordinator/Owner Sign-Off" toggle on a workflow status for budget or event approvals, avoiding full enterprise ITSM change-management boards.Preserving the Initial Production-Release Target for All Four Views via Staged Sub-Milestones: All four views (List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline) remain mandatory requirements for the Initial Production Release (Phase 1). To de-risk parallel development between the backend developer and Antigravity CLI, Phase 1 is structured into three sequential internal engineering milestones (M1.1 Core Spine + List & Board → M1.2 Calendar & Timeline + Summary/CSV → M1.3 Governance, Recovery & Production Hardening). The initial production release is not declared complete until all three sub-milestones pass acceptance criteria.Decisive Exclusions Prevent Enterprise Bloat: Over 35% of Jira's audited footprint consists of enterprise overhead—JQL syntax parsers, Workflow Schemes with post-function scripts, ITIL Incident/Problem/Change command centers, Opsgenie on-call rotations, CMDB hardware asset registers, and source-code commit parsers. Explicitly excluding these preserves our primary differentiator: broad work-management utility with a near-zero learning curve.2. Documented Scope and Limits of the Jira Capability Audit2.1 Six Audited Jira Product ScopesScope IDJira Product / Capability TierPrimary Target Audience in Atlassian EcosystemRelevance to Our 70–90 Person Community PlatformScope AJira Cloud Core & Work Management (Business/Operations Spaces, List, Board, Calendar, Basic Timeline, Forms, Templates, Core Work Items)Cross-functional business teams, event organizers, operations, marketing, and general task tracking.Primary Benchmark (High Relevance). Directly informs our 4 core views, task metadata, templates, and non-technical usability.Scope BJira Software (Agile & Engineering) (Backlogs, Scrum Sprints, Kanban Boards, Versions/Releases, Story Point Estimation, Velocity/Burndown/CFD Reports, DevOps Links)Software engineering squads practicing Scrum or Kanban.Selective Relevance. Kanban mechanics, backlog triage, estimates, and lightweight milestones apply broadly; strict Scrum ceremonies (burndown charts, velocity math, Git branch triggers) should remain optional or excluded.Scope CJira Platform & Administration (Global vs. Space Permissions, Permission/Issue Security Schemes, Workflows, Custom Fields, Automation Engine, Audit Logs, REST APIs, Webhooks)Site Administrators, Space Owners, and Platform Integrators.High Architectural Relevance (Requires Simplification). We need the capabilities (custom roles, custom fields, automations, audit logs, webhooks) without Jira's fragmented "Scheme" indirection.Scope DJira Service Management (JSM) (Customer Portals, Agent Queues, SLA Clocks, Approvals, ITIL Incident/Problem/Change Management, On-Call Schedules, Assets/CMDB, Knowledge Base)IT Helpdesks, Customer Support Centers, and SRE Incident Response Teams.Low Relevance (Except Intake Forms & Simple Approvals). Full helpdesk ticketing, SLA breach clocks, and hardware asset tracking are outside our scope; only lightweight request intake forms and simple status sign-offs are relevant.Scope EAdvanced Planning, Enterprise & AI (Plans, Goals, Rovo AI) (Cross-Project Advanced Roadmaps/Plans, Scenario Sandbox, Capacity Planning, Atlassian Goals/Home, Rovo AI Agents & Summarization)Enterprise PMOs (500–50,000 users) and paid AI add-on subscribers.Low-to-Moderate Relevance. Cross-project dependencies and high-level goal/milestone rollups are useful; multi-scenario sandbox roadmaps and paid AI agents are excluded from core scope.Scope FAtlassian Marketplace & Ecosystem Extensibility (Atlassian Forge, Connect Apps, OAuth 2.0 integrations, 5,000+ third-party plugins for timesheets, diagrams, and test management)Third-party commercial plugin vendors and enterprise customizers.Out of Scope for Initial Release (Except Webhooks/REST API). Building a multi-tenant third-party code execution sandbox (like Forge) is unnecessary for a 70–90 person community; clean REST APIs and outbound Webhooks suffice.2.2 Defensible Audit Boundary and Explicit ExclusionsCoverage Boundary: This audit covers documented capabilities in Jira Cloud (Free, Standard, Premium, and Enterprise tiers) and Jira Service Management Cloud as documented on support.atlassian.com and developer.atlassian.com as of October 2026.Explicit Audit Exclusions:Legacy / Discontinued On-Premise Editions: Jira Server (end-of-life) and Jira Data Center infrastructure clustering.Standalone Sister Products: Jira Align (enterprise SAFe portfolio management), Bitbucket pipelines, Confluence document wiki internals, Trello, and Loom video recording internals.Third-Party Marketplace Internals: Proprietary implementations of third-party Marketplace apps (e.g., Tempo Timesheets, ScriptRunner, Xray).Unverified / Undocumented Internals: In accordance with Research Prompt 01, no proprietary source code or decompiled bundles were inspected; all findings rely strictly on primary public documentation and observable product behavior.3. Comprehensive Capability Inventory and Source RegisterDuring our research, we catalogued 10 core capability families (A through J) required by the prompt plus 2 additional families (K and L) prominent in current 2026 Jira Cloud documentation:Family A: Work-Item Lifecycle & Details (FEAT-A01 to FEAT-A10) — Work types, CRUD/assignment, core metadata, comments/mentions/watchers, attachments/changelog, subtasks/links, cloning, fractional ranking, time tracking/worklogs, and bulk operations/archiving/trash.Family B: Work Hierarchy & Project Planning (FEAT-B01 to FEAT-B08) — Tenant/workspace/project/list hierarchy, configurable nesting depth, backlog triage, sprints/iterations, milestones/releases, cross-project links, timeline/roadmaps, and capacity/scenario planning.Family C: Views & Information Retrieval (FEAT-C01 to FEAT-C08) — List & Board views, Calendar & Timeline views, Personal Dashboard, Saved Views (Personal vs. Shared), Search & Faceted Filters (vs. JQL), Swimlanes/Quick Filters/Card customization, and Permanent Task Keys with historical alias lookup.Family D: Workflows & Customization (FEAT-D01 to FEAT-D07) — 5-category status model, transition rules, validators/approvals, custom fields & field visibility, project/task templates, board column/WIP/working-day settings, and categorized workspace/project settings.Family E: Reporting & Progress (FEAT-E01 to FEAT-E07) — Completion & overdue summaries, assignee workload distribution, milestone/release progress, Scrum burndown/velocity charts, Kanban cycle-time/CFD charts, auto-subscriptions, configurable notification rules & deadline reminders, real-time WebSocket updates & activity feeds, and external chat integrations.Family G: Governance & Administration (FEAT-G01 to FEAT-G08) — Community Admin vs. Workspace Owner hierarchy, email/password + Google OAuth + member invites, RBAC & custom roles,Coordinator default inclusion, privacy/security boundaries, role preview simulator, security audit log, and 30-day trash/retention.Family H: Automation & Extensibility (FEAT-H01 to FEAT-H05) — Trigger-Condition-Action rule builder, scheduled deadline reminders, loop prevention/idempotency/audit logs, rule actor attribution, and outbound webhooks/REST API.Family I: Service Management & Request Intake (FEAT-I01 to FEAT-I05) — Shareable request intake forms, customer portals & agent queues, workflow approval steps, SLA timers, and ITIL incident/problem/change/asset management.Family J: Platform Operation & Data Portability (FEAT-J01 to FEAT-J06) — CSV Feature-by-Feature Selection MatrixLegend for Decision Classes & Matrix CodesDecision Classes:D1 — Required for Initial Production Release (Phase 1): Essential for a complete, secure, and usable v1 release (delivered across sequential Phase 1 sub-milestones M1.1, M1.2, M1.3).D2 — Initial-Release Enhancement (Phase 1.x): High-value, low-risk capability included in the initial release window once M1.1 core dependencies are satisfied.D3 — Phase 2 or Phase 3 (Planned Roadmap): Deferred to prevent blocking the initial release, with structural prerequisites embedded in Day-1 schemas.D4 — Optional Extension or Community-Specific Module: Designed as an opt-in workspace plugin/toggle rather than enabled by default.D5 — Explicitly Excluded: Omitted permanently or indefinitely because it introduces high complexity or enterprise bloat with low community value.Applicability Roles: ADM = Global Admin, OWN = Workspace Owner, CRD = Coordinator, MEM = Member, ALL = All Roles.Feature IDFeature Name & Concise DefinitionFamily & ScopeUser Problem Solved & SourceRole FitValue / Effort / UX LoadData-Model, Backend & Frontend RequirementsPermissions, Privacy & DependenciesDecision & Delivery PhaseAcceptance Criteria & Deferred CompatibilityConfidence & Open QuestionsFEAT-A01Lightweight Work-Item Archetypes: Configurable task classification (Task, Milestone, Bug/Issue, Decision/Request) sharing one schema.Family A / Scope A, BDistinguishes bug reports or key decisions from standard tasks without Jira's complex Issue Type Schemes [SRC-01, SRC-03].ALLVal: HighEff: LowUX: LowDB: item_type enum/FK on tasks.BE: CRUD validation.FE: Icon+label selector in task composer & filter bar.Perm: Configurable by OWN/CRD.Dep: Core Task schema.D2 (Initial Enhancement — M1.2)AC: Users can filter by archetype; icon displays alongside permanent key.Compat: Single tasks table avoids multi-table joins.High (Verified). Newly Discovered Requirements Evaluation (Including Non-Software Community Fit)We evaluated all 15 candidate capabilities from Section 6 of the prompt against both software engineering squads and non-software community groups (hackathon/fest committees, student operations, outreach campaigns, and study groups):Candidate CapabilityNon-Software & Community UtilityEngineering / Technical UtilityRecommended Decision & Rationale1. Backlog Management (FEAT-B02)Lets an event committee dump 50 brainstormed ideas into a Backlog bucket without cluttering this week's active Todo board.Essential for staging unscheduled bugs and features before moving them into active development.Adopt in Initial Release (D1 — M1.1). Implement via the canonical Backlog status category and a 1-click collapsible Backlog tray on Boards/Lists rather than a separate complex screen.2. Sprint or Iteration Support (FEAT-B03)Study groups use "Weekly Study Cycles"; however, event and operations committees think in deadlines and phases, not Scrum sprints.High value for dev teams running 1–2 week iterations.Adopt as Opt-In Project Module (D4 — Phase 2/3). Keep disabled by default so non-software teams never see "Sprint" jargon; allow software projects to toggle on Cycles / Iterations.3. Milestones & Release Planning (FEAT-B04)High Value: Committees organize around concrete milestones ("Sponsor Pitch Deck Lock", "Main Stage Day 1").High Value: Dev teams organize around version launches ("v1.0 MVP Release").Adopt in Initial Release Window (D2 — M1.2). Name the capability Milestones (rather than "Fix Versions") so the mental model fits both events and software releases seamlessly.4. Work-Item Types Beyond Generic Task (FEAT-A01)Committees need to distinguish a Decision Needed or Purchase Request from a standard Task.Dev teams need to distinguish a Bug from a Feature Task.Adopt in Initial Release Window (D2 — M1.2). Provide a lightweight Type Badge (Task, Milestone, Bug/Issue, Decision/Request) without changing field schemas per type.5. Components or Work-Area GroupingAlready solved by our Lists (Logistics, Marketing, Finance) and Labels.Solved by Lists (Frontend, Backend, API) and Labels.Exclude as Separate Entity (D5). Adding Jira "Components" alongside Projects, Lists, Labels, and Custom Fields creates redundant taxonomy confusion.6. Watch / Follow Subscriptions (FEAT-A04)A faculty advisor or lead coordinator wants to follow progress on a high-stakes task (FEST-01) without being assigned to do the work.Tech leads watch critical architecture or bug tasks across teams.Adopt in Initial Release (D1 — M1.1). Add a 1-click Watch / Following bell icon and watcher avatar list in the Task Peek Drawer.7. Bulk Updates & Task Cloning (FEAT-A07, FEAT-A10)High Value: Event leads clone standard 10-subtask checklists for each guest speaker and bulk-reassign tasks when volunteers shift shifts.High Value: Bulk-moving unfinished tasks or bulk-labeling issues during triage.Adopt in Initial Release Window (D1/D2 — M1.2). Multi-select floating bar + 1-click Duplicate Task (with subtasks) saves massive manual effort.8. CSV Import / Export (FEAT-J01)Critical Onboarding Bridge: Almost every existing community club or committee currently tracks tasks in Google Sheets or Excel.Useful for exporting task lists for academic/project reports or migrating from Trello/Jira CSVs.Adopt (D2 CSV Export in M1.2; D3 Guided CSV Import in M1.3/Phase 2). Eliminates cold-start data entry friction.9. Basic Project Reports (FEAT-E01)Coordinators need a quick visual check: "Are we 80% ready for tomorrow's event? Who is overloaded with 15 tasks?"Leads need to see open vs. closed tasks and blocker counts.Adopt Lightweight Project Overview (D2 — M1.2). Ship a zero-config Project Overview panel showing Completion %, Overdue count, Milestone bars, and Tasks per Assignee.10. Request-Intake Forms & Approval Steps (FEAT-I01, FEAT-D03)High Value: Enables "Submit a Club Budget Request" or "Propose a Workshop" forms with a simple Coordinator sign-off toggle.Enables structured "Report a Bug" intake forms from external testers.Adopt in Planned Phases (D3 — Forms in Phase 2; Single-Step Sign-Off in Phase 3). Solves real community intake workflows without JSM complexity.11. Time Tracking & Work Logs (FEAT-A09)Volunteers and students do not log billable timesheets in 15-minute increments.Developers prefer lightweight complexity estimates (Points or T-shirt/Hours) over stopwatch timers.Exclude (D5). Retain only the simple single-field Estimate attribute (FEAT-A03).12. Goals & High-Level Work SummariesCovered by Projects + Milestones (FEAT-B04) + Project Overview (FEAT-E01).Covered by Milestones + Project Overview.Exclude Standalone OKR/Atlas Hierarchy (D5). Avoids adding a 5th hierarchy layer above Projects.13. Custom Dashboard Widgets (FEAT-E03)Non-technical users rarely configure JQL pie charts or 2D filter matrix gadgets.Fixed high-signal views outperform custom widget grids.Exclude Custom Widget Builder (D5). Rely on My Work (FEAT-C03) and Project Overview (FEAT-E01).14. Integration Webhooks (FEAT-H02)Posts automated event/campaign updates into community Discord or WhatsApp/Telegram bridges.Posts task/bug updates into engineering Slack/Discord channels.Adopt in Phase 3 (D3). Simple outbound HTTPS webhooks with Slack/Discord payload presets.15. Task Templates & Reusable View Presets (FEAT-D05, FEAT-C04)Lets committees save a "Speaker Onboarding Checklist" task template and pin "This Week's Deadlines" shared views.Lets dev teams save a "Bug Report Template" with pre-filled reproduction steps.Adopt (D1 Project Templates & Shared Views in Phase 1; D3 Reusable Task Templates in Phase 2).7. Preserve the UX Strategy & Guardrails Against Feature CreepEvery capability selected in Sections 4–6 has been audited against the UX architecture established in Research Prompt 03. To guarantee that adding features like Watchers, Milestones, Archetypes, Bulk Edit, and Intake Forms never degrades usability, the following binding UX constraints govern implementation:Progressive Disclosure Ceiling (Maximum 5 Default Composer Controls): Even after adding Work-Item Archetypes (FEAT-A01), Milestones (FEAT-B04), and Custom Fields (FEAT-D04), the Quick-Create Composer (C) and inline List creation row must not add extra mandatory inputs. Archetype defaults silently to Task (changeable via a small leading icon button), and Milestone/Custom Fields reside inside the expandable + More properties pill or Task Peek Drawer.One Canonical Task Model Across All Four Views: Milestones, Archetypes, Subtasks, and Dependencies are attributes of the single canonical Task entity—never separate siloed objects. Switching between List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline projects the exact same filtered task array in under 100ms.Strict Isolation of Personal Exploration from Shared Configuration: Adding Board Swimlanes (FEAT-C06) and Quick Filters follows the exact Copy-on-Write Shared View rule: toggling a swimlane or filter on a Shared View updates only the user's local URL/session draft (Modified • [Reset] [Save as Personal View]) until an Owner/Coordinator explicitly clicks [Update Shared View].WCAG 2.2 AA Non-Dragging Parity (SC 2.5.7): Every interactive capability—including new Milestone assignment, Timeline bar scheduling, and Bulk selection—must be 100% operable via single-pointer clicks and keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow roving tabindex, Space, Enter, Escape).Hypotheses & Validation Over Arbitrary Numerical Claims: All performance and usability thresholds (such as <3 min first-task completion, <50ms optimistic UI response, and SUS >= 75) are treated as measurable product hypotheses to be validated using the 10-user pilot protocol defined in Prompt 03 Section 11.8. Reconciling Conflicting Requirements Before Architecture FreezeBelow is the systematic resolution of the 10 architectural and product tensions prior to freezing the shared backend/frontend contracts:#Conflict AreaEstablished RequirementCore Conflict or Trade-OffRecommended Product DecisionBackend Contract / Data-Model ConsequenceFrontend (Antigravity CLI) UX ConsequenceStakeholder Sign-Off Needed?1Global Admin Visibility vs. Personal Workspace PrivacyGlobal administrator role + self-serve Personal Workspaces.Unrestricted admin access destroys user trust in Personal Workspaces as private scratchpads; zero admin visibility prevents quota/abuse management.Strict Content Privacy for Personal Workspaces. Global Admins see only aggregate metadata (Owner, Created Date, Storage MB, Task Count) for Personal Workspaces, never task titles/contents. Audited Break-Glass applies only to Shared Workspaces.Enforce workspace.type == 'PERSONAL' => requester_id == owner_id in task/file middleware even for GLOBAL_ADMIN. Expose /admin/workspaces/{id}/break-glass only for type == 'SHARED'.Render Personal • Private to You lock badge in header; Admin Console hides "Break-Glass" button on Personal rows.Yes (Confirm Privacy Guarantee).2Workspace-Owner Authority vs. Global Security RestrictionsWorkspace owners control workspace members, roles, and settings; platform requires security and auditability.If Owners can disable audit logging, bypass community auth policies, or invite unauthenticated external users when prohibited, community security breaks.Global Security Floor + Workspace Autonomy Ceiling. Global Admins set immutable community floors (Allowed Auth Providers, Max Upload Size, Audit Retention, Shared Workspace Creation Policy). Within those bounds, Workspace Owners have 100% autonomy over members, Coordinators, workflows, and views.Community-level policy settings take precedence in API validation; Workspace Owners cannot delete or mute audit_logs records.Workspace Settings displays inherited community limits as read-only info badges ("Max file size: 25 MB set by Community Admin").No (Standard Security Practice).3Coordinator Powers vs. Task Creator / Assignee PermissionsCoordinators included by default (removable by Owner); creators and assignees manage their tasks.Ambiguity when a Member creates a task, assigns another Member, and a Coordinator or third Member attempts to edit or delete it.Collaborative Execution Parity + Scoped Structural Guard. Any workspace member can update execution fields (Status, Priority, Due Date, Assignee, Comments). Constraints (mandatory requirements that must exist in the Phase 1 contract so Phase 2/3 features do not require destructive rewrites) from Candidate Implementation Techniques (flexible engineering choices left to the backend or frontend developer):Deferred CapabilityProven Structural Constraint (Mandatory in Phase 1 Contract)Candidate Implementation Technique (Developer Choice)1. Multi-Community Tenancy (FEAT-B01)Every top-level entity (workspaces, users, roles, audit_logs) must be scoped to a community_id tenant identifier in API routes/claims and data relationships.Candidate Techniques: Shared PostgreSQL tables with community_id foreign keys + Row-Level Security (RLS), OR application-layer tenant query middleware.2. Permanent Task Keys & Moves (FEAT-C07)Tasks must have an immutable internal primary ID (UUID/ULID) separate from their mutable display key (PREFIX-NUM), plus an alias lookup mapping historical keys to the internal ID.Candidate Techniques: Dedicated task_key_aliases (alias_key PK, task_id FK) table + PostgreSQL UPDATE ... RETURNING per-project sequence counter.3. Custom Roles (FEAT-G02b)All API authorization checks and frontend UI guards must evaluate granular capability strings (task:create, view:update_shared) rather than checking hardcoded role names (role == 'OWNER').Candidate Techniques: Bitmask integer encoding vs. JSONB/text-array of capability strings cached in the user's workspace session context.4. Fast List/Board Reordering (FEAT-A08)Task ordering must support single-item rank updates (O(1) write per move) without re-indexing thousands of sibling rows on every drag-and-drop operation.Candidate Techniques: Lexicographical fractional indexing strings (lexorank / base-62 midpoint strings) vs. floating-point gap allocation with background rebalancing.5. Automations, Webhooks & Snapshot Restore (FEAT-H01, FEAT-H02, FEAT-A10b)Every state-mutating transaction in Phase 1 must record a structured domain event containing {event_id, workspace_seq_id, actor_id, entity_type, entity_id, before_state, after_state, timestamp, is_automation}.Candidate Techniques: Transactional outbox table (domain_events) polled by a background worker vs. PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY or Redis Streams consumer.6. Scoped Offline Editing & Conflict Resolution (FEAT-J02)Phase 1 task mutation APIs (POST/PATCH) must accept a client-generated idempotency key (X-Mutation-Id), accept a base_version / per-field timestamp watermark, and return a structured 409 Conflict payload when a targeted field was modified more recently on the server.Candidate Techniques: field_updated_at JSONB map ({"status": "2026-10-29T...", "description": "..."}) on the tasks row vs. separate field-revision rows; client storage via Dexie.js / IndexedDB vs. TanStack Query Persist client.10. Concise Implementation-Readiness Criteria & Quality Strategy12.1 The Four Pre-Implementation & Milestone Quality GatesMarkdown### GATE 1: FEATURE COVERAGE & TRACEABILITY AUDIT (Before Freezing PRD)
[ ] Every established user requirement and all selected `D1, D2, D3, D4` capabilities from Prompt 04 have a unique `FEAT-ID` mapped to a specific milestone (`M1.1`, `M1.2`, `M1.3`, `Phase 2`, `Phase 3`, `Phase 4`).
[ ] All four views (`List, Board, Calendar, Timeline`) are explicitly scheduled inside Phase 1 (`M1.1` and `M1.2`) prior to Initial Production Release sign-off.
[ ] Explicitly excluded features (`D5`) are documented with clear rationale so neither developer builds out-of-scope functionality.

### GATE 2: CROSS-DOCUMENT CONSISTENCY & CONFLICT RESOLUTION (Before Schema Freeze)
[ ] All 10 architectural conflicts (Section 8) have locked defaults reflected identically in the UX specification, RBAC permission table, and database schema.
[ ] Terminology is 100% unified across docs: `Community -> Workspace (Personal | Shared) -> Project -> List -> Task -> Subtask`, `Coordinator`, `Milestone`, and the 5 canonical status categories (`Backlog, Todo, In Progress, Done, Canceled`).

### GATE 3: FRONTEND / BACKEND CONTRACT & MOCK VALIDATION (Before Coding Each Milestone)
[ ] Shared `openapi.yaml` (REST) and `ws-events.schema.json` (WebSocket) are committed and pass schema linting.
[ ] Day-1 architectural primitives (`community_id`, `task_key_aliases`, `effective_capabilities`, `rank_key`, `domain_events`, `X-Mutation-Id`, `field_updated_at`) are present in the `M1.1` contract.
[ ] Antigravity CLI Mock Service Worker (MSW) handlers validate against the exact OpenAPI response schemas, including `403`, `404`, and `409 Conflict` payloads.

### GATE 4: PRODUCTION LAUNCH READINESS REVIEW (At End of Milestone M1.3)
[ ] All 4 views pass functional, performance (`<400ms` p95 API, `<50ms` optimistic UI), and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility checks (`0` critical/serious axe violations; full keyboard & no-drag operability).
[ ] Security & authorization boundary suite passes 100% (Personal Workspace privacy from Global Admin, Coordinator removal by Owner, cross-workspace search isolation, signed attachment URLs).
[ ] Backup restoration, 10-second Undo, and 30-day Trash recovery are verified end-to-end on staging data.
12.2 Risk-Based Verification Strategy (High Signal, Zero Redundant Bloat)Instead of hundreds of brittle manual UI checklists, concentrate automated and manual testing on 6 high-risk failure boundaries:Authorization & Privacy Boundary Matrix (Automated API Tests): Parameterized integration test suite verifying that (a) User A cannot read/search/mutate User B's Personal Workspace (even with a GLOBAL_ADMIN token), (b) a removed Coordinator immediately loses REST and active WebSocket access to that Shared Workspace, and (c) Global Admin access to a private Shared Workspace requires calling the audited Break-Glass endpoint.Task Key Concurrency & Redirect Integrity (Automated Integration Test): Fire 25 concurrent POST /tasks requests against the same project to verify atomic PREFIX-1..25 assignment with zero collisions; move PREFIX-5 to another project (NEW-1) and verify GET /tasks/PREFIX-5 and Omnibar search resolve cleanly to NEW-1.Shared View Copy-on-Write Isolation (Playwright E2E Test): Open two parallel browser contexts on the same Shared Board View; have User A (Member) change filters and sort order; assert User B's board does not change and the database record for the Shared View remains untouched.Real-Time Sequence Gap & Optimistic Rollback (Integration Test): Simulate a 10-second WebSocket disconnect while 5 task updates occur on the server; verify the client catches up via GET /events?since_seq=X upon reconnect without losing state, and verify simulated HTTP 500/403 mutations smoothly roll back optimistic UI changes with an actionable toast.Recovery & Non-Destructive Safety Net (Playwright E2E Test): Archive a task and restore via the 10-second Undo toast (Z); archive a List of 5 tasks and restore via Workspace Trash; in Phase 3, trigger a concurrent offline edit on the same task description and verify the Side-by-Side 409 Conflict Resolver preserves both versions.WCAG 2.2 AA & Keyboard-Only Sweep (Automated axe-core + 10-Minute Manual Walk): Run @axe-core/playwright on List, Board, Calendar, Timeline, Task Drawer, and Settings in both Light and Dark themes, paired with a pointer-free keyboard walk of creating a task, moving it across Board columns via the Move to... menu, and scheduling its date on Calendar/Timeline.13. 1. Executive RecommendationsTo deliver a work-management platform for an initial 70–90 person community that feels effortless on Day 1 yet scales to multi-workspace, multi-community governance without Jira-style administrative fatigue, our UX architecture must enforce five core engineering and design commitments:Adopt a Single Persistent App Shell with Contextual Drawer Inspection: Never force users into full-page reloads or deep modal stacks to inspect or update a task. Keep the primary workspace view (List, Board, Calendar, or Timeline) anchored on screen and open task details in a URL-synchronized, resizable right-hand Task Peek Drawer (480px–640px on desktop; full-screen bottom sheet on mobile), with a Cmd/Ctrl + Enter option to expand to a full-bleed view when needed.Enforce Progressive Disclosure Across Three Strict Interaction Layers:Layer 1 (Everyday Execution — Zero Configuration Required): Quick task creation (C shortcut or inline + Add Task), inline status/priority/assignee pills, faceted filter chips, and personal cross-workspace triage (My Work).Layer 2 (Contextual View & Project Tuning — 1 Click Away): Switching between the 4 Core Views (List, Board, Calendar, Timeline), grouping/sorting toggles, saving Personal Views, and copy-on-write Shared View updates.Layer 3 (Structural Governance — Categorized Workspace Settings): Custom fields, workflow status mappings, configurable hierarchy depth, role matrices, permission previews, and audit/recovery logs remain cleanly isolated inside a dedicated Workspace Settings workspace view.Treat All Four Views as Synchronized Projections of One Canonical Data Model: List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline remain in the agreed initial-release target and share a single URL-serialized filter/sort bar. Even if engineered incrementally across sprints (List & Board first, followed immediately by Calendar & Timeline before initial release sign-off), the top View Switcher bar, shared filter state, and task card metadata tokens must be unified from the start.Build on Unstyled, WAI-ARIA Compliant Headless Primitives + Semantic CSS Variables: For implementation in Antigravity CLI, avoid heavy opinionated component libraries (MUI, Ant Design) that fight custom keyboard shortcuts and visual identity. Use Radix UI Primitives (for dialogs, menus, popovers, tabs, tooltips) combined with React Aria / custom roving-tabindex hooks (for complex 2D data grids, date pickers, and accessible drag-and-drop alternatives) styled via Tailwind CSS and semantic CSS custom properties (--bg-surface, --text-primary, --status-started).Standardize Safe Exploration ("Draft Local, Commit Explicit, Undo Anything"): Protect Shared Views from accidental filter/sort mutations by isolating temporary filter changes in the user's browser URL/session buffer until explicitly saved. Replace disruptive "Are you sure?" modals on everyday actions (archiving tasks, changing statuses, moving cards) with immediate execution plus a 10-second keyboard-accessible Undo toast (Z or Cmd/Ctrl + Z) backed by a 30-day soft-delete Trash.2. Evidence-Backed Usability Principles & Competitive Pattern Analysis2.1 Usability Principles Translated into Concrete Interface RequirementsEvery principle below is grounded in primary human-computer interaction research from the Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g) and the W3C Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI), translated directly into enforceable frontend requirements and verification criteria.#Usability Principle & MeaningWhy It Matters for Our ProductConcrete Interface RequirementVerification & Evaluation Method1Progressive Disclosure & Complexity Management (NN/g: Defer secondary or rarely used options to on-demand layers so novices face minimal friction)Our platform supports custom fields, dependencies, estimates, and configurable roles, which will overwhelm a 70–90 person community if exposed all at once.Quick-Create Task Composer displays only Title (required), Project/List, Status, Assignee, and Priority by default.
