Secondary attributes (Custom Fields, Dependencies, Watchers, Attachments, Subtasks) live under an expandable + More properties pill or inside the Task Detail Drawer.UI Audit: Count visible input controls in the default task creation flow (must be 5 or fewer visible fields before expansion).2Recognition Rather Than Recall (NN/g Heuristic #6: Make objects, actions, and options visible so users do not have to memorize syntax or hidden states)Traditional tools like Jira require users to memorize JQL syntax (project = OPS AND status CHANGED) or remember exact project prefixes.Replace text query languages with Faceted Filter Pills ([+ Filter] → menu of properties → multi-select checkboxes with icons/avatars) and a Command Bar (Cmd/Ctrl + K) that shows recent tasks, projects, and action verbs with keyboard hints.Usability Test: Ask new users to filter a project to "High priority tasks due this week assigned to me" without documentation; target 100% completion without typing syntax.3Information Architecture & Predictable Navigation (NN/g: Organize navigation around user mental models with strong information scent and stable landmarks)Users belong to both a Personal Workspace and multiple Shared Workspaces. Losing track of where they are causes tasks to be created in the wrong workspace.Maintain a persistent left Navigation Rail (240px) divided into 3 immutable zones: 1. Personal Triage (My Work, Inbox, Search), 2. Active Workspace Switcher & Projects, and 3. Workspace Settings / Admin (at the bottom).Tree-Testing: Measure first-click accuracy when asking users to locate Notification Preferences vs. Workspace Member Roles (target at least 85% first-click accuracy).4Cognitive Load & Decision Complexity (Hick's Law & Working Memory Limits: Reduce simultaneous choices and standardize status semantics)Allowing unconstrained status lists per project forces members to re-learn what "In Triage", "Staged", or "Hold" means in every project.Group all project workflow statuses under 5 Immutable System State Categories: Backlog, Todo, In Progress, Done, and Canceled. Each category has a distinct, consistent icon shape and color token across the entire app.Heuristic Check: Verify that every custom status created in any workspace maps to exactly one of the 5 canonical state icons and progress rollup buckets.5Feedback, Visibility of System Status & Error Prevention (NN/g Heuristics #1 & #5: Communicate system state immediately and prevent unconscious slips via constraints)Real-time collaboration and future offline editing fail if users cannot tell whether a change is saved locally, synced to the server, or blocked by permissions.Render optimistic UI updates in less than 50ms; display a subtle header sync indicator (Synced, Saving..., Offline — 2 changes queued). Prevent invalid inputs proactively (e.g., disable circular dependency selection in the task linker with an inline explanation).Network Throttling Test: Simulate 3G latency and offline drop in DevTools; verify sync state badge updates within 1 second and blocked dependency choices cannot be clicked.6Undo, Recovery & Safe Destructive Actions (NN/g Heuristics #3 & #9: Provide an immediate "emergency exit" for slips and reserve blocking modals for permanent loss)If confirmation modals pop up on every task archive or status change, users develop "modal blindness" and click Confirm reflexively.Tier 1 (Reversible Slips): Archiving tasks/lists, changing status/assignee, or clearing filters executes immediately with a 10-second Undo Toast.Tier 2 (30-Day Trash): Archived items move to Workspace Trash for 30 days.Tier 3 (Irreversible Destruction): Deleting a Project or Shared Workspace requires typing the entity name in a modal.Interaction Audit: Verify zero blocking confirmation dialogs exist on single-task archive, status change, or board move actions; verify Undo restores exact prior state.7Accessibility & Keyboard Interaction (W3C WCAG 2.2 AA & WAI-ARIA APG: Full operability without a pointer, visible focus, and semantic announcements)Power users rely on keyboards for speed, while users with motor or visual impairments rely on keyboard focus and screen readers for access.Support full roving-tabindex navigation in Lists and Boards, single-pointer/keyboard menu alternatives for all drag-and-drop actions (WCAG 2.5.7), 2px high-contrast focus rings (WCAG 2.4.11/2.4.13), and aria-live="polite" announcements for dynamic updates.Automated + Manual Audit: Zero critical/serious axe-core violations; complete end-to-end task creation, status update, and board move using only Tab, Arrow, Enter, Space, and Escape.8Responsive Design & Touch Ergonomics (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 & Mobile Ergonomics: Adapt layout density and hit targets to viewport and input pointer)Community coordinators and members check tasks, reply to comments, and triage statuses from mobile phones during events or commutes.Enforce a minimum 24×24 CSS px target size on desktop and 44×44 CSS px touch targets on mobile/coarse pointers (@media (pointer: coarse)). Collapse the desktop sidebar into a 5-item Bottom Navigation Bar on screens narrower than 768px.Device Emulation Test: Inspect all interactive controls at 375×812px viewport; verify zero horizontal page scroll and touch targets at least 44×44px.9Information Density in Productivity Applications (Visual Hierarchy & Scannability: Balance high data throughput with whitespace and typographic contrast)If task rows are too tall, users can only see 5 tasks at once; if cards are crammed with 12 badges, boards become unreadable walls of text.Default List rows to a compact 36px height (44px on touch) showing Task Key, Status Icon, Title, Labels (max 2 + "+N"), Due Date, and Assignee Avatar. Provide a view-level Density Toggle (Compact / Comfortable) and let users toggle visible properties per view.Viewport Density Check: On a 1440×900px desktop screen, List View must display at least 14 task rows above the fold without scrolling in Default/Compact mode.10Discoverability of Advanced Features (Contextual Signifiers & Just-in-Time Hints: Reveal power-user shortcuts where the manual action occurs)Keyboard shortcuts (C, /, Cmd+K), permission previews, and custom field configurations go unused if buried only in help docs.Display right-aligned Shortcut Keycaps inside every button tooltip and dropdown menu item (e.g., Change Priority   P, Assign to me   I). Place contextual footer links inside menus (e.g., + Create or manage labels... at the bottom of the Label picker for authorized roles).First-Use Observation: Check whether users discover how to add a custom option or use a shortcut via menu signifiers during unassisted task walks.2.2 Competitive Interaction Pattern Evaluation (Learning Without Copying)We evaluated ten core workflow patterns across Jira Cloud, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, and Plane to identify what works, what creates friction, and how our platform will implement an original, simpler architectural pattern:Pattern AreaBenchmark Products AnalyzedUser Problem SolvedDrawbacks in Existing ImplementationsOur Original, Simpler Design Pattern1. Task Creation & Quick EditingLinear (lightweight modal + inline shortcuts), Jira (heavy multi-field modal), Asana (inline row insertion).Capturing a task immediately when an idea or action item arises without losing current context.Jira's creation modal scrolls through 15+ fields. Linear's shortcut-heavy flow can hide fields from mouse-first users.Dual-Entry Composer: (1) Inline + Add task... row at the bottom of any List/Board group for rapid title-only entry (Enter saves and opens next row); (2) Global C / + New Task floating composer with 5 core pills and an expandable + More fields drawer.2. Board & List InteractionLinear & Plane (clean status-grouped rows/columns), ClickUp (dense multi-attribute grid).Scanning work status at a glance and updating status/priority/assignee without opening each task.ClickUp crams too many editable cells into narrow columns, causing horizontal scroll bars inside lists.Adaptive Property Row + Single-Click Pill Popovers: List rows pin Key + Status + Title on the left and right-align configurable metadata pills (Priority, Due Date, Assignee). Clicking any pill opens an instant searchable popover menu in place.3. Task Detail PanelsAsana & Plane (right slide-over drawer), Jira (split pane or modal overlay), Linear (full-page view).Reading full descriptions, subtasks, relationships, and comment threads while retaining list/board context.Linear's full-page routing loses visual sight of the board/list; Jira's modal obscures the entire screen.Synchronized Right Peek Drawer (540px default): Clicking a task opens a right-hand drawer over the trailing edge of the view while keeping the active List/Board visible and interactive on the left. Includes a header toggle to expand to full page (Cmd/Ctrl + Enter) or copy the permanent URL (/t/OPS-42).4. Search, Filtering & Command BarLinear (Cmd+K command palette + filter pills), Jira (JQL bar + basic dropdowns).Jumping to a known task by key (OPS-42) or narrowing a view of 200 tasks down to 5 relevant items.Jira's JQL intimidates non-engineers; standard search bars separate navigation commands from task search.Unified Omnibar (Cmd/Ctrl + K or /): Typing an exact or partial task key (OPS-12 or 12) ranks that task #1 for instant Enter navigation. In views, a visual + Filter Chip Builder chains Property [is / is not / contains] Value pills with a plain-language Match All (AND) / Match Any (OR) toggle.5. Personal vs. Shared ViewsPlane & Linear (saved views), Asana (project tabs), ClickUp ("Protect View" lock).Allowing individuals to slice data for their own workflow without scrambling the canonical team board.Asana and early Jira filters often caused users to accidentally overwrite a team's default sort/filter state.Sandbox-First View Bar: Modifying filters/sorts on any Shared View immediately creates an isolated Local Draft State highlighted by an amber pill: Modified • [Reset] [Save as Personal View]. Only Owners/Coordinators see [Update Shared View].6. Workspace SwitchingSlack / Linear / Plane (top-left workspace dropdown or icon rail).Moving cleanly between a private Personal Workspace and multiple community Shared Workspaces.Icon-only rails (Slack style) waste horizontal space when a user only has 2–3 workspaces; buried menus hide whether the user is in Personal vs. Shared space.Top-Left Context Switcher with Visual Mode Accent: The top of the sidebar features a prominent Workspace Pill displaying an explicit badge (Personal in warm neutral vs. Shared with workspace icon). Clicking it (or pressing G then W) opens a switcher with an instant search and a pinned My Work (All Workspaces) link.7. Settings & Permission ManagementJira (Permission Schemes & Role matrices), Plane (3-tier fixed roles), ClickUp (per-object ACLs).Granting coordinators and members appropriate autonomy without exposing dangerous administrative actions.Jira's decoupled Permission Schemes require admins to cross-reference 3 screens to figure out why a user cannot move a task.Role Archetypes + Live "Preview As" Simulator: Group permissions into 6 human-readable capability cards under 4 core roles (Owner, Coordinator, Member, Viewer) plus optional custom roles. Include a 1-click "Preview Workspace as [Role]" banner that renders the live UI with that role's exact restrictions.8. Onboarding & Empty StatesAsana & Linear (starter tasks), ClickUp (multi-modal video & tooltip tour popups).Helping a new community member complete their first task within 3 minutes of signing in.Multi-step tooltip popups (walkthrough carousels) are reflexively dismissed by users before they have context.Learn-by-Doing Personal Sandbox + Contextual Empty States: New users land in their Personal Workspace pre-populated with 3 interactive onboarding tasks (1. Complete this task, 2. Open & add a subtask, 3. Switch to Board View). Project empty states show a 1-click [Create First Task] button and [Apply Template] options.9. Notifications & Activity HistoryLinear & GitHub (triage inbox), Jira (noisy email blasts + cluttered history tab).Ensuring users never miss a direct @mention, assignment, or approaching deadline while filtering out noise.Mixing automated status-change logs with human comments in a single chronological wall buries important questions.Segmented Activity Stream & Priority Inbox: Inside a task drawer, provide a 3-way filter above the timeline: `All10. Mobile Task WorkflowsLinear Mobile Web / Asana App (bottom sheets, swipe triage).Checking tasks, replying to comments, and updating statuses smoothly on a 375px touchscreen.Trying to render multi-column Kanban boards or wide tables horizontally on mobile results in tiny targets and awkward diagonal panning.Single-Column Stage Switcher + Bottom Sheet Drawer: On mobile (less than 768px), Board View displays one status column at a time with horizontal segmented status tabs (`Todo (4)3. Information Architecture and Navigation Tree3.1 Architectural Principles of the Navigation ModelDual-Horizon Mental Model ("Cross-Workspace Me" vs. "Single-Workspace We"): Users in a 70–90 person community operate in two distinct modes: checking everything assigned to them across the community (My Work & Inbox) and collaborating inside a specific workspace and project (Shared Workspace Projects & Views). Placing Global Personal Triage above the Workspace Divider eliminates the need to switch workspaces just to see today's tasks.Maximum 2 Levels of Visible Sidebar Nesting: The left sidebar displays Workspace → Projects → Project Views / Lists. Tasks and subtasks never appear inside the left navigation tree; they belong exclusively in the main canvas and Task Peek Drawer.Predictable Settings Consolidation: Instead of scattering gear icons across boards, lists, and headers, all workspace configuration lives inside a single Workspace Settings entry at the bottom of the active workspace section, while personal profile/theme/notification preferences live under the User Avatar Menu.3.2 Complete Platform Navigation TreePlaintextPLATFORM ROOT SHELL
├── 1. GLOBAL COMMAND & TRIAGE ZONE (Cross-Workspace Scope — Always Visible at Top of Sidebar)
│   ├── [Omnibar Trigger: Search or Jump to...] (Cmd/Ctrl + K or /)
│   ├── [+ Quick Create Task Button] (Shortcut: C — defaults to current Project or Personal Workspace)
│   ├── My Work (Personal Cross-Workspace Dashboard)
│   │   ├── Tab: Assigned to Me (Grouped by Overdue / Due Soon / In Progress / Todo)
│   │   ├── Tab: Created & Watched by Me
│   │   └── Tab: Personal Saved Cross-Workspace Views
│   └── Inbox (Unified Notification Center with unread badge count)
│       ├── Filter: Action Required (@Mentions, Assignments, Due Reminders, Conflict Alerts)
│       └── Filter: Activity Updates (Status changes, comments on watched tasks)
│
├── 2. ACTIVE WORKSPACE ZONE (Scoped to Currently Selected Personal or Shared Workspace)
│   ├── [Workspace Switcher Header Pill] (Shows Workspace Name + "Personal" or "Shared" Badge)
│   │   ├── Switch to Personal Workspace (Always pinned at top of menu)
│   │   ├── Switch to Accessible Shared Workspaces (List with unread/active indicators)
│   │   ├── + Create Personal Workspace (Available to all users)
│   │   ├── + Create Shared Workspace (Visible/enabled per community creation policy)
│   │   └── [Community Switcher] (Future-ready header dropdown when user belongs to >1 Community)
│   │
│   ├── Workspace Overview & Shared Views
│   │   ├── Saved Workspace Views (Personal Views & Shared Team Views spanning multiple projects)
│   │   └── Workspace Files Hub (Centralized attachment & file browser — Phase 2 / Tab)
│   │
│   ├── Projects Section (+ New Project button for Owners/Coordinators)
│   │   └── [Project Item: e.g., "[OPS] Community Operations"] (Expandable accordion)
│   │       ├── All Project Tasks (Opens Main Canvas with 4-View Switcher: List | Board | Calendar | Timeline)
│   │       ├── Lists (Optional 1-level groupings under the project: e.g., "Logistics", "Sponsorships")
│   │       ├── Project Saved Views (Pinned Shared Views & Personal Views for this project)
│   │       └── Project Settings (Prefix key, custom fields, statuses, templates — Owner/Coordinator)
│   │
│   └── Workspace Administration Footer (Anchored at bottom of Sidebar)
│       ├── Trash & Recovery (30-day soft-deleted tasks, lists, and projects)
│       └── Workspace Settings (Opens dedicated categorized Settings Layout)
│
├── 3. GLOBAL COMMUNITY ADMINISTRATION (Visible ONLY to Global Administrators)
│   └── Community Admin Console
│       ├── Community Overview & Workspace Directory (Metadata-only view + Audited Break-Glass)
│       ├── Community Members, Invitations & Default Coordinators Pool
│       ├── Shared Workspace Creation Policies & Quotas
│       └── Community-Wide Security & Audit Log
│
└── 4. USER ACCOUNT & PERSONAL PREFERENCES (Bottom-Left User Footer / Avatar Menu)
    ├── Profile & Identity (Name, Avatar, Role badge, Timezone)
    ├── Appearance & Accessibility (Theme: Light / Dark / System, Density: Compact / Comfortable, Reduced Motion)
    ├── Personal Notification Rules (In-app, Email digests, Quiet hours, Reminder lead times)
    ├── Keyboard Shortcuts Cheat Sheet (Shortcut: ?)
    └── Sign Out
3.3 How Navigation Adapts by RoleTo prevent cognitive disorientation when a user is an Owner in Workspace A, a Coordinator in Workspace B, and a Member in Workspace C, the core navigation tree structure never shifts positions across roles. Instead, administrative affordances adapt predictably:Navigation SurfaceOrdinary MemberCoordinatorWorkspace OwnerGlobal AdministratorGlobal Triage (My Work, Inbox, Search)Full access across all joined workspaces + Personal Workspace.Full access; My Work includes a "Coordinator Watchlist" filter for overdue project tasks.Full access across owned and joined workspaces.Full access to own work (does not mingle other users' private tasks).Workspace Switcher (+ Create)Can create Personal Workspaces; + Create Shared Workspace shows a tooltip if restricted ("Request Shared Workspace from Admin").Can create Personal Workspaces + Shared Workspaces (if permitted by community policy).Full access to create Personal and Shared Workspaces.Full access to create workspaces and manage creation policy.Projects & Lists SidebarViews all accessible projects/lists; can create Personal Views.Sees + New Project and + New List buttons; can create/update Shared Views.Full CRUD on Projects, Lists, Templates, and Shared Views.Same as their workspace role within joined workspaces.Workspace Settings EntryLabel reads "Workspace Info & Members" (read-only member directory, workflow reference, and own notification rules).Opens Workspace Settings with edit access to delegated tabs (Projects, Workflows, Views, Templates, Member Invites if delegated).Full edit access to all 9 Workspace Settings categories + Role Preview Simulator + Audit Log.Full access if Owner; otherwise can access via Audited Break-Glass from the Community Admin Console.Community Admin ConsoleHidden (does not clutter sidebar).Hidden.Hidden.Visible as a dedicated shield-badged entry at the bottom of the left rail.4. Role-Specific Journeys and Interaction SequencesEach of the 14 required journeys is specified below to minimize modal interruptions, preserve context, and provide deterministic error recovery.Journey 1: A New Member Signs In and Completes Their First Meaningful TaskEntry Point & User Intent: User clicks an invitation link, completes authentication, and wants to understand how the platform works and complete their first assigned or starter task in under 3 minutes.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User lands on My Work (Personal Dashboard), which shows a clean welcome banner and 3 interactive starter tasks inside their Personal Workspace alongside any tasks already assigned to them in Shared Workspaces.User clicks the status pill on Starter Task #1 (PER-1: Mark this task as In Progress) → selects In Progress from the inline popover.User clicks the row for their first real assigned community task (OPS-12) → the right Task Peek Drawer slides open → user checks off a subtask, types a short status comment, and changes the status pill to Done.Essential Interface States: First-run welcome card (dismissible with 1 click); interactive progress pill (1 of 3 starter steps complete); active Task Peek Drawer over the dashboard list.System Feedback: Status pill transitions immediately (less than 50ms) with a subtle checkmark micro-animation; completing the starter checklist triggers a non-blocking celebration toast (You're ready to go!).Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User accidentally closes the welcome checklist before finishing. Recovery: A Getting Started (1/3) pill remains pinned at the bottom of the sidebar until completed or explicitly dismissed, with a Undo option.Relevant Permission Checks: Authenticated community member token; verified read/update access on OPS-12.Mobile-Specific Considerations: On mobile, the welcome banner collapses into a compact collapsible card at the top of My Work; tapping OPS-12 opens a full-height draggable bottom sheet with a sticky bottom comment/status bar.Journey 2: A User Creates a Personal WorkspaceEntry Point & User Intent: Any community member opens the top-left Workspace Switcher to create a private space for personal study, drafting, or individual task tracking.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User clicks the Workspace Switcher Pill (G then W) → selects + New Personal Workspace (or uses the default Personal Workspace created at signup).A lightweight dialog prompts for Workspace Name (e.g., My Study & Drafts) and Default Prefix (auto-suggested as ME or SAM from the name, editable 2–6 uppercase letters).User presses Enter → routed immediately into the new Personal Workspace's default project list view with the inline task composer focused.Essential Interface States: Workspace Switcher menu; 2-field creation dialog with live prefix preview (Tasks will be numbered SAM-1, SAM-2...); Empty Project state with focused inline input.System Feedback: Header badge explicitly displays Personal Workspace • Private to you with a lock icon so the user has 100% confidence in privacy.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User creates a task in their Personal Workspace that they later realize belongs in a Shared Workspace. Recovery: Task Drawer ... menu includes Move to Workspace / Project, which re-keys the task to the destination project prefix and warns that it will become visible to that workspace's members.Relevant Permission Checks: Allowed for all active authenticated community members (unless restricted by an explicit global quota).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Workspace Switcher opens as a bottom sheet; prefix input auto-capitalizes on mobile virtual keyboards.Journey 3: An Authorized User Creates and Configures a Shared WorkspaceEntry Point & User Intent: A Global Admin or authorized Creator clicks + New Shared Workspace in the Workspace Switcher to set up a collaborative workspace for a team or event.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User opens Workspace Switcher → clicks + New Shared Workspace → opens a clean 2-Step Staged Creation Drawer.Step 1 (Identity & Starter Template): Enters Workspace Name (Annual Tech Fest), first Project Name (Core Operations), Project Prefix (FEST), and selects one of the 3 Built-in Templates (Event & Operations, Engineering Sprint, or Simple Task Tracker).Step 2 (Initial Leadership & Coordinators): Displays a pre-checked box: [✓] Include Community Coordinators by default (4 people) with individual removable chips for each Coordinator, plus an input to invite Co-Owners or Members.User clicks Create Shared Workspace → lands directly on the pre-populated Project Board/List view.Essential Interface States: Step 1 Template selector cards (showing preview badges of included statuses and lists); Step 2 Coordinator auto-inclusion review chips; Initial populated workspace view.System Feedback: Toast confirmation: Workspace "Annual Tech Fest" created with 3 default lists and 4 coordinators.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User picks the wrong starter template. Recovery: Workspace Settings → Projects & Templates allows switching status presets or archiving empty starter lists in 2 clicks.Relevant Permission Checks: community:create_shared_workspace capability check. If an unauthorized member views the switcher, the option is either hidden or shows a disabled item with "Ask a Global Admin to create a shared workspace".Mobile-Specific Considerations: Full-screen 2-step wizard with sticky bottom Next / Create Workspace primary button.Journey 4: A Workspace Owner Invites Members and Configures Coordinator AccessEntry Point & User Intent: Workspace Owner wants to add 15 team members, promote one to Co-Owner, and remove one default Coordinator who is not participating in this workspace.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Owner clicks Workspace Settings → Members & Roles (or clicks the Invite button in the workspace header).In the Invite Bar, Owner selects or pastes community members (with instant autocomplete by name/email), selects the target role (Member, Coordinator, or Owner), and clicks Add to Workspace.In the Active Members Table, Owner filters by Role: Coordinator (Default) → clicks the role dropdown next to the non-participating Coordinator → selects Remove from Workspace (or changes role to Member).Essential Interface States: Multi-select member autocomplete input; Role selector dropdown with 1-line capability summary per role; Active Members list showing badge Auto-added Coordinator.System Feedback: Inline row update + toast: @UserX removed from Annual Tech Fest [Undo]. Audit log records MEMBER_ADDED and COORDINATOR_REMOVED_BY_OWNER.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Owner tries to remove themselves when they are the last remaining Workspace Owner. Recovery: System blocks the action inline (Error Prevention) with a clear message: "Every workspace requires at least one Owner. Promote another member to Owner before leaving."Relevant Permission Checks: workspace:manage_members and workspace:manage_coordinators (restricted to Workspace Owners and Global Admin break-glass).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Member rows stack name, email, and role badge vertically; role actions open in a touch-friendly action sheet.Journey 5: A Coordinator Creates Tasks, Assigns Work and Monitors DeadlinesEntry Point & User Intent: A Coordinator opens a project to break down an upcoming deliverable into assigned tasks with due dates and monitor what is falling behind.Recommended Sequence of Actions:In List View, Coordinator clicks + Add task under the Logistics list → types Book main auditorium AV equipment, presses Tab to set Assignee (@Rohan), Tab to set Priority (High), Tab to set Due Date (Next Friday), and presses Enter (which saves FEST-14 and immediately opens a fresh inline row below it for rapid batch entry).To monitor deadlines, Coordinator clicks the + Filter chip → selects Due Date: Overdue or Due Within 3 Days → clicks Save as Shared View ("Upcoming Deadlines").Essential Interface States: Inline rapid-creation row with keyboard Tab stops across property pills; color-coded Due Date pills (Red = Overdue, Amber = Due within 48h, Neutral = Future).System Feedback: Each Enter press assigns the next sequential permanent key (FEST-14, FEST-15) optimistically and notifies the assignee.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Setting a due date in the past by accident. Recovery: Date picker displays a non-blocking amber warning badge (Selected date is in the past) and allows immediate correction.Relevant Permission Checks: task:create, task:assign, and view:create_shared (all granted to Coordinators by default).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Floating Action Button (+) at bottom-right opens the mobile Quick Task Composer sheet with horizontal scrollable property pills (Assignee, Due Date, Priority, List).Journey 6: A Member Opens an Assigned Task, Updates Progress and CommentsEntry Point & User Intent: A Member receives a notification or sees FEST-14 in My Work, opens it to move its status to In Progress, and posts a question for the Coordinator.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Member clicks FEST-14 in My Work or Inbox → the Task Peek Drawer opens on the right.Member clicks the Status Pill at the top of the drawer (or presses shortcut S) → selects In Progress.Member clicks into the bottom Comment Composer, types @CoordinatorA Vendor asked if we need 4 wireless mics or 6?, attaches a PDF quote via drag-and-drop or the paperclip button, and presses Cmd/Ctrl + Enter to post.Essential Interface States: Task Peek Drawer showing header (FEST-14, Status, Priority, Assignee), scrollable body (Description, Subtasks, Attachments, Activity Stream), and sticky bottom Comment Composer with @mention and #TASK-KEY autocomplete popover.System Feedback: Status pill updates instantly across both the Drawer and the underlying List row; posted comment appears immediately in the stream with a Sending... → timestamp transition.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Member navigates away or closes the drawer while mid-way through typing a long comment. Recovery: Unsent comment text and edited descriptions are auto-saved to local storage per task_id and display a Draft saved indicator so zero text is lost.Relevant Permission Checks: task:update_status and task:comment (granted to all Workspace Members).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Comment composer pins above the mobile virtual keyboard; @ button sits directly in the composer toolbar so users don't have to hunt for the symbol on mobile keyboards.Journey 7: A User Creates and Manages SubtasksEntry Point & User Intent: A Member or Coordinator opens task FEST-14 and wants to split the work into 3 actionable checklist steps with individual assignees and permanent keys.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Inside the Task Peek Drawer for FEST-14 (or via the expand chevron ▸ on a List View row), user clicks + Add subtask.User types Confirm stage power outlets, optionally assigns @Satadru and a due date on the inline subtask row, and presses Enter (generating FEST-15 linked as a child of FEST-14).As subtasks are completed, the parent task card/row automatically updates its Subtask Progress Pill ([✓ 1/3]).Essential Interface States: Expandable subtask list inside the Task Drawer and List View; parent progress badge (1/3); breadcrumb link at the top of a subtask drawer (Parent: FEST-14 Book main auditorium AV equipment).System Feedback: Checking a subtask checkbox updates the parent's 1/3 → 2/3 progress bar immediately. When 3/3 subtasks are marked Done, a non-blocking inline prompt asks: "All subtasks complete — mark parent FEST-14 as Done? [Mark Done] [Keep In Progress]".Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User creates a subtask that grows too large and needs to become a standalone parent task (or vice versa). Recovery: Task ... menu includes Convert to standalone task and Convert to subtask of... (disabled if the task already contains subtasks when a 1-level depth limit is active, with an explicit explanation tooltip).Relevant Permission Checks: task:create within the project.Mobile-Specific Considerations: Subtasks render as full-width tap rows inside the parent task sheet with 44×44px status toggle targets on the left.Journey 8: A User Switches From a List to a Board, Calendar or TimelineEntry Point & User Intent: A user viewing a project in List View wants to visualize the same filtered set of tasks as a Kanban Board, a monthly Calendar, or a dependency Timeline.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User clicks the segmented View Switcher in the top project toolbar (List | Board | Calendar | Timeline) or presses V then B / C / T.The main canvas transitions immediately to the selected view while preserving all active filter chips and search queries in the toolbar.Essential Interface States: Segmented View Switcher (role="tablist" or toolbar radio group); persistent Filter Bar below the view header; contextual notice on Calendar/Timeline when tasks lack dates (12 tasks without due dates — click to expand Unscheduled Tray).System Feedback: View switches in under 100ms using cached client task data without re-fetching unchanged tasks from the backend.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User switches to Calendar or Timeline and thinks tasks disappeared because those tasks have no due_date or start_date. Recovery: Both Calendar and Timeline feature a prominent collapsible Unscheduled Tasks Drawer (12 unscheduled) on the right edge so users can see undated tasks and schedule them via click or drag.Relevant Permission Checks: Project read access (all members can switch view projections locally).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Segmented view switcher uses compact icon+label tabs; Timeline switches to a vertical Agenda/Milestone list with a toggle for horizontal pinch-zoom canvas.Journey 9: A User Searches for a Task by Its Permanent KeyEntry Point & User Intent: A colleague mentions FEST-14 (or an older moved key OLD-09) in a meeting or chat, and the user wants to open it immediately from anywhere in the app.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User presses Cmd/Ctrl + K (or /, or clicks the top sidebar Search button) to open the Omnibar.User types FEST-14 (or just 14, or OLD-09).The Omnibar detects the key pattern, places FEST-14: Book main auditorium AV equipment as the top highlighted result with an [Exact Key Match] badge (or [Redirected from OLD-09]), and pressing Enter opens the task directly.Essential Interface States: Modal Omnibar with instant debounced results (less than 100ms); result groups (Exact Key Match, Tasks, Projects, Views, Commands); redirect alias badge when resolved via task_key_aliases.System Feedback: If a historical key (OLD-09) is searched or accessed via URL (/t/OLD-09), the app opens FEST-14 and shows a subtle informational banner in the drawer header: Moved from OLD-09.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User searches for a task key from a private workspace they do not have permission to view, or a key that does not exist. Recovery: Display a single safe empty state: "No accessible task found matching 'SEC-99'. Check the task key or verify you are a member of that workspace." (Prevents leaking private task existence).Relevant Permission Checks: Backend search endpoint filters results strictly by the user's active workspace memberships.Mobile-Specific Considerations: Tapping the search icon in the mobile bottom navigation bar opens a full-screen search view with the keyboard automatically focused and recent task keys shown as tap chips above the keyboard.Journey 10: A User Changes Filters Without Unexpectedly Modifying a Shared ViewEntry Point & User Intent: A Member opens the team's pinned "Sprint Board" (Shared View) and wants to filter down to only their own tasks (Assignee: Me) without hiding cards on their teammates' screens.Recommended Sequence of Actions:User opens the Shared View "Sprint Board" → clicks + Filter → selects Assignee: Me.The board filters immediately in the user's browser tab and updates the URL query string (?view=sprint-board&assignee=me).An inline Draft State Pill appears next to the view title: Unsaved changes • [Reset] [Save as Personal View] (plus [Update Shared View] if the user is an Owner/Coordinator).User works on their tasks and clicks Reset (or navigates away), leaving the canonical Shared View completely untouched for the rest of the community.Essential Interface States: Clean Shared View state (globe icon next to view title); Modified Local Draft state (amber dot + Reset and Save as... buttons); Save View popover distinguishing Personal View (Only visible to you) from Shared View (Visible to workspace).System Feedback: Tooltip on the Modified badge states: "Your filter changes are only visible to you until saved."Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: An Owner or Coordinator clicks Update Shared View by mistake when they only meant to save a personal filter. Recovery: Clicking Update Shared View triggers a 10-second Undo toast: Updated shared view "Sprint Board" for all members [Undo].Relevant Permission Checks: Any member has view:create_personal; only Owners, Coordinators, and the view's creator have view:update_shared.Mobile-Specific Considerations: Filter chips collapse into a compact Filters (2 active) • [Reset] button that opens a bottom filter sheet.Journey 11: An Owner Customizes Permissions and Understands Their ConsequencesEntry Point & User Intent: A Workspace Owner wants to adjust what Coordinators or a custom "Event Volunteer" role can do and verify exactly how the workspace will look and behave for that role before saving.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Owner navigates to Workspace Settings → Roles & Permissions.Owner selects the Coordinator role (or clicks + Create Custom Role cloned from Member) and toggles capability cards presented in plain language (e.g., turning off Delete Projects & Lists while keeping Create & Edit Shared Views enabled).Owner clicks Preview Workspace as [Role] at the top of the settings panel.The interface renders the live workspace wrapped in a high-visibility top border banner: PREVIEW MODE: Viewing workspace as "Event Volunteer" — Destructive actions disabled [Exit Preview].Owner verifies that the Delete Project menu item is disabled with an explanatory lock tooltip, exits preview, and clicks Save Role Changes.Essential Interface States: Capability bundle cards with plain-language impact summaries ("Affects 12 members currently assigned to this role"); Dependency lock indicators; Full-screen interactive Role Preview banner.System Feedback: Attempting to uncheck a prerequisite capability (e.g., unchecking View Tasks while Edit Tasks is checked) automatically unchecks or locks dependent toggles with an inline explanation: "Editing tasks requires permission to view tasks."Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Owner restricts a role too aggressively and members report they cannot create tasks. Recovery: Owner opens Roles & Permissions → Change History and clicks Restore Default Role Permissions in 1 click.Relevant Permission Checks: workspace:manage_roles (strictly limited to Workspace Owners).Mobile-Specific Considerations: Role capability matrix renders as vertical accordion cards per role on mobile screens.Journey 12: A User Encounters a Failed Save, Network Interruption or Synchronization ConflictEntry Point & User Intent: A user is updating tasks during an unstable internet connection (or while offline in the planned offline-editing delivery phase) and another user edits the same task concurrently.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Network Drop / Queued Edit: While the connection is down, the top header displays a non-blocking amber pill: Offline — 2 changes queued locally. The user edits FEST-14's priority (High → Urgent) and description. Both rows show a subtle Queued clock icon.Reconnection & Auto-Merge: When connectivity returns, the client replays the queue. Because no one else changed priority, the priority update succeeds automatically.Conflict Detection: However, a Coordinator updated FEST-14's description while the user was offline. The server returns HTTP 409 Conflict for the description field.Explicit Resolution: A persistent banner appears in the top bar and inside FEST-14: 1 Sync Conflict on FEST-14 [Resolve]. Clicking Resolve opens a clean side-by-side Conflict Resolver Drawer showing Server Version (by @CoordinatorA at 2:14 PM) vs. Your Offline Version, with three 1-click buttons: [Keep Server Version], [Apply My Version], or [Keep Server & Post Mine as Comment].Essential Interface States: Header Connection/Queue status pill; Task-level Queued and Conflict badges; Side-by-side Conflict Resolver modal/drawer; Permission-revoked recovery drawer (if user's edit rights were revoked while offline, allowing Copy to Clipboard or Save to Personal Workspace).System Feedback: Never silently overwrite or discard a user's typed text. Once resolved, display a green confirmation toast: All offline changes synced.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: User closes the browser tab before resolving a conflict. Recovery: Unresolved conflict payloads persist in local IndexedDB storage and re-surface the banner on next app load.Relevant Permission Checks: Live server-side permission re-verification at the moment of sync replay.Mobile-Specific Considerations: On mobile, the side-by-side diff stacks into a segmented toggle ([Their Version] | [My Version]) with sticky bottom resolution buttons.Journey 13: A User Accidentally Archives Work and Restores ItEntry Point & User Intent: A Member or Coordinator accidentally archives a task (or an entire List of 10 tasks) and wants to restore it to its exact previous location and status.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Immediate Recovery (0–10 seconds): Right after archiving FEST-14, a bottom-right toast appears: Archived FEST-14 "Book main auditorium AV" [Undo] (Shortcut: Z). Clicking Undo (or pressing Z) immediately restores FEST-14 to its exact board column and list position.Later Recovery (Up to 30 days): If the 10-second toast has expired, the user clicks Trash & Recovery at the bottom of the workspace sidebar.User sees a chronological list of archived items (filterable by Tasks, Lists, Projects, or Archived by Me), clicks Restore next to FEST-14, and the task returns to its original project and list.Essential Interface States: 10-second Undo Toast with visual countdown bar; Trash & Recovery View displaying item key, title, original project/list path, who archived it, and days remaining until permanent purge (29 days left).System Feedback: Restoring a List restores all tasks that were archived as part of that List batch operation in a single transaction.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Restoring a task whose original parent List or Project was also archived or deleted. Recovery: The Restore handler detects the missing parent container and prompts: "Original list 'Logistics' is archived. [Restore List + Task Together] or [Restore Task to Project Root]".Relevant Permission Checks: Any member can restore tasks they created or archived; Coordinators and Owners can restore any item in the workspace Trash; only Owners can click Delete Permanently before the 30-day expiry.Mobile-Specific Considerations: Undo toast pins above the mobile bottom navigation bar so it never obscures tab navigation (WCAG 2.4.11).Journey 14: An Administrator Performs a Restricted Administrative ActionEntry Point & User Intent: A Global Administrator needs to intervene in a Shared Workspace whose sole Owner left the community (or adjust community-wide workspace creation policies) with full audit accountability.Recommended Sequence of Actions:Global Admin clicks Community Admin Console in the bottom-left sidebar → opens Workspace Directory.The table shows Shared Workspace metadata (Name, Owners, Member Count, Created Date, Last Active) without exposing task titles or descriptions by default.Admin clicks Manage Ownership (Break-Glass) on the orphaned workspace → a high-friction Audited Action Dialog opens.Admin selects a new Owner (@CoordinatorB), types a mandatory Audit Reason (minimum 15 characters, e.g., "Previous owner graduated; promoting active coordinator per committee request"), and clicks Confirm & Log Override.Essential Interface States: Metadata-only Workspace Directory table; High-Friction Audited Action Modal with mandatory reason input and explicit warning banner (This action will be recorded permanently in the Community & Workspace Audit Logs and notify workspace leadership).System Feedback: Action executes, sends an automated in-app/email notification to @CoordinatorB and any existing workspace owners, and appends a tamper-evident entry to the Audit Log.Common Mistakes & Recovery Paths: Mistake: Admin selects the wrong user as Co-Owner. Recovery: Admin or the newly promoted Owner can adjust the role in Workspace Members, which records a follow-up audit event.Relevant Permission Checks: community:global_admin role verification + re-authentication/session freshness check.Mobile-Specific Considerations: Community Admin Console tables use horizontal card summaries on mobile; break-glass modal remains fully operable on mobile for urgent administrative recovery.5. Detailed Behavioral Specifications for All Four ViewsAll four views (List, Board, Calendar, Timeline) remain part of the agreed initial-release target and operate as real-time projections over the exact same project/workspace task dataset and shared Filter/Sort toolbar.5.1 View Comparison & Shared vs. Personal Configuration MatrixSpecification Dimension1. List View2. Board View (Kanban)3. Calendar View4. Timeline View (Gantt)Primary User NeedHigh-density scanning, rapid batch task creation, inline property editing, and hierarchical subtask expansion.Visualizing workflow stage bottlenecks, moving work across status columns, and managing work-in-progress (WIP).Scheduling due dates across days/weeks/months and spotting deadline clustering.Visualizing multi-day task durations (start_date → due_date), project phases, and blocks / blocked_by dependency chains.Default Grouping, Sorting & FiltersGroup: By Status Category (or by List).Sort: Manual fractional rank (lexorank), then Priority.Filter: Active tasks (Status != Canceled).Columns: Workflow Statuses.Sub-group (Swimlanes): None by default (optional: Assignee, Priority, List).Sort: Manual column rank.Time Scale: Month view (with Week & 4-Day Agenda toggles).Date Field: Due Date.Side Tray: Unscheduled tasks.Time Scale: Weeks / Months.Row Grouping: By List (or Parent Task).Sort: Start Date, then Due Date.Main Pointer InteractionsClick cell pill to edit inline; click row title/key to open Task Drawer; click ▸ to expand subtasks inline; multi-select checkboxes for bulk actions.Drag card across columns/ranks; click card to open Task Drawer; click Status/Priority/Assignee badge on card face to change inline; + Add task at top/bottom of column.Click any calendar day cell to create task due on that day; drag task chip to reschedule; click chip to open Task Drawer; drag from Unscheduled Tray onto a date.Drag bar body to shift start/due dates; drag left/right bar handles to resize duration; hover dependency connector line to highlight blocking task; click row to open Drawer.Empty & Loading StatesLoading: 8 row skeletons (36px height) matching column widths.Empty Project: Illustration + [+ Create First Task] + [Use Template].Empty Filter: "0 tasks match active filters" [Reset Filters].Loading: 4 column skeletons with 3 card placeholders each.Empty Column: Subtle dashed drop zone (No tasks in Review — Drag here or click +).Loading: Month grid skeleton.No Dated Tasks: Grid remains visible with a prominent callout on the right Unscheduled Tasks Tray: "14 tasks have no due date — select a task to schedule".Loading: Split-pane skeleton (left task tree + right time grid).No Dated Tasks: Bars render as unscheduled markers in the left table with a 1-click [Set Dates] pill on hover/focus.Keyboard & Single-Pointer Alternatives (WCAG 2.2 AA)2D Roving Tabindex Grid: ↑/↓ moves between rows; ←/→ moves across property cells (Key, Status, Title, Priority, Due, Assignee); Enter/Space opens cell editor; Shift+↑/↓ selects multiple rows; Alt+↑/↓ reorders row rank.No-Drag Card Move (WCAG 2.5.7): ←/→ moves focus between columns; ↑/↓ moves between cards; pressing M (or clicking the card's ... / Status badge) opens a Move to Column / Position menu; Space lifts card for Arrow-key move + Enter to drop.Keyboard Date Grid: Arrow keys move focus day-by-day; PageUp/PageDown switches months; pressing Enter on a focused day opens task creation or lists tasks on that day; pressing D on a focused task opens the accessible Date Picker popover.Split-Pane Keyboard Control: Left table supports full keyboard editing of Start Date, Due Date, and Blocked By fields so users never have to drag canvas bars with a mouse (WCAG 2.5.7). Alt+←/→ shifts task dates by ±1 day.Accessibility Requirementsrole="treegrid" (when subtasks expand) or role="grid" with aria-rowcount, aria-sort on headers, and aria-expanded on parent tasks.Each column is a <section aria-labelledby="col-heading-id"> showing task count; live region (aria-live="assertive") announces "Moved FEST-14 to In Progress, position 2 of 5".Grid cells announce full date + task count ("Friday, November 6, 2026, 3 tasks due"). Color coding for overdue/priority is paired with icons (!, clock).Left treegrid provides complete textual equivalents for every bar duration and dependency ("FEST-18, Nov 4 to Nov 8, blocked by FEST-14").Behavior Under Restricted PermissionsRead-only viewers can expand subtasks, sort/filter locally, and open drawers, but inline property pills render without dropdown chevrons and show a lock tooltip on click.Drag handles are disabled (cursor: default); clicking a status badge explains why transitions are locked (e.g., "View-only access").Day creation buttons and drag-rescheduling are disabled; clicking a chip opens the read-only Task Drawer.Bar resize handles are hidden; clicking a task opens the read-only Task Drawer.Real-Time Update BehaviorRemote field changes flash a subtle 500ms highlight on the updated cell. Newly created remote tasks insert smoothly without jumping the user's current scroll offset or focused input.If a teammate moves a card that the current user is not actively dragging, the card animates (180ms layout transition) to its new column. If the user is editing/dragging that exact card, defer visual move until drop and reconcile.Remote due-date changes move the chip to the new day cell and show a subtle highlight pulse.Remote date/dependency changes update bar position and redraw SVG dependency arrows smoothly.User-Configurable View OptionsGroup by (Status, List, Assignee, Priority, None), Sub-group, Sort order, Visible property columns, Subtask display (Collapsed, Expanded, Hidden), Row density (Compact, Comfortable).Column grouping (Status, Priority, Assignee), Swimlane grouping, Card visible properties (toggle Labels, Due Date, Estimate, Subtask count), Hide empty columns toggle.Time scale (Month, Week, 4-Day), Date field plotted (Due Date vs. Start–Due Span), Show weekends toggle, Show completed tasks toggle.Zoom scale (Day, Week, Month, Quarter), Row grouping (List, Project, Assignee), Show dependency lines toggle, Show critical/blocked highlights toggle.Personal vs. Shared View BoundaryShared View stores: Default filters, grouping, sort, and default visible columns.Personal Preference stores: Row density (Compact/Comfortable) and temporary unsaved filter/sort exploration.Shared View stores: Column/Swimlane grouping, filters, and card property toggles.Personal Preference stores: Collapsed column state for personal focus (unless explicitly saved to Shared View).Shared View stores: Plotted date field, filters, and weekend visibility.Personal Preference stores: Current navigated month/week offset and Month vs. Week zoom toggle.Shared View stores: Row grouping, filters, and dependency line visibility.Personal Preference stores: Horizontal scroll position (defaults to Today line on load) and zoom scale (Week/Month).5.2 Deep-Dive Interaction Mechanics for Critical View ChallengesA. Accessible Alternatives to Drag-and-Drop on Boards (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 Compliance)Continuous pointer dragging is physically difficult on trackpads, error-prone on mobile touchscreens, and inaccessible to keyboard and switch-device users. Every Board card supports three equivalent non-dragging mechanisms:Single-Click Status Badge on Card Face: Every board card renders its status icon on the top-left of the card. Clicking or tapping that icon opens a menu of all workflow statuses; selecting a status moves the card to that column immediately.Card Context Menu (Move to...): Clicking the ... button on any card (or pressing M while focused) opens a structured popover allowing the user to pick Column (Todo / In Progress / Done) and Position (Top of column / Bottom of column / After [Task]) with single clicks.Keyboard Pick-Up & Arrow Reordering: Pressing Space on a focused card enters "Reorder Mode" (announced via aria-live), allowing ←/→ to move across columns and ↑/↓ to change vertical rank, confirmed with Enter or canceled with Escape.B. High-Efficiency Inline Editing in ListsSingle-Click Property Pills, Double-Click or Action-Icon Title Rename: Clicking a task's Title or Key in List View performs the most common action: opening the Task Peek Drawer (preventing accidental title edits when users just want to read a task). An explicit Rename icon (✎) appears on hover/focus next to the title (or by pressing R / F2 on a focused row) to edit the title inline.Zero-Modal Property Mutation: Clicking Status, Priority, Assignee, Due Date, or Labels cells opens a lightweight, anchored combobox popover (220px wide) directly over the cell. Typing filters the options immediately (e.g., typing "h" selects High Priority), and pressing Enter commits the change and returns keyboard focus to the cell.Multi-Select Bulk Action Floating Bar: Checking 2 or more row checkboxes (or pressing Shift + ↑/↓ then X) reveals a floating dark pill bar at the bottom center of the viewport: 4 tasks selected • [Change Status] [Assign] [Set Priority] [Set Due Date] [Move to List] [Archive] [Clear Esc].C. Date Interactions and Unscheduled Triage in CalendarsThe "Unscheduled Tasks" Problem: In real community projects, 30%–50% of tasks start without a due date. A Calendar View that silently hides undated tasks makes users distrust the view.Solution — Collapsible Unscheduled Tray + Single-Pointer Assignment: Calendar View features a right-hand Unscheduled Tasks Tray showing a badge count (e.g., 9 Undated Tasks). Users can schedule a task either by dragging it onto a calendar date or (for single-pointer/keyboard users) clicking the [Set Date] pill on the undated card to pick a date from a calendar popover.Multi-Day vs. Due-Date Display: Tasks with only a due_date render as compact single-day pills showing Status Icon + Key + Title + Priority Dot. Tasks with both start_date and due_date can optionally render as continuous horizontal banners across their active days.D. Dependency Readability & Low-Clutter TimelinesAvoiding "Spaghetti Lines": Traditional Gantt charts draw hundreds of overlapping SVG arrows across the entire screen, making the chart unreadable once a project exceeds 20 tasks.Solution — Progressive Dependency Highlighting:By default, Timeline View draws clean horizontal duration bars color-coded by Status Category, with subtle connector lines only for active/unresolved blocking links (blocks where the upstream task is not Done).If an upstream blocking task's due_date falls after the downstream blocked task's start_date, the connector line and a warning badge on the blocked bar turn High-Contrast Danger Red (! Date Conflict: Blocked by FEST-14).Hovering or focusing any task bar highlights its direct upstream blockers and downstream dependents at 100% opacity while dimming unrelated bars to 40% opacity.Left-pane split table (320px wide, collapsible) always remains synchronized row-for-row with the right-hand canvas so users can edit Start Date, Due Date, and Dependencies via standard accessible inputs without touching the graphical canvas.6. Design-System Foundations and Component Inventory6.1 Visual Foundations & Semantic Token ArchitectureTo ensure Antigravity CLI generates consistent, maintainable UI components across Light and Dark modes without hardcoded hex values, all styling must consume a 3-tier token architecture (Primitive Palette → Semantic Role Tokens → Component Tokens) exposed as CSS Custom Properties and mapped into tailwind.config:A. Color Roles & Semantic Tokens (WCAG 2.2 AA Contrast Verified)Every status and priority state pairs a Semantic Color Token with a Distinct Geometric Icon Shape so colorblind users never rely on hue alone (WCAG 1.4.1).Token CategorySemantic CSS VariableLight Theme Role / TargetDark Theme Role / TargetContrast & Usage RuleSurfaces & Backgrounds--bg-canvas--bg-surface-primary--bg-surface-elevated--bg-surface-subtle--bg-surface-hoverApp background (#F8FAFC)Cards, List rows (#FFFFFF)Drawers, Modals (#FFFFFF)Sidebar, Board columns (#F1F5F9)Row/Button hover (#E2E8F0 @ 50%)App background (#0B0F17)Cards, List rows (#111827)Drawers, Modals (#1E293B)Sidebar, Board columns (#0F172A)Row/Button hover (#1E293B)In Dark Mode, elevation is communicated via lighter surface luminance + 1px inner border rather than dark drop shadows.Typography & Icons--text-primary--text-secondary--text-muted--text-on-accentTask titles, body (#0F172A)Metadata, keys, labels (#475569)Placeholders, hints (#64748B)Primary button text (#FFFFFF)Task titles, body (#F8FAFC)Metadata, keys, labels (#94A3B8)Placeholders, hints (#64748B)Primary button text (#FFFFFF)--text-primary ≥ 12:1; --text-secondary ≥ 7:1; --text-muted ≥ 4.6:1 against --bg-surface-primary (exceeds WCAG AA 4.5:1).Borders & Focus Rings--border-subtle--border-strong--focus-ringRow dividers (#E2E8F0)Input borders (#CBD5E1)High-contrast focus (#2563EB)Row dividers (#1E293B)Input borders (#334155)High-contrast focus (#60A5FA)--border-strong and --focus-ring maintain at least 3:1 non-text contrast against adjacent surfaces (WCAG 1.4.11 & 2.4.13).Canonical Workflow Statuses--status-backlog--status-todo--status-in-progress--status-done--status-canceledSlate Dashed Circle (#64748B)Neutral Hollow Circle (#334155)Amber/Blue Half-Filled Circle (#D97706 / #2563EB)Emerald Check Circle (#059669)Muted Slash Circle (#94A3B8)Slate Dashed Circle (#94A3B8)Neutral Hollow Circle (#CBD5E1)Amber/Blue Half-Filled Circle (#FBBF24 / #60A5FA)Emerald Check Circle (#34D399)Muted Slash Circle (#64748B)Every custom status inherits one of these 5 icon geometries (14×14px SVG) + semantic color tokens.Priority & Feedback--priority-urgent--priority-high--priority-medium--priority-low--feedback-danger--feedback-warningRed Exclamation Box (#DC2626)Orange 3-Bar Signal (#EA580C)Amber 2-Bar Signal (#D97706)Slate 1-Bar Signal (#64748B)Error/Destructive (#DC2626)Modified/Offline (#D97706)Rose Exclamation Box (#F87171)Orange 3-Bar Signal (#FB923C)Amber 2-Bar Signal (#FBBF24)Slate 1-Bar Signal (#94A3B8)Error/Destructive (#F87171)Modified/Offline (#FBBF24)Priority icons use distinct bar counts (!, 3 bars, 2 bars, 1 bar, ---) so priority is readable even in grayscale.B. Typography & Readable Text DensityFont Stack:UI & Body (--font-sans): 'Inter', 'Plus Jakarta Sans', or system UI fallback (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif) with font-feature-settings: "cv02", "cv03", "cv04", "cv11" enabled for high legibility at small sizes.Task Keys, Shortcuts & Numeric Data (--font-mono): 'JetBrains Mono' or 'Geist Mono' with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so task keys (FEST-09, FEST-100), dates, and estimates align vertically in List columns without jitter.Type Scale:text-xs (12px / 16px line-height): Task keys, keyboard shortcut keycaps, badges, column counts, timestamps.text-sm (13.5px / 20px line-height): Default UI & Task Row Title size — optimal for data-dense productivity tables while preventing eye strain.text-base (15px / 24px line-height): Task Detail Drawer body text, comments, and long-form descriptions (constrained to 65ch max line width for comfortable reading).text-lg (18px / 26px line-height, font-semibold): Task Drawer Title, View Headers, Modal Titles.text-xl (22px / 30px line-height, font-semibold): Dashboard Page Headers.C. Spacing, Layout Scale, Radius & ElevationBase Grid: 4px spatial grid (4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48px).Component Sizing Heights:size-xs (24px height): Inline metadata pills and filter chips (meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 minimum 24×24px target size).size-sm (32px height): Standard toolbar buttons, search inputs, segmented view toggles.size-md (36px height): Default form inputs, primary modal buttons, compact List rows.size-touch (44px height): Automatically applied via @media (pointer: coarse) to buttons, menu items, and mobile list rows.Border Radius: --radius-sm: 4px (badges, keycaps, checkboxes); --radius-md: 6px (buttons, inputs, board cards); --radius-lg: 10px (drawers, popovers, dialogs).Iconography: Lucide Icons (lucide-react), standardized at 16×16px (1.75px stroke width) for UI controls and 14×14px (2px stroke width) for inline status/priority indicators.6.2 Component Architecture InventoryComponent GroupVariants & Core AnatomyBehavioral & State Rules1. Buttons & Icon ButtonsPrimary, Secondary (Outline), Ghost, Destructive, Icon-Only. Sizes: sm (32px), md (36px), touch (44px).Every Icon-Only button must require an aria-label prop at the TypeScript level and wrap in a 300ms-delayed Tooltip showing its label + shortcut keycap ([Archive]  E). Loading state replaces the leading icon with a 14px spinner while preserving button width.2. Text Inputs, Search & Filter ControlsStandard Input, Inline Editable Title, Search Omnibar, Faceted Filter Chip ([Property] [Operator] [Value] [×]).Filter chips support keyboard navigation (←/→ between chips, Enter to change value, Backspace/Delete to remove chip). Inline editable titles commit on Enter or Blur and revert on Escape.3. Dropdowns, Comboboxes & MenusAction Dropdown Menu, Searchable Property Combobox (Assignee, Status, Priority, Labels), Context Menu (Right-Click / ...).All property selectors use a Searchable Combobox pattern: opening the menu immediately focuses a top filter input ("Change status...") so users can either click an item or type 2 letters and press Enter.4. Dialogs, Drawers & Side PanelsRight Peek Drawer (Task details, non-blocking to main view), Modal Dialog (Creation wizards, destructive confirmations), Bottom Sheet (Mobile views).Drawers allow clicking tasks in the main canvas to switch the active task in-place without closing/reopening the drawer. Modals trap focus (focus-trap), lock background scroll, and require an explicit confirmation button before closing if unsaved form text exists.5. Task Cards, Rows & Detail ViewsList Row (36px/44px), Board Card (vertical stacked card), Calendar Chip (22px bar), Task Detail View (Drawer or Full Page).All 4 representations consume a shared <TaskPropertyPills/> sub-component so changing a status, priority, or assignee works identically whether clicked from a List row, Board card, or Detail Drawer.6. Status, Priority & Assignee Indicators<StatusBadge/> (5 canonical category icons + color), <PriorityBadge/> (signal bars + label), <AssigneeChip/> (Avatar + fallback initials + unassigned dashed circle).Clicking any indicator directly opens its respective Combobox popover (unless user role is read-only, in which case it displays a permission explanation tooltip).7. Tables & Data GridsTask TreeGrid (List View with expandable subtask rows), Admin Directory Table (Members, Workspaces, Audit Logs).Supports sticky group headers, column resizing, horizontal scroll shadows on narrow viewports, keyboard roving tabindex (0 on active cell, -1 on others), and virtualized row rendering (@tanstack/react-virtual) when rows exceed 100 items.8. Tabs & Segmented View ControlsView Switcher (`ListBoard9. Tooltips, Banners, Toasts & Confirmation DialogsTooltip (label + <kbd> keycap), System Banner (Offline, Role Preview, Conflict), Toast Stack (bottom-right, max 3 visible), Destructive Modal.Actionable Undo Toasts stay visible for 10 seconds, pause their countdown timer on pointer hover or keyboard focus (WCAG 2.2.1), and can be triggered globally via Z or Cmd/Ctrl + Z.10. Empty States, Skeletons & Error PresentationsView Empty State (contextual to Zero Data vs. Zero Filter Matches), Geometry-Matched Skeletons, Inline Retry Error Card.Skeletons must match the exact height and layout of the target view (36px rows for List; 4 columns for Board) to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) on load.11. Navigation Elements & Mobile Bottom NavDesktop Collapsible Sidebar (240px), Breadcrumb Header Bar, Mobile 5-Tab Bottom Navigation Bar (56px height).Desktop sidebar toggles with [ shortcut and auto-collapses to an off-canvas drawer below 1024px. Mobile Bottom Nav pins My Work, Projects, + New Task, Inbox, and Search.6.3 Interaction Foundations & Motion RulesInteractive State Matrix: Every interactive element must define 6 explicit visual states:Default: Resting semantic surface and border.Hover: --bg-surface-hover background transition (80ms).Focus-Visible: 2px solid var(--focus-ring) with 2px offset (never outline: none without a high-contrast replacement).Active / Pressed: Subtle scale (0.98) or darkened surface luminance.Disabled / Locked: opacity: 0.55, aria-disabled="true" (kept focusable with a tooltip when disabled due to permissions so screen-reader and keyboard users learn why the control is unavailable).Loading / Optimistic Pending: Subtle pulse or inline spinner after 400ms delay (avoid flashing spinners for requests that resolve in under 400ms).Motion Guidelines & When to Avoid Animation:Keep Under 180ms: Drawer slide-ins (160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), popover scale/fade (100ms), and board card drop settlement (150ms).Zero Animation on High-Frequency Actions: Switching between tabs/views, opening the Cmd/Ctrl + K Omnibar, moving keyboard focus across List rows, and filtering tasks must occur instantaneously (0ms) so the interface feels crisp and never lags behind typing speed.Reduced Motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): Automatically strips all spatial slide/scale transforms and replaces them with instant state changes or 80ms opacity fades.6.4 Component-Library Strategy for Antigravity CLICandidate ApproachAccessibility (WCAG / ARIA)Maintainability in Antigravity CLICustomization & Bundle WeightRecommendation1. Heavy Opinionated UI Kits (MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI)Good baseline, but complex overrides often break ARIA relationships.Poor. Fighting built-in CSS-in-JS specificity to build compact 36px task rows and custom keyboard shortcuts creates brittle code.Heavy bundle size; generic corporate aesthetic that looks like a stock template.Reject.2. Pure Custom Components From ScratchHigh Risk. Building accessible focus traps, roving tabindex grids, and screen-reader comboboxes from scratch introduces regressions.Poor. Wastes implementation time reinventing low-level browser focus and portal position math.Lightweight, but prohibitive engineering cost.Reject.3. Recommended Hybrid: Headless Accessible Primitives (Radix UI + React Aria / cmdk + @dnd-kit) Styled via Tailwind CSS (Shadcn-style local ownership)Excellent. WAI-ARIA 1.2 focus management, screen-reader announcements, and keyboard navigation are baked into the primitives.Ideal for Antigravity CLI. Components live directly in src/components/ui/ as clean, inspectable TypeScript + Tailwind files using our semantic CSS variables.Zero runtime CSS-in-JS overhead; 100% control over visual identity, density, and custom keyboard shortcuts.Adopt as Canonical Frontend Stack.Concrete Primitive Mapping:Dialogs, Drawers, Dropdowns, Popovers, Tooltips, Tabs: @radix-ui/react-* primitives.Command Bar & Searchable Comboboxes: cmdk (or React Aria ComboBox).Accessible Drag-and-Drop (Board & List Reordering): @dnd-kit/core + @dnd-kit/sortable configured with Keyboard, Pointer, and Touch sensors plus live ARIA announcements.Date & Range Pickers (Calendar / Timeline inputs): react-aria-components DatePicker / Calendar primitives (best-in-class keyboard & screen-reader date segment entry).7. Desktop, Tablet and Mobile BehaviorRather than squeezing desktop screens onto a phone, the layout shell and interaction patterns adapt across three structural breakpoints:Viewport TierBreakpoint RangeNavigation ShellTask Detail PresentationView Adaptations & Touch ErgonomicsDesktop & Widescreen1024px and widerPersistent Left Sidebar (240px, collapsible to 0px with [ shortcut) + Main Canvas + Inline Right Task Peek Drawer (540px).Side-by-side Right Peek Drawer allows viewing/clicking the List or Board while inspecting a task.Full 36px compact rows; hover actions visible (Rename, Quick Copy Key, ...); full multi-column Board and split-pane Timeline.Tablet / Small Laptop768px – 1023pxCollapsible Off-Canvas Left Sidebar Drawer (triggered via top-left Hamburger or Cmd/Ctrl + \) + Full-Width Main Canvas.Overlay Right Slide-Over Sheet (480px) with semi-transparent backdrop (Escape or backdrop tap closes).Touch targets scale to 40px–44px when @media (pointer: coarse) is detected; Board scrolls horizontally with CSS scroll-snap per column; Timeline left table collapses to 200px.Mobile (App-Like PWA Experience)Less than 768px (320px – 767px)Top Context Header (Workspace/Project Title + View Switcher) + Sticky 5-Tab Bottom Navigation Bar (My Work, Projects, + Create, Inbox, Search).Draggable Full-Screen Bottom Sheet (92vh expanded) with sticky top header (FEST-14 + Close ×) and sticky bottom Comment/Status bar.• List View: Two-line stacked task rows (56px height: Line 1 = Status Icon + Title; Line 2 = Key + Due Date + Priority + Assignee Avatar).• Board View: Single-Column Stage Switcher — top horizontal pill bar switches between `Todo (4)8. Accessibility Requirements and Reference SourcesThe table below distinguishes Formal Compliance Requirements (strictly required to pass W3C WCAG 2.2 Level AA and WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices 1.2) from General Productivity Usability Enhancements (recommended best practices for speed and ergonomics):Requirement AreaClassificationConcrete Testable SpecificationPrimary Reference & Direct URL1. Non-Dragging Alternatives for Board, List & TimelineFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 — Level AA)Every action executable via drag-and-drop (moving a card between Board columns, reordering List rank, resizing Timeline dates) must also be executable with a single pointer click/tap (Status/Position menu, Date picker inputs) and via keyboard.W3C Understanding SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html)2. Minimum Target Size & Touch ClearanceFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 — Level AA) + Mobile EnhancementCompliance: All interactive controls on desktop must occupy at least 24×24 CSS pixels (or have a 24px spacing offset circle).Enhancement: On touch viewports (pointer: coarse), enforce 44×44 CSS pixels minimum hit targets (aligning with WCAG 2.5.5 AAA / Apple HIG).W3C Understanding SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum):[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)3. Visible Focus Appearance & Focus Not ObscuredFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7, 2.4.11 & 2.4.13)Focused elements must display a solid 2px perimeter outline (--focus-ring) with at least 3:1 contrast against both unfocused state and adjacent surface. Sticky headers, bottom navbars, and floating Undo toasts must never completely obscure the currently focused element when tabbing.W3C Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured & SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html)[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html)4. Logical Focus Order & Modal/Drawer Focus ManagementFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 & WAI-ARIA APG Dialog Pattern)Opening a Modal or Mobile Bottom Sheet moves focus inside the container and traps Tab cycling until closed; pressing Escape closes the overlay and returns focus to the exact trigger element (e.g., the task row or button that opened it).W3C Understanding SC 2.4.3 Focus Order & WAI-ARIA APG Dialog:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html)[https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)5. Composite Widget Keyboard Navigation (Grids, Tabs, Comboboxes, Menus)Formal Compliance (WAI-ARIA APG 1.2 Composite Patterns)Use a single Tab stop per composite widget (List Grid, View Tabs, Property Menu) and manage internal movement via Arrow keys (roving tabindex or aria-activedescendant) so keyboard users do not have to press Tab 80 times to cross 10 task rows.W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) — Grid, Combobox & Tabs:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)6. Non-Color Cues for Status, Priority & ErrorsFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 — Level A)Never convey task status, priority, overdue state, or form validation errors through color alone. Pair every status with its distinct geometric SVG icon (dashed circle, half-circle, checkmark) and every priority with signal bar counts (!, 3, 2, 1) plus accessible text labels.W3C Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)7. Text & Non-Text Contrast RatiosFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 & 1.4.11 — Level AA)Body text and task titles must maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for large 18pt+ headings). Input borders, checkbox outlines, status icons, and active tab indicators must maintain at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent surfaces in both Light and Dark themes.W3C Understanding SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) & SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)8. Dynamic State Announcements (aria-live)Formal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages — Level AA)Optimistic status updates, filter result counts ("Showing 4 tasks matching filter"), toast notifications, and connection state changes ("Offline — changes queued") must be announced via polite aria-live="polite" or role="status" regions without stealing keyboard focus.W3C Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)9. Single-Key Shortcuts & Conflict PreventionFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4 — Level A) + Power-User EnhancementGlobal single-character shortcuts (C for create, / for search, Z for undo) must be suppressed whenever focus is inside an <input>, <textarea>, or contenteditable element, and users must be able to toggle single-key shortcuts off in Personal Preferences → Accessibility.W3C Understanding SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts.html)10. Reduced Motion & Hover/Focus Content PersistenceFormal Compliance (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 & SC 2.3.3)Popovers and tooltips triggered on hover/focus must be dismissible (Escape key), hoverable (pointer can move into the tooltip without it vanishing), and persistent. Respect @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) across all transitions.W3C Understanding SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus:[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html)9. Error Handling, Feedback, Undo and Recovery PatternsA high-trust productivity platform must handle happy paths silently, make everyday mistakes effortlessly reversible, and treat network/sync failures transparently without ever losing user input.9.1 Optimistic UI Lifecycle & Rollback FeedbackPlaintext[User Action: e.g., Drag FEST-14 to "Done" or Change Priority to "Urgent"]
       │
       ├──► 0–16ms: Apply Optimistic State to Local UI Store immediately.
       │            (Save previous state snapshot `{prevStatus: 'In Progress'}` in Undo/Rollback buffer)
       │
       ├──► 0–400ms: Silent background mutation (`PATCH /api/v1/tasks/FEST-14` with `X-Mutation-Id`).
       │             If >400ms: Show subtle pulsing dot next to the updated property pill.
       │
       ├──► ON HTTP 200 OK:
       │    Confirm server state, clear pending indicator, record action in local `Cmd/Ctrl + Z` stack.
       │
       └──► ON HTTP 4xx / 5xx FAILURE (when online):
            1. Smoothly animate card/pill back to `{prevStatus: 'In Progress'}`.
            2. Display an actionable Error Toast with plain-language diagnosis:
               - If 403 Forbidden: "Couldn't move FEST-14: Only Coordinators can mark tasks Done in this project."
               - If 5xx / Timeout: "Couldn't save change to FEST-14 due to a server error. [Retry Now]"
9.2 Three-Tier Destructive Action & Recovery ArchitectureTierAction ExamplesImmediate UI BehaviorRecovery Mechanism & WindowConfirmation Modal Used?Tier 1: Everyday Reversible ChangesChanging task status, priority, assignee, due date, moving card on board, modifying local view filters.Executes immediately (less than 50ms).Press Cmd/Ctrl + Z (or click [Undo] on toast for batch/move operations) to dispatch the inverse mutation.Never.Tier 2: Soft-Delete / Archive OperationsArchiving a Task, Subtask, or List; removing a Coordinator/Member; updating a Shared View's filters.Executes immediately and displays a 10-second Undo Toast at bottom-right.0–10s: Click [Undo] or press Z.Up to 30 Days: Open Workspace Trash & Recovery (or Audit Log for views/members) and click [Restore].No for single tasks; Compact popover confirmation only when archiving a List containing 10 or more active tasks.Tier 3: Permanent / High-Impact DestructionPermanently purging an item from Trash before 30 days; deleting an entire Project or Shared Workspace; Global Admin Break-Glass override.Opens a Blocking High-Friction Modal stating exact blast radius ("This will permanently delete 42 tasks and 8 attachments").Irreversible (except via infrastructure database backup). Modal requires typing the Project/Workspace key (FEST) to enable the red confirm button.Yes (Mandatory Type-to-Confirm Modal).9.3 Network Interruption, Offline Queue & Conflict Resolution UITransient Disconnect (1–5 seconds): Silent exponential-backoff WebSocket reconnection; no alarming banners shown to the user.Sustained Offline State (greater than 5 seconds):Top application bar displays a compact, non-blocking pill: ⚡ Offline Mode — Viewing cached workspace (3 edits queued).Supported offline edits (creating tasks, posting comments, editing scalar task fields and descriptions) are written to a local IndexedDB mutation_queue and tagged with a subtle clock badge (Queued) on the task row/drawer.Unsupported offline structural actions (modifying workspace permissions, deleting projects, configuring custom fields) are disabled with a clear tooltip: "Requires an active internet connection."Sync Conflict Resolution Pattern (When Server State Diverged During Offline Window):Non-Overlapping Fields Auto-Merge: If the user changed Priority offline while a teammate changed Due Date online, the server merges both fields cleanly with zero user interruption.Same-Field / Description Conflict (HTTP 409): The server rejects only the conflicting field mutation and returns {server_value, server_actor, server_updated_at, client_value}.
