The UI highlights a Resolve Conflict (1) pill in the header and inside the task drawer, presenting three non-destructive choices:[Keep Teammate's Version] (discards local field edit, keeps copy in clipboard option).[Overwrite with My Version] (commits local value on top of latest revision, preserving teammate's prior value in the Task Activity Log).[Keep Teammate's & Save Mine as Comment] (safest zero-loss fallback for long rich-text descriptions).Permission Revoked While Offline (HTTP 403 on Replay): If a Workspace Owner removed the user or downgraded their role while they were editing offline, the queued changes are never deleted. They are moved into a local Unsynced Drafts Recovery Drawer where the user can click [Save to My Personal Workspace] or [Copy Text to Clipboard].10. Workspace Settings Architecture and Permission Comprehension Strategy10.1 Four-Tier Governance ScopesTo keep configuration powerful without cluttering everyday task views, all administrative controls are partitioned across four explicit scopes:Scope LevelEntry LocationWho Can AccessCategories Contained1. Global Community AdministrationLeft Sidebar Footer → Community Admin ConsoleGlobal Administrators only• Community Overview & Workspace Directory (Metadata + Audited Break-Glass)• Community Member Directory & Default Coordinators Pool• Shared Workspace Creation Policy & Storage Quotas• Community-Wide Security & Admin Audit Log2. Workspace-Owner SettingsActive Workspace Sidebar Footer → Workspace SettingsWorkspace Owners (Full R/W)All 9 Workspace Settings categories (listed in Section 10.2 below), including destructive workspace lifecycle, custom roles, and workspace audit logs.3. Delegated Coordinator SettingsActive Workspace Sidebar Footer → Workspace SettingsCoordinators (Scoped R/W)Same Workspace Settings shell, with edit controls enabled for delegated operational categories (Projects & Prefixes, Tasks/Fields/Workflows, Shared Views, Templates, Workspace Files, Trash Recovery) and read-only lock badges on Owner-only tabs (Role Definitions, Workspace Deletion).4. Personal User PreferencesBottom-Left User Avatar → Account & PreferencesEvery Individual User• Profile & Identity (Name, Avatar, Timezone)• Appearance & Density (Light/Dark/System, Compact/Comfortable rows, Reduced Motion)• Personal Notification & Reminder Rules• Keyboard Shortcuts Toggle & Reference10.2 The 9 Categorized Workspace Settings ModulesInside Workspace Settings, a clean left sub-navigation groups options into 9 logical categories so users never face a monolithic scrolling wall of switches:General Settings: Workspace Name, Icon/Color accent, Description, Default Landing View (List vs. Board), and (at bottom) Owner-only Archive or Transfer Workspace.Members & Invitations: Active members list, pending invitations, role assignment dropdowns, and the Default Community Coordinators inclusion toggle ([✓] Automatically add new Community Coordinators to this workspace — configurable per workspace by the Owner).Roles & Permissions: Built-in role cards (Owner, Coordinator, Member, Viewer) + custom role builder + Interactive "Preview as Role" Simulator.Projects, Hierarchy & Task Keys: Project list, Project Key Prefix configuration (2–6 uppercase letters with automatic historical alias redirection), and workspace/project Subtask Depth Policy (defaults to 1 level — Recommended for Board clarity, with an explicit Owner toggle to allow Up to 2 levels if required by a specific workflow).Custom Fields & Workflows:Workflow Status Mapper: Visual list grouped under the 5 Canonical State Categories (Backlog, Todo, In Progress, Done, Canceled). Owners/Coordinators can rename statuses, reorder them, or add custom statuses inside any category in seconds.Custom Fields Registry: Create project- or workspace-scoped fields (Text, Number, Single-Select, Multi-Select, Date, User, Checkbox), toggle whether they appear on Board/List cards, and archive unused fields without losing historical data.Views & Saved Layouts: Manage all Shared Views across the workspace, set the default pinned view order for projects, and re-assign ownership of orphaned shared views.Notifications & Reminders: Workspace-level default notification triggers (e.g., notify assignees 24 hours before due date) and optional webhook integrations in later phases.Templates: Manage the Built-in Starter Templates (Engineering Sprint, Event & Operations, Simple Tracker) and save custom project/task templates from existing project structures.Files, Storage, Audit History & Recovery:Files & Storage: Workspace storage usage meter, attachment size limits, and bulk file management.Audit History: Filterable, exportable log of administrative events (Role changes, Member removals, Prefix updates, Shared view edits, Admin Break-Glass actions).Trash & Recovery: 30-day soft-deleted tasks, lists, and projects with 1-click restoration.10.3 Plain-Language Permission Comprehension & Contradiction PreventionHuman-Readable Capability Bundles (No Raw CRUD Jargon): Instead of exposing database flags like TASK_ACL_WRITE_BIT_4, permissions are grouped into 6 plain-language cards with concrete examples:Workspace Governance: "Rename workspace, manage roles, view audit logs, or delete projects."Member Management: "Invite new members and assign Member or Coordinator roles."Project & Workflow Structure: "Create projects/lists, configure custom fields, and edit workflow statuses."Shared Views & Templates: "Create, edit, or pin Shared Views and templates visible to the whole team."Task Execution & Collaboration: "Create tasks, update statuses/priorities/dates, move cards, comment, and upload files."Task Destructive Actions: "Move tasks across projects or permanently purge archived items from Trash.""Why Can/Can't This User Do X?" Permission Inspector: Inside Roles & Permissions, an Owner can select any Workspace Member from a dropdown (Inspect permissions for: @Sarthak) to see their effective capabilities and which role grants each capability (e.g., Can edit Shared Views → Granted via Coordinator role).Contradiction Lock Guards: Capabilities enforce a strict dependency hierarchy in the UI:Enabling Create/Edit Shared Views or Create Tasks automatically enables and locks View Projects & Tasks.Enabling Permanently Delete Tasks automatically requires Archive Tasks.Every role matrix modification shows a live blast-radius summary before saving: "Saving this change will grant Shared View editing to 8 members in the Coordinator role."11. Usability Validation Plan and Provisional Success MetricsRather than running an expensive multi-month lab programme, we will validate the interface using a 2-Wave Hallway & Pilot Validation Protocol with 10–12 members of our target 70–90 person community before full community rollout.11.1 Role-Specific Validation ProtocolParticipants: 10 community members split across experience levels and roles:4 New / Non-Technical Members (never used Jira or Linear before).3 Experienced Users (familiar with Jira, Trello, or Notion).2 Coordinators (responsible for organizing events or project squads).1 Workspace Owner / Global Admin.Session Format: 25-minute unassisted screen-share (15 minutes on Desktop, 10 minutes on Mobile phone) using a seeded staging environment (Annual Tech Fest workspace with 35 realistic tasks).Test Scenario IDTarget RolePrompt Given to Participant (Zero Hints)Usability Pitfalls to Watch ForVAL-01: First-Task Time-to-ValueNew Member"Sign in, find the task assigned to you about the auditorium audio setup, mark its first subtask complete, move the task to In Progress, and leave a comment asking about microphones."Hunting through the sidebar instead of using My Work; failing to notice the status pill is clickable; confusion between subtask checkbox and parent status.VAL-02: Rapid Creation & Key LookupCoordinator & Member"Create a new high-priority task due this Friday under the 'Logistics' list. Then use the keyboard or search bar to jump directly to task FEST-08."Opening a heavy modal when inline creation was faster; typing FEST-08 into a view filter instead of the Cmd/Ctrl + K Omnibar.VAL-03: View Switching & Safe FilteringMember & Coordinator"Switch the project from List View to Board View, filter the board to show only High Priority tasks, and make sure you haven't changed the board for your teammates."Anxiety about breaking the shared board; inability to notice the Unsaved changes • [Reset] draft indicator; losing track of undated tasks when switching to Calendar/Timeline.VAL-04: Mistake Recovery (Archive & Undo)All Roles"Archive task FEST-12. Now imagine you did that by mistake — bring it back. Next, find a task that was archived yesterday and restore it."Missing the 10-second Undo toast; hunting inside Workspace Settings instead of the dedicated Trash & Recovery sidebar item.VAL-05: Workspace Setup & Permission ComprehensionWorkspace Owner"Create a new Shared Workspace, remove one of the default Coordinators, and verify what a standard Member is allowed to see and do on the board."Overlooking the pre-checked Default Coordinators chip list; failing to notice the Preview as Role simulator button.VAL-06: Keyboard-Only & Mobile Touch Sweep2 Power Users + 2 Mobile Users"On desktop, put the mouse aside and move a card from Todo to Done using only the keyboard. On your phone, update two tasks and reply to an inbox mention."Getting trapped inside a combobox or grid; attempting awkward drag gestures on mobile instead of tapping the single-column status switcher or bottom sheet pills.11.2 Measurable Outcomes & Provisional Target ThresholdsNote on Rigor: Thresholds marked (Sourced Standard) come directly from W3C WCAG 2.2 or established psychometrics (Jeff Sauro / Bangor et al. Visual-Direction Comparison and RecommendationWe must establish a cohesive, original visual identity before locking final brand hex values. Below is a comparison of three distinct visual directions suitable for a modern, low-friction productivity platform:Visual DirectionCore Aesthetic & Surface CharacterAdvantagesDrawbacks & RisksDirection A: "Warm Editorial Studio" (Inspired by paper notebooks, warm stone surfaces #FAF8F5, serif display headers, soft rounded pills)Warm cream/parchment backgrounds, low-contrast warm borders, literary feel (similar to Notion/Craft).Inviting and non-intimidating for casual or non-technical community members; feels calm for long text reading.Poor for high-density task views. Warm beige backgrounds reduce chromatic contrast against Amber/Orange status and priority badges; 36px data grids and dependency timelines look muddy.Direction B: "Crisp Architectural Precision" (RECOMMENDED) (Neutral cool-slate daylight surfaces #F8FAFC / #FFFFFF, deep carbon-navy dark mode #0B0F17, tabular monospace keys, 1px crisp structural hairlines, vibrant semantic status accents)High-clarity studio instrumentation: clean neutral canvases let Status Icons, Priority Signals, and Due Date Badges serve as the primary bursts of color.Optimal readability and scannability across all 4 views. Neutral cool-slate surfaces maximize WCAG contrast (greater than 7:1) for colored status pills; scales effortlessly between Light and Dark themes; feels fast, modern, and trustworthy for both engineers and operations leads.Can feel slightly clinical if empty states and onboarding lack warmth (easily solved with warm accent illustrations in empty states and friendly microcopy).Direction C: "High-Contrast Atmospheric Dark-First" (Deep obsidian #050508, neon electric gradients, translucent glassmorphism backdrop-blur-xl overlays)Cyberpunk / developer-tool aesthetic with glowing borders and heavy blur layers.Visually striking in screenshots; appeals strongly to hardcore terminal/developer audiences.High eye fatigue and GPU performance cost. Heavy backdrop-filter blurs cause scroll jank on large Kanban boards and Timelines; intimidates non-technical community coordinators; poor daylight readability on mobile screens.Recommendation: Adopt Direction B ("Crisp Architectural Precision") with Warm Human Micro-InteractionsWhy Direction B Wins: In a multi-view task manager where users scan 20–50 tasks containing Statuses, Priorities, Due Dates, Labels, and Avatars, the chrome must be quiet so the data can speak. Direction B uses neutral slate surfaces (Slate 50–900), a warm Indigo/Cobalt primary interactive accent (#4F46E5 Light / #6366F1 Dark), crisp 6px card radii, and tabular monospace task keys (FEST-14), giving the platform an original, refined identity that is equally welcoming in bright daylight and late-night dark mode.13. Design Decisions, Assumptions and Unresolved IssuesIn accordance with Section 4 of the research prompt, we explicitly separate Established Decisions, Recommended UX & Architectural Defaults for unresolved product boundaries, and Open Stakeholder Questions so nothing is silently assumed.13.1 Resolution Matrix for Unresolved Product BoundariesUnresolved Boundary (From Prompt Section 4)UX & Trust ImplicationsRecommended Default (Clearly Labeled Recommendation)Frontend & Backend Contract Impact1. Global Administrator Visibility into Personal WorkspacesIf Global Admins can silently browse a user's Personal Workspace, users will not trust it for personal drafting or study notes. Conversely, admins need to see community storage quotas.Recommendation: Strict Privacy for Personal Workspaces. Global Admins can view aggregate storage usage (e.g., 14 MB used) and account status, but cannot view projects, tasks, or files inside any user's Personal Workspace. Audited Break-Glass Override applies only to Shared Workspaces.UI displays a Private to You lock badge on Personal Workspaces. Backend /tasks and /projects endpoints reject requests for a Personal Workspace if requester_id != workspace.owner_id, even for GLOBAL_ADMIN.2. Final Task-Edit Permissions (Role vs. Creator vs. Assignee)If ordinary Members can only edit tasks assigned to them, collaborative triage breaks down. If anyone can permanently delete any task or move it out of the project, chaos ensues.Recommendation: Two-Tier Task Permission Split.• Execution Edits (Status, Priority, Due Date, Assignee, Description, Subtasks, Comments, Attachments): Permitted for Task Creator, Assignee, Coordinators, Owners, and Workspace Members (with a workspace toggle if an Owner wants a strict "Members can only edit own/assigned tasks" mode).• Structural/Destructive Actions (Move across projects, Archive others' tasks, Permanent delete): Restricted to Task Creator (archive own), Coordinators, and Workspace Owners.API returns a permissions: { canEdit, canArchive, canMove, canDelete } boolean map on task payloads (or role capability bitmask) so the frontend disables restricted controls with exact explanatory tooltips.3. Flexible Hierarchy vs. 1-Level Subtask DefaultUnlimited subtask nesting breaks Kanban Board cards and hides deeply nested work, yet certain complex projects may legitimately want a 2nd breakdown level.Recommendation: Configurable Hierarchy Spine with a 1-Level Default. Default every workspace/project to Project → List (optional) → Task → Subtask (Max Depth = 1). In Workspace Settings → Projects & Hierarchy, provide a Workspace Owner setting: Subtask Nesting Depth: [1 Level (Recommended for Boards)] / [Up to 2 Levels].Database uses self-referencing parent_task_id with a hierarchy_depth SMALLINT column (0 = Task, 1 = Subtask, 2 = Nested Subtask) validated against project.max_subtask_depth. UI hides + Add Subtask when task.hierarchy_depth >= project.max_subtask_depth.4. Incremental Delivery of All 4 Views in Initial Release TargetAll 4 views (List, Board, Calendar, Timeline) are part of the agreed initial-release target, though Antigravity CLI will build them incrementally across implementation sprints.Recommendation: Unified View Toolbar & Shared Data Contract From Sprint 1. Build the View Switcher bar (`ListBoard5. Incremental Delivery of Custom Roles & Advanced SettingsBuilding the full custom role matrix UI and automation builder in Sprint 1 delays core task workflows, but hardcoding role checks blocks future custom roles.Recommendation: Capability-Driven Frontend Guards from Day 1. Ship the 4 built-in roles (Global Admin, Owner, Coordinator, Member) first, while coding every frontend check against granular capability flags (can('view:share'), can('project:create')). Unlock the Custom Role Builder UI in the next sprint without refactoring any view components.User session payload returns effective_capabilities: string[] per workspace so frontend components never check role === 'OWNER' directly.6. Backend API & Database Contract AlignmentBecause a separate developer is implementing the backend while Antigravity CLI builds the frontend, mismatched assumptions about ranking, key aliases, or conflict payloads will stall integration.Recommendation: Mock-First OpenAPI + WebSocket Event Spec. Freeze the REST + WebSocket JSON schemas before writing view code, including lexorank ordering strings, task_key_aliases redirects, X-Mutation-Id headers, and structured 409 Conflict field diffs.Antigravity CLI develops against a deterministic MSW (Mock Service Worker) layer matching the exact shared contract while the backend is built in parallel.14. Implementation Agent Feature-Build Checklist (For Antigravity CLI)Every feature, view, or component built by an implementation agent must pass this 12-point verification gate before being marked complete:Markdown### ANTIGRAVITY CLI FEATURE-BUILD VERIFICATION CHECKLIST

[ ] 1. ZERO HARDCODED COLORS OR SIZES: Uses semantic CSS tokens (`--bg-surface-*`, `--text-*`, `--status-*`, `--focus-ring`) and looks crisp in both Light and Dark themes with >= 4.5:1 text contrast and >= 3:1 UI border/icon contrast.
[ ] 2. PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE RESPECTED: Primary creation/editing surfaces show <= 5 core controls by default; secondary metadata is tucked into expandable popovers or the Task Peek Drawer.
[ ] 3. FULL KEYBOARD OPERABILITY (NO MOUSE REQUIRED): Every interactive flow can be completed using only `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`, `Arrow` keys, `Enter`, `Space`, and `Escape`. Composite lists/boards use roving `tabindex` (`1 Tab stop` per widget group).
[ ] 4. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 NO-DRAG ALTERNATIVE: If the feature involves drag-and-drop (Board move, List reorder, Calendar/Timeline date drag), an equivalent single-click menu or keyboard input is present and tested.
[ ] 5. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 TARGET SIZES: All clickable targets are >= 24x24px on desktop and automatically scale to >= 44x44px under `@media (pointer: coarse)` / mobile viewports (< 768px).
[ ] 6. NON-COLOR STATUS & PRIORITY CUES: Every status, priority, overdue badge, and error state pairs its semantic color with a distinct SVG icon shape and accessible text/ARIA label.
[ ] 7. OPTIMISTIC UI & ROLLBACK SAFETY: User mutations update the UI in < 50ms, include an `X-Mutation-Id` header, smoothly roll back on API error, and show a plain-language actionable toast on failure.
[ ] 8. SAFE EXPLORATION & UNDO: Shared View filter/sort tweaks remain in local URL/session draft state (`Modified • [Reset]`) until explicitly saved. Archiving/moving triggers a 10-second Undo toast (`Z`) rather than a blocking modal.
[ ] 9. EXPLICIT PERMISSION GUARDS: Restricted controls check `can('<capability>')` rather than hardcoded role names, and display a helpful explanatory lock tooltip ("Only Workspace Owners and Coordinators can...") instead of vanishing mysteriously or throwing raw 403s.
[ ] 10. ALL 6 UI STATES IMPLEMENTED: Component explicitly handles (1) Loading Skeleton (geometry-matched), (2) Empty Data State, (3) Empty Filter Result State, (4) Populated State, (5) Permission-Locked State, and (6) Network/Sync Error State.
[ ] 11. FOCUS MANAGEMENT & ESCAPE EXIT: Opening any Dialog, Drawer, Combobox, or Mobile Sheet moves focus inside cleanly, and pressing `Escape` closes the top layer and restores focus to the exact trigger element.

Executive FindingsWork-management platforms fail mid-sized communities (70–90 members) when they force an false choice between unstructured simplicity (Trello, basic to-do lists) and administrative overhead before value delivery (Jira Cloud, ClickUp). Research across five established platforms (Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, and open-source Plane) alongside Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g) usability findings demonstrates three core strategic truths for this product:Progressive Disclosure Must Govern Configuration: Jira and ClickUp expose schema administration (workflow schemes, permission schemes, custom field contexts, and deep hierarchy toggles) during everyday work, creating high cognitive friction and frequent permission lockouts. Linear and Plane succeed in fast onboarding by locking in an opinionated core workflow (Backlog → Todo → In Progress → Done → Canceled) while hiding custom properties, workflow transitions, and automations under categorized workspace settings.Foundational Data Architecture Must Precede Feature Surface: Trying to ship all requested capabilities—four view types (List, Board, Calendar, Timeline), custom RBAC, cross-project dependencies, workflow automation, workspace file hubs, and offline conflict-resolved editing—in a single release creates unacceptable schedule and state-synchronization risk between a separate backend developer and an Antigravity CLI frontend. However, six structural primitives must be built into the Day-1 database and API contract even if their full UI is deferred:Top-level community_id tenant scoping on all tables.Immutable UUID task identities paired with a task_key_aliases redirect ledger (PROJ-12 → NEW-45) for permanent task keys.Fixed 4-level entity spine (Workspace → Project → List [optional grouping] → Task → Subtask [depth = 1]).Fractional indexing (lexorank string column) for zero-collision List and Board ordering.Append-only domain_events outbox table powering activity history, audit logs, real-time WebSocket broadcasts, and future automations.Field-level updated_at timestamps and client mutation_id idempotency envelopes to enable Phase 3 offline queue replay without rewriting REST/WebSocket endpoints.Clear Boundary Defaults Eliminate 80% of Permission & Sync Bugs: Ambiguities around Global Admin vs. Workspace Owner privacy, Coordinator default access, shared view filtering ("View Drift"), and offline permission revocation must be resolved via deterministic product defaults before API schemas are written.2. Conflicts, Dependencies and Recommended DefaultsBelow is the architectural analysis of the nine tension points in our established requirements, separating the Product Decision (what the user experiences) from the Implementation Decision (how the backend and Antigravity CLI enforce it).7.1 Global Administrator Powers vs. Workspace-Owner AutonomyThe Conflict: If Global Admins have unrestricted read/write access to all Personal Workspaces and private Shared Workspaces by default, users cannot trust Personal Workspaces as private scratchpads, and Workspace Owners lose true autonomy. Conversely, if Global Admins have zero visibility into Shared Workspaces, an orphaned workspace (where the Owner leaves the community) becomes unrecoverable.Recommended Default: Tenant Metadata Governance + Audited Break-Glass Recovery.Product Decision: Global Admins manage community-level membership, control who can create Shared Workspaces, and view Shared Workspace metadata (name, owner list, member count, storage used). Global Admins cannot browse the tasks inside a user's Personal Workspace. For private Shared Workspaces where the Global Admin is not a member, they can only join or assign a new Owner via an explicit "Administrative Override" action that notifies all current Workspace Owners and writes a permanent entry to the workspace's Audit Log.Implementation Decision: Enforce workspace_memberships checks on all task/project queries even for GLOBAL_ADMIN tokens, exposing a separate POST /api/v1/admin/workspaces/{id}/break-glass endpoint that requires a reason string, emits a high-priority WORKSPACE_ADMIN_OVERRIDE audit event, and grants temporary Owner membership.7.2 Coordinator Access vs. Task-Level PermissionsThe Conflict: Requirements state that Coordinators are included in new Shared Workspaces by default (though removable by the Owner) and that tasks/views have configurable permissions. If task-level read restrictions ("Private Tasks") are introduced alongside workspace-wide Coordinator roles, board task counts, dependencies, and Coordinator triage dashboards become inconsistent across users.Recommended Default: Workspace/Project Visibility Boundary (No Task-Level Read Hiding in MVP).Product Decision: All members of a Shared Workspace (including active Coordinators) have read visibility into projects and tasks within that workspace. Coordinators are automatically added to newly created Shared Workspaces via a pre-checked "Include Community Coordinators" list during workspace creation, and Workspace Owners can remove any Coordinator at any time from Workspace Settings. If work requires restricted visibility, it belongs in a separate Shared Workspace or a Personal Workspace.Implementation Decision: Scope read authorization at the workspace_id (and optional project_id in Phase 2) level rather than adding per-task ACL join tables, keeping board/list query execution under 15ms.7.3 Task Creator Permissions vs. Assignee PermissionsThe Conflict: When a Member creates a task and assigns it to someone else (or is assigned a task created by a Coordinator), conflict arises if both try to edit structural fields or delete the task.Recommended Default: Collaboration Parity for Execution; Role Gating for Destruction.Product Decision: Any Workspace Member can create tasks and edit execution attributes (status, assignee, priority, due date, description, comments, labels) on tasks in their workspace—with the Assignee and Creator automatically subscribed as watchers. However, destructive or structural actions (permanently deleting a task, moving a task to another Project, or altering custom field schemas) are restricted to the Task Creator (within 1 hour of creation if no subtasks/comments exist), Coordinators, and Workspace Owners. Any member can Archive (soft-delete) a task they created, which remains recoverable for 30 days.Implementation Decision: Distinguish task:update_execution (granted to MEMBER, COORDINATOR, OWNER) from task:move_project and task:hard_delete (restricted to COORDINATOR and OWNER).7.4 Flexible Hierarchies vs. Consistent Task RelationshipsThe Conflict: Allowing arbitrary hierarchy depth (Project → Folder → List → Task → Subtask → Sub-subtask) alongside cross-project dependencies (blocks / blocked_by) breaks Kanban boards, creates circular rollup loops, and confuses users about whether to use a List, a Parent Task, or a Dependency.Recommended Default: Fixed 4-Tier Spine (Project → List → Task → Subtask [Max Depth 1]) + Explicit Typed Links.Product Decision: Every Project contains Tasks. Lists act as optional, single-level structural groupings within a Project (e.g., Phase 1, Marketing, Backlog). Tasks can have Subtasks (strictly 1 level deep), which receive their own permanent task keys (PROJ-14) and appear nested under their parent in List View or as a progress pill (2/4 subtasks) on Board cards. Cross-project or peer dependencies use explicit Task Relationships (blocks, is_blocked_by, relates_to, duplicates) with circular-dependency validation.Implementation Decision: Represent hierarchy via project_id (required), list_id (nullable FK), and parent_task_id (nullable self-FK with a database trigger/service check verifying parent.parent_task_id IS NULL). Store peer relationships in a dedicated task_links table with cycle detection on blocks edges.7.5 Shared View Customization vs. Simultaneous Collaborative EditingThe Conflict: If User A and User B both open a Shared Board View and User A filters by Priority = High or changes the sort order, syncing that filter mutation immediately to the database causes User B's screen to suddenly lose cards ("View Drift").Recommended Default: Copy-on-Write Ephemeral Drafts for Shared Views.Product Decision: Opening a Shared View loads its canonical filter, sort, and grouping configuration. When any user changes filters or sorting, those changes apply locally in their browser tab (reflected in URL query parameters) and display a subtle badge: Modified • [Reset] [Save as Personal View]. Only Workspace Owners, Coordinators, or the View Creator see an additional button: [Update Shared View for Everyone]. Meanwhile, changes to underlying task data (moving a card, changing status) broadcast in real time to all viewers.Implementation Decision: Separate /api/v1/views/{id} (saved view configuration JSON) from transient client filter state stored in React URL router state / Zustand memory in the Antigravity CLI frontend.7.6 Offline Editing vs. Permission Revocation and Concurrent ChangesThe Conflict: A user goes offline for 3 hours, edits 5 tasks, and reconnects. During those 3 hours, either (a) a Workspace Owner removed the user from the workspace/revoked their edit role, or (b) a teammate edited the same task's status or description.Recommended Default: Scoped Offline Queue + Per-Field Last-Write-Wins (Scalar) + Non-Destructive Conflict Drafts (Rich Text & Revoked Access).Product Decision:Scope Limit: Offline mode (Phase 3) permits creating new tasks, adding comments, and updating scalar task fields (status, priority, assignee, due date, description). Administrative actions (changing permissions, deleting projects, editing workflows) are online-only.Permission Revocation on Reconnect: The server evaluates permissions against the user's current live role at the moment of sync, never their cached offline role. If access was revoked while offline (HTTP 403), the rejected changes are not silently discarded; they are saved into a local "Export / Copy Unsynced Changes" recovery drawer (or saved as a private draft task in the user's Personal Workspace) with a clear explanation.Concurrent Edits: Scalar fields (status, priority, due_date) merge per-field (so User A changing priority offline and User B changing due_date online both succeed without conflict). If the same scalar field or rich-text description was modified on the server after the offline client's base timestamp (base_revision), the server rejects the overwrite (409 Conflict) and the UI displays a side-by-side Conflict Resolution Banner: [Keep Server Version] [Apply My Offline Change] [Save Mine as Comment].Implementation Decision: Every offline mutation envelope includes {mutation_id, task_id, base_version, changed_fields_only, client_timestamp}. The backend validates live RBAC first, compares base_version against per-field version counters, and returns structured 409 conflict payloads when the same field diverged.7.7 Custom Roles and Settings vs. Understandable UXThe Conflict: Exposing a 40-checkbox permission matrix for custom roles overwhelms non-technical Workspace Owners and creates contradictory states (e.g., granting Delete Task without View Task).Recommended Default: 4 Immutable System Role Archetypes + 6 Bundled Capability Toggles (Phase 2).Product Decision: Workspaces start with 4 crystal-clear built-in roles (Owner, Coordinator, Member, Read-Only Guest/Viewer). When a Workspace Owner creates a Custom Role in Phase 2, they clone one of the 4 base roles and toggle 6 high-level capability bundles (Manage Workspace Settings, Manage Members, Create/Edit Projects & Workflows, Create/Edit Shared Views, Delete/Move Tasks, Comment & Update Task Status) rather than raw database CRUD flags. Dependent permissions auto-select automatically.Implementation Decision: Map the 6 UI capability bundles to granular backend permission scopes via a static translation dictionary so the UI stays simple while API enforcement remains exact.7.8 Real-Time Updates vs. Network Failure and Stale DataThe Conflict: Optimistic UI updates make boards feel instantaneous, but dropped WebSocket connections or failed HTTP mutations can leave a user staring at phantom state that never reached the server.Recommended Default: Bounded Optimistic UI + Monotonic Sequence Watermarks + Visual Connection Pill.Product Decision: Dragging a card or toggling a status updates the UI immediately (less than 16ms) with a subtle pending indicator if the request takes longer than 400ms. If the mutation fails, the card smoothly animates back to its prior state with an actionable error toast. If the real-time connection drops for more than 5 seconds, a non-blocking top status pill appears (Reconnecting — viewing cached state...) and automatically reconciles missed events upon reconnection without a full page reload.Implementation Decision: Assign a monotonically increasing workspace_seq_id to every workspace domain event. When a WebSocket reconnects, the client sends its last seen workspace_seq_id (GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/events?since_seq=1042) to catch up on missed deltas, or triggers a clean query cache invalidation if the gap exceeds 500 events.7.9 Production-Ready Initial Release vs. Overall Feature ScopeThe Conflict: Attempting to deliver all 4 views, custom RBAC UI, workflow automation, file hubs, and offline sync in Phase 1 will either delay launch indefinitely or result in a buggy, half-tested platform.Recommended Default: Strict Phase Gating with Complete Schema Readiness (Section 4 & 5 Model).Product Decision: Ship Phase 1 (MVP) when List View, Board View, Personal Dashboard, Permanent Keys, 4 Core Roles, Comments/Notifications, Audit Logs, and 30-day Trash meet 100% production quality and security standards. Hold Calendar, Timeline, Custom Role UI, File Hub, Automations, and Offline Sync for Phases 2 and 3.Implementation Decision: Enforce schema-first contract freezes per phase using shared OpenAPI 3.1 specifications and mock servers so Antigravity CLI and backend development proceed in parallel without blocking each other.8. Concise Decision LogA. Established Decisions (Locked Requirements from Prompt Context)EST-01: Platform supports Personal Workspaces (self-serve) and Shared Workspaces (permission-controlled) with multi-community readiness.EST-02: Role hierarchy includes Global Administrator, multiple Workspace Owners, Coordinators (included in new Shared Workspaces by default, removable by Owner), Members, and configurable custom roles.EST-03: Work items use automatic permanent task keys (PREFIX-NUM) with owner-configured project prefixes, supporting projects, lists, tasks, subtasks, dependencies, and cross-project relationships.EST-04: Roadmap encompasses List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline views, shared/personal saved views, custom fields, 2–3 built-in templates, comments/mentions/notifications, workspace file management, audit logs, recovery mechanisms, rule automations, and selected offline editing.B. Recommended Architectural & Scope Decisions (Proposed for Sign-Off)REC-01 (Hierarchy Cap): Lock entity hierarchy at Community → Workspace → Project → List (optional grouping) → Task → Subtask (max depth = 1). Represent all deeper or cross-project associations via typed task_links (blocks, blocked_by, relates_to).REC-02 (Canonical Workflow Spine): Require every custom workflow status created by a Workspace Owner to map to one of 5 immutable system state categories (Backlog, Todo, In Progress, Done, Canceled) so cross-workspace dashboards and progress bars remain consistent.REC-03 (Copy-on-Write Shared Views): Isolate filter/sort changes on Shared Views to the user's local session URL state by default; require an explicit "Update Shared View" action by an Owner/Coordinator/Creator to mutate the shared configuration.REC-04 (Audited Break-Glass Admin Boundary): Prevent Global Admins from reading Personal Workspaces; require an explicit, audit-logged "Break-Glass Override" action for a Global Admin to enter or reassign ownership of a private Shared Workspace they do not belong to.REC-05 (3-Phase Delivery Gate with Day-1 Schema Primitives): Ship List, Board, Personal Dashboard, 4 Core Roles, Permanent Keys, Core Custom Fields, 3 Templates, Notifications, Audit Logs, and 30-day Trash in Phase 1 (MVP) while embedding community_id, capability-based RBAC strings, workspace_files, domain_events, and X-Mutation-Id field timestamps in the Day-1 schema to support Phase 2 (Calendar, Timeline, Custom Role UI, File Hub, Reminders) and Phase 3 (Automations, Scoped Offline Editing, Field Snapshot Restore).C. Unresolved Questions (Requiring Stakeholder Decision Before Architecture Freeze)UNR-01 (Project Prefix Mutation Policy): When a Workspace Owner changes an existing Project's prefix (e.g., from MKT to GROWTH), should existing tasks re-key to GROWTH-1..N (with MKT-1..N preserved in the redirect alias table), or should only newly created tasks receive the new prefix? (Recommended default: Re-key all tasks in the project to the new prefix and store all old MKT-* keys in task_key_aliases so every historical link and comment reference resolves seamlessly).UNR-02 (Attachment Storage Quota per Workspace): For our initial 70–90 user community, what per-file size limit (e.g., 25 MB or 50 MB) and per-workspace storage cap should the backend enforce in object storage?UNR-03 (External Notification Channels in MVP): Does MVP require only in-app real-time notifications + email digests, or do we need outbound webhook/Slack/Discord notifications in Phase 1? (Recommended default: In-app Inbox + transactional Email in MVP; outbound Webhooks in Phase 3 alongside the Automation Engine).

Executive VerdictVerdict: Conditionally (No for general workflow research; Yes only for isolated offline HAR/network payload schema analysis via CLI).Primary Reasoning: Our goal is to build an original, low-friction task and workspace management platform for 70–90 users inspired by Jira's workflows, not to clone proprietary binary logic or desktop clients. Because Jira is a cloud SaaS application with extensive public REST/GraphQL documentation and observable browser behavior, over 90% of our research needs (UI states, task keys, permission patterns, board interactions) can be fulfilled faster and more safely using official Atlassian documentation, an authorized free Jira Cloud sandbox, and standard Chrome DevTools.Why REA is Overkill as a Primary Tool: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) excels at static binary decompilation (via Hopper/Ghidra/IDA) and Electron app.asar extraction. While it includes Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) browser observation and HAR capture analysis, live CDP attachment requires strict opt-in flags, strips HTTP response headers/bodies on passive live captures, and faces a strict 64 MiB WebSocket message boundary that large SaaS bundles like Jira Cloud frequently exceed.   Where REA Adds Conditional Value: If we encounter complex, undocumented client-side behavior (e.g., optimistic UI state mutations during board drag-and-drop or batch rank updates) and export a sanitized .har file from our own authorized Jira sandbox, running REA's standalone CLI (inspect-web-network-capture) offline is a clean way to generate structured JSON evidence reports to feed into our research chat.   2. Provider Model: REA delegates heavy analysis to external providers while normalizing output into structured Evidence bundles (containing verified facts, provenance, coverage limits, and an explicit list of unresolved "unknowns"). JavaScript & Electron Apps: Static inspection of extracted directories and .asar archives (entry points, module graphs, preload scripts, IPC channel mappings, and source maps) without executing code.   Native Binaries: Mach-O, ELF, PE, .NET assemblies, Go binaries, and WASM (requires Hopper, Ghidra 12.1.2 + JDK 21, IDA Pro, or caller-supplied objdump/Rizin). On Linux, static JS/Electron analysis and provider launches require a procps-compatible ps binary on PATH for process ownership verification. Windows x64 support is marked experimental.   Browser Prerequisite: A Chromium-family browser launched manually by the user with --remote-debugging-port on a loopback interface (127.0.0.1) using a dedicated profile.   Material Limitations, License & Security GuidanceLicense (Verified): REA-authored code is MIT licensed. Third-party analysis engines (Hopper, IDA Pro, JEB) retain their own commercial licenses. REA does not launch, own, or terminate the debugging browser.   64 MiB CDP Boundary: Enforces a strict 64 MiB limit per WebSocket message (payload_limit failure if exceeded) and an 8 MiB budget / 10-second deadline for HTTP target discovery.   Discarded Live Bodies: In passive live CDP page capture, HTTP response headers and bodies are discarded; pre-attachment network activity is unavailable, and source maps are not automatically fetched during live page inspection. (Full payload analysis requires exporting a HAR 1.2 file and using inspect-web-network-capture). Permission enforcement is backend-driven; REA cannot inspect backend RBAC evaluation.Two test accounts (Admin + Member) in a free Jira sandbox.Multi-Account Manual Observation.Settings & User-Management Flows (Invites, role assignment, workspace config)Yes (100%). Standard CRUD forms and invitation states observable via normal UI walk-throughs.None.Authorized Jira sandbox.Manual UI Walkthrough + Screenshots.Key Technical & Legal Boundaries for Hosted Jira InspectionBackend Opacity (Verified): Jira Cloud's core domain logic (permission evaluation, lexorank balancing, workflow state machines, notification fan-out, and conflict resolution) executes on Atlassian's backend servers. No client-side tool (including REA) can recover backend source code or database schemas.   Authentication & Anti-Bot Protections (Verified): Jira Cloud uses multi-step Atlassian ID authentication, strict CORS/CSRF tokens, and session cookies. REA does not bypass authentication; you must manually authenticate in a dedicated browser profile before attaching or exporting HAR files.   Minified Bundles & CDP Limits (Verified): Jira Cloud serves massive, heavily code-split Webpack/React bundles without public source maps. Attaching REA's live CDP inspector (analyze_web_bundle or inspect_web_page) frequently hits the 64 MiB WebSocket message limit (payload_limit) or produces low-signal minified AST summaries while omitting live response bodies.Terms of Service Restriction (Verified): Atlassian Cloud Terms of Service explicitly prohibit users from attempting to "reverse engineer, disassemble, decompile, translate or otherwise seek to obtain or derive the source code, underlying ideas, algorithms, file formats or non-public APIs" of the hosted service. Pointing automated decompilation or bundle-reconstruction tools at hosted Jira Cloud scripts creates unnecessary ToS compliance exposure, whereas reading public REST API docs and observing standard UI workflows as an authorized user is standard benchmarking.   5. Recommended Research WorkflowTo maintain strict separation between research and implementation, avoid unnecessary tool installation, and stay well within legal/technical boundaries, follow this 4-step workflow:1.Public Specification & API Mining (No Local Tools):Covers ~70% of architectural data modeling.Use your standalone Gemini/Argon research chat to analyze Atlassian's public REST API v3 documentation (/rest/api/3/issue, /project, /role, /workflow) and Atlassian Design System guidelines. Extract canonical entity relationships (how permanent task keys handle project moves, how parent/subtask hierarchies are constrained, and how activity changelogs are structured) without touching any reverse-engineering tool.2.Two-Persona Sandbox Benchmarking (Standard Browser):Requires a free, authorized Jira Cloud workspace.Spin up a free Jira Cloud workspace populated with dummy community data (e.g., 2 workspaces, 3 projects, 20 sample tasks). Open two browser profiles side-by-side (Owner/Coordinator and Standard Member). Walk through each target workflow manually to observe real-time synchronization, permission-denied states, empty states, and inline editing ergonomics.3.Structured Evidence Capture (Standard DevTools / Optional REA CLI):Sanitize all captures before saving.For complex client-server interactions (such as optimistic drag-and-drop board reordering or offline reconnection behavior), use standard Chrome DevTools (Network & Performance tabs) to inspect the request/response sequence.Optional REA CLI Path: If a workflow generates dozens of interdependent network calls and you want an automated state-change summary, export a .har file from DevTools (using a throwaway test account), strip authentication headers/cookies, and run npx -y rea-agents@latest inspect-web-network-capture ./sanitized.har har --json in an isolated terminal folder to produce a structured JSON Evidence report.4.Synthesis & Simplification in Research Chat:Bridge from research to clean-room specification.Feed your structured observation notes (and any sanitized JSON evidence reports) into your Gemini/Argon research chat. Prompt the research chat to strip away Jira's enterprise bloat and synthesize clean, original data models and state transition specs tailored for our 70–90 person community. Only when these clean-room Markdown specs are finalized should they be handed over to Antigravity CLI for frontend implementation and to your backend developer for API design.Standardized Workflow Evidence TemplateUse this Markdown template in your research notes for every examined workflow so findings remain clean-room, verifiable, and actionable:Markdown### Workflow Target: [e.g., Task Move Across Board Columns]
- **Source & Method:** [e.g., Public REST API Docs + Authorized Sandbox Observation]
- **Preconditions & Role:** [e.g., Authenticated Coordinator; Board has >2 tasks in target column]
- **Interaction Sequence (Inputs -> State Changes):**
  1. User drags Task `COMM-12` from "In Progress" to "Review" between `COMM-08` and `COMM-15`.
  2. Optimistic UI updates card position and column badge immediately (<16ms).
  3. Client dispatches `PUT /transition` + `PUT /rank` (before `COMM-15`).
- **Edge, Empty, Loading & Error States:**
  - *Loading:* Subtle card opacity shift; no blocking spinner unless transition requires a modal screen.
  - *Error / Rollback:* On HTTP 403/500, card animates back to origin column + toast notification displays reason.
  - *Permission Denied:* Member without transition rights sees locked drag handle / greyed-out drop zone.
- **Verified Evidence vs. Uncertainties:**
  - *Verified:* Rank updates use lexicographical string markers rather than integer indices (prevents full-table re-indexing).
  - *Needs Manual Validation:* Conflict resolution behavior when two users move the same card while one is briefly offline.
- **Simplification & Original UX Opportunity:**
  - *Drop from Jira:* Remove mandatory transition screens and complex workflow scheme validators.
  - *Our Design:* Use lightweight fractional indexing for task ordering and instant inline status pills with undo-toast support.

Risks and SafeguardsAuthorization & Terms of Service Risk:Risk: Attaching automated reverse-engineering or bundle-decompilation tools to hosted Jira Cloud violates Atlassian's Cloud Terms of Service.   Safeguard: Restrict all research to public documentation and normal human interaction inside an authorized sandbox workspace you control. Do not run analyze_web_bundle or decompilers against proprietary SaaS code.   Credential & Privacy Exposure in Captures:Risk: HAR files and REA Evidence bundles retain HTTP headers, session cookies, CSRF tokens, and query tokens. REA's own documentation warns: "Credential-name warnings identify places to review; they do not remove those values." Furthermore, automated SAST scans (Plexicus, Oct 21, 2026) flagged 5 low-severity "Secrets" leads in the repository snapshot and noted that runtime MCP permissions and prompt injection require operator vigilance.   Safeguard: Never use production or personal accounts during capture sessions. Use throwaway sandbox credentials, run a dedicated empty browser profile, and strip Cookie and Authorization headers before saving or uploading any HAR/JSON snippet to an AI chat.   Clean-Room & Intellectual Property Contamination:Risk: Feeding decompiled client bundles directly into an implementation agent (like Antigravity CLI) risks generating derivative code or copying proprietary implementation quirks.   Safeguard: Maintain a strict clean-room firewall. Research outputs must be written as behavioral requirements and abstract state descriptions (using the template in Section 5)—never raw copied scripts or proprietary bundles.Development Environment & Supply-Chain Hygiene:Risk: rea-agents is a rapidly mutating package (jumping from v0.2.0 in July 2026 to v6.8.0 in late October 2026 with hundreds of open PRs). Running global installs or auto-configuring MCP servers across all local coding agents modifies global config files (~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json).   Safeguard: Do not install rea-agents globally on your primary implementation setup. If tested at all, run it pinned to an exact version inside a disposable container/VM or with --dry-run first.   8. 1. Governing Contract Principles, API Conventions & Error Model
1.1 Canonical Contract Architecture ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
To enable parallel development between Antigravity CLI (Frontend) and the Backend Developer with zero invented behavior, integration is governed by one version-controlled contract bundle located in /contracts/:

HTTP REST Specification (/contracts/openapi.yaml): Authored in OpenAPI 3.1.0 ([https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0.html](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0.html)), which natively aligns with JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 (jsonSchemaDialect: "[https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema)").

Realtime WebSocket Protocol (/contracts/ws-events.schema.json): Authored in JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 defining client-to-server control frames and server-to-client workspace delta envelopes.

Single Source of Truth Rule: Neither developer may add, rename, or alter an endpoint, query parameter, enum value, or error code in application code without first updating /contracts/ and running the schema linter and type generator.

1.2 Global Identity Routes vs. Community-Scoped Routes ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
Because a User identity is global while membership, roles, and data isolation are scoped per Community and Workspace, all endpoints follow a strict two-tier URI hierarchy:

Tier 1 — Global Identity & Session Endpoints (/api/v1/auth/* and /api/v1/me/*): Operate on the authenticated user's global identity, active sessions, linked OAuth providers, and the list of communities the user belongs to.

Tier 2 — Community-Scoped Operational Endpoints (/api/v1/communities/{communityId}/...): Every workspace, project, list, milestone, task, view, comment, file, notification, and audit log route is nested under /api/v1/communities/{communityId}/....

Zero-Trust Scope Validation: The {communityId} and {workspaceId} path parameters identify the requested resource scope; they are never treated as proof of access. On every request, backend middleware resolves the authenticated user_id from the session token, verifies active membership in {communityId} and {workspaceId}, and binds an immutable server-side SecurityContext.

1.3 Common HTTP Conventions
Convention Area	Normative Specification
API Versioning & Naming	URI path major versioning (/api/v1/...). Resource collections use plural kebab-case nouns (/workspaces, /saved-views, /custom-fields, /audit-logs). JSON properties use camelCase (workspaceId, currentKey, dueDate).
Content Types	Requests and responses use application/json; charset=utf-8. Error responses use application/problem+json; charset=utf-8 (RFC 9457). CSV exports return text/csv; charset=utf-8.
Resource Identifiers & Task Key Lookup	Internal primary keys are UUIDv7 strings (time-sortable, URL-safe, e.g., "0192d8f0-7b2a-7000-8000-1a2b3c4d5e6f"). Task endpoints accept UUID taskId at /tasks/{taskId}, while human-readable keys (FEST-14 or historical alias OLD-09) resolve via /workspaces/{workspaceId}/tasks/by-key/{taskKey}.
Date-Only vs. Timestamp Semantics	
• Timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt, archivedAt): RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC strings with millisecond precision ("2026-10-30T08:15:30.120Z").


• Calendar Dates (startDate, dueDate, targetDate): ISO 8601 date-only strings ("2026-11-15"). Storing due dates as YYYY-MM-DD prevents a task due on "November 15" from shifting to "November 14 at 19:00" when viewed by a teammate in a different timezone. Deadline reminders evaluate against the workspace's configured default timezone (or user's timezone preference).

Cursor Pagination & Stable Ordering	Collection endpoints use opaque cursor pagination (?cursor=<base64url>&limit=50, default 50, max 200). Every cursor encodes the sort key tuple plus the unique tie-breaker (sort_value, id) so concurrent inserts or rank moves never cause duplicate or skipped rows across pages. Response envelope wraps data: T[] and pageInfo: { nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean, totalCount?: number }.
Idempotent Mutations (X-Mutation-Id)	All state-mutating requests (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE) must include X-Mutation-Id: <UUIDv4>. The server stores (user_id, mutation_id) in idempotency_records for 7 days. Re-sending an already committed X-Mutation-Id returns the original HTTP status and body plus header X-Idempotent-Replayed: true without re-executing side effects.
Correlation IDs (X-Request-Id)	Clients may send X-Request-Id: <UUIDv4> (if omitted, the server generates one). The server echoes X-Request-Id in all response headers and embeds it as correlationId in all error payloads and structured server logs.
Rate Limiting & Retry Headers	Responses include standard IETF draft rate-limit headers: RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset (seconds until window reset). When throttled (HTTP 429), the server returns Retry-After: <seconds> and retryAfterMs in the Problem Details body. Default tiers: 120 req/min for standard reads, 60 req/min for single writes, 10 req/min for bulk/CSV operations per user.
Missing vs. Inaccessible Resources (Anti-Enumeration Rule)	
• Unjoined Workspace or Another User's Personal Workspace: Always return 404 Not Found (identical to a non-existent UUID/key) so an attacker cannot probe which workspace IDs or task keys (SEC-01..SEC-99) exist in unauthorized spaces.


• Joined Workspace Where User Lacks Action Capability: When the user has read visibility into the workspace/task (e.g., an ordinary Member attempting to delete a Project or edit a task locked under Conflict 2), return 403 Forbidden with requiredCapability and a human-readable explanation so the UI can explain why the action was blocked.

1.4 RFC 9457 Problem Details Error Model ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
All non-2xx responses conform to RFC 9457 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs, application/problem+json), which obsoletes RFC 7807, extended with deterministic machine-readable fields for validation, permissions, and concurrency conflicts:

JSON
{
  "type": "https://api.workplatform.internal/errors/validation-failed",
  "title": "Request Validation Failed",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "One or more fields failed domain validation.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/communities/com_01/workspaces/ws_01/tasks",
  "errorCode": "TASK_VALIDATION_FAILED",
  "correlationId": "req_0192d8f4-9c11-7000-8000-001122334455",
  "retryable": false,
  "fieldErrors": [
    {
      "field": "dueDate",
      "pointer": "/dueDate",
      "code": "DATE_BEFORE_START_DATE",
      "message": "Due date (2026-11-01) cannot be earlier than start date (2026-11-05)."
    }
  ]
}
Standard HTTP Status Code & Application errorCode Mapping
HTTP Status	Problem type Suffix	Canonical errorCode Values	Meaning & Client Handling Contract
400 Bad Request	/malformed-request	MALFORMED_JSON, INVALID_QUERY_AST, INVALID_CURSOR, MISSING_MUTATION_ID	Syntactically invalid request, malformed cursor, or missing X-Mutation-Id header. Not retryable without fixing client request syntax.
401 Unauthorized	/unauthenticated	SESSION_EXPIRED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, OAUTH_CODE_INVALID	Missing or expired session. Client attempts silent token refresh or redirects to Sign-In while preserving local unsaved drafts.
403 Forbidden	/permission-denied	INSUFFICIENT_CAPABILITY, TASK_EDIT_RESTRICTED_BY_POLICY, PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY, PERSONAL_WORKSPACE_PRIVATE, SIGNOFF_REQUIRED	Actor is authenticated and can see the resource, but lacks permission. Includes requiredCapability and policyMode extensions. In offline replay, triggers Local Recovery Quarantine.
404 Not Found	/resource-not-found	RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, TASK_KEY_NOT_FOUND	Resource does not exist or belongs to a workspace/community the actor is not authorized to view (anti-enumeration).
409 Conflict	/state-conflict	FIELD_REVISION_CONFLICT, PROJECT_PREFIX_IN_USE, LAST_OWNER_CANNOT_LEAVE, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH	Concurrent modification of the same field (conflictingFields array attached), duplicate prefix/slug, or governance invariant violation.
410 Gone	/resource-gone	EVENT_SEQ_OUT_OF_RETENTION, INVITE_EXPIRED, TASK_PERMANENTLY_PURGED	Requested WebSocket since_seq gap exceeds the 500-event delta buffer (client must invalidate query cache and refetch view), or item was permanently purged from Trash.
413 Content Too Large	/payload-too-large	FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, BULK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED	Attachment exceeds maxFileSizeBytes (provisional default 25 MB) or bulk array exceeds 100 task IDs.
422 Unprocessable Content	/validation-failed	TASK_VALIDATION_FAILED, DEPENDENCY_CYCLE_DETECTED, MAX_SUBTASK_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, CUSTOM_FIELD_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED	Well-formed JSON that violates domain invariants (includes fieldErrors[]).
429 Too Many Requests	/rate-limit-exceeded	RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED	Client exceeded rate quota. Includes retryable: true and retryAfterMs. Client backs off exponentially.
500 / 503	/internal-error, /service-unavailable	INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE	Unexpected server fault. Includes retryable: true and correlationId. Optimistic UI rolls back cleanly and offers [Retry].

3. OpenAPI 3.1.x Structure and Reusable Component Schemas
Below is the canonical root skeleton for /contracts/openapi.yaml, utilizing OpenAPI 3.1.0 and JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 (type: ["string", "null"] nullable syntax):

YAML
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Community Work & Workspace Management Platform API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: >-
    Authoritative HTTP contract shared between Antigravity CLI (Frontend)
    and Backend implementation across Milestones M1.1–M1.3 and Phases 2–4.
jsonSchemaDialect: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
servers:
  - url: /api/v1
    description: Version 1 API Root

security:
  - SessionCookieAuth: []
    CsrfHeaderAuth: []
  - BearerTokenAuth: []

components:
  securitySchemes:
    SessionCookieAuth:
      type: apiKey
      in: cookie
      name: __Host-session
    CsrfHeaderAuth:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: X-CSRF-Token
    BearerTokenAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT

  parameters:
    CommunityIdParam:
      name: communityId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
    WorkspaceIdParam:
      name: workspaceId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
    MutationIdHeader:
      name: X-Mutation-Id
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Client-generated UUIDv4 guaranteeing idempotent mutation execution.
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid
    PreviewRoleIdHeader:
      name: X-Preview-Role-Id
      in: header
      required: false
      description: >-
        Optional downward-scoping role UUID for Owner/Admin "Preview as Role" simulation.
        Never elevates privileges; blocks state-mutating requests unless explicitly bypassed.
      schema:
        type: string
        format: uuid

  schemas:
    PageInfo:
      type: object
      required: [nextCursor, hasMore]
      properties:
        nextCursor:
          type: ["string", "null"]
        hasMore:
          type: boolean
        totalCount:
          type: ["integer", "null"]

    ProblemDetails:
      type: object
      description: RFC 9457 Problem Details envelope (application/problem+json)
      required: [type, title, status, detail, errorCode, correlationId, retryable]
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          format: uri
        title:
          type: string
        status:
          type: integer
        detail:
          type: string
        instance:
          type: string
        errorCode:
          type: string
        correlationId:
          type: string
        retryable:
          type: boolean
        retryAfterMs:
          type: ["integer", "null"]
        requiredCapability:
          type: ["string", "null"]
        policyMode:
          type: ["string", "null"]
        fieldErrors:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [field, code, message]
            properties:
              field: { type: string }
              pointer: { type: string }
              code: { type: string }
              message: { type: string }
        conflictingFields:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldConflictDetail"

    FieldConflictDetail:
      type: object
      required: [field, clientBaseRevision, serverCurrentRevision, clientValue, serverValue, serverUpdatedAt, serverActor]
      properties:
        field:
          type: string
        clientBaseRevision:
          type: integer
        serverCurrentRevision:
          type: integer
        clientValue: {}
        serverValue: {}
        serverUpdatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        serverActor:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/UserRefDto"
4. Canonical Data-Transfer Schemas (DTOs)
4.1 Architectural Trade-Off: Embedding effectivePermissions on TaskDto vs. Separate Endpoint ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
The Question: Should the backend include computed action flags (effectivePermissions) directly inside each TaskDto, or should the frontend fetch a separate /permissions endpoint and compute task editability on the client?

Trade-Off Analysis:

Option 1 (Client-Side Rule Re-Implementation): If the frontend only receives workspace role capabilities, Antigravity CLI must re-implement Conflict 2's contextual rules (isCreator || isCoordinator || (isAssignee && field === 'status') || workspace.taskEditPolicy === 'COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER' || status.requiresSignoff). Any discrepancy between frontend and backend logic causes false-positive enabled buttons that throw 403 errors or false-negative locked controls.

Option 2 (Embedded effectivePermissions on TaskDto + effectiveCapabilities[] on WorkspaceDetailDto — CHOSEN): Computing 8 boolean flags in memory during task serialization on the backend takes less than 5 microseconds per task (zero extra SQL queries, since created_by, assignee_ids, workspace.settings, and SecurityContext.capabilities are already loaded in memory) and adds ~140 bytes to the JSON payload (less than 3 KB across 50 tasks after gzip compression).

Decision:

WorkspaceDetailDto includes effectiveCapabilities: CapabilityCode[] for workspace- and project-level UI guards (e.g., showing + New Project or Workspace Settings).

Every TaskSummaryDto and TaskDetailDto includes a computed effectivePermissions: TaskEffectivePermissionsDto object so Antigravity CLI binds UI affordances directly to authoritative backend truth.

4.2 Core Public DTO Contracts (TypeScript / JSON Schema Representation)
Note how internal database fields (password_hash, storage_key, next_task_seq, raw ip_hash, unprocessed outbox timestamps) are strictly excluded from public DTOs:

5. Query/Filter AST Schema & Four-View Projection Semantics
5.1 Single Shared Query Endpoint with View Projections ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
Architectural Clarification: All four mandatory views (List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline) call the exact same query endpoint (POST /api/v1/communities/{cid}/workspaces/{wid}/tasks/query) passing the same canonical ViewQuerySpec AST alongside a projection mode ('LIST' | 'BOARD' | 'CALENDAR' | 'TIMELINE').

Why One Endpoint with Projection Metadata Wins: The filter, sort, permission scoping, and custom-field evaluation pipeline is 100% identical across all four views. The projection parameter only instructs the backend whether to include auxiliary view metadata in the response envelope (such as unscheduledCount and unscheduledPreview for Calendar/Timeline, or per-column totals when paginating wide Kanban boards). When a user already has a project's tasks cached in TanStack Query (up to 500 tasks), switching between List ↔ Board ↔ Calendar ↔ Timeline happens in-memory on the client in under 100ms with zero network round-trips.

5.2 Complete Filter Field Identifiers, Operators & Custom-Field Syntax
TypeScript
export type FilterOperator =
  | 'EQ' | 'NEQ' | 'IN' | 'NOT_IN'
  | 'CONTAINS' | 'IS_EMPTY' | 'IS_NOT_EMPTY'
  | 'GT' | 'GTE' | 'LT' | 'LTE' | 'BETWEEN';

export type CanonicalFilterField =
  | 'projectId' | 'listId' | 'statusId' | 'statusCategory'
  | 'priority' | 'itemType' | 'assigneeId' | 'createdById'
  | 'watcherId' | 'labelId' | 'milestoneId' | 'cycleId'
  | 'startDate' | 'dueDate' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt'
  | 'estimatePoints' | 'hasBlocker' | 'isOverdue' | 'q'
  | `cf.${string}`; // Custom field key, e.g., "cf.sponsor_tier"

export interface FilterGroupNode {
  conjunction: 'AND' | 'OR'; // Max nesting depth = 2 (Root group + 1 sub-group)
  conditions: Array<FilterConditionLeaf | FilterGroupNode>;
}

export interface FilterConditionLeaf {
  field: CanonicalFilterField;
  operator: FilterOperator;
  // Special token "$CURRENT_USER" resolves server-side to the authenticated user_id
  // Special tokens "$TODAY", "$NEXT_7_DAYS" resolve against workspace timezone
  value?: string | number | boolean | string[] | [string, string] | null;
}

export interface ViewQuerySpec {
  filter: FilterGroupNode;
  groupBy: 'statusId' | 'statusCategory' | 'listId' | 'priority' | 'assigneeId' | 'milestoneId' | 'none';
  subGroupBy: 'none' | 'assigneeId' | 'priority' | 'listId'; // Board swimlanes
  sortBy: Array<{
    field: 'rankKey' | 'priority' | 'dueDate' | 'startDate' | 'createdAt' | 'currentKey' | `cf.${string}`;
    direction: 'ASC' | 'DESC';
  }>;
  subtaskMode: 'NESTED' | 'TOP_LEVEL_ONLY' | 'FLATTENED';
  includeBacklog: boolean; // When false on Board View, hides BACKLOG category columns into tray
  includeCompleted: boolean;
  dateWindow?: {
    dateField: 'dueDate' | 'startToDueSpan';
    from: string; // "YYYY-MM-DD"
    to: string;   // "YYYY-MM-DD"
    includeUnscheduled: boolean; // Populates unscheduledTasks[] for Calendar/Timeline tray
  };
}
5.3 URL Serialization of Transient Filters vs. Saved Views (FEAT-C04)
To prevent "View Drift" (where one member filtering a Shared Board scrambles teammates' screens), the frontend enforces a strict two-layer state contract:

Persisted Saved View (SavedViewDto): Stored in the database via POST/PATCH /saved-views with scope: 'PERSONAL' | 'SHARED'.

URL Transient Diff Parameters: When a user opens ?viewId=v_sprint and clicks a filter chip (Assignee: Me) or changes grouping, the frontend never calls PATCH /saved-views automatically. Instead, it serializes the override into compact URL query parameters:?viewId=v_sprint&f.assigneeId=IN:$CURRENT_USER&group=priority
The UI compares the active URL state against savedView.querySpec; whenever isEqual(urlSpec, savedView.querySpec) === false, the toolbar renders the Draft State Bar:

For all users: Modified • [Reset] [Save as Personal View]

For OWNER, COORDINATOR, or view creator: adds [Update Shared View]

6. Task-Key Semantics & Update/Bulk-Operation Contracts
6.1 Precise Task-Key Lifecycle & Resolution Rules (FEAT-C07)
We distinguish Immutable Task Identity (task.id UUIDv7) from Permanent Key Resolvability (currentKey + task_key_aliases):

Lifecycle Operation	Exact Backend & Contract Behavior ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
1. Task Creation	Within the POST /tasks transaction, the backend locks the project counter (UPDATE projects SET next_task_seq = next_task_seq + 1 WHERE id = :pid RETURNING key_prefix, next_task_seq - 1), assigns current_key = 'FEST-14', and inserts ('FEST-14', task.id) into task_key_aliases. Concurrent creations never collide.
2. Prefix Uniqueness & Reservation	A keyPrefix (2–6 uppercase alphanumeric chars starting with a letter, regex ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,5}$) is unique across all projects and all historical prefixes in task_key_aliases within the same workspaceId.
3. Project Prefix Change (MKT → GRW)	When an Owner renames a project's prefix from MKT to GRW, a single transaction updates every task in that project (MKT-1..N → GRW-1..N) preserving each task's numeric suffix, inserts GRW-1..N into task_key_aliases, and keeps MKT-1..N in task_key_aliases. The retired prefix MKT remains reserved in that workspace so no future project can create conflicting MKT-* keys.
4. Cross-Project Move (Within Same Workspace)	Moving OPS-12 to project FEST atomically allocates the next sequence number in FEST (FEST-45), updates task.current_key = 'FEST-45', and registers 'FEST-45' in task_key_aliases while keeping 'OPS-12' → task.id active. If OPS-12 has subtasks (OPS-13, OPS-14), all subtasks move in the same transaction and receive sequential FEST-46, FEST-47 keys with aliases preserved.
5. Cross-Workspace Move (Personal → Shared)	Moving a task from a user's Personal Workspace (ME-04) to a Shared Workspace (FEST) executes a cross-workspace transfer: the task receives FEST-48 in the target workspace, and the Personal Workspace retains a tombstone alias redirect ME-04 → { targetWorkspaceId, targetTaskId } visible only to the personal workspace owner.
6. Cross-Community Boundary (Clone Only)	Tasks cannot be moved across separate Community tenants (strict tenant isolation). Instead, moving work across communities is performed via CSV Export/Import or Cross-Community Clone (creates a fresh UUID and key).
7. Alias Resolution on Archive vs. Permanent Purge	
• Archived Task (in 30-day Trash): Looking up OPS-12 or FEST-45 still resolves and returns the task with archivedAt != null so users see "This task is in Trash [Restore]".


• Permanently Purged Task: Hard-deleting a task from Trash deletes its Task row and marks its task_key_aliases entries as purged_at = NOW(). Historical key lookups return 410 Gone (TASK_PERMANENTLY_PURGED), and sequence numbers are never reused.

6.2 Single-Task Update, Ordering & All-or-Nothing Bulk Mutation Contract (FEAT-A08, FEAT-A10b)
A. Fractional Ordering (rankPlacement) Contract
Rather than requiring the client and server to run identical floating-point math, PATCH /tasks/{taskId} accepts a declarative rankPlacement object alongside an optional client-computed optimistic rankKeyHint:

JSON
{
  "statusId": "st_in_progress",
  "rankPlacement": {
    "afterTaskId": "0192d8f0-1111-7000-8000-000000000001",
    "beforeTaskId": "0192d8f0-2222-7000-8000-000000000002"
  }
}
The backend validates that afterTaskId and beforeTaskId exist in the target container, generates the authoritative lexicographical midpoint rankKey (with 30-bit jitter if after and before were concurrently moved to the same rank), updates only that 1 task row (O(1)), and returns the canonical rankKey in the 200 OK response and WebSocket TASK_REORDERED delta.

B. All-or-Nothing Atomic Bulk Operations (POST /tasks/bulk)
Strict Atomicity Rule ([Recommended Architectural Decision]): Bulk updates (up to 100 taskIds per request) execute inside a single all-or-nothing database transaction. Partial-success bulk APIs (where 14 tasks update and 3 fail) break client Undo (Z) expectations and leave boards in an inconsistent half-migrated state.

Pre-Commit Validation Report: Before committing, the backend checks permissions and domain invariants across all requested taskIds. If any task fails authorization or validation, the entire transaction rolls back and the API returns 403 or 422 containing a failedTasks: Array<{ taskId, currentKey, errorCode, message }> array so the UI can highlight the exact offending rows ("Cannot bulk-move 2 tasks because you lack permission on FEST-09 and FEST-11 — [Exclude 2 tasks & Apply to remaining 15]").

Batch Undo Support: Every successful POST /tasks/bulk call returns a single undoBatchId UUID and records the prior per-task snapshots under that batch ID, allowing a single POST /tasks/bulk/undo call (triggered by the 10-second Undo toast) to revert all 15 tasks atomically.

7. Realtime Event Envelope and JSON Schema Design
7.1 WebSocket Transport, Subscription & Gap Recovery Protocol (FEAT-F02)
Endpoint & Authentication: Clients connect to wss://<host>/api/v1/ws. Authentication uses the same __Host-session HTTP-only cookie (with strict Origin header validation matching the allowed frontend origin) or a short-lived (60-second), single-use WebSocket ticket obtained via POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket.

Workspace Room Subscription (SUBSCRIBE_WORKSPACE): After connecting, the client sends a subscription frame specifying the active communityId, workspaceId, and its last processed sequence number (lastSeenSeq):

JSON
{
  "type": "SUBSCRIBE_WORKSPACE",
  "requestId": "sub_01",
  "communityId": "0192d8e0-0000-7000-8000-000000000001",
  "workspaceId": "0192d8e0-0000-7000-8000-000000000002",
  "lastSeenSeq": 1042
}
The server verifies live membership in workspaceId and responds with SUBSCRIPTION_ACK containing { currentSeq: 1045 }.

Heartbeat & Stale Connection Detection: The server sends an application-level PING frame every 25 seconds; the client responds with PONG within 10 seconds. If no frame is received for 35 seconds, the client marks connection state as RECONNECTING (showing the non-blocking top status pill after 5 seconds) and reconnects with exponential backoff + jitter (500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s, max 15s).

Sequence Ordering, Echo Deduplication & Authoritative Catch-Up:

Every workspace event carries a strictly sequential integer workspaceSeq (1043, 1044, 1045...) and the originating mutationId.

Echo Deduplication: If event.mutationId exists in the client's recentlyCommittedMutationIds set, the client advances its lastSeenSeq = event.workspaceSeq and skips re-applying the delta.

Gap Detection (event.workspaceSeq > client.lastSeenSeq + 1) or Reconnect (currentSeq > lastSeenSeq): WebSocket frames are never assumed to have guaranteed delivery. Whenever a sequence gap is detected, the client pauses live buffer application and calls GET /api/v1/communities/{cid}/workspaces/{wid}/events?sinceSeq=1042.

Delta Replay vs. Full View Refetch: If the catch-up endpoint returns 200 OK (500 or fewer missed events), the client applies those deltas sequentially into the normalized TanStack Query task store. If the endpoint returns 410 Gone (EVENT_SEQ_OUT_OF_RETENTION because more than 500 events occurred while the laptop was asleep), the client invalidates its active workspace queries and performs a clean background refetch.

Immediate Permission Revocation (WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED): If a member or Coordinator is removed from a workspace (removeWorkspaceMember), the WebSocket broker immediately pushes a WORKSPACE_ACCESS_REVOKED frame to that user's socket, detaches the socket from room:workspace:{wid}, and the frontend redirects the user to their Personal Workspace with an informational toast.
