8. Mutation Idempotency, Offline Synchronization & Conflict-Resolution Contract
8.1 Server-Managed Field Revisions vs. Client Clocks ([Recommended Architectural Decision])
Why Client Clocks Must Never Be Used for Conflict Detection: Mobile phones and laptops frequently suffer NTP clock drift of several seconds or minutes. If User A's laptop clock is 2 minutes ahead of real time, timestamp-based Last-Write-Wins (client_timestamp > server_timestamp) would allow User A's stale offline edit to silently overwrite a newer edit made by User B.

Authoritative Per-Field Revision Mechanism (fieldRevisions):

Every Task row maintains an integer version counter (1, 2, 3..., incremented by 1 on every update) and a JSONB map field_revisions: Record<string, number> storing the exact task version at which each individual field was last modified:

JSON
{
  "version": 7,
  "fieldRevisions": {
    "title": 1,
    "descriptionMd": 5,
    "statusId": 7,
    "priority": 3,
    "dueDate": 2
  }
}
When a client edits a task (online or queued offline), it records the task's fieldRevisions snapshot at the moment the user began editing (baseFieldRevisions) and sends only the modified fields (patch) along with baseFieldRevisions:

JSON
{
  "patch": {
    "priority": "URGENT",
    "descriptionMd": "Updated speaker AV requirements with 6 wireless mics."
  },
  "baseFieldRevisions": {
    "priority": 3,
    "descriptionMd": 5
  }
}
Server Evaluation Rule (Safe Per-Field Merge vs. Same-Field Conflict):

For each field k in request.patch:

If server.fieldRevisions[k] === request.baseFieldRevisions[k], field k has not been touched by anyone else since the user read the task. Even if a teammate updated statusId (bumping server.version to 7), priority (revision 3 === 3) merges cleanly without conflict!

If server.fieldRevisions[k] > request.baseFieldRevisions[k], another user modified field k concurrently. The backend rejects the mutation with 409 Conflict (FIELD_REVISION_CONFLICT) and returns the structured conflictingFields[] array containing both clientValue and serverValue.

8.2 Staged Offline Synchronization Contract (FEAT-J02)
Day-1 Contract Primitives (Built in M1.1 So Endpoints Never Change Later)
X-Mutation-Id request header and idempotency_records deduplication table.

version, fieldRevisions, and fieldUpdatedAt properties on TaskDetailDto.

baseFieldRevisions optional object on UpdateTaskRequest.

409 Conflict Problem Details schema with conflictingFields[].

Phase 3 Client Offline Queue & Batch Replay Contract (POST /sync/mutations)
Supported Offline Operations:

CREATE_TASK (Assigns a temporary client key DRAFT-1 in IndexedDB; server replaces with canonical PREFIX-NUM upon sync and returns { clientTempId, taskId, assignedKey }).

UPDATE_TASK_FIELDS (Scalar fields: title, descriptionMd, statusId, priority, startDate, dueDate, estimatePoints, assigneeIds, labelIds, customFields).

CREATE_COMMENT (Queued threaded comment on an existing or offline-created task).

Explicitly Online-Only Operations: Workspace/project creation or deletion, role/permission changes, prefix changes, file binary uploads, and bulk operations.

Sequential Replay & Live Authorization Contract:

TypeScript
export interface OfflineSyncBatchRequest {
  clientSyncId: string;
  mutations: Array<{
    mutationId: string; // UUIDv4
    queuedAtClient: string; // Informational only (displayed in UI, never used for conflict math)
    opType: 'CREATE_TASK' | 'UPDATE_TASK_FIELDS' | 'CREATE_COMMENT';
    targetEntityId: string;
    payload: Record<string, unknown>;
    baseFieldRevisions?: Record<string, number>;
  }>;
}

export interface OfflineSyncBatchResponse {
  results: Array<{
    mutationId: string;
    status: 'APPLIED' | 'IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY' | 'CONFLICT_409' | 'DENIED_403' | 'VALIDATION_FAILED_422';
    entityId?: string;
    assignedKey?: string;
    updatedTask?: TaskDetailDto;
    problem?: ProblemDetails; // Populated on 409, 403, or 422
  }>;
}
Community-Safe Recovery When Permissions Are Revoked Offline (DENIED_403):
If a user edits FEST-14 offline in Community A and their workspace access (or community membership) is revoked before they reconnect:

The server rejects that queue item with status: 'DENIED_403'.

The client moves the rejected mutation out of the active sync queue into a persistent local IndexedDB unsynced_recovery_drafts store scoped to communityId.

Strict Community Boundary Rule: The client never automatically uploads a rejected draft from Community A into a workspace in Community B. Instead, the UI presents an explicit recovery drawer:

If the user is still an active member of Community A (only removed from that specific Shared Workspace), they can click [Save as Private Draft in My Community A Personal Workspace] or [Copy Text to Clipboard].

If the user's membership in Community A itself was suspended/revoked, they can click [Copy My Offline Edits to Clipboard / Download .md] or [Discard Draft].

Queue Expiration Policy: Unsynced mutations older than 14 days pause automatic background replay and prompt the user on sign-in ("You have 2 offline changes from 15 days ago — [Review & Sync] or [Discard]").

9. Authentication, Role-Preview Safeguards & File-Upload/Download Contract
9.1 Session Transport, CSRF Protection & Google OAuth Flow (FEAT-G01, FEAT-J03)
Session Cookie & CSRF Contract:

Primary browser authentication uses an HTTP-only, secure cookie: Set-Cookie: __Host-session=<opaque_token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1209600 (14-day sliding window, rotated every 24 hours).

To prevent Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-mutating requests (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE), login and /me/context return a session-bound csrfToken string, which Antigravity CLI attaches as the X-CSRF-Token header on all mutations. The backend rejects any cookie-authenticated mutation lacking a valid X-CSRF-Token or bearing an untrusted Origin header (403 CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED).

Role-Preview Simulation Safeguard (X-Preview-Role-Id — FEAT-G03):

UI Simulation vs. Backend Enforcement: When a Workspace Owner activates "Preview Workspace as [Role]", Antigravity CLI sets X-Preview-Role-Id: <roleId> on API requests.

Strict Downward-Scoping & Read-Only Guard:

The backend verifies the caller is a Workspace Owner or Global Admin (any other caller sending X-Preview-Role-Id has the header ignored).

For GET / query requests (getWorkspace, getTaskById, queryWorkspaceTasks), the backend computes effective_capabilities = caller_capabilities ∩ preview_role_capabilities, so the Owner sees the exact effectivePermissions and filtered UI state that the target role experiences.

Mutation Block During Preview: Any state-mutating request (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE, except read-only query POST .../tasks/query) sent while X-Preview-Role-Id is present is rejected with 403 PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY ("Exit Role Preview mode before making changes to workspace data"), guaranteeing an Owner never accidentally mutates production tasks while testing a role.

9.2 Secure Two-Phase File Upload & Authorized Download Contract (FEAT-A05a, FEAT-A05b)
Textual Explanation of Diagram: The sequence diagram below illustrates the complete file lifecycle: (1) pre-upload validation of MIME type, 25 MB size limit, and workspace storage quota before issuing a short-lived pre-signed S3 PUT URL, (2) direct browser-to-object-storage upload and completion confirmation, and (3) live authorization re-validation on every download request so a user removed from a workspace immediately loses access to previously uploaded files.

Code snippet
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UI as Antigravity CLI (Browser)
    participant API as Backend M11: File Service
    participant DB as Relational DB
    participant S3 as Private Object Storage (S3/R2)

    Note over UI,S3: Phase 1: Authorized Upload with Quota & Size Validation
    UI->>API: POST /workspaces/{wid}/files/upload-url\n{filename: "stage-quote.pdf", mimeType: "application/pdf", sizeBytes: 4200000, taskId: "tsk_14"}
    API->>DB: Verify live `file:upload` capability + Check (usedBytes + sizeBytes <= quotaBytes)
    API->>DB: INSERT workspace_files (status = 'PENDING', size_bytes = 4200000)
    API->>S3: Sign PUT URL (TTL = 10 min, exact Content-Type & Content-Length locked)
    API-->>UI: 201 Created {fileId, uploadUrl, requiredHeaders, expiresAt}
    UI->>S3: PUT <uploadUrl> (Binary File Stream)
    S3-->>UI: 200 OK (ETag)
    UI->>API: POST /workspaces/{wid}/files/{fileId}/complete {sha256Hash}
    API->>S3: HEAD object (Verify object exists & size matches)
    API->>DB: UPDATE workspace_files SET status = 'ACTIVE' + Emit FILE_ATTACHED event
    API-->>UI: 200 OK (WorkspaceFileDto)

    Note over UI,S3: Phase 2: Live Re-Validated Download (Zero Permanent Public URLs)
    UI->>API: GET /workspaces/{wid}/files/{fileId}/download-url
    API->>DB: Re-verify caller is STILL an active member of {wid} & file is not purged
    alt Caller Still Authorized
        API->>S3: Sign GET URL (TTL = 15 min, Content-Disposition: attachment)
        API-->>UI: 200 OK {downloadUrl, expiresAt}
        UI->>S3: GET <downloadUrl>
    else Access Revoked During Session
        API-->>UI: 404 Not Found (RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND)
    end
Allowed MIME Types & executable Blocking: The backend blocklists executable and script extensions/MIME types (.exe, .sh, .bat, .html, .svg inline scripts unless served with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=... and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff) to prevent Stored XSS via uploaded attachments.

Orphan Upload Cleanup: A scheduled background job (M11) sweeps workspace_files WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour' and deletes any uncompleted multipart/pending objects so abandoned uploads never consume workspace quota.

Contract & Integration Concern	Antigravity CLI (Frontend) Responsibility	Backend Developer Responsibility
1. Schema & Type Generation	Consume auto-generated TypeScript interfaces (src/contracts/api-types.gen.ts) via typed API client hooks; never hand-write endpoint URLs or response shapes inside UI components.	Validate incoming requests and outgoing responses against /contracts/openapi.yaml and /contracts/ws-events.schema.json in CI.
2. Authentication, CSRF & Preview Headers	Store csrfToken in memory, attach X-CSRF-Token and X-Mutation-Id on all writes, attach X-Preview-Role-Id when Role Preview mode is active, and disable mutation triggers during Preview mode.	Issue __Host-session cookie, validate CSRF & Origin headers, enforce downward-only X-Preview-Role-Id capability intersection, and reject preview mutations (403 PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY).
3. Authorization & UI Affordances	Read workspace.myRole.effectiveCapabilities and task.effectivePermissions to enable/disable buttons and display contextual lock tooltips (restrictedReasonCode).	Act as the sole authoritative enforcement point across all 6 stages of the security pipeline; compute effectivePermissions on every returned task DTO.
4. Task Ordering (rankKey)	Compute an optimistic local rankKey for instant <16ms drag/menu reordering and send rankPlacement: { afterTaskId, beforeTaskId } to the server.	Validate afterTaskId/beforeTaskId, compute the authoritative jittered rankKey midpoint, persist in O(1), and broadcast the canonical rankKey.
5. Four-View Projection & Transient Filters	Serialize transient user filter/sort tweaks into browser URL search parameters (?viewId=...&f.priority=...), display the Copy-on-Write Modified • [Reset] bar, and render List, Board, Calendar, and Timeline over the normalized client task cache.	Execute POST .../tasks/query against ViewQuerySpec, enforce workspace/project isolation, populate unscheduledTasks when requested, and persist SavedView records only on explicit /saved-views calls.
6. Realtime Sequence & Gap Recovery	Track lastSeenSeq per subscribed workspace, deduplicate echoed mutationId packets, detect sequence gaps (seq > lastSeenSeq + 1), call GET .../events?sinceSeq=, and refetch the active view if 410 Gone is returned.	Assign monotonic workspace_seq_id inside the outbox transaction, push delta packets to authorized workspace sockets, immediately kick removed members, and retain at least the last 500 events per workspace for delta catch-up.
7. Offline Queue & Conflict Resolution	Persist offline mutations (CREATE_TASK, UPDATE_TASK_FIELDS, CREATE_COMMENT) in IndexedDB with baseFieldRevisions, replay sequentially on reconnect, present the 3-way Conflict Resolver Drawer on 409, and quarantine 403 revoked edits into the local Personal Recovery Store.	Deduplicate X-Mutation-Id via idempotency_records, evaluate live RBAC at replay time, compare baseFieldRevisions per edited field, auto-merge non-overlapping fields, and return conflictingFields[] on same-field collisions.
12. Mocking, Code Generation and Parallel Integration Workflow
To allow Antigravity CLI and the Backend Developer to build Milestone M1.1, M1.2, and M1.3 in parallel without blocking each other:

1
Contract Freeze & Automated Type Generation
Single source of truth before writing UI or controller code
Both developers agree on /contracts/openapi.yaml and /contracts/ws-events.schema.json. Running npm run contracts:generate executes redocly lint (verifying OpenAPI 3.1 validity) and openapi-typescript + openapi-zod-client to output src/contracts/api-types.gen.ts and runtime Zod validators.

2
Deterministic Shared Seed Dataset (/contracts/fixtures/seed-v1.json)
75-user community fixture shared by MSW and backend test suites
Maintain one canonical JSON fixture file representing our 75-person community ("SVIET Tech & Ops Community"), containing:

4 test personas with deterministic UUIDs (usr_admin, usr_owner, usr_coord_reetabrata, usr_member_sarthak).

1 Personal Workspace (ME-1..5) and 2 Shared Workspaces (FEST-1..35 and OPS-1..15), including 1 historical moved task alias (OLD-09 → FEST-14), 3 blocking dependency links (1 with a date conflict), 5 unscheduled tasks, and 2 archived tasks in Trash.

3
Contract-Driven Mock Service Worker (MSW) in Antigravity CLI
Simulates real validation, 403 policies, 409 conflicts, and WebSocket deltas
Antigravity CLI runs against an MSW handler layer (src/mocks/handlers.ts) seeded with seed-v1.json. The MSW layer enforces the exact same X-Mutation-Id header check, Conflict 1 & 2 permission flags, fieldRevisions conflict check (?simulateConflict=true query toggle), and simulated WebSocket sequence broadcasts so all 6 UI states (Loading, Empty, Empty Filter, Populated, Permission-Locked, and Error/Conflict) are tested before the backend is even deployed.

4
Backend Schemathesis Conformance & Milestone Integration Gate
Automated contract verification at each sub-milestone boundary
The Backend Developer runs automated OpenAPI conformance tests (using Schemathesis or Prism proxy validation) against their local server seeded with seed-v1.json. At the end of M1.1, M1.2, and M1.3, Antigravity CLI switches VITE_API_MODE=live to run the Playwright E2E suite directly against the live backend.

13. Contract-Versioning, Change-Management Rules & Risk-Based Contract Checks
13.1 Contract-Versioning & Change-Management Rules
Additive-Only Changes Within /api/v1: Adding an optional request property, adding a new field to a response DTO, or adding a new endpoint is non-breaking and may be merged via a standard Contract PR after regenerating api-types.gen.ts and MSW mocks.

Breaking Change Prohibition: Renaming or removing an existing JSON property, changing a property's type, tightening a nullable field to non-nullable in requests, or removing an enum value is strictly prohibited without incrementing the operation version or coordinating a simultaneous dual-side update recorded in the Decision Log.

Deprecation Lifecycle: Deprecated fields must be marked deprecated: true in openapi.yaml with an x-deprecation-sunset milestone note and remain populated by the backend until all frontend references are removed.

13.2 The 11 Risk-Based Automated Contract Checks (High Signal, Zero Bloat)
Rather than writing hundreds of redundant unit tests, every build must pass these 11 targeted contract checks protecting our highest-risk integration boundaries:

Check ID	Protected Integration Boundary / Failure Mode	Automated Verification Mechanism
CHK-01 Schema Conformance	Response DTO or Problem Details error drifts from openapi.yaml (e.g., missing effectivePermissions or returning null on a required field).	Validate every 2xx and 4xx/5xx API test response against the compiled OpenAPI 3.1 JSON Schema validator in CI.
CHK-02 Auth, CSRF & Role-Preview Guard	Cookie-authenticated write succeeds without X-CSRF-Token, or a mutation succeeds while X-Preview-Role-Id is active.	Send PATCH /tasks/{id} (a) without X-CSRF-Token → assert 403 CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED; (b) with X-Preview-Role-Id → assert 403 PREVIEW_MODE_READ_ONLY.
CHK-03 Tenant Isolation & Anti-Enumeration	User in Community A (or unjoined Workspace B) probes /workspaces/{wid}/tasks/by-key/SEC-01 or /search?q=SEC and learns whether the task exists.	Assert that querying a non-existent task key and an existing task key in an unauthorized workspace/Personal Workspace return byte-identical 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND responses and 0 search hits.
CHK-04 Idempotent Mutation Deduplication	Network retry of POST /tasks or PATCH /tasks/{id} with the same X-Mutation-Id creates a duplicate task or increments version twice.	Dispatch identical POST /tasks request twice with the same X-Mutation-Id; assert only 1 database row is created, version == 1, and the 2nd response carries X-Idempotent-Replayed: true.
CHK-05 Per-Field Concurrent Update & Conflict	Two users edit the same task concurrently: (a) different fields (priority vs. dueDate) fail unnecessarily, or (b) the same field (descriptionMd) silently overwrites without 409.	Test (a): Send concurrent patches to priority and dueDate with baseFieldRevisions → assert both return 200 OK and merge. Test (b): Send stale baseFieldRevisions.descriptionMd → assert 409 FIELD_REVISION_CONFLICT with conflictingFields[0].
CHK-06 Atomic Task-Key Generation & Alias Redirect	Concurrent task creations collide on PREFIX-NUM, or moving OPS-12 to FEST-45 breaks links to OPS-12.	Fire 20 parallel POST /tasks requests → assert 20 unique sequential keys FEST-1..20. Move FEST-5 to project OPS → assert GET .../by-key/FEST-5 returns 200 OK with currentKey: "OPS-1" and matchedAlias: "FEST-5".
CHK-07 All-or-Nothing Bulk Mutation Rollback	A bulk update of 10 tasks where 1 task is unauthorized leaves 9 tasks mutated and 1 unchanged.	Call POST /tasks/bulk with 9 valid task IDs and 1 task ID where the actor lacks permission → assert 403, failedTasks.length == 1, and verify all 9 valid tasks remain at their original version in the database.
CHK-08 Realtime Sequence Gap & 410 Resync	Client misses WebSocket messages during a disconnect and applies out-of-order state, or fails to recover when the gap exceeds 500 events.	Simulate gap (lastSeenSeq = 10, server at 15) → assert client calls GET .../events?sinceSeq=10 and patches cache to 15. Simulate 410 Gone → assert client invalidates and refetches active view query.
CHK-09 Offline Replay Live-RBAC & Recovery	User queues an edit offline, has their workspace membership removed, and reconnects; server either erroneously applies the edit or client silently deletes the user's text.	Remove user from workspace, then call POST /sync/mutations → assert item returns DENIED_403 and assert frontend stores payload in unsynced_recovery_drafts scoped to communityId.
CHK-10 Live File-Download Re-Authorization	A removed workspace member reuses a bookmarked /files/{fileId}/download-url endpoint to fetch private attachments.	Remove member from workspace → call GET .../files/{fileId}/download-url → assert 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND (no pre-signed URL issued).
CHK-11 Cross-View Query Consistency	Applying a ViewQuerySpec filter returns different task sets across List, Board, Calendar (scheduled + unscheduled), and Timeline projections.	Execute POST .../tasks/query with identical filter across all 4 projection values → assert the union of returned taskIds (including unscheduledTasks on Calendar/Timeline) is 100% identical.
14. Major Unresolved API Decisions and Their Consequences
In strict compliance with Section 3.C of the prompt, the three unresolved stakeholder policies from Prompt 05 are not marked as approved decisions. Below is how our API contract handles them safely today via explicit policy fields, and what changes (if any) occur once stakeholders sign off:

Unresolved Policy ID	Provisional Default in Contract ([Unresolved Stakeholder Decision])	How the API Contract Accommodates Both Outcomes Without Breaking Schema	What Remains Open Until Stakeholder Sign-Off
UNR-API-01 (Global Admin vs. Personal Workspace Privacy)	PRIVATE_STRICT: Global Admins see Personal Workspace quota metadata (adminListWorkspaceDirectory), but adminBreakGlassOverride and task/file endpoints return 403 PERSONAL_WORKSPACE_PRIVATE / 404 on Personal Workspaces.	MeContextDto.communities[].policies.personalWorkspaceAdminPolicy exposes 'PRIVATE_STRICT' | 'AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS'. If stakeholders choose AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS, the exact same POST .../break-glass endpoint simply enables break-glass on type == 'PERSONAL' workspaces with zero DTO or route changes.	Confirm whether the backend should reject POST .../break-glass on PERSONAL workspaces permanently (PRIVATE_STRICT) or allow it with owner notification (AUDITED_BREAK_GLASS).
UNR-API-02 (Default Task-Editing Policy in Shared Workspaces)	CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT: Task definitions are editable by Owners, Coordinators, and Task Creator/Assigner; Assignees update status/progress/subtasks/comments; ordinary Members create tasks and comment.	WorkspaceDetailDto.settings.taskEditPolicy ('CREATOR_COORDINATOR_STRICT' | 'COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER') and TaskDto.effectivePermissions already decouple the frontend from the policy rule. Regardless of which default is chosen, Antigravity CLI simply reads task.effectivePermissions.canEditDefinition. ## Appendix AF — DEC-OPEN-02 Option A product decision and implementation trace

**Decision date:** 31 October 2026  
**Authority:** Explicit product-owner approval in this conversation.  
**Status:** OWNER CONFIRMED — Option A.

The Workspace Owner sets the maximum allowed assignee-editable field groups and the default applied to newly created tasks. The Task Creator chooses the allowed subset for each task. An active Workspace Owner may override the task-level choice for governance and continuity. The same task-level grant set applies to all active assignees on a task.

The allowed field groups are `TITLE_DESCRIPTION`, `DATES_PRIORITY`, and `CUSTOM_FIELDS_LINKS`. Existing assignee execution rights for status, subtasks, comments and estimates are unchanged. Per-assignee differences and task-specific restrictions of broader role/contextual rights are not supported.

**Wire changes:** OpenAPI `0.3.20-draft` adds `assigneeEditableFieldGroupsAllowed` and `assigneeEditableFieldGroupsDefault` to Workspace DTO/settings; adds `assigneeEditableFieldGroups` to CreateTaskRequest, UpdateTaskRequest and TaskDto; and adds `canManageAssigneeFieldGrants` to TaskPermissions. AuditEventType adds `TASK_ASSIGNEE_FIELD_GRANTS_CHANGED`, and AuditEventMetadataDto adds allow-listed before/after group arrays. The old `assigneeCanEditDatesPriority` boolean is removed. The WebSocket event schema remains unchanged.

**Validation boundary:** Static contract and document validation can verify enum/reference/property consistency. Runtime proof still requires tests for creator authorization, Owner override, non-creator Coordinator/Assigner denial, current-ceiling enforcement, default-on-create behavior, multiple assignees, assignment revocation, collaborative mode, optimistic concurrency and all-or-nothing updates.


Validation note: CR-16 historical validator evidence applies to 0.3.17-draft only; run the new 0.3.19 focused validator for this amendment.

## Appendix AH — DEC-OPEN-02 implementation acceptance matrix

| Scenario | Expected behavior | Verification owner |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace policy defaults | New Workspace has empty allowed/default arrays; default must always be a subset of allowed. | Backend contract + DB integration |
| Owner configures ceiling | Only active Workspace Owner can change allowed/default arrays; invalid default subset rejects atomically. | Backend + Security |
| Task creation default | Omitted task grant property applies current Workspace default; explicit subset is accepted; out-of-ceiling group returns 422. | Backend + Frontend |
| Creator task-level edit | Active Task Creator can update task grant groups within ceiling; field revision conflict returns 409 and no partial write. | Backend |
| Non-creator denial | Coordinator/Assigner who is not the Task Creator and is not an Owner cannot change task grant groups; returns 403. | Backend + Security |
| Owner override | Active Workspace Owner can change grants on any task in the Workspace, still within allowed ceiling. | Backend + Security |
| Active assignee effect | Only active assignees gain the selected additional field-group permissions; all active assignees share the same set. | Backend + Frontend |
| Assignment revocation | Removing an assignee immediately removes all task-assignee grants for that user. | Backend + Realtime |
| Ceiling reduction | Removing a group from Workspace ceiling immediately removes effective permission for that group across existing tasks. | Backend + Security |
| Default change | Changing Workspace default affects newly created tasks only; existing task selections remain unchanged. | Backend |
| Collaborative mode | Per-task grants never restrict broader edit rights independently granted by `COLLABORATIVE_MEMBER`. | Backend + Frontend |
| Offline replay | `assigneeEditableFieldGroups` and Workspace policy arrays cannot be queued offline. | Frontend + Backend |
| Atomic patch | A mixed task edit + forbidden grant change is rejected as a whole; no partial task or permission mutation. | Backend integration |
| Auditability | Workspace ceiling/default changes and per-task grant changes record actor, scope, before/after group codes and event correlation without leaking task content. | Backend + Security |

These are required tests, not claims that the tests or database migrations have already been executed.
